incidents.title: Venezuela demands return of gold reserves held in U.K.
incidents.description: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez called on the Bank of England to release approximately $1.9 billion in Venezuelan gold reserves that have remained inaccessible since 2019. The demand followed renewed diplomatic engagement between Venezuela and the U.K., which agreed in September to restore ambassador-level representation.

incidents.title: Estonia to reinforce border with Russia
incidents.description: On Oct. 28, Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem announced an initiative to build 150 bunkers along the approximately 183-mile-long Estonian/Russian border.

incidents.title: Ukraine fires over 600 drones at Moscow region
incidents.description: Ukraine fired over 600 drones at the Moscow region, disrupting air traffic at major airports during the overnight period of Oct. 28-29.

incidents.title: Kremlin aide says trilateral talks could resume, declines to set date
incidents.description: Senior Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov said trilateral peace talks among Russia, Ukraine and the United States could began after Nov. 4 in Abu Dhabi depending on “battlefield conditions.” Ushakov added that Ukraine’s European allies would be excluded from the talks.

incidents.title: U.S. adds medical organizations to entity list
incidents.description: The U.S. placed three medical companies on its Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List, barring their products from entry or distribution in the United States. China condemned the move as a violation of the recent consensus between the two countries to limit trade restrictions.

incidents.title: U.S. secretary of defense visits Philippines
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth traveled to the Philippines and Singapore to discuss regional security with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and partner nations, ahead of an upcoming meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The visit focused on laying the foundations for a deepened potential U.S.-ASEAN security framework.

incidents.title: India opposes Cuba embargo
incidents.description: India voted with 129 other countries at the U.N. General Assembly to end U.S. economic restrictions on Cuba. India’s representative also objected to national sanctions measures that have consequences outside of the country imposing them and reiterated New Delhi’s preference for resolving international disputes through diplomacy.

incidents.title: India confirms China border friction
incidents.description: The head of India’s Indo-Tibetan Border Police confirmed that Indian and Chinese forces have confronted one another at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh and that the situation remains unresolved. His comments marked the Indian government’s first official acknowledgment of the latest confrontations along this portion of the disputed frontier, following earlier reports of increased Chinese activity in the area.

incidents.title: U.N. approves resolution seeking end to U.S. embargo after Cuban diplomat ejected
incidents.description: Following an Oct. 27 shouting match on the floor of the U.N. General Assembly between Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parilla and U.S. Envoy to the U.N. Mike Waltz, the body approved a nonbinding resolution to end to the U.S. embargo on Cuba. Support for the perennial resolution fell to a 30-year low, with 130 countries in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions. Waltz reported Cuban diplomat Richard Tur de la Concepcion was ejected from the U.S. for allegedly shoving a U.S. diplomat during the confrontation.

incidents.title: Russian energy company accused of financing Alaskan pipeline
incidents.description: Former Polar LNG CEO Joel Riddle has alleged that Russian energy company Novatek secretly provided financing for a proposed liquefied natural gas project in Alaska, potentially violating U.S. sanctions. Riddle, who resigned in September, claimed the Russian company had a greater role in the project than was publicly disclosed. Polar LNG and its Abu Dhabi-based parent company denied the allegations but acknowledged that Novatek had made a payment toward a proposed minority ownership stake in the project. Novatek also denied financing the project's operations or holding any ownership interest. The proposed facility, separate from the larger Alaska LNG pipeline project, would use Russian-built liquefaction equipment and is awaiting federal authorization.

incidents.title: Indonesian students protest wildfire response
incidents.description: Hundreds of students and civil society activists demonstrated in Jakarta, Bandung, and Makassar against Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s handling of widespread wildfires and his economic policies. Protesters demanded the government declare the fires a national disaster and reduce spending on programs such as free school meals, while police and military personnel blocked some demonstrators in Jakarta, resulting in scuffles.

incidents.title: Indonesian sovereign wealth fund bids for stock exchange stake
incidents.description: Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara submitted a proposal to acquire a stake in the Indonesia Stock Exchange as authorities accelerate plans to convert the exchange from a member-controlled organization into a shareholder-owned company. The proposed restructuring follows warnings from Morgan Stanley Capital International over market transparency and a sharp stock market decline, while Danantara’s bid remains under consideration.

incidents.title: U.S. senator warns against sanction violations, despite Trump deal
incidents.description: U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal warned a company currently importing a 40,000-metric-ton shipment of Russian diesel to New York that it was in violation of U.S. sanctions and may face legal repercussions despite a deal announced by U.S. President Donald Trump to waive specific sanctions on the import of Russian diesel.

incidents.title: U.N. approves resolution seeking end to U.S. embargo after Cuban diplomat ejected
incidents.description: Following an Oct. 27 shouting match on the floor of the U.N. General Assembly between Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parilla and U.S. Envoy to the U.N. Mike Waltz, the body approved a nonbinding resolution to end to the U.S. embargo on Cuba. Support for the perennial resolution fell to a 30-year low, with 130 countries in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions. Waltz reported Cuban diplomat Richard Tur de la Concepcion was ejected from the U.S. for allegedly shoving a U.S. diplomat during the confrontation.

incidents.title: U.S. warns Gulf allies of possible resumption of high-intensity conflict with Iran
incidents.description: U.S. officials warned Gulf allies to prepare for a likely resumption of high-intensity military operations against Iran following the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.

incidents.title: Houthis bomb Aden airport
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group bombed the Aden international airport, a critical node of transport for Yemen’s internationally recognized government, on Oct. 28, disrupting air traffic.

incidents.title: Vance offers to lead direct peace talks with Iran
incidents.description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance reached out to Gen. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s National Security Council and former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander, through Qatari mediators, offering to personally lead direct peace talks with senior Iranian officials.

incidents.title: Netanyahu-led bloc falls short of parliamentary majority
incidents.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc was projected to win 53 of 120 seats in the Knesset, a higher share of seats than won by the opposition-led bloc but short of the 61 needed to form a parliamentary majority. If coalition negotiations fail to form a unity government, another election could be held in 2027.

incidents.title: U.S. bans BYD on Japanese bases
incidents.description: The U.S. military has imposed a ban on all vehicles associated with Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD Co in the Kadena airbase in Okinawa, citing security concerns over the possible collection of sensitive information by the automaker in what could be the first of successive bans at other U.S. bases globally.

incidents.title: Cyclone Arnab hits India
incidents.description: Cyclone Arnab made landfall in Andhra Pradesh on Oct. 28, leaving at least three people dead and causing flooding, property damage, and electricity outages. Authorities evacuated around 180,000 people in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha ahead of the storm, while transportation and schools faced disruptions.

incidents.title: Brazilian opposition candidate Bolsonaro lands in Florida
incidents.description: Despite an order by Brazil’s Supreme Court to surrender his civilian and diplomatic passports, after losing the presidential election on Oct. 25, right-wing Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro fled to the United States, where the State Department said he and his family will be granted visas. Bolsonaro is a subject of a money laundering investigation by the Brazilian high court.

incidents.title: Canada reports limited progress in U.S. trade talks
incidents.description: A Canadian government official with knowledge ‌of the discussions said some progress had been made in trade talks between Canada and the United ​States. Reuters reported on Monday that the two countries were working ​on a deal to ease U.S. ​tariffs on Canadian steel and autos.

incidents.title: Canada, UAE sign comprehensive trade deal
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement expected to take effect in 2027. The deal aims to reduce or eliminate tariffs on over 99% of current Canadian exports to the UAE, create a more predictable environment for trade and investment, and expand market access for Canadian goods and services.

incidents.title: Bank of Canada raises key interest rate
incidents.description: The Bank of Canada raised its key policy rate 25 basis points to 2.5% and warned that further increases may be needed to curb inflation. The bank also adjusted its inflation forecast for 2027 to 3.1%, up from 2.0% in July.

incidents.title: Ethiopia aquires Russian aircraft and air defense systems
incidents.description: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the delivery of 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets, with four S-400 air defense batteries scheduled for later delivery. Russia confirmed that an initial batch of two aircraft had been delivered. Abiy credited Russian President Vladimir Putin with accelerating delivery of the jets by a year.

incidents.title: German auto exports rise
incidents.description: Germany's export expectations increased significantly in October according to the Ifo Institute, a major economic think tank. For industry writ large, exports increased from 9% to 12.2% this year. Export increases are concentrated in the automobile sector, where a 12.7% monthly rise was projected.

incidents.title: Report alleges Myanmar circumvented sanctions with import of Iranian fuel
incidents.description: Reuters reported that the U.S.-sanctioned tanker Reef brought jet fuel from Iran to Myanmar in December 2025 with false documentation claiming it was part of a $16 million purchase of South African diesel. Satellite imagery analyzed by SynMax Intelligence tracked the ship’s journey from its true origin, the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. This revelation follows earlier reporting that covert shipments of jet fuel from Iran to Myanmar have continued into 2026, despite U.S. sanctions on both governments.

incidents.title: Localized ceasefire takes effect in southern Ukraine
incidents.description: A localized humanitarian ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine around the city of Oleshky in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region that began Oct. 27, has held as of Oct. 30, after being proposed by U.S. first lady Melania Trump.

incidents.title: Jordan bombs southern Syria following attack on Christian community
incidents.description: Jordan reported killing at least 20 Islamic State militants after conducting bombings in southern Syria in response to an attack against a funeral in a Jordanian Christian community that killed at least nine people on Oct. 23. Syrian authorities said the Jordanian bombings killed at least seven civilians.

incidents.title: U.S., Japan, continue Keen Sword 27 drills
incidents.description: The U.S. and Japan are continuing their two-week long Keen Sword 27 joint military drills, focusing on antiship capabilities near Kyushu and Japan’s southwestern islands. The drills are largely seen as a test of both countries’ abilities to counter China’s naval control in the event of a Taiwan contingency.

incidents.title: El Salvador deploys 1,000 troops to Haiti following gang ambush
incidents.description: El Salvador sent approximately 1,000 soldiers to Haiti after four Salvadoran personnel serving in a U.N.-backed security mission disappeared during an Oct. 18 gang attack near Port-au-Prince. The U.S. provided military transport aircraft to support the deployment.

incidents.title: Trump plans to rescind regulation of methane produced from oil drilling
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced the termination of a Biden-era regulation targeting methane leaks and byproducts emitted during oil and gas production, arguing that it would encourage domestic oil and gas production and reduce costs.

incidents.title: Trump suggests Venezuela could become 51st U.S. state
incidents.description: During a campaign appearance in Texas, U.S. President Donald Trump highlighted a shipment of Venezuelan oil arriving in the U.S. and raised the possibility of incorporating Venezuela as the country’s 51st state.

incidents.title: DRC opposition parties meet in Rome for security conference
incidents.description: Leaders of several opposition political parties such as ADD Congo and the Article 64 Coalition (C64) met in Rome to discuss the ongoing security crisis in the eastern part of the country. This represents the first meeting of the parties since C64’s launch earlier this year. Opposition leaders used the meeting to call for the full implementation of U.N. Security Council Resolution 2773, which calls for the withdrawal of Rwandan forces and assistance to the Front for the Refounding of the Nation. Alongside announcing their intent to meet with former President Joseph Kabila and President Félix Tshisekedi separately, assembled opposition leaders formally rejected Tshisekedi’s constitutional reforms and militarized approaches to the DRC’s security crisis.

incidents.title: DRC opposition meets in Rome
incidents.description: Leaders from several opposition political parties such as ADD Congo and the Article 64 Coalition (C64) met in Rome to discuss the ongoing security crisis in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the first meeting of the parties since C64’s launch earlier this year. Opposition leaders called for full implementation of U.N. Security Council Resolution 2773, which calls for the withdrawal of Rwandan forces and assistance to the Front for the Refounding of the Nation. Alongside announcing their intent to meet with former President Joseph Kabila and President Félix Tshisekedi separately, assembled opposition leaders formally rejected Tshisekedi’s constitutional reforms and militarized approaches to the DRC’s security crisis.

incidents.title: France’s consumer confidence hits 13-year low
incidents.description: According to the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies, France’s consumer confidence dropped from 85 to 80 in October, its lowest level since June 2013 amid sustained nationwide protests. This reading was five points below economists’ expectations and is 20 points below its historical average of 100 recorded between January 1987 and December 2025.

incidents.title: Shortages raise Sudan fuel and transportation prices
incidents.description: Fuel prices in Sudan have risen to 40,000 Sudanese pounds ($4.30) per gallon in Gazira state and 35,000 pounds ($3.80) in Port Sudan. Fuel shortages have spawned hourslong waits for drivers. The Transport Chambers Union raised intercity bus fares by 40% and minibus fares by 30% this month.

incidents.title: Indonesia reduces natural gas exports to Singapore
incidents.description: Indonesia reduced pipeline natural gas exports to Singapore by 31 million standard cubic feet per day, approximately 8% of its pipeline supply to the country, citing maintenance shutdowns and increased domestic demand. Following concerns raised by Singapore’s prime minister, Indonesian Energy Minister Bahilil Lahadalia said the reduction remained within minimum contractual supply requirements.

incidents.title: Hezbollah readies for resumption of war with Israel
incidents.description: Lebanese security sources said Hezbollah has utilized aid worth tens of millions of dollars from Tehran to rearm for a possible resumption of hostilities with Israel in the case of renewed U.S./Israeli strikes inside Iran.

incidents.title: EU planning trade measures against China in 2027
incidents.description: The European Union is reportedly planning further measures against Chinese chemical, furniture, and machinery imports as early as the beginning of 2027. The revelation comes a few weeks following the EU and China signing a trade deal limiting the number of Chinese hybrid vehicles flowing into the bloc.

incidents.title: Appeals court rejects Department of Justice bid to disqualify California ballots
incidents.description: A three-judge panel of the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected a Justice Department attempt to disqualify 20,000 ballots in California that it alleged were cast by noncitizens. The court sent the case back to a federal district court.

incidents.title: Student List party wins Serbian election
incidents.description: A student-backed electoral coalition secured a majority in Serbia’s snap parliamentary election, defeating Aleksandar Vučić’s ruling alliance following nearly two years of protests demanding his removal from power. Vučić conceded defeat as tens of thousands celebrated across the country.

incidents.title: French protest leaders vow to continue demonstrations
incidents.description: French student leaders declared that they would continue protesting despite government promises to reduce class sizes, take out $4.5 billion in loans for school renovations, and reform university admissions, arguing that their demands have not been fully met.

incidents.title: China announces plan to reactivate Venezuelan power plant
incidents.description: China Machinery Engineering Corporation plans to reactivate a 600-megawatt generating unit at Venezuela’s Planta Centro power station, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the project. The oil-fueled unit would restore approximately one-quarter of the facility’s former generating capacity. Located in Carabobo state, the complex has operated at minimal capacity since 2021 due to aging equipment, mechanical failures, and fuel shortages. The work is part of ongoing repairs to Venezuela’s electricity infrastructure following years of recurring outages, with conditions worsening after earthquakes in June.

incidents.title: DRC government detains opposition leader
incidents.description: The DRC’s central government detained Prince Epenge, president of opposition party Action for Democracy and Development Congo, claiming he was “spreading false rumors” over a former party colleague who was killed in a September protest. Epenge, who was detained on his way to a political summit in Rome, was being held incommunicado.

incidents.title: Ethiopian forces hold senior opposition fighter
incidents.description: Ethiopian National Defense forces captured Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) Maj. Gen. Yohannesd Woldegiorgis, also known as John Medid, was captured by Ethiopian National Defense Forces and remains in custody, although some reports say he voluntarily surrendered. His detention highlights growing internal divisions and loss of cohesion among the TPLF amid ongoing military pressure.

incidents.title: French students to continue protests despite government concessions
incidents.description: French student leaders declared that they would continue a protest campaign despite government promises to reduce class sizes, put $4.5 billion in loans toward school renovations, and reform university admissions, arguing that their demands have not been fully met.

incidents.title: German business morale improves
incidents.description: According to a survey by Ifo Institute, a major economic think tank, German business morale slightly increased this month from 89.9 to 90.2 in their index. This marks the sixth consecutive month in which business confidence increased. The sentiment was largely concentrated in the manufacturing sector, which has seen an increase in orders and a boost in government investment.

incidents.title: INE president Guadalupe Taddei announces resignation
incidents.description: Guadalupe Taddei, president of the National Electoral Institute (INE), the autonomous body that organizes Mexico’s federal elections, announced on Oct. 25 that she will resign. Her decision follows findings by the Superior Audit Office of the Federation of conflicts of interest and diverted funds in INE contracts, along with criticism that her driver served as a legal representative for a company that supplies electoral materials.

incidents.title: North Korean leader visits China
incidents.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un traveled to China to formally inaugurate a recently opened river bridge connecting the countries. The move comes as both countries have forged closer ties, along with Russia.

incidents.title: China holds fifth plenum
incidents.description: The Chinese Communist Party's Central Committee held its fifth plenum this week, with President Xi Jinping taking the stage to remark on the importance of “party self-governance." The term likely refers to the high importance Xi has placed on anti-corruption campaigns and the need for loyal party members. The plenum is the last substantive party meeting prior to next year’s 21st Party Congress, during which a new Central Committee will be chosen and Xi’s term as head of the party will likely be renewed.

incidents.title: Venezuelan opposition leader returns from exile
incidents.description: María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela through Colombia after nearly a year abroad, having previously been barred from returning by Venezuelan authorities and facing opposition from the U.S. government. U.S. officials did not intervene to prevent her return.

incidents.title: Brazilian president wins fourth term
incidents.description: Incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a presidential runoff over Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro by more than 4 million votes, stifling Bolsonaro’s far-right movement. Bolsonaro initially had called for the annulment of the election after a Supreme Court justice ordered polls remain open for two more hours due to issues with public transport.

incidents.title: Houthis claim to have attacked Saudi pumping station
incidents.description: On Oct. 26, Yemen’s Houthis rebels claimed that they had attacked pumping stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline and an airport in Riyadh. Saudi authorities have not confirmed these claims, although Saudi-led military forces have reported intercepting a missile headed toward Riyadh and destroying two missile launchers in Sanaa. Saudi forces also announced additional strikes against Houthi weapons facilities and military sites.

incidents.title: 35,000 refugees displaced in Kenya following regional Ethiopian clashes
incidents.description: At least 35,000 Ethiopians have sought refuge in Kenya from the Moyale fighting that broke out on the 23rd between the security forces of the Oromia and Somali Regional States. The United Nations reported that most of the arrivals are women and children. Camps have been set up on both sides of the border.

incidents.title: Sudanese Founding Alliance appoints new leader
incidents.description: The Sudanese Founding Alliance appointed Idris Madallal as head of the Security and Intelligence Service. Madallal, a former Rapid Support Forces leader, has appointed several security directors in states under RSF control.

incidents.title: U.S. pushes Mexico to allow U.S. personnel to witness counter-cartel operations
incidents.description: The New York Times reported on Oct. 24 that U.S. officials delivered a memo to Mexico proposing that U.S. security personnel to accompany counter-cartel operations inside the country, as well as expanded intelligence sharing. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum remains firmly opposed to the presence of U.S. forces on Mexican territory.

incidents.title: UAE beaches closed due to oil spill
incidents.description: Public beaches and coastal areas in Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain, and portions of Sharjah have been closed due to an oil leak from an offshore tanker. Major response operations are currently underway with crews from the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment working to contain the spill and clean up the oil. The ministry strongly advised people to avoid affected areas and follow official recommendations.

incidents.title: France deploys 70,000 security personnel as nationwide protests continue
incidents.description: On Oct. 24, France deployed over 70,000 police and gendarmes across the country, an increase of 10,000 from the previous week, in an effort to prevent further looting and vandalism as hundreds of thousands protested deteriorating school conditions, rising living costs, and economic inequality. Clashes broke out between police and protesters in several cities while stores, museums, and metro stations shut down in Paris amid heightened security concerns.

incidents.title: Rubio calls on Cubans to work with the CIA to topple government
incidents.description: As U.S. President Donald Trump said Washington would “take care of Cuba” after dealing with Iran at a rally in Florida, Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans to covertly work with the CIA to overthrow the Cuban government. Rubio’s post on X encouraging Cubans “seeking positive change” to engage in “a discrete partnership with the CIA” was then reposted by the CIA.

incidents.title: Iran demands sanctions relief amid U.S. threats
incidents.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said sanctions relief from the U.S. was a precondition to resuming peace talks, as the U.S. and Israel are believed to be preparing for a high-intensity bombing campaign after U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.

incidents.title: Rubio calls on Cubans to work with the CIA to topple government
incidents.description: As U.S. President Donald Trump said Washington would “take care of Cuba” after dealing with Iran at a rally in Florida, Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans to covertly work with the CIA to overthrow the Cuban government. Rubio’s post on X encouraging Cubans “seeking positive change” to engage in “a discrete partnership with the CIA” was then reposted by the CIA.

incidents.title: Typhoon Champi slams into Taiwan
incidents.description: One person was killed and over 500 were injured as Typhoon Champi ripped across Taiwan, bringing down trees and disrupting power as the storm made its way north toward China and Japan. More than 288,000 homes lost electricity. The storm forced airline cancellations across Taiwan and damaged infrastructure as well as forcing widespread closures of offices and schools.

incidents.title: DRC armed forces recruit out of universities
incidents.description: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) have rolled out a large scale, nationwide recruitment campaign at DRC’s universities. Eligible recruits will receive both academic and military training.

incidents.title: Germany secures winter gas supplies
incidents.description: Germany signed a series of agreements worth $275 million to secure natural gas supplies for the winter. This occurs amid fuel reserve shortfalls, with German gas storage facilities only 61.1% full, well below the 75.4% levels last year.

incidents.title: Far-right emails hacked
incidents.description: A group of hackers seized 420,000 emails from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) containing information that threatens to undermine the AfD's growing popularity. The emails revealed illegal donations from outside the EU and internal communications from multiple senior and middle party members who engaged in pro-Nazi and racist rhetoric.

incidents.title: Philippines want undersea cable cooperation with Taiwan
incidents.description: The Philippine Deputy Chief of mission to the U.S., Felipe F. Carino III, gave a speech in Washington D.C. where he expressed openness to collaborating with Taiwan in naval patrols to protect undersea cables from sabotage.

incidents.title: Venezuelan government, opposition reach new transition agreements
incidents.description: Government and opposition negotiators concluded a third round of transition talks with agreements to review the legal procedures behind political disqualifications and create a joint commission seeking the release of Venezuelan gold held at the Bank of England. The latest round followed earlier agreements covering judicial reform and political participation.

incidents.title: Oromia and Somali regional security forces exchange hostilities in Moyale
incidents.description: Security forces from the Oromia and Somali regional states clashed in Moyale near the Kenyan border over a another Somali state's flag flag at an office in an Oromia-administrated area. The fighting has led to at least 35,000 being displaced along the Kenyan and Ethiopian borders.

incidents.title: France enacts curfews amid protests
incidents.description: After curfews on the night of Oct. 19 quelled some of the worst riots France has seen in years, the Paris police said it will extend nightly curfews in the city center for as long as necessary, while authorities in Lyon and Marseille have announced curfew extensions on a day-by-day basis. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said France will deploy military troops to aid police forces across the country on Oct. 24, ahead of another round of anticipated mass protests.

incidents.title: NATO to increase Black Sea presence
incidents.description: NATO announced that it will increase its military presence in the Black Sea, including manned and unmanned patrol craft and intelligence personnel, in response to ongoing regional escalation between Russia and Ukraine.

incidents.title: Ukraine, Russia and U.S. agree to resume trilateral talks
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed support for resuming tri-lateral peace talks with the United States, following talks with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff with Zelenskyy in Oslo on Oct. 21 and with Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 22. Zelenskyy said Ukraine is willing to freeze the conflict along its current battle lines, while Putin said Russia will be prepared to resume talks as early as November.

incidents.title: U.S., Israel reportedly prepare for renewal of Iran bombing campaign
incidents.description: The United States and Israel are reportedly preparing for a renewed bombing campaign in Iran that would target Iranian energy and nuclear infrastructure, following the U.S. mid-term elections on Nov. 3.

incidents.title: U.S., Japan hold island defense military drill
incidents.description: The U.S. and Japan conducted a large joint military exercise, the biennial Keen Sword 27, which focused on defending Japan’s southern islands. Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense praised the exercises, which for the first time involved participant third countries and had elements focusing on a possible defense of Taiwan.

incidents.title: Taiwan reports spike in cyberattacks
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Government Service Network stated that it had received over 185 million cyberattacks in July, marking a higher number than the baseline. This comes as Taiwanese authorities have been warning of potential increases in cyberattacks ahead of the upcoming Taiwanese midterm election on Nov. 28.

incidents.title: APEC Finance ministers agree to high-level cooperation
incidents.description: Finance ministers from participating countries of the upcoming Asia Pacific Economic met this week, where according to Chinese Finance Minister Lan Foan, they agreed to strengthen high-level communication and to coordinate on “external risks and challenges.”

incidents.title: Mexico charges former government official with treason over U.S. drug operation
incidents.description: Mexican federal prosecutors charged former Chihuahua Attorney General César Jáuregui with treason on Oct. 21, accusing him of letting U.S. personnel take part in an April drug lab raid without federal approval. The raid became public after two U.S. agents died in a car crash returning from the operation, and a federal judge ordered Jáuregui to stay in pretrial detention while the court decides whether the case moves forward.

incidents.title: El Salvador launches operation to rescue personnel held by Haitian gangs
incidents.description: Four Salvadoran members of the U.N.-backed international security force in Haiti were being held hostage by gangs, prompting President Nayib Bukele to announce a military operation to recover them.

incidents.title: Democratic Party leaders sue Trump administration over election authority
incidents.description: Democratic Party leaders from both the House and Senate have filed a lawsuit in federal court to obtain a court order that would prevent the Trump administration from establishing federal control over state election processes. The lawsuit alleges that these actions could undermine states’ authority over election administration and lead to eligible voters being improperly removed from voter rolls or denied ballots.

incidents.title: Trump administration asks federal judge to reconsider permit for wind farm project
incidents.description: The White House has directed the Justice Department to ask a federal judge to reconsider the permit allowing for the construction of the New England Wind project, a Biden-era wind farm project to be built off the coast of Massachusetts. The Justice Department filed the request as part of the administration’s efforts to restrict the development of green energy infrastructure.

incidents.title: Cuba accuses U.S. of threatening countries to vote against lifting embargo
incidents.description: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez alleged the U.S. threatened countries with tariffs, visa restrictions, and other retaliatory measures to compel them to vote “no” on lifting the U.S. embargo against Cuba ahead of an annual U.N. General Assembly vote. Rodriguez accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz of leading a months-long pressure campaign.

incidents.title: U.K. clears new gas field construction
incidents.description: The U.K. has cleared the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea for gas production, prioritizing domestic supply as international energy prices remain high. The project could raise British gas output by 6% at peak production and is expected to begin operating before November, modestly reducing import dependence ahead of the winter. However, its contribution to lowering energy costs will likely be limited.

incidents.title: Russia prepares to export diesel to U.S.
incidents.description: Russia is preparing to export an initial 40,000 metric tons of diesel to the United States on Oct. 22 under Washington’s temporary sanctions waiver. Moscow expects shipments to increase substantially in November, targeting 500,000 tons that month and another 1 million tons subsequently.

incidents.title: U.N. climate report details rising temperatures
incidents.description: According to the United Nations report ahead of next month’s Conference of the Parties (COP31) Summit in Türkiye, the world will unavoidably exceed the Paris Climate Agreement’s 1.5-degree Celsius warming limit in the next few years. Immediate and sustained emissions cuts by one-fifth are needed to minimize overshoot beyond that level. This puts pressure on COP31 negotiations to accelerate mitigation and climate funding in the face of the U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Agreement.

incidents.title: France’s borrowing costs reach 24-year hig
incidents.description: France’s 10-year benchmark government bond yield surpassed 5% for the first time in 24 years, indicating heightened investor concerns over France’s budget deficit, rising public debt, and mass protests ahead of the 2027 presidential election. This bond yield increase could also raise borrowing costs for homeowners and businesses, further pressuring France’s economy.

incidents.title: French cities renew curfews amid protests
incidents.description: After curfews on the night of Oct. 19 quelled some of the worst riots France has seen in years, the Paris police said it will extend nightly curfews in the city center as long as necessary, while authorities in Lyon and Marseille have announced curfew extensions on a day-by-day basis. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said France will deploy military troops to aid police forces across the country on Oct. 24, ahead of another round of anticipated protests.

incidents.title: U.S./Ukraine tensions rise over air defense delays
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the U.S. of delaying air defense systems to Ukraine amid an increase in Russian strikes. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged that delays had taken place but denied that they were deliberate.

incidents.title: Houthis strike Yemeni government facility
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group killed over 70 people and wounded hundreds in an Oct. 19 ballistic missile strike against a military training facility operated by the internationally recognized Yemeni government.

incidents.title: Turkish parliament moves to ratify defense agreement with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: The Turkish parliament began the ratification process of the Mecca mutual defense agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

incidents.title: Chinese vessels patrol Pratas islands
incidents.description: Taiwan reported two separate incidents of Chinese vessels approaching the Pratas islands in the South China Sea near Taiwan. A Chinese spokesperson stated the vessels were “safeguarding order” around the islands, which lie between Hong Kong and Taiwan and which many analysts state could be vulnerable to potential future Chinese aggression.

incidents.title: Taiwan added as country-of-origin in Japan
incidents.description: Japan-Taiwan Friendship Parliamentarians’ League in Tokyo announced that Japan now had the ability to list “Taiwan” as a place of origin rather than “China” following a recent easing in licensing rules.

incidents.title: Mexico and U.S. close to reaching trade deal
incidents.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Oct. 20 that the U.S. and Mexico are “very close” to reaching a trade agreement, corroborating statements made by U.S. President Donald Trump at a rally on Oct. 19. This comes as both governments look to reach a deal before the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, with Mexico pushing for lower U.S. tariffs on steel, aluminum, and cars.

incidents.title: Indonesian wildfire damage exceeded 7,000 square miles in September
incidents.description: Satellite data from deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas showed that fires had burned approximately 7,400 square miles across Indonesia by the end of September, more than double the cumulative area recorded through August. The fires have also disrupted more than 2,600 domestic flights since Aug. 11, while hazardous smoke continues to affect communities in Indonesia and neighboring countries.

incidents.title: Indonesia restricts stock declines
incidents.description: Indonesian stocks rebounded after the Indonesia Stock Exchange reduced the maximum daily share price decline from 15% to 7% following a two-day selloff that erased approximately $82 billion in market value. The benchmark index had fallen 14.8% over Oct. 16 and 19 after index provider Morgan Stanley Capital International proposed removing Indonesia from its emerging market indexes over concerns about ownership transparency and trading practices.

incidents.title: Indonesia faces antigovernment protests
incidents.description: Indonesian authorities deployed approximately 9,500 police officers across Jakarta as students and environmental activists protested President Prabowo Subianto's administration on the second anniversary of his inauguration. Protesters criticized the government's response to widespread wildfires, economic conditions, and corruption, amid declining public support for Prabowo, whose approval rating fell to 44.5% in a recent survey.

incidents.title: Chinese rare earth exports to EU rebound
incidents.description: Chinese shipments of rare earths to the EU rose by 20.5% in September, the highest rebound since February. These figures reflect the period leading up to the trade agreement on Chinese electric vehicle imports to the bloc.

incidents.title: White House announces $8 billion relief package for farmers
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has announced a new "Harvest Fuel Relief" program aimed at providing financial assistance to farmers during the upcoming harvest season. The program is intended to offset losses incurred due to rising diesel prices, which disproportionately affect the diesel-dependent agriculture industry.

incidents.title: DRC National Assembly bankrolls development programs
incidents.description: DRC's National Assembly approved $625 million in additional funding to four ongoing programs created in partnership with the International Development Association, a concessional branch of the World Bank Group. The programs include microfinancing packages promoting women’s entrepreneurship and children’s nutrition initiatives, and full implementation of the funds is pending approval from a body composed of both houses of the country’s parliament. Status Quo

incidents.title: Fighting continues in Ethiopia’s Tigray region
incidents.description: The TPLF rebel group claimed it killed 1,511 federal soldiers around Mirena as government troops pushed toward Adet. On Oct. 20, a drone strike near Finarwa, about 50 miles southwest of Mekelle, killed four civilians, including two children. The drone operator was not identified.

incidents.title: India, U.S. advance trade talks
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar in Mumbai as the countries’ negotiations over a bilateral trade agreement moved closer to execution. Rubio said nearly all the negotiating work had been completed, with discussions also covering energy purchases, technology, defense and investment.

incidents.title: India faces U.N. scrutiny over protest crackdown
incidents.description: U.N.-appointed human rights experts criticized India’s response to recent youth-led demonstrations, referencing accounts of mass detentions, mistreatment in custody, restrictions on public gatherings and internet shutdowns. The experts urged Indian authorities to investigate alleged abuses by security forces and review the measures they use to keep protesters under control.

incidents.title: U.S.-based terrorism suspects confess in Cuba
incidents.description: The Cuban government said survivors of a group of men from the U.S. that had attempted a sea incursion into Cuban territory and opened fire on a Cuban coast guard vessel in February confessed to their actions and now face terrorism charges. Cuban officials accused the U.S. of allowing terrorists to operate on American soil.

incidents.title: Meta claims equal treatment for all Brazilian election candidates
incidents.description: Meta responded to a Brazilian Supreme Court request filed Oct 19 that gave it 24 hours to provide evidence it has not systematically disadvantaged any candidates’ campaigns on its platform, insisting it has not favored any candidate. The order came after a lawsuit filed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva alleging his advertisements were taken down and that Meta’s AI chatbot favored his opponent, right-wing Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro.

incidents.title: Canada restricts diplomats’ contact with U.S. midterm candidates
incidents.description: Canadian diplomats have been instructed not to meet with or attend events involving U.S. candidates before the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections and to maintain a low profile to avoid perceptions of election interference. Shortly after the Canadian government distributed the written guidance, the U.S. embassy in Ottawa published a “fact sheet” alleging that Canada targeted Republican-held states with pressure tactics, including counter-tariffs affecting exporters in those states.

incidents.title: Germany secures $252 billion in Berlin investment conference
incidents.description: At a Berlin summit of multinational corporations, including Amazon and Nvidia, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pitched Germany as an attractive place to invest, highlighting state investments in defense, semiconductors, and AI. According to the economy ministry, attendees committed to investing $252 billion in the German economy.

incidents.title: Sudanese Army suspected of drone strike in Abyei region
incidents.description: A drone attack, allegedly from Sudan’s army, struck the Amiet market in Abyei, causing 153 casualties and significant property damage. These attacks targeted fuel depots and trucks coming from South Sudan, bound for the Rapid Support Forces. South Sudan’s Foreign Ministry has emphasized peace and stability in the region, urging the Sudanese Army to prevent further incidents.

incidents.title: Russian Foreign Minister meets Iranian counterpart
incidents.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aqaqchi in Tehran on Oct. 19 to discuss the status of ongoing negotiations with the United States.

incidents.title: Putin proposes trilateral meeting with Trump, Xi
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin suggested to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

incidents.title: India avoids Russia oil tariffs
incidents.description: India escaped a U.S. tariff threat after President Donald Trump used the Graham Act’s waiver authority to suspend the application of sanctions tied to purchases of Russian oil. Secretary of State Marco Rubio later said Washington kept in mind the nearing India-U.S. trade agreement when deciding to grant the waiver.

incidents.title: Cuban delegation publicly confronts U.S. ambassador to U.N.
incidents.description: Cuba’s ambassador to the U.N. Ernesto Soberón Guzmán and other representatives of the Cuban delegation yelled at U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz as he left an event at the U.N. headquarters spotlighting Cuba’s political prisoners and government corruption. Panelists implored diplomats in attendance to vote “no” or abstain ahead of the Oct. 27-28 U.N. General Assembly’s annual non-binding resolution to condemn and lift the U.S. embargo on Cuba.

incidents.title: Brazilian presidential candidates debate before runoff vote
incidents.description: Incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and rival Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro spoke directly to voters during a debate on Oct. 18. Bolsonaro focused on rising food prices and government spending, while Lula emphasized his government’s record in securing two investment-grade ratings as proof that such spending hasn’t made Brazil less investable.

incidents.title: Albertans vote to remain in Canada
incidents.description: A proposal in Alberta to hold a binding referendum on the province’s secession from Canada was soundly defeated, 76% to 24%, in an Oct. 19 vote. Over 1.35 million people voted, and Prime Minister Mark Carney said Albertans “made a clear choice.”

incidents.title: U.S.-based terrorism suspects confess in Cuba
incidents.description: The Cuban government said survivors of a group of men from the U.S. that had attempted a sea incursion into Cuban territory and opened fire on a Cuban coast guard vessel in February confessed to their actions and now face terrorism charges. Cuban officials accused the U.S. of allowing terrorists to operate on American soil.

incidents.title: Cuban delegation publicly confronts U.S. ambassador to U.N.
incidents.description: Cuba’s ambassador to the U.N. Ernesto Soberón Guzmán and other representatives of the Cuban delegation yelled at U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz as he left an event at the U.N. headquarters spotlighting Cuba’s political prisoners and government corruption. Panelists implored diplomats in attendance to vote “no” or abstain ahead of the Oct. 27-28 U.N. General Assembly’s annual non-binding resolution to condemn and lift the U.S. embargo on Cuba.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Russian petroleum facilities
incidents.description: An Oct. 18 Ukrainian offensive involving more than 1,000 drones sparked fires at petroleum facilities in St. Petersburg and caused power outages affecting 20,000 residents. Russia extended its campaign against Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure, with attacks in Odesa leaving 32,700 households without power.

incidents.title: Germany summons Iranian ambassador over disrupted antisemitic attack
incidents.description: Germany's Foreign Office summoned Iranian Ambassador Majid Nili Ahmadabadi to protest Tehran’s alleged involvement in a foiled plot to assassinate Volker Beck, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany. According to German authorities, two men, a Danish national and an Afghan national, were arrested in July 2025 on suspicion of plotting to kill Beck at the direction of Iranian intelligence. On Oct. 15, 2026, both were convicted and sentenced to 8.5 years and 4.5 years in prison, respectively.

incidents.title: European diplomats assaulted by Israeli settlers in the West Bank
incidents.description: A group of European diplomats was physically assaulted by masked Israeli settlers in the West Bank on Oct. 18.

incidents.title: Drug seizures in Asia spike as result of Myanmar instability
incidents.description: Methamphetamine seizures have increased across Asia due to an increased supply of cheap product from conflict-ravaged Myanmar. Thailand is the biggest market for the drugs, and tablet prices have dropped over the past decade due to increased patterns of instability in Myanmar, where ethnic armed groups control much of the countryside in the ongoing civil war. Sales of the drugs have allowed various belligerents in the conflict to acquire cash for the purchase of weapons and supplies.

incidents.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump weighed in on Israel’s upcoming elections by endorsing sitting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, calling him “a great warrior prime minister.”

incidents.title: Iran awaits U.S. response to conditional offer to re-open the Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Oct. 18 that Iran was willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days of the U.S. agreeing to a seven-point conditional offer but that Iran had not received a response from U.S. officials.

incidents.title: Beijing predicted to be “super aged” by 2035
incidents.description: Projections from the Beijing Daily predict that Beijing’s population will become “super aged” by 2035, with at least a third of the population being 60 years old or older. This comes as the government has increasingly focused on natalist policies, spending over $26 billion last year in an attempt to boost births.

incidents.title: Venezuelan opposition parties rally behind Machado
incidents.description: Members of the Unitary Democratic Platform (PUD) met in Caracas and maintained María Corina Machado as the coalition’s leader while continuing to push for a new presidential vote.

incidents.title: Trump waives sanctions on Russia
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump waived sanctions against Russia days before they were scheduled to go into effect amid warming ties between the U.S. and Russia and increasing tensions between the U.S. and Ukraine, including reporting that Elon Musk directly ordered Starlink restrictions in Ukraine.

incidents.title: Houthi rebels besiege city of Taiz
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group continued its campaign to capture the southwest Yemeni city of Taiz from forces of Yemen's internationally recognized government, who are undergoing a counteroffensive backed by Saudi Arabia.

incidents.title: Tunisians protest against president
incidents.description: Thousands of Tunisians took to the streets of Tunis to protest President Kais Saied over concerns related to government overreach and economic conditions in the country.

incidents.title: Rubio warns of increasing escalation in Ethiopia, Eritrea
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said “separatists” attacking inside Ethiopia had drawn an Ethiopian response and that the buildup of troops on both sides of the border could lead to a larger regional war. Rubio said he had spoken to representatives of both countries.

incidents.title: China anti-corruption body warns party officials
incidents.description: Former Chongqing Mayor Huang Qifan and Bao Hui, former head of the standing committee of the Chengdu people’s congress in Sichuan province, are being investigated in a latest round of anti-corruption measures by the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Commission of Supervision. The Commission warned other party members that rank and contributions to the government would not shield anyone they investigate for corruption.

incidents.title: French protests turn to riots
incidents.description: On Oct. 17, French protests that began as a student-led movement advocating for better school conditions turned into riots, sparking some of the worst protest violence the country has seen in decades. While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent groups attacked police officers, torched public buildings, and looted stores.

incidents.title: Berlin coalition preliminary negotiations conclude
incidents.description: Following Berlin’s September elections, negotiations are underway between the Left Party, Social Democrats, and Green Party to form a left-wing coalition government. Exploratory talks have concluded with an outline for the composition and objectives of the next government. A major achievement of the Left Party, the largest party in the putative coalition, is an agreement to socialize 160,000 housing units in Berlin owned by large landlords.

incidents.title: Indonesian stocks suffer largest plunge since 1998 financial crisis
incidents.description: Indonesia’s benchmark stock index fell more than 11%, triggering a temporary trading halt, after MSCI warned it could remove the country from global benchmark indexes. Indonesian stocks have lost nearly 40% of their value in 2026.

incidents.title: France braces for nationwide protests amid student unrest
incidents.description: Hundreds of demonstrations were planned across France for the weekend following weeks of high school protests over educational conditions, with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu warning authorities feared unrest.

incidents.title: Reports emerge that Iranian tanker delivered jet fuel past U.S. blockade to Myanmar junta in September
incidents.description: A tanker loaded with Iranian jet fuel evaded the ongoing U.S. blockade and reached Myanmar in September, evading U.S. sanctions by delivering the fuel to the Myanmar junta. Myanmar’s jet fuel industry was sanctioned by the U.S. in 2023 after multiple reports of airstrikes against civilians, though the junta government denies intentional targeting of noncombatants.

incidents.title: DRC bans travel for senior military officials
incidents.description: DRC Deputy Prime Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Muadiamvita announced that all generals and senior officials of FARDC are no longer authorized to leave the country under any circumstances. The measure was announced just three days after former President Joseph Kabila’s ascension to the Front of the Refounding of the Nation’s leadership, the restructured AFC/M23 coalition. The measure, from the office of President Félix Tshisekedi, also bars all future pre-authorized travel for senior officials regardless of purpose in coordination with the Deputies of Migration and National Intelligence.

incidents.title: DRC bans political opposition
incidents.description: DRC's central government has formally banned the activities of 13 political opposition formations in a statement signed by Deputy Prime Minister Jacquemain Shabani. Among the targeted formations is the political party of former President Joseph Kabila, the People’s Party for Reconstruction and Democracy, amid political debates concerning Kabila’s new leadership of a restructured AFC/M23.

incidents.title: Ethiopian government names caretaker government in Tigray
incidents.description: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed named a six-month federal caretaker government for Tigray to stabilize the region and prepare an election. The same day, the TPLF rebel group said the body had “neither legality nor enforceability” and warned against any movement at Mekelle airport, which lies within the caretaker territory.

incidents.title: Starlink restriction disrupts Ukrainian combat operations
incidents.description: An unannounced one day restriction to the speed of Starlink satellite communications disrupted Ukrainian combat operations before being returned to normal operating speed according to Ukrainian defense officials.

incidents.title: U.S. strikes deal on Russian diesel
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a deal that would lift U.S. sanctions to allow Russia to sell 300,000 metric tons of diesel amid an increase in diplomatic tensions between Washington and Ukraine.

incidents.title: Russia, Ukraine bombard energy infrastructure
incidents.description: Russia and Ukraine exchanged a series of strikes against each other's energy infrastructure, despite an impromptu announcement of a ceasefire on all energy facilities made by U.S. President Donald Trump. Trump said it's time for Ukraine to “get a new president,” amid a series of public outbursts against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

incidents.title: Two vessels sink in Strait of Hormuz in unattributed attacks
incidents.description: Two commercial vessels sank in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct. 14 after being hit by unknown munitions in separate, unattributed incidents. The sinkings come amid reports that Iran is seeking to escalate disruptions of international shipping in the strait in order to impose increased economic and political costs on the U.S. in the lead-up to midterm elections on Nov. 3.

incidents.title: North Korea test-fires submarine-launched cruise missiles
incidents.description: North Korea’s state media reported a test-firing of two submarine-launched cruise missiles this week for the first time since 2024. It follows a separate incident earlier this week when South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff reported that North Korea fired an unspecified number of ballistic missiles into the sea east of the peninsula, with one reportedly flying over 900 kilometers.

incidents.title: Trump reverses plan to broadcast U.S. military execution
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has called off a planned livestream of the execution of former U.S. Army Maj. Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 U.S. soldiers in an attack at Fort Hood in 2009. The reversal came following strong public backlash and concerns from the U.N. Human Rights Office that livestreaming an execution may constitute torture.

incidents.title: Iranian cleric slain
incidents.description: An Iranian cleric was killed in his home in the city of Sari, the Tasnim news service reported. No motive or suspects have been identified.

incidents.title: Egyptian authorities suspend cargo trucks travelling to Sudan
incidents.description: Trucks at Egypt’s Qustul border crossing to Sudan have stopped because of security destabilization in Sudan’s Northern State, threatening a crucial route for bilateral trade. Egypt’s General Authority for Land and Dry Ports also ordered officials to limit the crossing of passenger vehicles.

incidents.title: Ukrainian army advances in Donetsk
incidents.description: The Ukrainian armed forces have re-captured 101 square kilometers of territory from the Russian army in Donetsk oblast while inflicting thousands of casualties during ongoing operations as part of Operation Vivaldi, according to Ukrainian defense officials who did not specify when the operation began.

incidents.title: Houthis damage Saudi Aramco HQ
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group targeted multiple Saudi energy facilities, including an attack that damaged Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in the city of Dhahran on Oct. 13. Houthi officials pledged to continue the attacks amid vows of retaliation from Saudi Arabia.

incidents.title: China sentences dozens in Myanmar scam center crackdown
incidents.description: Courts in China’s Fujian province sentenced three Myanmar-based gang members to death, three to life imprisonment, and 55 to shorter prison terms on telecom fraud and gambling charges. The individuals sentenced were part of the Wei family criminal network and ran scam compounds in Myanmar’s Kokang region. According to Chinese state media, the sentences are part of Beijing’s accelerating crackdown on cross-border Burmese scam networks.

incidents.title: Basij officers killed in Iran attacks
incidents.description: At least two officers of Iran’s Basij paramilitary security force, including a female commander, were killed in what Iranian authorities characterized as targeted attacks in Iran on Oct. 14.

incidents.title: Netanyahu says Israel plans no pre-election attack on Iran
incidents.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he does not intend to preemptively bomb Iran prior to Israel’s elections on Oct. 27, saying that such an attack would not be "convenient."

incidents.title: China purchases U.S. soybeans
incidents.description: Chinese traders purchased at least eight Panamax cargoes of U.S. soybeans, close to 650,000 metric tons, marking the first such purchase since the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in September. The shipments are scheduled for delivery beginning in December.

incidents.title: Trump claims Taiwan ready to purchase Alaskan gas
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that Taiwan was ready to buy up to $80 billion worth of liquefied natural gas from a proposed Alaskan pipeline. Taiwan, meanwhile, confirmed a $4 billion investment in the project while stating it would still be conducting budget approvals in subsequent negotiations.

incidents.title: U.S. expands military deployments across Latin America
incidents.description: The U.S. began deploying a 600-soldier Army battalion to Panama for training exercises, with troops also expected to train with forces in Colombia and Honduras, as the Pentagon expanded regional counternarcotics operations.

incidents.title: U.S. Social Security payouts to rise 3.6% in 2027
incidents.description: Social Security recipients are expected to receive a 3.6% cost of living adjustment beginning in 2027. For average recipients, the adjustment would amount to about $75 more monthly.

incidents.title: U.S. lifts sanctions on Venezuelan National Assembly president
incidents.description: The Trump administration removed sanctions on National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez, the brother of acting President Delcy Rodríguez and a longtime senior government official.

incidents.title: India, Canada deepen ties
incidents.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney agree to advance bilateral cooperation in trade, energy, technology and security in a phone call. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand subsequently met with Modi and Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar in New Delhi while both governments reaffirmed efforts to conclude a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. Ottawa also announced that Modi will visit Canada in December.

incidents.title: Brazil shortens work week to 40 hours
incidents.description: Brazil’s Senate passed a constitutional amendment shortening the work week from 44 to 40 hours for many workers. Incumbent President Lula da Silva championed the amendment, while Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who is facing Lula in a presidential runoff election, announced his support for the amendment on Oct. 13 in a reversal of his position.

incidents.title: German trial of alleged Nord Stream saboteur begins
incidents.description: The trial of Serhii Kuznetsov, a Ukrainian man accused of leading a saboteur group that destroyed the Nord Stream pipeline, began in Hamburg. The attack, one of the largest acts of economic sabotage in recent history, destroyed a major pipeline supplying Russian natural gas to Germany and continues to serve as a source of tension between Germany and ally Ukraine.

incidents.title: Houthis surround city of Taiz
incidents.description: Houthi forces have encircled the city of Taiz in Yemen, near the Red Sea port city of Mokha, despite an ongoing high-intensity counteroffensive by Yemeni government forces supported by the Saudi air force.

incidents.title: China, North Korea open new connecting bridge
incidents.description: China and North Korea formally opened a new bridge over the Yalu River in a renewed push to boost bilateral trade. The opening comes as North Korea has taken steps recently to increase ties with both China and Russia, though Pyongyang had repeatedly pushed back construction of the bridge.

incidents.title: Mexican authorities release alleged cartel leader after police kidnapping
incidents.description: Morelos state police freed José David Vergara, the alleged leader of the Pueblos Unidos criminal group, whom they had arrested on drug possession charges in Totolapan, in exchange for the release of three police officers who had been kidnapped by the group. Mexico’s Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said the exchange was made to avoid larger confrontations.

incidents.title: U.S. recalls acting envoy after Nicaragua rejects ambassador nominee
incidents.description: Acting U.S. envoy Elias Baumann returned to Washington for consultations after Nicaragua rejected U.S. ambassador nominee Natasha Franceschi. President Daniel Ortega has accused the U.S. of attempting to interfere in Nicaragua’s domestic affairs.

incidents.title: U.S. immigration agents raid congresswoman’s home
incidents.description: Homeland Security Investigations agents conducted a raid on the Washington, D.C., home of U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, a Democrat. Omar, a naturalized U.S. citizen, has claimed the raid is an attempt at political intimidation by the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump ahead of midterm elections. A Department of Homeland Security spokesman did not provide details as to the objective of the raid, although the White House has called her citizenship called into question.

incidents.title: Venezuelan workers protest over labor grievances
incidents.description: An estimated 2,000 healthcare, education, and university workers marched in Caracas to demand government action on labor issues, with union representatives delivering a petition signed by more than 45,000 healthcare professionals to government officials. The petition demanded that bonuses be converted to wages and that upcoming holiday bonuses be calculated using income, not salary.

incidents.title: BIMSTEC adopts Delhi Declaration
incidents.description: The seven Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation(BIMSTEC) members adopted the Delhi Declaration at the grouping’s first Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi on Oct. 13. Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand committed to more cooperation against drug and human trafficking, cybercrime, money laundering, terrorism, and illicit arms smuggling.

incidents.title: Former DRC president heads restructured military coalition
incidents.description: Former DRC President Joseph Kabila launched the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a new political-military coalition that has formally replaced the Congo River Alliance (AFC) and incorporates the M23, who control large areas of the eastern DRC. Kabila, who was sentenced to death in absentia by the internationally recognized DRC government in 2025, assumed the new coalition’s presidency while M23 military commander Sultani Makenga retained command of the coalition’s armed forces. The FRN announced that it was prepared “to put an end to tyranny by any means necessary, including the use of force,” while stating that organizational restructuring would not change participation in the ongoing Doha peace process with Kinshasa.

incidents.title: Brazilian farmers threaten to invade Indigenous territory if Flávio Bolsonaro wins presidential election
incidents.description: A group of Parakanã Indigenous individuals received WhatsApp messages from farmers threatening to invade their territory in the event of a victory by Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who is favored to win Brazil’s presidential runoff. The territory experienced significant deforestation during the term of former President Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio’s father.

incidents.title: Brazilian environment minister claims Amazon fires set intentionally
incidents.description: Environment and Climate Change Minister João Paulo Capobianco said fires burning in the Amazon jungle had been set deliberately. Since the beginning of October, 1,600 active fire events have been recorded in Amazonas state, a dramatic increase from last year. The federal and state governments are using aircraft, firefighting operations, burn bans, and a state of emergency to address the fires.

incidents.title: German chancellor doubles down on reform agenda
incidents.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that he would push forward with pension reforms, even if they harm his popularity. Merz argues they are necessary to improve Germany’s fiscal health and to “once again offer the younger generation decent prospects.”

incidents.title: Berlin coalition talks hit roadblock over Israel
incidents.description: Following September’s Berlin Senate elections that resulted in a left-wing majority, negotiations have been underway to determine the objectives and terms of a coalition government led by the Left Party and involving the Social Democrats and Greens. On Oct. 13, the talks broke down over the Left’s position regarding Israel, with the Social Democrats and Greens demanding the Left agree to a declaration that recognizes Israel’s “non-negotiable right to exist.” This demand is controversial among the Left’s supporters who condition recognition on a commitment by Israel to equal rights for Palestinians living under its control. If the parties cannot reach an agreement, they face a coalition government led by the Christian Democratic Union or another election.

incidents.title: Ethiopian troops reach town on the border with Eritrea, fear of regional war escalates
incidents.description: Ethiopian troops were seen in the town of Zalambessa on the Ethiopian-Eritrean border near Ethiopia's northernmost point. This is latest in the in the government’s counter offensive that began in recent weeks following attacks by Tigrayan Rebels supported by Eritrean forces and has driven rebels and Eritrean forces back across the border.

incidents.title: Egypt acknowledges operation targeting illegal gold mine in disputed Sudanese region
incidents.description: The Egyptian military said it conducted the third phase of a “large-scale operation” against an illegal gold mining area in the Halaib Triangle, which Sudan and Egypt both claim. Emergency Lawyers, a Sudanese rights group, said an air strike there attributed to Egypt killed at least 72 people and that another 223 had been detained.

incidents.title: El Niño-linked drought raises famine risk in Sudan
incidents.description: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IFSPC) reports food insecurity and acute malnutrition exacerbated by El Niño-caused drought, specifically in the Darfur and Kordofan regions. The drought is also contributing to poor vegetation growth and water shortages. Two displacement camps have reported acute malnutrition above famine thresholds.

incidents.title: Houthis kill 13 in Riyadh airport strike
incidents.description: An Oct. 10 Houthi missile strike on the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 13 people and wounded over 300, as Houthi officials vowed more attacks against the Saudi capital.

incidents.title: Indian sailors missing after Hormuz attacks
incidents.description: Two merchant vessels with Indian nationals on board were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct. 11. A drone strike on the MT Petro Dolphin left two of its 11 Indian crew members missing, while all aboard the MT Valthera were reported safe after the tanker was hit by a projectile and caught fire. India condemned the attacks and called for the protection of commercial shipping and freedom of navigation.

incidents.title: DRC considers prisoner reintegration in new bill
incidents.description: A new bill introduced by MP Elvis Atsongya Kiyaya in the National Assembly proposes reintegration of prisoners into the workforce and addresses the societal stigma of imprisonment. To this end, the bill proposes agriculture, livestock raising, and vocational work programs, accompanied by savings accounts that would be accessible to former inmates. These programs would not only supplement prisoner care costs for the state but allow former inmates to re-enter society with certifiable work experience, with no mention of previous incarceration.

incidents.title: Indonesia strengthens domestic gas ownership
incidents.description: Italian energy company Eni agreed to sell 10% interests in seven Indonesian oil and natural gas blocks to state-owned Pertamina and private energy company Medco Energi, including producing fields and major gas discoveries in East Kalimantan. The agreements increase Indonesian companies’ ownership of domestic natural gas resources and their potential share of future production revenues, subject to regulatory approval.

incidents.title: Indonesia wildfires destroy hundreds of homes
incidents.description: Wildfires in the Bangka Belitung province in Indonesia destroyed 305 homes, affecting approximately 1,800 people, including 500 who were forced to evacuate after the fire broke out on Oct. 10. The blaze is part of Indonesia’s most severe wildfire season in 11 years, with fires across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo causing hazardous levels of smoke in Malaysia and Singapore.

incidents.title: Cuba denies involvement with fuel shipments seized by U.S. authorities
incidents.description: In an interview with Reuters, Cuban Minister of Energy and Mines Vicente de la O Levy rejected U.S. claims that Havana had ties to fuel shipments destined for the island after the U.S. Department of Homeland Security seized nearly $3 million of biodiesel. De la O Levy reiterated Cuba’s plan to transition to renewable energy despite being slowed by heightened U.S. sanctions on oil.

incidents.title: Carney calls for Canadian unity ahead of Alberta secession vote
incidents.description: Ahead of Alberta’s Oct. 19 secession vote, Prime Minister Mark Carney, an Alberta native, used his Thanksgiving message, filmed at his former high school in Edmonton, to call for national unity, warning that Canada faces threats to its economy, security, and way of life. This comes amid a growing separatist movement, fueled in part by upset over federal energy and environmental policies, and follows a Globe and Mail investigation alleging that separatist organizers discussed offering access to Alberta’s water and oil royalties in exchange for U.S. support for independence during a meeting with U.S. Republican operatives.

incidents.title: Wildfire destroys 300 homes in Bangka Belitung province in Indonesia
incidents.description: A wildfire in the Bangka Belitung province in Indonesia has destroyed more than 300 homes, affecting approximately 1,800 people, and forced 500 residents to evacuate. The destruction occurred during Indonesia’s most severe wildfire season in 11 years, with fires across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo causing hazardous haze in Malaysia and Singapore.

incidents.title: German labor minister resigns, citing personal reasons and political attacks
incidents.description: Bärbel Bas resigned from her post as labor minister and leader of the Social Democratic Party (SPD), referencing her stepdaughter’s death and the attacks from Christian Democratic Union (CDU) politicians. Her resignation opens a leadership vacuum in the SPD, the junior member of the ruling coalition.

incidents.title: Cyberattack hits French supermarkets
incidents.description: Hackers breached systems governing refrigeration systems in over 500 supermarkets across France, raising the temperature of freezers and refrigerators to up to 122 degrees Fahrenheit and causing millions of euros worth of spoiled food. The targeted refrigeration systems were manufactured by the Danish company Danfoss, but authorities have not yet identified the attackers.

incidents.title: Trump announces energy ceasefire without Russia, Ukraine acknowledgement
incidents.description: On Oct. 11, U.S. President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire on energy infrastructure in Russia and Ukraine, although no ceasefire had been agreed to.

incidents.title: China sanctions Belizean, Paraguayan officials over Taiwan ties
incidents.description: China imposed sanctions on Belizean Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca and Paraguay’s communications minister over their countries’ diplomatic relations with Taiwan. Belize rejected the sanctions as unwarranted while Taiwan condemned them.

incidents.title: Cubans reliant on mutual aid for medicine amid U.S. sanctions
incidents.description: Cuban citizens launched community aid programs through WhatsApp and Telegram to combat medicine supply shortages until Cuba’s economic reforms allow private pharmacies to open. Cuban authorities attributed medicine supply shortages of up to 90% to foreign shipping companies fearing U.S. sanctions, while Cubans are wary of the affordability of privatized medication.

incidents.title: U.S. removes sanctions from daughter of junta-linked Myanmar businessman
incidents.description: The U.S. Treasury Department removed sanctions on Theint Win Htet, the daughter of a junta-aligned Myanmar businessman, after she sued the department in July.
