Her father, Thein Win Zaw, owns the Shwe Byain Phyu Group, which was sanctioned in January 2024 under President Joe Biden for supplying fuel to the military junta. The decision closely follows reporting on possible talks between the junta government and the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump.

incidents.title: Glucksmann wins France’s center-left primary
incidents.description: French Member of the European Parliament Raphael Glucksmann won the primary election for France’s social-democratic Place Publique party with 66% of the vote. Glucksmann has distinguished himself politically from far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon and centrist French President Emmanuel Macron.

incidents.title: Taiwanese president gives Nation Day address
incidents.description: In a speech on Taiwan’s National Day, President Lai Ching-te reiterated that that Taiwan’s right to exist must be respected and said the island’s defensive buildup should not be seen as a provocation. China called the speech a distortion of the truth.

incidents.title: China, EU, finalize hybrid car trade deal
incidents.description: China and the EU reached a deal following EU Trade Commissioner, Maroš Šefčovič’s trip to Beijing last week to moderate Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the EU, cutting them by half over the next four years, though no implementation plan was communicated. China also stated it would reduce tariffs on European imports while the EU is set to impose further trade restrictions on other imported goods.

incidents.title: Trump pressures Sheinbaum for energy deal
incidents.description: The Financial Times reported that U.S. President Donald Trump urged Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to sign energy deals with U.S. companies during a call in September. Sources familiar with the matter attributed Trump’s push to the delay in formal rounds of trade negotiations that had been scheduled to resume in September and have not been rescheduled.

incidents.title: Canadian employment falls by 68,000 in September
incidents.description: Canada recorded the loss of 68,000 jobs in September, a decline of 0.3%, following a loss of 42,000 jobs in August. Employment losses were concentrated among youths aged 15-24 and women between 25-54, indicating continued weakness in segments of the labor market.

incidents.title: U.S. agrees to purchase Russia diesel exports
incidents.description: Trump announced an agreement to increase Russian diesel exports to global markets through a temporary easing of U.S. energy sanctions despite Ukrainian criticism that the arrangement would provide Moscow with additional war revenue. Trump subsequently declared a ceasefire on attacks on energy infrastructure between Russia and Ukraine, although neither government confirmed that agreement. Ukraine had suspended attacks on Russian oil refineries for three days at Washington’s request, but Zelenskyy announced their resumption after Russian forces continued to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure. A Ukrainian attack on a Russian refinery in Ryazan on Oct. 15, effectively ended the proposed truce and further strained relations between Kyiv and Washington.

incidents.title: Ethiopia tells U.N. Security Council Eritrea has launched ‘all-out invasion’
incidents.description: After reports that Eritrean troops had been sighted in northern Ethiopia, Gedion Timothewos, the Ethiopian foreign minister, wrote in a letter to the U.N. Security Council that his country has no option but to defend itself, following what he described as an "all out invasion" by Eritrea. In response, Eritrea noted it had shown restraint since landlocked Ethiopia declared in 2023 its intent to gain access to the sea.

incidents.title: Lithuania reinforces border with Kaliningrad
incidents.description: Lithuania deployed soldiers along its border with the Russian Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad in a preventive measure, according to Latvian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas. The move comes amid an uptick in threats from Russia over its willingness to use nuclear weapons to defend the exclave as well as security incidents along Lithuanian’s border with Belarus.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Russian data center
incidents.description: A Ukrainian drone strike hit a data center owned by Yandex, a major Russian tech company, on Oct 8.

incidents.title: U.S. senators urge Trump to enact Russian sanctions early
incidents.description: U.S. Sens. Jeanne Shaheen, a Democrat, and Roger Wicker, a Republican, have urged U.S. President Donald Trump accelerate enforcement of a sanctions package targeting Russia ahead its scheduled Oct. 16 implementation, in light of Russia’s escalating bombardment of Ukrainian cities and the deployment of North Korean soldiers to the country.

incidents.title: Rubio says “no prospects” for peace with Russia
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that there presently “no prospects” to achieve a diplomatic solution with Russia to end its war with Ukraine.

incidents.title: Pezeshkian asks Iranians to reduce energy use
incidents.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian asked Iranian households to reduce their energy consumption by 10% each in a bid to soften the economic fallout from the war and U.S. sanctions campaign.

incidents.title: Hurricane Isaias delays oil shipments
incidents.description: Hurricane Isaias has forced operators to temporarily suspend 1.28 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil production in the Gulf of Mexico, representing approximately 63% of the region’s output. Natural gas production has also declined by 57%, with personnel evacuated from 121 offshore platforms. The hurricane is expected to go ashore on the Gulf Coast on Oct. 10, potentially extending production disruptions if infrastructure is damaged. The shutdown adds further pressure to global oil supplies amid ongoing disruptions in the Middle East.

incidents.title: Germany, United Kingdom launch joint security partnership
incidents.description: Under a new bilateral partnership, Germany and the United Kingdom will share intelligence and coordinate action to monitor, deter, and disrupt cyber and sabotage threats to critical infrastructure. Both identified Russian subversive activity as the primary (but not exclusive) threat in both domains.

incidents.title: Russia carries out large-scale bombardment across Ukraine
incidents.description: Russia conducted a large-scale bombardment in multiple regions of Ukraine on Oct. 7 that killed at least 30 people and wounded over 100.

incidents.title: EU enacts sweeping sanctions against Russia
incidents.description: The EU sanctioned over 1,600 people and entities associated with Russia’s defense industry in the bloc's single largest expansion of its sanctions campaign against Russia on Oct. 7.

incidents.title: Trump orders DoD to prepare for resumption of operations against Iran
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has reportedly ordered the Department of Defense to prepare for a possible resumption of large-scale combat operations against Iran.

incidents.title: Houthis bomb Saudi airports
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group bombed the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and the Abha International Airport near the Saudi/Yemeni border on Oct. 6 and 7, killing at least three people.

incidents.title: Syria weighs contributions to Saudi defense
incidents.description: Syria is considering contributing security assistance to Saudi Arabia’s defense, according to unnamed Syrian and U.S. officials, following meeting between Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Oct. 6 in Riyadh.

incidents.title: Taiwan to receive first batch of Harpoon missiles
incidents.description: Taiwan is set to receive its first batch of 128 U.S. Harpoon antiship missiles by the end of the year. The complete order totals 400 missiles a with the military expected to add a fourth coastal combat group by next year.

incidents.title: Germany blocks Chinese acquisition of German logistics firm
incidents.description: Germany blocked Cosco, a Chinese state-owned shipping company, from acquiring Zippel, a German logistics company. The economy ministry cited concerns over increased Chinese control over German supply chains for the intervention.

incidents.title: Cracks in German anti-far right firewall draw recriminations
incidents.description: After the election of Tobias Rausch, a far-right politician, as speaker of Parliament in Germany’s Saxony-Anhalt state, the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and its center-left coalition partner, the Social Democrats, exchanged recriminations over suspicions that four votes supporting Rauch came from CDU members. Because the voting was secret, there was no certainty over who cast the votes.

incidents.title: China, EU hold last round of trade talks before EU summit
incidents.description: China has rejected a proposal from the EU to voluntarily cap exports of hybrid cars to the bloc, as the EU readies itself to impose a slew of trade restrictions and tariffs on Chinese imports at a Brussels summit. This comes as EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is visiting Beijing this week for a last round of trade talks, with the Chinese side expressing openness to the EU imposing its own cap on hybrid vehicle imports.

incidents.title: Cyberattack targets South Korean financial sector
incidents.description: A cyberattack has resulted in data breaches among multiple South Korean financial sector entities. While the source of the attack has not been attributed, U.S. cyberdefense firm CrowdStrike reported that the attackers used Chinese-origin AI and Chinese language prompts.

incidents.title: F-35 components obtained by China
incidents.description: An F-35 cockpit canopy and weapons-bay door coated in radar-absorbing material were obtained by China after the parts were routed through Hong Kong to make up for delays in transit, violating the U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations. The shipment originating in Australia had been meant to travel through South Korea and Taiwan to get to San Francisco.

incidents.title: Mexico bars dual citizens from presidency
incidents.description: Reforms prohibiting presidential candidates, state governors, and the mayor of Mexico City from holding dual citizenship took effect on Oct. 7. Critics argue the moves were designed to weaken opposition to the ruling Morena party.

incidents.title: Myanmar’s leader makes first state visit to Malaysia since 2021 coup
incidents.description: Malaysia welcomed Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar's president and former junta leader, for a state visit with Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a sign of increasing international legitimacy being afforded to the once shunned Burmese junta government. Plans call for Min Aung Hlaing to take part in a formal welcome ceremony and a bilateral meeting with Ibrahim. Malaysia recently moved forward with the repatriation of ‌thousands of Myanmar refugees despite protests from human rights groups.

incidents.title: Indonesia court dismisses challenge to vice president
incidents.description: Indonesia’s Constitutional Court dismissed a petition seeking to disqualify Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka on procedural grounds, despite finding insufficient evidence that his foreign educational credentials satisfied election law educational requirements. The ruling preserves executive continuity but leaves his eligibility in question, potentially allowing further institutional or parliamentary challenges.

incidents.title: U.S. intercepts fuel exports valued at $3 million headed to Cuba
incidents.description: CBS News has reported that the U.S. Department of Homeland Security seized 620,000 gallons of biodiesel from Port Everglades and the Port of Houston it said was bound for Cuba in the first major seizure of its kind since the U.S. imposed a fuel blockade on Havana. U.S. officials have not identified or charged anyone with violating U.S. export restrictions in connection with the seizures.

incidents.title: Crackdown targets transnational environmental crime
incidents.description: An Interpol-coordinated operation across nine Latin American and Caribbean countries resulted in 233 arrests and identified about 230 square miles of illegally cleared forest. The investigations uncovered suspected links between those environmental crimes and companies and transnational financial networks.

incidents.title: Latin American, Caribbean states convene for ECLAC session
incidents.description: Representatives from across the region convened in the Dominican Republic for the 41st session of the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC), a United Nations regional commission, to discuss economic, social, and environmental development and establish priorities.

incidents.title: U.S. prepares new charges against Maduro
incidents.description: U.S. authorities were preparing additional criminal charges against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, over allegations that U.S. citizens detained in Venezuela were subject to torture.

incidents.title: Witnesses report Eritrean troops in northern Ethiopia
incidents.description: At least two witnesses claim to have seen "dozens" of Eritrean troops driving through Adigrat, 25 kilometers south of the Eritrean border, these reports are unverified. Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Meskel did not deny that troops had crossed the border but said Ethiopia’s government was creating “a fallacious narrative of ‘self-defense’ to rationalize and camouflage its war of aggression.”

incidents.title: Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces mediate conflict in Nuba Mountains
incidents.description: Maj. Gen. Hassan Mahjoub al-Fadil of the Rapid Support Forces investigated and mediated a deadly conflict between Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North and Otoro community which resulted in a “cessation of hostilities” so the initiative can proceed. More than 500 Otoro were killed and 25,000 displaced, and there have been disputes over native administration boundaries and political-military rivalries.

incidents.title: Kenyan living in DRC dies in Nairobi
incidents.description: Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case following the death of a Kenyan national in Nairobi who had been living in the DRC for seven years. DRC’s latest Ebola outbreak – its 17th – is its deadliest, having claimed over 4,000 lives. Over 8,300 cases have been recorded across seven provinces. The death in Kenya marks the first case outside of DRC during the current outbreak without containment.

incidents.title: French high schools close as student protests escalate
incidents.description: The Union Syndicale Lycéenne, a French high school union, said 2,000 high schools were closed across France on Oct. 6 due to escalating student-led protests involving at least 250,000 people driven by dilapidated school buildings, staff shortages, and overcrowded classrooms. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who called the demonstrations the most violent school protests in recent French history, said at least 700 police officers, 215 students, and 85 school staff members have been injured since they began in mid-September.

incidents.title: Mecca Agreement allies agree to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: Pakistan and Türkiye formed a coalition with Saudi Arabia to defend their Mecca Agreement ally against ongoing Houthi rebel attacks. As of Oct. 5, the Saudi-led coalition is conducting an extensive air campaign named Operation Dawn of Yemen in support of Yemeni government security forces waging a full-scale counteroffensive against the Houthis.

incidents.title: Vance says Iran must reduce Iranian enrichment
incidents.description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make “meaningful” reductions in its uranium enrichment capabilities before the U.S. will agree to a peace deal.

incidents.title: China moves assets to new Laos overseas base
incidents.description: Satellite imagery obtained by Reuters shows Chinese military vehicles and aircraft being moved to a new joint training facility in Laos, marking what could be the first Chinese base in Southeast Asia.

incidents.title: Far-right politician elected head of German state parliament for first time in post-WWII era
incidents.description: The state parliament of Saxony-Anhalt elected Tobias Raush, a member of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), to serve as speaker. His election was supported by the Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW), a conservative-leftist party, signaling a further deterioration of the "firewall" against cooperation with the AfD.

incidents.title: Taiwan opens second mission to U.S.
incidents.description: Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung attended the official opening of the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Phoenix, Arizona, marking its second official quasi-diplomatic presence in the United States. Taiwan has opened new semiconductor manufacturing plants in the state as part of its trade agreement with the U.S.

incidents.title: U.S., China, explore idea of reciprocal nuclear site visits
incidents.description: The U.S. and China have started discussing the idea of engaging in reciprocal visits to each other’s nuclear sites, including weapons testing sites, an idea raised by China in bilateral meetings earlier this year. The talks are seen as the first in efforts to enhance communications over nuclear capabilities following repeated attempts by the U.S. to bring China and Russia to the table to discuss nuclear nonproliferation. Officials expect further talks on the topic to take place before the end of the year.

incidents.title: Indonesia strengthens worker protections
incidents.description: Indonesia’s Parliament approved legislation increasing severance protections and restricting efficiency-based dismissals, addressing labor grievances that contributed to previous protests over the Job Creation Law. The reforms could reduce labor unrest, although higher employment costs could weigh on hiring and investment.

incidents.title: FBI whistleblower alleges Trump administration pushed for investigation into protesters
incidents.description: Former FBI supervisory intelligence analyst Jill Fields has filed a whistleblower complaint alleging the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump pressured the agency to open an investigation into people who participated in protests against Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Los Angeles. The complaint alleges the investigation directives violated the protesters' constitutional right to free speech.

incidents.title: Chinese economic growth continues to fall short of target
incidents.description: Economic analysis shows that China’s economy grew by 4.4% in the third quarter of 2026, only a tenth of a percentage point higher than growth in the second quarter. The rise is largely attributed to the AI sector and to a large export volume but falls below the minimum 4.5% target China had set for the year.

incidents.title: Pezeshkian says talks with U.S. are “meaningless”
incidents.description: U.S. President JD Vance said that Iran must make “meaningful” reductions in its ability to enrich uranium before the U.S. will agree to a peace deal. Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that talks with the U.S. are “meaningless” so long as they continue under the threat of military pressure.

incidents.title: U.S.-India trade talks stall
incidents.description: Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said negotiations over an India-U.S. trade agreement had reached a “plateau,” with further concessions becoming difficult for both sides. The talks remain stalled as the two governments continue negotiations over tariffs and market access.

incidents.title: Brazilian Supreme Court justice mulls release of former president from house arrest
incidents.description: Supreme Court Justice Kassio Nunes Marques told aides he sees “excesses” in the handling of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro’s case in which he was convicted for an attempted coup. Sources familiar with the justice said he is considering freeing Bolsonaro through an injunction.

incidents.title: Canada’s trade surplus surges in August
incidents.description: Canada’s total trade surplus grew from $693 million in July to $2.95 billion in August. This surge was largely driven by higher oil prices, currency depreciation, and U.S. trade barriers, as exporters increased shipments to the U.S. by 8.1% before 50% U.S. tariffs went into effect.

incidents.title: DRC hosts high-level mediation between insurgents and African Union in Goma
incidents.description: A high-level delegation from the African Union Panel of Facilitators consisting of several former presidents of neighboring countries met with the leadership of AFC/M23 in Goma to assess the group’s position on de-escalation and the peace process. Additionally, the African Union body reaffirmed its call for immediate cessation of hostilities.

incidents.title: Ethiopia faces pressure from regional neighbors after Egypt meeting
incidents.description: A joint statement issued Oct. 4 by the leaders of Egypt, Somalia, Eritrea, and Sudan targeted Ethiopia’s recent actions in the region, stating that Red Sea governance is the exclusive responsibility of littoral states, and rejecting unilateral measures harming the existing water uses of the two downstream Nile states.

incidents.title: Mexico’s president demands proof of alleged cross-border gunfire
incidents.description: Mexico has requested evidence from U.S. officials of alleged gunfire from Mexican side of its border with the United States targeting U.S. personnel Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexican security officials had not detected any such incident.

incidents.title: Mexico sends troops to border in joint operation with U.S.
incidents.description: Mexico deployed 500 army and national guard personnel to Tamaulipas to participate in a joint security operation with the U.S. military on the U.S.-Mexican border. The deployment was ordered in response to a Sept. 26 incident in which shots allegedly were fired from the Mexican side of the border at U.S. Coast Guard personnel.

incidents.title: Myanmar junta institutes blackouts to prevent El Niño-influenced grid collapse
incidents.description: Myanmar’s government announced rolling blackouts, seeking to prevent a collapse of the national electricity grid, citing increasing demand caused by extreme weather it attributed to the record-breaking El Niño climate phenomenon. The Burmese Ministry of Electricity and Energy claimed that high temperatures had substantially increased energy usage and forecast that water levels in hydropower reservoirs would decline substantially during the coming summer, leading to spot blackouts up to the 2027 rainy season.

incidents.title: Indonesia expands military command structure
incidents.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto inaugurated 204 new Indonesian National Armed Forces units, including six regional military commands and new army, navy, and air force formations.

incidents.title: Cuba’s president accuses U.S. of hypocrisy over tightening sanctions
incidents.description: In a podcast with Prime Minister Manuel Marrero, Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel accused the U.S. of hypocrisy for placing restrictions on privately owned Cuban businesses despite Cuba’s free-market reforms. Newly imposed sanctions revoking Cuban entrepreneurs’ ability to open U.S. bank accounts prompted Díaz-Canel to argue that the U.S.’s promotion of economic opening is “all a lie, all a fallacy.”

incidents.title: U.S. energy firms sign agreements for Venezuelan oil, gas development
incidents.description: Baker Hughes signed agreements with Venezuelan state-owned PDVSA and several other energy companies establishing frameworks to develop Venezuelan natural gas infrastructure, liquefied natural gas capacity, and future oil and natural gas projects.

incidents.title: India joins Afghanistan talks
incidents.description: India participated in the Moscow Format consultations on Afghanistan alongside Russia, China, Iran, Pakistan, and Central Asian states. Afghanistan was represented by Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi, while India reiterated its support for Afghanistan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The meeting exposed a widening Pakistan-Afghanistan security dispute as friction between the two prevented a unified joint statement from being issued at the end of the talks.

incidents.title: Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party secures biggest Brazilian Senate caucus
incidents.description: 28 members of the incoming Senate will be from the far-right Liberal Party, along with 12 senators from other allied parties. This bloc could control key committees that have the power to pass bills without sending them to the floor, as well as the power to push through certain government appointments and provide a check on the judiciary, which Bolsonaro has vowed to rein in.

incidents.title: Canadian separatist party secures minority government in Quebec
incidents.description: The separatist Parti Québécois (PQ) will form a minority government in Quebec after securing 60 seats in the provincial legislature – four short of a majority. The PQ will have to rely on support from opposition parties to pass legislation and survive confidence votes.

incidents.title: Ethiopian government forces seize Mekelle
incidents.description: The Tigray Peace Forces, a pro-government militia, said its fighters now control Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region. The Tigray People's Liberation Front, which leads the opposition alliance, said⁠ it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be "temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else."

incidents.title: Israel condemns British Green party’s declaration of Zionism as “racism”
incidents.description: Israel said that the U.K.’s Green Party was granting "legitimacy to terrorism” after it voted to label Zionism a form of racism and an “ethnonationalist political project” as part of its platform.

incidents.title: India proposes Ukraine truce
incidents.description: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said India had submitted the most comprehensive of four proposals under consideration to help halt the Russia-Ukraine war. Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar later confirmed that India has been discussing Black Sea shipping, grain and energy exports, and possible non-attack arrangements with both Russia and Ukraine.

incidents.title: Brazilian presidential race moves to runoff
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro advanced to the presidential runoff on Oct. 25. Bolsonaro won 47.03% of the vote in the initial balloting, while Lula brought in 45.16%. This margin is the smallest in Brazilian presidential election history, and no candidate who led the first round has lost the runoff.

incidents.title: EU diesel imports drop to record low
incidents.description: European diesel supplies tightened as imports fell to a record low in September – 600,000 barrels lower per day than September 2025 – with China suspending fuel exports and Russian supplies remaining constrained. Europe is particularly exposed because diesel demand remains high while roughly 30% of EU refinery capacity has been closed since 2009, increasing reliance on imported refined fuels. Strategic stock releases could become necessary if U.S. diesel exports are restricted before Persian Gulf supplies recover, since that would further tighten an already limited pool of available cargoes.

incidents.title: Food aid trucks hit by drones in South Kordofan, Sudan
incidents.description: Attacks on two World Food Program (WFP) trucks on the Dilling-Kadugli road in South Kordofan left one driver dead. The WFP and an EU delegation have called for an investigation since no perpetrator was identified. U.S. envoy Massad Boulos noted this incident was part of a “clear and dangerous pattern” of attacks on humanitarian aid operations.

incidents.title: German chancellor’s approval rating hits record low
incidents.description: A survey conducted by public broadcaster ARD found only 1 in 10 respondents expressed satisfaction with Friedrich Merz's performance as chancellor, a record low score. The decline in popularity comes amid declining electoral fortunes for Merz’s Christian Democratic Union, industrial challenges, and cost-of-living issues.

incidents.title: Hundreds gather to protest Mississippi redistricting
incidents.description: A protest was held in Jackson, MS, to oppose the Republican-led state government’s efforts to create a new congressional district map, which critics claim is designed to disenfranchise Black voters.

incidents.title: Middle East oil producers rely on alternate pipelines to transport oil
incidents.description: Middle Eastern energy logistics are undergoing a strategic shift as Gulf producers increasingly rely on alternative transport infrastructure to maintain oil exports amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Gulf crude and condensate exports, excluding those from Iran, averaged 16.5 million barrels per day in September, matching pre-war levels. However, only 60% of those shipments passed through the Strait of Hormuz, compared with 83% before the conflict. Saudi Arabia and the UAE have increasingly relied on pipelines and alternative shipping arrangements to bypass the waterway, despite higher transportation and insurance costs. This shift highlights the growing strategic importance of alternative export infrastructure in maintaining global oil supplies during regional crises, while potentially weakening Iran’s leverage over oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: U.K. passes new sanctions on Russian energy, grants exception to Japan and South Korea
incidents.description: The U.K. enacted new sanctions against Russia’s energy sector on Oct. 1 but simultaneously extended a carve-out for Japanese and South Korean imports of Russian liquefied natural gas.

incidents.title: Yemeni government forces, Houthis clash near Mocha
incidents.description: The internationally recognized government of Yemen reported that its military forces are engaged in intense ground fighting against Houthi rebel group personnel throughout the southwest province of Taiz, near the Red Sea port city of Mocha.

incidents.title: U.S. officials deem 2027 China invasion of Taiwan unlikely
incidents.description: Multiple U.S. officials speaking anonymously have stated they do not believe a military confrontation between China and Taiwan is likely next year despite calls from Chinese President Xi Jinping for the military to be ready for such an event by 2027. The officials cite delays caused by Xi’s anticorruption campaign as well as a desire by China to influence the result of the 2028 Taiwanese general election.

incidents.title: U.S. slows airplane part exports to China
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Commerce has slowed the export of airplane parts to China in recent weeks as the Trump administration seeks to gain leverage in future trade discussions with China. Further restrictions are reportedly being considered to impede China’s ability to stockpile parts.

incidents.title: South Korea to invest in U.S. nuclear energy, LNG
incidents.description: South Korea stated it would invest in building eight nuclear power stations in the U.S. worth $120 billion as part of last year’s agreed $350 billion investment plan. South Korea and the U.S. also both agreed to review a liquefied natural gas project in Alaska, which includes the construction of a pipeline and LNG port terminal.

incidents.title: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia
incidents.description: Following the Ethiopian government’s decision to declare 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata and close its embassy in Eritrea’s capital of Asmara, Eritrean officials have announced the termination of all diplomatic ties with Addis Ababa. Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs denounced Ethiopia’s allegations of hostility, stating that the actions of PM Abiy Ahmed’s government over the past three years have constituted a “publicly pronounced declaration of war” and that Ethiopian accusations against Eritrea are attempted justifications for an invasion of the country to attain ocean port access.

incidents.title: Russia makes nuclear threat against NATO
incidents.description: Russia sent a letter to NATO officials warning that it would be willing to use nuclear weapons to regain access to the Russian Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad if NATO forces were to cut it off in a future conflict scenario.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy claims North Korea preparing for additional deployment to Russia
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed on Sept. 28 that there are at least 8,000 North Korean soldiers currently deployed inside Russian territory and that Pyongyang is preparing the deployment of an additional 10,000 to support Russia's war effort in Ukraine.

incidents.title: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza kill at least 7
incidents.description: Israel killed at least 7 Palestinians in separate airstrikes in Gaza on Sept. 28.

incidents.title: China revises mobilization law
incidents.description: China revised a law for the first time since its passing in 2010 that would grant it increased control over civilian infrastructure and energy centers in the event of a military mobilization. The law is set to come in effect in October and would allow the Chinese government to requisition and expropriate civilian vehicles, infrastructure, and energy facilities.

incidents.title: Foreign mining companies weigh Venezuelan coal deals
incidents.description: Glencore, Peabody Energy, Heeney Capital, and Drummond considered agreements to extract coal in Venezuela, with discussions focused on operational control and rights to purchase production rather than mine ownership.

incidents.title: Modi, Trump review India-U.S. strategic ties
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump reviewed bilateral cooperation across trade, defense, energy, and critical technologies during a phone call and agreed to maintain close engagement. The conversation came as Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal traveled to the U.S. to advance an interim trade agreement and after Washington enacted new sanctions legislation targeting purchasers of Russian energy.

incidents.title: U.S. directs funds to civil society groups opposing Brazil’s Supreme Court
incidents.description: The U.S. State Department granted a $1 million award titled “Countering Lawfare and Censorship in Brazil” to civil society groups opposing “judicial overreach” and “censorship” from Brazil’s Supreme Court. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio obligated this grant and 42 others totaling $175.3 million to right-wing causes worldwide despite Congressional objections.

incidents.title: Brazil’s intelligence agency accuses U.S., Russia of election interference
incidents.description: The Brazilian intelligence agency ABIN alleged election interference from the U.S. and Russia in a meeting with German and French delegations ahead of its Oct. 4 presidential election. The U.S. State Department and Russian embassy declined to comment on these allegations.

incidents.title: U.S. tightens travel rules to Cuba, bans Cuban entrepreneur access to U.S. banks
incidents.description: Effective Sept. 30, the U.S. Treasury Department imposed additional restrictions on travel to Cuba and banned independent Cuban entrepreneurs from accessing U.S. banks. The policy also prohibits Americans from engaging in business dealings with sanctioned Cuban entities through an intermediary, closing a gap that previously only banned direct payments.

incidents.title: Civilian death toll rises as Ethiopian military advances into Tigray
incidents.description: Fighting between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and government Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) in the Alamata area of Ethiopia's Tigray region left 52 civilians dead, anonymous sources at local hospitals told the BBC. Social media clips of military equipment movements indicated that government troops have taken control of the town as they push north toward the Tigrayan regional capital of Mekelle.

incidents.title: Russian bombardment of Ukrainian energy infrastructure kills at least 7
incidents.description: Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia was not considering a release of political prisoners in exchange for U.S. sanctions relief after reports in U.S. media claimed that U.S. President Donald Trump gave his approval for U.S. Special Envoy for Hostage Affairs John Coale’s proposed initiative.

incidents.title: Iranian students protest in Tehran
incidents.description: Iranian students at the Allameh Tabataba'i University in Tehran staged protests against mandatory hijab policies and deteriorating economic conditions on Sept. 29. The Basij security forces put down the demonstration.

incidents.title: IRGC publishes open letter to American people
incidents.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps published a 25-page letter in English addressed to the American people, urging U.S. citizens to vote against U.S. President Donald Trump’s candidates and policies in the upcoming midterm elections.

incidents.title: U.S. completes Iraq withdrawal
incidents.description: The U.S. completed its withdrawal of forces out of Iraq on Sept. 28, seeing through a deal originally negotiated by former President Joe Biden’s administration.

incidents.title: U.S. Senate blocks resolution mandating report on Israeli violence in the West Bank
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate rejected a resolution that would have mandated a State Department report on settler violence in the West Bank be released to Congress. All Senate Republicans except one, plus and Democratic Sen. John Fetterman, voted against the resolution.

incidents.title: Venezuela, Qatari energy company discuss expansion into new gas fields
incidents.description: Qatar-based UCC Oil and Gas Holding said it was in talks to enter additional Venezuelan fields after receiving a long-term license with BP and ADNOC subsidiary XRG to develop the Loran gas project. The pact would grant the three companies rights to produce up to 4 trillion cubic feet of natural gas.

incidents.title: Iranian students hold protest in Tehran
incidents.description: Iranian students at the Allameh Tabataba'i University in Tehran staged protests against mandatory hijab policies and deteriorating economic conditions on Sept. 29. The Basij security forces put down the demonstration.

incidents.title: LNG Canada finalizes investment for pipeline project
incidents.description: The LNG Canada consortium made a final investment decision to expand the production capacity of a “nation-building” liquefied natural gas project to 28 million metric tons a year. Phase 2 of the project is expected to cost between $21 billion and $23 billion and has the potential to become one of the world’s top LNG exporters.

incidents.title: U.S. bans select Canadian imports
incidents.description: The United States imposed a partial ban on imports of Canadian alcohol, dairy products, and motorcycles. The ban only applies to about 0.25% of Canada’s exports to the U.S. The ban is unlikely to have a significant economic impact.

incidents.title: Myanmar regime bombs market, killing civilians
incidents.description: Myanmar's military regime hit a crowded market near the Myanmar-Bangladesh border in an air strike, killing 50 civilians and injuring an estimated 58. The U.N. confirmed the regime targeted a crowded market and reaffirmed Myanmar as being unsafe for returning refugees.

incidents.title: Myanmar prepares for repatriation of 1,500 nationals
incidents.description: Malaysia has begun to repatriate 1,500 of the 190,000 Myanmar nationals residing in Malaysia, amid a mounting refugee crisis and online disinformation campaigns targeting the Rohingya population. Rohingya Muslims are estimated to represent up to two-thirds of the refugees in Malaysia and, despite fearing persecution back in Myanmar, lack refugee status as Malaysia is not a signatory of the 1951 U.N. Refugee Convention. Following the plan’s announcement in late July, over 160 civil society organizations have petitioned in protest citing the ongoing conflict in Myanmar following the 2021 coup. It remains unclear how many of the initial 1,500 Myanmar nationals are Rohingya.

incidents.title: Taiwan expands antiship arsenal
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense has allocated close to $700 million of its regular defense budget to the development of an additional 200 Hsiung Feng antiship missiles between 2027 and 2035. Officials have commented on the need to develop greater of antiship capabilities in the event of a military confrontation with China.

incidents.title: Venezuelan opposition supporters rally for elections, Machado’s return
incidents.description: Hundreds of opposition supporters demonstrated in Caracas and several state capitals, calling for presidential elections and the safe return of opposition leader María Corina Machado.

incidents.title: Heavy rain, flooding kill 62 in northern India
incidents.description: At least 62 people died and 46 were injured after three days of heavy rainfall triggered widespread flooding across Uttar Pradesh left more than 1,000 homes damaged. Flooding also forced more than 75,000 people to evacuate in Odisha, while neighboring Nepal reported 21 deaths from weather-related incidents over the same period.

incidents.title: Disinformation targeting Brazil’s presidential challenger reaches Supreme Court
incidents.description: Viral social media posts circulated claiming that if elected, right-wing presidential candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro would strip Brazil’s patron saint of her title. Justice Andres Mendonça of Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court ordered this content to be taken down, but his ruling was overturned by Justice Flávio Dino, setting up a full-court session of Brazil’s Supreme Court to consider the case.

incidents.title: Sudan's foreign minister demands investigation into U.S. visa denial at U.N.
incidents.description: At the U.N. General Assembly's general session, Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salim demanded an investigation into the U.S. denial of a visa to General Abdel Burhan of the Sudanese Armed Forces and warned against expanding the U.N. Darfur arms embargo, while U.N. envoy Al-Harith Idriss accused the UAE of arming and financing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

incidents.title: Sudan sees sharp decline in cholera cases
incidents.description: The U.N. reported a sharp drop in cholera cases after a WHO/UNICEF vaccination campaign reached over 900,000 people. The U.N. cautioned that drone strikes and ground fighting continue to threaten relief access despite improvements.

incidents.title: Indonesia purchases 105 amphibious combat vehicles from U.S.
incidents.description: Indonesia's Navy Chief of Staff Adm. Muhammad Ali announced Jakarta’s purchase of 105 AAV-M35 amphibious combat vehicles from the United States. Indonesia's Marine Corps is set to receive these vehicles at a pace of 35 annually, with the final batch arriving in 2028. Ali did not answer questions on the total cost of the purchase.

incidents.title: Indonesian rupiah declines significantly against U.S. dollar
incidents.description: The rupiah's exchange rate closed below 18,000 to $1. The rupiah's decline is due to oil price volatility, disruptions to Indonesia's energy supply caused by foreign wars, and a dollar strengthened by a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike.

incidents.title: Indonesia reforms coal export governance
incidents.description: Indonesian Trade Ministry Director of Industrial and Mining Product Export Rivai Abbas announced new regulations aimed at streamlining licensing for coal exports. Significant reforms include streamlining the licensing process for coal exports and establishing mechanisms to improve data sharing between ministries with the aim of enhancing the traceability of coal exports.

incidents.title: Ethiopian general accuses Sudan, Eritrea of backing rebel groups
incidents.description: As fighting between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and the Ethiopian army continued, Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) Field Marshal Birhanu Jula accused Eritrea and Sudan of backing the TPLF and allied militant groups. The accusation comes as the TPLF captured the town of Erebti in the Afar region, with as many as 150,000 civilians displaced by the fighting. Ethiopia has claimed to have inflicted high casualties upon TPLF troops during attempted offensives.

incidents.title: Three dead after migrant boat leaving France shipwrecked
incidents.description: A migrant dinghy attempting to cross the English Channel from France to the United Kingdom shipwrecked six kilometers from the British shore, resulting in the deaths of three people. French authorities rescued all 102 other passengers.

incidents.title: Rhine River remains critically low
incidents.description: Water levels along the Rhine River, one of Europe’s most important trade arteries, are among the lowest on record, enhancing pressure on domestic shipping and manufacturing amid rising energy prices.

incidents.title: AFC/M23 launches drone attack on DRC airfield
incidents.description: The AFC/M23 rebel coalition conducted its first reported attack on Pinga in Walikale territory, using a drone to target an Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) position at the town’s airfield. The drone later returned for a second reconnaissance, prompting FARDC fire and temporarily disrupting schools and economic activity.

incidents.title: Sudan, Egypt accused of backing armed opposition groups in Ethiopia
incidents.description: Ethiopia's military chief Marshal Birhanu Jula accused Sudan and Egypt of backing armed opposition groups, and Sudan's army spokesperson answered by accusing Ethiopia of facilitating the operations of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

incidents.title: French far-right party wins 9 senate seats
incidents.description: Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and an allied party now hold a record 14 seats in the French Senate, enough to form a group in the chamber. This means the RN will have more guaranteed speaking time and input over parliamentary processes.

incidents.title: German, Russian foreign ministers meet on sidelines of U.N. General Assembly
incidents.description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York, where Wadephul demanded Russia abandon its “dangerous path of escalation” with Germany and its EU and NATO allies. While both sides confirmed discussing bilateral ties and the war in Ukraine – with Berlin adding that Wadephul urged Lavrov to “do everything possible to reach an agreement on grain exports via the Black Sea” – Lavrov countered that the German delegation offered nothing beyond what had already been stated publicly.

incidents.title: Trump rejects Iran peace offer
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian peace proposal presented at the meeting of the U.N. General Assembly in New York on Sept. 26, aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. On Sept. 27, Iran said it remained committed to achieving a diplomatic solution to the conflict.

incidents.title: U.S., China cut tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods
incidents.description: Following last week’s summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, China and the U.S. agreed to cut tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, including cosmetics and agricultural goods, as well as other “non-sensitive” goods. The Chinese cut on tariffs did not include soybeans, which had previously been a subject of contention between the countries.

incidents.title: U.S. Department of Transportation to lower vehicle fuel economy standards
incidents.description: The Trump administration has begun repealing a Biden-era regulation that mandated the fleetwide average for auto manufacturers must operate at 50.4 miles per gallon or higher. Under the revised regulations, the new fleetwide average will be permitted to operate as low as 34.9 miles per gallon. The environmental group The Sierra Club has condemned the move, noting that the new fuel economy standard is expected to significantly increase greenhouse gas emissions and is scheduled to be in effect through 2031.

incidents.title: Canada procures surveillance aircraft
incidents.description: Canada’s federal government announced a preliminary agreement to acquire six GlobalEye surveillance aircraft from Swedish firm Saab. The aircraft will be used to detect aircraft, missiles, and drones. If the deal is finalized, Saab would build the aircraft Canada in collaboration with Canadian firm Bombardier.

incidents.title: U.S. Army Reserve assesses support units for potential Cuban operations
incidents.description: The U.S. Army Reserve is investigating whether it can provide the military’s Southern Command with personnel, a move that anonymous U.S. officials said related to military planning for Cuba, CBS News reported. CBS reviewed an internal Army message that, while it made no specific mention of Cuba, sought feedback from subordinate commands regarding police, medical staff, logistics units, and other personnel in the next three to four months.

incidents.title: Planned German government spending cuts trigger union protests
incidents.description: Over 175,000 trade union protestors across Germany protested the Merz administration’s planned spending cuts to healthcare, social services, and pensions.

incidents.title: DRC adopts new Ebola response plan
incidents.description: The Congolese government approved a new 180-day multisectoral “One Health” plan as the common framework for preventing and responding to the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak and announced the phased introduction of free health care in Ituri province for the duration of the epidemic. The policy strengthens the state-led response in the outbreak’s epicenter as transmission remains high nationally and conflict continues to impede containment efforts

incidents.title: White House cancels nearly $1 billion in Congress-approved spending
incidents.description: The Trump administration announced the cancellation of nearly $1 billion of government funding approved by Congress. The majority of the cuts relate to services for immigrant and refugee populations. Multiple members of Congress disputed the legality of the cuts.

incidents.title: Brazil’s president bans fixed-odds betting
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a provisional executive order banning the operation, offering, intermediation, and advertising of fixed-odds betting. This ban will take immediate effect but requires congressional approval within 120 days to remain enacted. Betting platform users have until Oct. 5 to withdraw funds from accounts.

incidents.title: Mexico to revise its FDI approach for 2027
incidents.description: Mexico’s Secretariat of Economy proposed changes to its current strategy for attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) set to begin in 2027, including a 30.9% reduction from 2026 in funding to promote foreign trade and draw FDI. Mexico’s 2027 FDI strategy aims to channel investment toward strategic sector growth, job creation, and ensuring that announced projects become operational.

incidents.title: Myanmar nationals protest new deportation law in Thailand
incidents.description: Thailand’s newly passed deportation law has sparked widespread criticism from Myanmar nationals living in Thailand and civil society organizations. Human Rights Watch asserts that Thailand's nonrecognition of Myanmar nationals’ refugee status, the absence of non-refoulement, and the newly fast-tracked deportation process will facilitate the forced return of Myanmar nationals and activists, putting them at risk of being killed by the junta.

incidents.title: Erdoğan calls for de-escalation in Black Sea in meeting with Zelenskyy
incidents.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan called Ukrainian attacks against Russian ships in the Black Sea “inexplicable” during a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York.

incidents.title: Federal judge orders White House to restore press access to banned outlets
incidents.description: Federal District Judge Tim Kelly ordered the White House to restore press access to CNN, Politico, and MS NOW in an injunction related to a lawsuit filed by the three media outlets alleging the ban, instituted by President Donald Trump, violates their First Amendment rights.

incidents.title: Venezuela commits to elections; no timeframe given
incidents.description: Interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez told the U.N. General Assembly that elections would form part of Venezuela’s ongoing political transition, without providing a timetable for a vote.

incidents.title: European states increase reliance on coal
incidents.description: European power producers are increasing their reliance on coal as disruptions to flows through the Strait of Hormuz push natural gas costs higher. European benchmark gas prices exceeded 80 euros ($91) per megawatt-hour in September, their highest level in three years, making coal-fired electricity more economical than gas generation. Analysts expect European coal-fired power output to increase by roughly 25 percent over the next six months as gas-fired generation falls by a similar amount. However, Europe has limited capacity to expand coal use much further following years of plant closures, with Germany’s remaining coal fleet expected to operate near its practical maximum during the fourth quarter.

incidents.title: Canada begins carbon removal project
incidents.description: Canada is developing a framework under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change to enable domestic carbon removal projects to sell verified credits in international carbon markets. The policy could expand demand beyond Canada’s relatively small domestic market and attract investment into emerging removal technologies, including direct air capture. Canada has around 11 metric megatons of announced carbon removal capacity awaiting construction. Access to overseas buyers could also support Ottawa’s broader effort to strengthen economic ties with Europe and Asia amid trade tensions with the United States.

incidents.title: Brazilian president airs campaign ad claiming U.S. election meddling
incidents.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s presidential campaign accused the U.S. of meddling in the Oct. 4 presidential election to “colonize” Brazil and control its natural resources in a campaign advertisement. The ad aired a day after 31 U.S. members of Congress issued a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticizing President Donald Trump for efforts to undermine Brazil’s election.

incidents.title: Russian drones crash in Romania, Moldova
incidents.description: At least one drone of Russian origin crashed in Romanian and Moldovan territory, respectively, during a large-scale drone attack by Russia targeting Ukraine’s Chernivisti region on Sept. 24. No casualties were reported in Romania or Moldova.

incidents.title: Indonesia commits soldiers to Gaza stabilization force
incidents.description: Indonesia has agreed to contribute several thousand soldiers to the International Stabilization Force (ISF), a Board of Peace-backed peacekeeping mission that is expected to take over the administration of Gaza. This marks a reversal of Jakarta’s previous decision to disengage from Board of Peace discussions regarding Gaza after the Iran war’s outbreak. According to the U.S., Indonesia will contribute senior personnel to the mission, including for the ISF deputy director role.

incidents.title: U.S., Greenland, Denmark sign security deal
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump, Danish President Mette Frederiksen, and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed a security deal that significantly increases U.S. force presence in Greenland and will lead to the construction of a “Golden Dome” defense system, according Trump.

incidents.title: IRGC assisting Houthi ground campaign
incidents.description: Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps personnel conducted advise-and-assist missions on the ground in Yemen alongside Houthi forces during the Yemeni Houthi rebel group’s 48-hour offensive that resulted in the capture of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast.

incidents.title: Israeli security forces kill senior IDF leader
incidents.description: The Israel Defense Forces and Israel’s primary domestic security agency, the Shin Bet, killed Hamas finance chief Muhammad Abu Alwan in Gaza on Sept. 23 in a joint operation.

incidents.title: Shortages in Ontario’s manufacturing sector
incidents.description: The trade group Canadian Manufacturers and Exporters reported Ontario manufacturers are facing shortages of skilled labor across several trades. Dennis Darby, the group’s CEO, said about 50,000 jobs, mostly in the steel, aluminum, automotive, and fabrication industries, have been impacted by U.S. tariffs. Retirement, immigration, and gaps between education and the industry are contributing to the shortage of needed labor.

incidents.title: U.S. dollar hits record high in Cuba’s informal market
incidents.description: The U.S. dollar exchange rate reached 722 pesos in Cuba’s informal currency markets, marking the sixth straight record high since the dollar surpassed 700 pesos a week ago as Cuba’s economy continues to deteriorate.

incidents.title: Tigrayan forces seize airports, villages in multiregion ground offensive
incidents.description: The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) seized control of the region’s Mekelle and Shire airports and the town of Abala in the neighboring Afar region in an offensive that it described as a response to “intensive bombardments” by the central government’s Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF). Fighting has also been reported in the Amhara region. The attacks came days after the TPLF announced a coalition with the Afar Revolutionary Democratic Unity Front and the Amhara Fano National movement, suggesting possible cross-group coordination could be facilitating the offensive.

incidents.title: Senior U.S. envoys meet with Iranian delegation at U.N.
incidents.description: U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and senior presidential adviser and Donald Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner met with the Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York on Sept. 22. Trump described the meeting positively and said he expected a follow-up soon.

incidents.title: Xi, Trump meet in Washington, extend trade truce
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Washington, where he was met at the airport by U.S. President Donald Trump. U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent announced that both countries had agreed to a two-month extension to last year’s trade truce.

incidents.title: India, U.S. discuss Russian oil tariff concerns
incidents.description: In a discussion with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar raised concerns about the bill passed by the U.S. Congress that would authorize tariffs of up to 100% on major purchasers of Russian energy, including India. Rubio later said U.S. President Donald Trump, who had yet to sign the bill into law, could apply national security waivers in individual cases.

incidents.title: Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) seize Mekelle and Shire airports
incidents.description: The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) seized control of the Tigray region’s Mekelle and Shire airports and the town of Abala in the neighboring Afar region in an offensive that it described as a response to “intensive bombardments” by the central government’s Ethiopian National Defense Forces. Fighting has also been reported in the Amhara region. The attacks come days after the TPLF announced a coalition with the Afar Revolutionary Democratic Unity Front and Amhara Fano National Movement, suggesting possible cross-group coordination could be facilitating the offensive.

incidents.title: U.S. withholds Sudanese leader’s visa ahead of U.N. General Assembly
incidents.description: The United States has apparently withheld an entry visa for Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, the army chief of the Sudanese Armed Forces, who as head of the country’s Sovereign Council is its de facto president, ahead of his scheduled address to the U.N. General Assembly. Reports noted that the visa would be contingent on al-Burhan signing a U.S.-proposed 90-day ceasefire agreement. Al-Harith Idriss Al-Harith, the Sudanese representative to the U.N., asked U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres for "immediate intervention" with U.S. authorities.

incidents.title: U.S. asserts neither faction represent legitimate Sudanese governance
incidents.description: U.S. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said neither the Sudan Armed Forces nor the Rapid Support Forces, nor their leaders, represent legitimate governance for Sudan, and that the United States would raise the cost of the war on all belligerents and their supply networks. The statement moves U.S. policy from conditioning one leader's access to publicly delegitimizing both.

incidents.title: Consumer prices, inflation rise in Myanmar
incidents.description: To preserve foreign currency reserves amid sanctions, Myanmar’s regime has restricted imports across the board, increasing the cost of appliances, household items, and general consumer goods exponentially. Many families have turned to a thriving second-hand market to find most cost-effective options as rising inflation, a volatile exchange rate, and unreliable shipments of consumer goods result in prices that are triple those seen in 2021-22.

incidents.title: Indonesian lawmakers pass agricultural reform law
incidents.description: Indonesia's legislature passed a law establishing an executive body to enact significant land reforms aimed at resolving property disputes, rehabilitating abandoned land, and redistributing land to reduce rural inequalities.

incidents.title: EU extends sanctions against Russia
incidents.description: On Sept. 22 the EU approved legislation to extend 3,000 existing sanctions against Russia for an additional 36 months.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy, Trump meet
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with U.S. President Donald Trump as U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York on Sept. 22 to discuss peace efforts.

incidents.title: Brazil bars political candidates with alleged criminal ties
incidents.description: Prosecutors in Brazil have started to use a broader interpretation of a 2024 Superior Electoral Court ruling to challenge candidacies based on evidence of crimes rather than conviction. The prosecutors said the measures are being used to keep organized crime out of politics, while experts raised concerns about due process. Candidates barred by local courts under this precedent may still appeal the decision.

incidents.title: Brazil’s president warns against foreign election interference
incidents.description: In a speech at the U.N. General Assembly, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva warned against external interference in Brazil’s election process amid tensions with the United States. Lula also encouraged the United Nations to take stronger action in response to continuing wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, stating that the U.N.’s “credibility has never been lower.”

incidents.title: Iraq cancels Iranian flights from Baghdad in response to U.S. sanctions threat
incidents.description: Iraq ordered the suspension of all Iranian commercial flights into Baghdad effective Sept. 23, following threats from the U.S. to sanction all airports open to flights from Iranian airlines. U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent said that the sanctions would aim to shut down all Iranian airlines.

incidents.title: Canadian asset manager launches exchange-traded fund
incidents.description: Ninepoint Partners, a Canadian investment company, has launched the Ninepoint North American Energy Independence Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF), the first fund listed in the United States for investment in energy firms spanning the two countries. The ETF will invest in up to 50 U.S., Canadian, and eventually Mexican stocks, initially consisting mostly of U.S.-based gas and oil producers and Canadian pipeline companies.

incidents.title: Erdoğan calls for U.N. Security Council reform
incidents.description: urkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan said the U.N. Security Council should abolish the veto procedure as he called for reform to the international body while addressing the U.N. General Assembly on Sept. 22.

incidents.title: South Korea, U.S. hail investment progress
incidents.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and U.S. President Donald Trump both stated that South Korean investment plans in the U.S. as part of the $350 billion investment package pledged by Seoul last year to the U.S. were progressing. The South Korean Industry Ministry cited a Texas gas project and an Alaskan LNG venture as two examples of success.

incidents.title: China issues fentanyl enforcement guidelines
incidents.description: China issued a list of guidelines for law enforcement authorities on how criminal cases should be handled regarding fentanyl-related crimes, a day before President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington. The White House had previously stressed the importance of stemming the flow of fentanyl precursor products from China.

incidents.title: Trump administration to remove Obamacare subsidies for 760,000
incidents.description: Vice President JD Vance said approximately 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees will lose access to subsidies amid accusations of fraud. Vance claimed some people were removed because they did not provide Social Security numbers or verified immigration status, although he did not specify how many people fell into this category.

incidents.title: India, Central European countries establish diplomatic talks
incidents.description: India and the Visegrád Group, comprising Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and Czechia, held their first ministerial meeting and agreed to meet annually and establish an annual business forum. The four countries backed India’s bid for permanent U.N. Security Council membership, and their discussions covered expanded defense, technology, space, and transportation infrastructure cooperation.

incidents.title: Saudi pipeline resumes operations
incidents.description: Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which was hit by an attack attributed to Iraqi militias last week, has resumed operations, allowing exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu to restart. Before the shutdown, Saudi Arabia was sending around 4 million barrels per day through the pipeline, which has a capacity of 7 million bpd. The gradual recovery should begin to ease supply concerns and put downward pressure on oil prices, while reassuring Asian buyers that Saudi Arabia is restoring a key alternative export route through the Red Sea amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: German energy price per megawatt reaches 180 euros
incidents.description: Wholesale German power prices for January have climbed above 180 euros ($205) per megawatt-hour (MWh), more than 60% higher than a year ago, as higher natural gas prices, constrained Qatari LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, reduced French nuclear power output, and low hydropower stocks have combined to tighten Europe’s winter power outlook. Europe is better insulated from outright shortages than during the 2022 energy crisis because of expanded LNG import capacity and diversified natural gas supply, but its greater dependence on global LNG markets leaves electricity prices vulnerable to prolonged disruptions and weak renewable generation output.

incidents.title: Sudanese paramilitary drones strike multiple sites in state capital
incidents.description: Drone attacks attributed to Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group struck multiple sites in El Obeid, North Kordofan's state capital, including four that struck the Sudanese Armed Forces headquarters and Ministry of Finance offices in the city, with damage not immediately known. Another strike later that day killed two civilians and injured more than 20 others, with attacks continuing throughout the day.

incidents.title: Rural Myanmar communities face mass conscription, taxation
incidents.description: Civilians in Shan state reported widespread conscription and extortion by both regime and local resistance forces, raising familial rates of debt amid growing abductions and arbitrary arrests throughout the region. Monthly quotas of conscription and rising taxation thresholds, perpetrated by the military and resistance-aligned Pa-O National Organization, have sustained the personnel needed for the protracted civil war and pushed substantial portions of the population below the poverty line.

incidents.title: Myanmar's ruling party reaffirms leadership
incidents.description: Myanmar's ruling Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP) re-elected Chairman Khin Yi as it admitted President Min Aung Hlaing as an official party member, a status that is only now possible as the nation’s constitution bars those holding his previous position of military commander-in-chief from holding party affiliation. Party officials have speculated that Min Aung Hlaing may have been eyeing the chairmanship for himself, as his duties as president not only force him to split power of governance with the legislature but also require USDP support to continue past this current term.

incidents.title: Mexico to boost U.S. imports
incidents.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Mexico plans to increase imports from the U.S. and decrease imports from other trade partners amid the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) trade review process.

incidents.title: DRC armed forces launch operation after mass abduction at mining site
incidents.description: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC) launched an operation in Djugu territory, Ituri province, after suspected fighters from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP), an antigovernment armed movement, attacked the Nyampala mining site and abducted 25 people. Six of the abducted were Chinese nationals, and four were FARDC soldiers. FARDC subsequently targeted suspected CRP positions around Nyampala, Liko, and Luna with heavy weapons.

incidents.title: Macron, Trump discuss Ukraine and Red Sea
incidents.description: French President Emmanuel Macron pushed the issue of supplying defensive weapons to Ukraine in a meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. The leaders also discussed securing transit of oil through the Red Sea to slow price increases.

incidents.title: Trump decides against Yemen intervention
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump called off planned strikes against the Yemeni Houthi rebel group despite a request by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Sept. 22. The Houthis announced that they had assured Trump administration officials that they would not target U.S. vessels in the Red Sea as the U.S. agrees to refrain from direct action against the Houthis.

incidents.title: U.S. monitoring Chinese research vessels off Alaska
incidents.description: Adm. Bob Little, commander of the U.S. Coast Guard’s Arctic District, said nine Chinese research vessels have been detected in international waters near Alaskan maritime zones since 2025. The vessels failed to notify U.S. authorities in advance of their deployment as dictated by protocol.

incidents.title: AfD wins 38% of vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania election
incidents.description: The right-wing Alternative for Germany (AfD) party took 38.2% of the vote in state elections in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union dropped below the 5% threshold required to name representatives to the state’s parliament for the first time since World War II. The results, however, left AfD short of the majority needed to control the parliament, boosting the prospects that the second-place Social Democrats (35%) will be able to form a coalition and remain in power.

incidents.title: Ukraine fires over 1,000 drones into Russia
incidents.description: Ukraine fired over 1,000 missiles and drones into Russia, primarily targeting the Moscow region, on Sept. 20. The large-scale attack came in addition to a number of separate drone strikes against Russian energy infrastructure sites over the course of the week.

incidents.title: Cuban-American elites draft plans for Cuba’s future
incidents.description: The Wall Street Journal reported that a group of wealthy Cuban-Americans with ties to U.S. President Donald Trump have been drafting plans for a post-communist Cuba in backroom meetings held in Miami. The plans include establishing a Cuban stock exchange, an investment summit in Havana, and discussions over who could lead Cuba after a political transition.

incidents.title: Ethiopian opposition groups announce coalition against Abiy government
incidents.description: Seven Ethiopian opposition groups, including the Tigray People’s Liberation Front and Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM), announced the formation of the “Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Coalition for Survival.” Zemene Kassie, the head of the AFMN, said the goal of the coalition was to remove the Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party from power in Addis Ababa and institute a transitional government. Also included in the coalition are the regionally based Oromo Liberation Army, Ogaden National Liberation Front, Afar National Unity Revolutionary Front, Benishangul Peoples’ Liberation Movement, and Gumuz Peoples’ Democratic Movement.

incidents.title: Left-wing party takes 25.7% of the vote in Berlin’s state election
incidents.description: The left-wing Die Linke party finished first in Berlin’s state election with 25.7% of the vote, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union trailed with 18.8%.

incidents.title: Far-right leads in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
incidents.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) won 38.2% of the vote in state elections in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union dropped below the 5% threshold required to claim parliamentary seats for the first time since World War II. The AfD fell short of a majority, leaving the Social Democrats (35%) in position to form a governing coalition.

incidents.title: North Korea test-launches two ballistic missiles
incidents.description: North Korea launched two short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea following a statement accusing the United States of raising tensions on the Korean Peninsula. This comes weeks after the U.S. downgraded its involvement in joint military drills with South Korea, citing Trump’s relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as a reason.

incidents.title: Australia, New Zealand deepen naval ties
incidents.description: Australia and New Zealand agreed to deepen naval cooperation. The agreement, dubbed “Plan Tasman,” will tighten cooperation on naval training, development, and warfighting.

incidents.title: New Zealand vessels transit Taiwan Strait
incidents.description: Two New Zealand ships – the frigate Te Mana and the oiler Aotearoa – transited the Taiwan Strait as part of their broader Indo-Pacific deployment.

incidents.title: Indonesia considers state control over strategic commodity exports
incidents.description: President Prabowo Subianto announced that Indonesia will put strategic commodity exports such as palm oil, nickel, tin, gold, coal, coffee, and rubber under the control of state-owned enterprises. Prabowo cited a desire to increase state revenues and prevent export underreporting and tax evasion.

incidents.title: U.S. allows restrictions on military exports to Ethiopia to lapse
incidents.description: The U.S. State Department removed Ethiopia from as a restricted nation under the International Traffic in Arms Regulation on Sept. 18, which will allow exports of defense hardware and military technology to the country to resume. At the same time, the U.S. Treasury Department announced the expiration of Executive Order 14046, issued by former U.S. President Joe Biden, that had imposed financial and travel restrictions on Ethiopian officials accused of human rights violations during the 2020-2022 Tigray war.

incidents.title: Trump promises new "AI Force"
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump promised to create an "AI Force," comparing it to the U.S. Space Force, and to appoint an official responsible for overseeing U.S. AI development. Trump did not specify the responsibilities the organization would carry or whether it would operate in a civilian or military capacity.

incidents.title: Venezuelans widely oppose U.S. oil agreement
incidents.description: A Meganálisis survey found that 80% of Venezuelan respondents opposed the oil agreement reached with the United States in August, while 13% supported it and 8% were undecided.

incidents.title: India, Canada advance trade negotiations
incidents.description: India and Canada completed their fourth round of negotiations over a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. Negotiators had concluded two chapters, with both governments targeting completion by the end of 2026. The proposed agreement covers goods, services, and investment, alongside broader bilateral discussions on clean energy, AI, and critical minerals.

incidents.title: France hosts Lebanese, Jordanian leaders for summit on Lebanese security
incidents.description: French President Emmanuel Macron hosted King Abudllah II of Jordan and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in Paris on Sept. 17 to discuss security aid to the Lebanese army and the creation of an international security force to replace the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon.

incidents.title: Indonesia acquires first aircraft carrier from Italy
incidents.description: The Giuseppe Garibaldi, Italy's sole aircraft carrier, arrived in Tanjung Priok for transfer to Indonesia's navy. Indonesia plans to retrofit the 41-year-old vessel to allow it to serve as a mobile command post that can launch drones and helicopters to support humanitarian responses in Indonesia's outlying islands. This is part of President Prabowo Subianto's efforts to expand and modernize Indonesia's military by deepening ties with the Italian defense industrial base, with Jakarta eying the acquisition of Italian submarines and trainer aircraft.

incidents.title: Brazil’s president unveils plan to combat organized crime
incidents.description: Ahead of Brazil’s Oct. 4 general election, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched a pilot plan to expand the federal government’s role in fighting organized crime.
