This plan, which will first be used in Rio de Janeiro, allows for increased coordination of policing; shared intelligence among federal, state, and municipal agencies; highway surveillance; and cargo inspections.

incidents.title: Cuba hit with nationwide blackout
incidents.description: Cuba experienced its sixth blackout this year after the state power grid collapsed in the early afternoon on Sept. 18. A handful of Havana neighborhoods had power restored by early evening, though most of the city remained without electricity.

incidents.title: France asks EU to secure diesel, jet fuel supplies
incidents.description: In a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, French President Emmanuel Macron urged a relaxing of fuel quality specifications to allow for increased refinery output amid supply shocks due to war in the Middle East and sanctions on Russian oil. Additionally, the letter called for a postponement of the reporting requirement for methane emitters.

incidents.title: Poland scrambles fighter jets in response to Russian drone strikes near Ukrainian border
incidents.description: Poland scrambled fighter aircraft and delayed commercial air travel in eastern Poland, as Russian drone strikes came close to Polish territory on Sept. 17.

incidents.title: Russia bombards Kyiv, Odesa
incidents.description: Russia carried out airstrikes against several Ukrainian cities over the course of the week, with the Kyiv and Odesa regions enduring the heaviest bombardment.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes oil infrastructure in Russia’s Rostov region
incidents.description: Ukraine conducted drone strikes against oil infrastructure in Russia’s Rostov region on Sept. 16.

incidents.title: Turkiye proposes ceasefire in Black Sea
incidents.description: The Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs shared a draft memorandum with Russia and Ukraine on Sept. 17 that proposes a ceasefire on civilian cargo ships in the Black Sea. Neither Russia nor Ukraine has commented publicly on the proposal.

incidents.title: Trump hopeful about Iran peace prospects
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. is “hopefully” moving closer to the end of the war with Iran and claimed that Iran wants to “make a deal.”

incidents.title: Japan, U.S. lawmakers reiterate defense of First Island Chain
incidents.description: A delegation of Japanese lawmakers met with members of the U.S. Senate and the Congressional Taiwan caucus in Washington, where U.S. and Japanese lawmakers agreed that the U.S. must defend the First Island Chain, while stating that Japan would necessarily be involved in a Taiwan contingency.

incidents.title: EU asks China to restrict hybrid vehicle exports
incidents.description: The EU has requested that China voluntarily cut back its exports of hybrid cars to the bloc, stating that it wants to limit hybrid vehicle imports from China to 15% of the EU market. The EU had previously set October as a deadline for obtaining “tangible results” from trade negotiations with China and stated if China does not reduce its exports voluntarily, the EU would impose import restrictions of its own.

incidents.title: Taiwan builds representative office in the Philippines
incidents.description: Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung confirmed that efforts to establish a Taiwanese representative office in the Philippines’ southern Cebu province are underway with the goal of establishing a “Taiwan-Philippines Economic Corridor.” The move drew sharp words of condemnation from China.

incidents.title: Trump dismisses AI safety fears as “hoax”
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has pushed back on growing calls from both Congress and AI tech leaders to regulate the industry, calling concerns about AI safety a “hoax.” Trump’s comment comes after Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark emphasized the need for a “kill switch” to become a mandated industry standard. Clark’s concerns come following multiple rogue AI incidents and the resignation of Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon over concerns about uncontrolled AI.

incidents.title: Sudanese army, allied forces claim recapture of 11 areas in North Kordofan
incidents.description: The Sudanese Armed Forces claimed to have recaptured 11 population centers along the Forty Days Road corridor toward Darfur. This follows previous drone attacks on Rapid Support Forces (RSF) reinforcement lines. The army claimed to have inflicted heavy RSF losses and pursued retreating fighters to the Darfur border.

incidents.title: Myanmar urged to negotiate repatriation efforts with Malaysia
incidents.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim formally invited Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing for a state visit to expedite the repatriation process of Malaysia’s 215,000 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar. Current plans remain at a standstill, with the initial partial repatriation of 5,000 Myanmar nationals – including an unspecified number of Rohingya – pending Naypyidaw’s approval.

incidents.title: Brazil’s president increases welfare program payments
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a decree increasing Bolsa Familia monthly welfare benefits by 15%, citing accumulated inflation since March 2023. Families will receive the new amount beginning Oct. 19 – less than a week before a potential Oct. 25 presidential run-off vote.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions hit Cuban military and nickel sector
incidents.description: U.S. officials sanctioned 11 Cuban enterprises and officials tied to the country’s military and nickel reserves on Sept. 17. The sanctions target three military officials, four military companies focused on research and development, and four state enterprises linked to Cuba’s nickel reserves.

incidents.title: Ukraine claims to have killed Russian general
incidents.description: Ukrainian forces reportedly killed Russian Maj. Gen. Anton Grunis with a drone strike in Russian-occupied Donetsk. Grunis was decorated by Russian President Vladimir Putin with the Hero of Russia award in August.

incidents.title: U.S. Congress advances new Russian sanctions bill
incidents.description: The U.S. Congress advanced legislation that would enact new sanctions and tariffs against Russia’s energy and defense sectors, as well as its “shadow fleet” exports. The bill, named after the late U.S. Sen. Lindsay Graham, still needs the signature of U.S. President Donald Trump to go into effect.

incidents.title: Sudanese government downs drones near Ethiopian border
incidents.description: The Sudanese army announced that it shot down multiple drones targeting hydroelectric dams near its border with Ethiopia on Sept. 15. The Upper Atbara and Setit dam complex in Gedaref state and the Khashm al-Girba dam in Kassala state were the reported targets of the drones, which were downed without casualties or infrastructural damage. The incident occurred days after Sudanese general Yasir al-Atta accused Ethiopia of attempting to occupy farmland in Sudanese border territories, denoting another cross-border escalation between the two nations.

incidents.title: Iranian, Chinese foreign ministers meet in Beijing
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, in Beijing on Sept. 17 to discuss the ongoing war between Iran and the United States. Following the meeting, Araghchi said that decisions were reached that will “decide the future strategic balance” of the Middle East.

incidents.title: North Korea pledges nuclear arsenal expansion
incidents.description: North Korea’s newly appointed Defense Minister Kim Kang Il told the Beijing Xiangshan Forum that North Korea’s nuclear status is “irreversible,” pledging to continue to expand the country’s arsenal while blaming the U.S.’s military alliances with Japan and South Korea for regional militarization.

incidents.title: U.S. removes Venezuela from drug control failure list
incidents.description: The United States removed Venezuela from the list of countries it deems to have failed to meet international drug-control commitments, ending a designation that has lasted since 2005. U.S. President Donald Trump cited increased counternarcotics cooperation with Venezuela’s interim government and said Colombia may soon be removed as well.

incidents.title: U.N. finds Venezuela’s repressive institutions remain intact
incidents.description: The U.N. Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela reported that security institutions, laws used to criminalize dissent, colectivos, and officials previously implicated in serious abuses largely remained in place, while documenting 64 new torture cases since Jan. 3. The report nevertheless recorded fewer long-term political detentions and enforced disappearances, hundreds of prisoner releases, and greater allowance for protests and civil society activity.

incidents.title: Brazil's central bank cuts interest rates
incidents.description: Copom, the rate-setting committee at Brazil’s central bank, unanimously decided to cut interest rates by 25 basis points, lowering the Selic rate to 13.75%. This is the fifth consecutive rate cut from Copom since March; the body is next scheduled to meet in November, days after Brazil’s October presidential election.

incidents.title: Canada invited to become “associate” EU member
incidents.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced that the EU will work with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to admit Canada as the bloc’s first “associate member.” The meaning of an associate membership was not made clear. U.S. President Trump said he would impose tariffs on the EU if he perceives the agreement to have “bad intention.”

incidents.title: U.S. sends humanitarian aid to Cuba
incidents.description: Five provinces in Cuba are expected to receive a shipment of humanitarian aid from the U.S. in the coming weeks, according to U.S. officials. The shipment is part of a broader $100 million aid program announced by the U.S. earlier this year as the country’s humanitarian crisis deepens.

incidents.title: Cuba introduces 10,000- and 20,000-peso bills
incidents.description: The Cuban Central Bank announced that banknotes worth 10,000 and 20,000 pesos would enter circulation on Sept. 17. The measure comes as inflation has made existing bills inadequate for covering necessities on the island.

incidents.title: U.S. Federal Reserve raises interest rates
incidents.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, lifting the benchmark federal funds rate a quarter point to 4%. The Federal Open Market Committee asserted this would bring the U.S. inflation rate back on track to its target of 2%, citing oil price increases as a major factor for the rising rate of inflation. This comes despite pressure from Trump to keep borrowing costs down ahead of midterm elections.

incidents.title: AI tech giants call for government oversight
incidents.description: The CEOs of the country’s leading AI firms – OpenAI’s Sam Altman, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, and xAI’s Elon Musk – have called for the need to slow frontier AI development and for more governmental oversight of the industry. This follows recent calls made by former Anthropic and OpenAI employees warning of the risks posed by unfettered AI development to humanity, reigniting the public debate over the technology, with polling showing a majority of Americans believing that AI poses a serious threat. OpenAI has also flagged recent “concerning” behaviors of AI agents and stated it was introducing new internal regulations. Trump has rejected the idea of any government regulation, citing the need to stay ahead of China in the AI race.

incidents.title: Trump falsely claims Russia, Ukraine agreed to ceasefire against energy infrastructure
incidents.description: After U.S. President Donald Trump falsely claimed Sept. 14 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to a ceasefire on each other's energy infrastructure, Ukraine and Russia both expressed openness to the idea. Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov spoke in favor of the proposal, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to agree if the U.S. could guarantee that Russia would abide by the agreement.

incidents.title: Saudi airstrikes against Houthis intensify following reported drone strike aimed at Mecca
incidents.description: Saudi Arabia reportedly conducted over 450 airstrikes against the Yemeni Houthi rebel group following a week of attacks against Saudi cities, including a drone aimed at the holy city of Mecca, an accusation that Houthi officials deny. Saudi officials have yet to comment on a Houthi claim to have shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet.

incidents.title: Indonesia negotiates market access with Bulgaria
incidents.description: Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Food Affairs Zulkifli Hassan and Bulgaria's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy, Investments, and Industry Alexander Poulev met in Jakarta to discuss how to increase Indonesian access to the Bulgarian and European markets. While no agreement was signed, progress was made in trade negotiations to increase Indonesian access, especially for its main exports of cocoa, palm oil, and halal food products.

incidents.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump’s challenge to mail-in ballots
incidents.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled against U.S. President Donald Trump’s plan to provide the United States Postal Service (USPS) with the authority to withhold certain mail-in ballots. The measure would have prohibited the USPS from delivering mail-in ballots to citizens not listed on a government-approved register.

incidents.title: DRC armed forces, Wazalendo reverse AFC/M23 gains
incidents.description: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Wazalendo forces retook the strategic Miko position and the villages of Remeka, Katuunda, Kareta, and surrounding areas in Masisi after day-long fighting with AFC/M23, while government forces also reoccupied Mindjendje in neighboring Walikale. AFC/M23 forces withdrew from several positions but fighting continued the following day, including around Kasake and toward Ngungu.

incidents.title: Brazil’s Supreme Court postpones decision on corruption investigation
incidents.description: In a livestreamed and contentious hearing of Brazil’s Supreme Court, Justice Flávio Dino formally asked for more time to review Justice Andre Mendonça’s corruption probe request into Justice Alexandre de Moraes. The decision on whether to open an investigation into de Moraes for alleged ties to Daniel Vorcaro’s multibillion-dollar bank fraud scheme will now be delayed for up to 90 days, possibly landing after Brazil’s October presidential election.

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia suspends oil exports from Yandu
incidents.description: Brent crude prices rose 1.3% on Sept. 15 to $107.05 a barrel as concerns over supply disruptions persisted after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure took the kingdom’s East-West Pipeline offline. Saudi Arabia announced that some September-loading crude cargoes to Europe would be canceled, while oil loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu were suspended. The disruption is expected to have significant supply implications: Roughly 4% of global oil supply had been rerouted through the pipeline due to the disruptions at Bab el-Mandab, volumes that could be lost from the market if the outage persists.

incidents.title: EU removes energy regulation provision
incidents.description: European Parliament lawmakers voted on Sept. 15 to remove a provision that would allow the bloc to temporarily suspend its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) if the policy significantly raises the price of imported goods. CBAM applies carbon charges to imports, including steel and fertilizers, based on emissions generated during production, intended to prevent foreign producers from gaining a cost advantage over European industries subject to EU carbon pricing. The decision puts Parliament at odds with EU member states that favor keeping the emergency safeguard to limit potential price shocks.

incidents.title: UAE state owned oil company buys Iraqi oil
incidents.description: The UAE’s national oil company, ADNOC, has been the top buyer of discounted Iraqi crude oil for the last two months, expanding its trading presence to address Iran war supply concerns. ADNOC agreed to buy 32 million barrels of Iraqi oil in August at $24.90 to $27 per barrel and 40 million barrels in September at $18 to $25 per barrel, according to Iraqi sources. In the face of Iran war supply restrictions, this strategic shift helps the UAE remain a flexible global energy supplier and maximize earnings.

incidents.title: Opposing Sudanese political groups agree to broaden consultations
incidents.description: Sudan's Islamist Popular Congress Party (PCP) and Abdel Wahid al-Nur's SLM-AW faction, two groups on opposite sides of the country’s civil war, agreed to broaden consultations toward ending the war during a meeting in Addis Ababa. The groups called for comprehensive negotiations over piecemeal ceasefires, agreed to expand the draft "Sudanese Declaration of Principles toward Building a New Homeland" into an inclusive civilian platform, and explicitly barred the dissolved National Congress Party from any process.

incidents.title: Myanmar seeks new U.N. representative
incidents.description: Myanmar's military regime called upon the United Nations to deny recertification of Myanmar’s permanent envoy to the U.N., Kyaw Moe Tun, ahead of the 81st session of the credential committee. Kyaw Moe Tun has called for an international response to the repression in Myanmar since the 2021 military coup, citing human rights violations, and the regime has accused him of “illegal activities.”

incidents.title: Militants threaten companies operating in Ethiopia’s Oromia state
incidents.description: Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), an Ethiopian militant group, demanded mining companies in the Oromia region conduct “thorough and transparent deliberations” with local communities to facilitate economic benefit from extraction operations. The group threatened further actions like the deadly Sept. 4 attack that drove U.K. company KEFI Gold and Copper to suspend activities at the Tulu Kapi gold project.

incidents.title: Cambodia calls for Myanmar’s re-entry into ASEAN
incidents.description: Following Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing’s visit to Phnom Penh, Cambodia called for the total reintegration of Myanmar into the Association for Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). During the visit, the nations signed agreements on investment into Myanmar’s Dawei Special Economic Zone and improvements to their bilateral trading and taxation frameworks.

incidents.title: Houthis expand control of Red Sea islands
incidents.description: The Houthis expanded their control of Yemeni territory by capturing the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands in the Red Sea. Over 125,000 civilians have been displaced by ongoing fighting.

incidents.title: Germany’s ruling Christian Democratic Union wins Lower Saxony state election
incidents.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union will remain in power in the northwestern state of Lower Saxony after securing 27.2% of the popular vote. Far-right party Alternative for Germany, which won a landslide victory in the Sept. 6 Saxony-Anhalt election, garnered only 15.9% of the vote.

incidents.title: Indonesia strengthens protections for women, children
incidents.description: Indonesia's Minister for Home Affairs Tito Karnavian, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Arifah Fauzi, and Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Yandri Susanto, signed a joint decree that establishes guidelines for regional and village governments to enhance protections for women and children in economic development initiatives.

incidents.title: Trump suggests Chinese automakers welcome in the U.S.
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has suggested that the U.S. would not impede Chinese automakers from building cars in the United States if they hire local workers. Lawmakers in Washington have warned against the suggestion, citing dangers in becoming too reliant on Chinese auto parts, which could pose risks to the domestic supply chain.

incidents.title: EPA removes regulations on greenhouse gas emissions for power plants
incidents.description: The Environmental Protection Agency has announced it will be removing Biden-era regulations on coal- and gas-fired power plants. The removal of these regulations now permits power plants to operate without the sequestration equipment used to reduce carbon emissions.

incidents.title: China introduces overseas travel regulations
incidents.description: China has introduced new controls on overseas travel for its citizens, specifically targeting civil servants, members of the Communist Party, and state-owned enterprise employees, in the latest move by President Xi Jinping to regulate state secrets and advanced technologies.

incidents.title: Iranian food prices rise sharply
incidents.description: Iran is experiencing a sharp nationwide increase in food prices, in particular bread and meat, as food producers are unofficially raising prices above the standard government set rate. In turn, many Iranians have been forced to purchase bread on credit.

incidents.title: Canadian Prime Minister launches investment summit in Toronto
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney hosted a two-day private-sector investment summit in an effort to attract billions of dollars to Canada. The summit opened with an announcement about data center expansion planned by Bell Canada. Asset managers such as the BlackRock CEO, Blackstone president, and others were in attendance.

incidents.title: Welsh, Scotish, and Northern Irish ministers call of independence
incidents.description: The first ministers of Wales, Northern Ireland, and Scotland jointly called on the British government to prepare for their independence during a Sept. 14 meeting in Cardiff, asserting that “Westminster’s time is coming to an end.” British Prime Minister Andy Burnham responded that he was more focused on the cost-of-living crisis than “constitutional debates.”

incidents.title: Myanmar regime launches large-scale offensive in Sittwe
incidents.description: Myanmar's military regime launched a 1,000-person offensive in Rakhine state to secure the Chinese-funded deep-sea port project at Sittwe beginning. Regime forces have since suffered hundreds of casualties amid exchange of heavy artillery fire, airstrikes, and attack drones, local civilian observers said.

incidents.title: Drones hit state capital in southern Sudan
incidents.description: Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group used explosive drones to strike several targets in Ed Damizin, the capital of Blue Nile state, the Sudan Tribune reported based on eyewitnesses. At least 11 attacks hit fuel stations, the airport, and the headquarters of the 4th Infantry Division.

incidents.title: Myanmar president makes state visit to Cambodia
incidents.description: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Cambodia for a two-day state visit. Alongside his Cabinet ministers, Min Aung Hlaing met with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manut and powerful former leader Hen Sun, a meeting that concluded with agreements on regional security.

incidents.title: Radio France staff protest appointment of far-right commentator
incidents.description: Employees of French public broadcaster Radio France began a strike in protest of Charles Sapin, the deputy editor-in-chief at far-right weekly Valeurs Actuelles, who has had a weekly segment at Radio France’s France Inter station since late August. Sapin’s segment was not aired Sept. 13 due to the protests. France Inter Director Celine Pigalle defended Sapin’s appointment as important for pluralism.

incidents.title: Ebola spreads to seventh DRC province as North Kivu transmission accelerates
incidents.description: The World Health Organization reported 7,258 confirmed Ebola cases and 3,510 deaths across 62 health zones in the Democratic Republic of the Congo after the outbreak reached Sub-Ubangi, the country’s seventh affected province. Transmission declined in parts of Ituri but continued to rise in North Kivu, where 555 cases were reported over the preceding 21 days.

incidents.title: Mexican police bust illicit crypto farm
incidents.description: Mexican police uncovered an illegal cryptocurrency mining operation hidden in Puebla state, the fourth of its kind discovered in the Sierra Norte region this year. Authorities suspect that the crypto building was used to launder illicit revenues and are investigating whether the farm used stolen electricity from a nearby hydroelectric dam.

incidents.title: Drone strike of Iraqi origin disables major Saudi oil pipeline
incidents.description: A drone strike that originated from Iraq struck and disabled a key Saudi oil pipeline, with Saudi Arabia attributing the attack to members of the Irani-backed Popular Mobilization Forces in Iraq.

incidents.title: Far-right victory in Saxony-Anhalt prompts nationwide protests in Germany
incidents.description: In response to the victory of Alternative for Germany in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, approximately 150,000 demonstrators across 20 German cities turned out in rallies organized by the campaign group Pruef, which advocates for banning the party.

incidents.title: Indonesia, Russian firm near aluminum deal
incidents.description: Indonesian regulators say they are in the final stage of talks with Rusal, a Russian aluminum manufacturer, to grant permits for the construction of a facility to convert bauxite, a critical mineral, into aluminum.

incidents.title: India hosts BRICS summit, secures joint declaration
incidents.description: India hosted the BRICS leaders’ summit in New Delhi on Sept. 12-13, where members adopted the New Delhi Declaration urging restraint in the Middle East, protection of global trade and energy flows, and action against cross-border terrorism. Both Iran and the United Arab Emirates backed the statement despite their differences over the Iran conflict.

incidents.title: India, China advance diplomatic relations
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged to strengthen business and transportation ties during talks in New Delhi on Sept. 12, Xi’s first visit to India in seven years. The leaders agreed to address trade imbalances and supply chain concerns while reaffirming their commitment to a negotiated boundary settlement.

incidents.title: Myanmar grounds flights amid explosive drone attack
incidents.description: Myanmar's second-largest airport, Tada-U, temporarily grounded flights due to explosive drone attacks staged by local resistance forces at a nearby military airbase. Independent news organizations reported several Russian-made fighter helicopters and jets were destroyed amid regime casualties, while state-owned media declared the attack as a “war crime” with no reported vehicle nor personnel losses. Tada-U airbase is where the regime launches its airstrike campaign in the north, prompting the rebel incursion.

incidents.title: France apologizes for comment questioning U.S. commitment to human rights
incidents.description: The French mission to the U.N. issued an apology for an earlier statement claiming the U.S. was “not anymore” a beacon of human rights after the U.S. voted against extending U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk’s term. The U.S. State Department had been holding up the approval of Aurélien Lechevallier as French ambassador to the U.S. since the beginning of the spat; an anonymous U.S. State Department official told AFP the apology was appreciated.

incidents.title: DRC creates task force to accelerate U.S. minerals partnership
incidents.description: The Congolese government established the DRC-USA Task Force to speed implementation of its strategic minerals partnership with the United States, Reuters reported. The body is intended to convert the agreement into concrete economic and security projects as Kinshasa seeks more Western investment in its copper and cobalt sectors and greater diversification away from Chinese financing.

incidents.title: Trump downplays evidence of China aid to Iran
incidents.description: U.S. officials stated they had evidence that China shared high-resolution imagery of a U.S. base in Jordan, leading to a lethal Iranian attack that killed three U.S. troops in July, marking the clearest evidence of Chinese aid to Iran so far. When asked about the report, Trump downplayed the evidence, stating that “China spies on us, [...] we spy on them too.”

incidents.title: Brazil’s presidential challenger under investigation for corruption
incidents.description: Documents ordered unsealed by Brazilian Supreme Court Chief Justice Edson Fachin revealed a corruption investigation into right-wing presidential challenger Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro relating to the ongoing Banco Master case. The investigation was authorized in July by Justice Andre Mendonça, who also led an investigation into fellow Justice Alexandre de Moraes for corruption relating to the same Banco Master case. Bolsonaro denies any wrongdoing.

incidents.title: U.S. diesel prices peach $6 per gallon
incidents.description: Average U.S. diesel prices have broken records, rising past $6 per gallon as the Iran war chokes global energy supply. As reported by the AAA motor club, the national average on Sept. 11 was $6.05, an increase from $5.85 the previous week and $3.70 during the same period last year. The increases are expected to lead to economic and social repercussions, such as an increase in transportation costs, additional charges for shipping, and pressure on consumers.

incidents.title: China helped Iran bypass sanctions
incidents.description: Senior Iranian sources revealed that China has been helping Iran bypass Western sanctions by selling credits for Chinese goods, including military gear, in exchange for continued access to discounted Iranian oil.

incidents.title: Top Taiwanese leaders attend democracy conference during surprise Italy visit
incidents.description: Taiwanese Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim and Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung made a surprise visit to Ventotene, Italy, to participate in the Conference for Freedom and Democracy. While they will not officially meet with any Italian ministerial leadership, Pina Picierno, vice president of the European Parliament, said the visit had been kept secret for fear of Chinese reprisals and complications. A Chinese spokesperson called the visit “despicable” and has lodged complaints with both the EU and Italy.

incidents.title: China increase U.S. soybean purchases
incidents.description: Traders have revealed that China recently stepped up purchases of soybeans from the U.S., buying 1 million metric tons of them this week alone, bringing the total purchases to nearly half of the promised 25 million tons China is expected to buy annually through 2028. This comes as preparations are underway for the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington set for September.

incidents.title: Canada finalizes aid package for Ukraine
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy finalized an agreement that will allocate roughly $250 million for Ukraine to acquire air defense interceptors. Carney said Canada will increase drone production in the coming years and send a third of that production to Ukraine.

incidents.title: Cholera outbreak hits Sudan's southern and western regions
incidents.description: The World Health Organization reported a cholera outbreak across Darfur and Kordofan and expressed concern that it could spread to El Obeid. Over 1,330 cases have been reported along with 114 deaths.

incidents.title: Ukraine conducts long-range strike into Siberia
incidents.description: Ukrainian forces struck a Russian energy facility in the Yamalo-Nenets region of northwest Siberia, 1,988 miles from the Russian/Ukrainian border, on Sept. 9, marking Ukraine's deepest strike into Russian territory of the war.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran exchange attacks; U.S. forces in Jordan targeted
incidents.description: The U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired on at least 10 ships, including commercial oil vessels and U.S. naval craft, as well as targeting U.S. forces in Jordan on Sept. 9.

incidents.title: Trump renews threats against Iranian underground nuclear facilities
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to bomb Pickaxe Mountain in Iran’s Isfahan province, reportedly the location of underground infrastructure related to Iranian uranium enrichment efforts in the Natanz nuclear facility.

incidents.title: Pakistan urges Iran to restrain Houthis
incidents.description: Pakistani officials urged Iran to restrain the Yemeni Houthi rebel group following escalatory attacks against four cities in Saudi Arabia. Pakistan, a recent signatory to a mutual defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, warned that it would respond to defend its treaty ally if Houthi attacks continued.

incidents.title: Taiwan launches election interference investigations
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau said it launched 54 probes into suspected instances of election interference ahead of November’s local elections. This was followed by a warning from Raymond Greene, director of the American Institute in Taiwan, who said Taiwan must guard itself from new instances of AI-enabled election manipulation.

incidents.title: Russia, North Korea complete bridge construction
incidents.description: Russia and North Korea celebrated the completion of a bridge linking both countries over the Tumen River after 16 months of construction. Both countries hailed it as a milestone in increased trade and tourism, with 300 vehicles able to cross it daily, though Ukrainian sources have warned the infrastructure would facilitate the delivery and exchange of military weapons and personnel.

incidents.title: DHS says it won’t act against Salvadoran immigrants under Temporary Protected Status
incidents.description: The Department of Homeland Security said it would take no action against some 200,000 Salvadoran immigrants whose Temporary Protected Status (TPS) allowing them to remain in the United States expired Sept. 9. DHS officials did not specify when the TPS for those immigrants would be reviewed.

incidents.title: Two former Iranian presidents call for an end to the war
incidents.description: Former Iranian presidents Hassan Rouhani and Mohammad Khatami have called for Iran to make peace with the U.S., citing Iranian public opinion. Sitting hardliners within the Iranian government and state media outlets rebuked their stance, rejecting the notion that public opinion should affect Iran’s conduct of the war.

incidents.title: Brazilian Supreme Court Justice orders reinstatement of suspended federal police chief
incidents.description: Justice Flávio Dino ordered the reinstatement of Brazilian federal police chief Andrei Rodrigues and intelligence chief Leandro Almada a day after their removal by Justice Andre Mendonça over allegations of illegal monitoring of justices, stating that the firings would impact ongoing investigations. Chief Justice Edson Fachin canceled the court’s scheduled session on Sept. 9 for final confirmation of Dino’s decision, which would take immediate effect until the 10-member court reconvenes.

incidents.title: Paramilitary drones strike Sudanese capital
incidents.description: Rapid Support Forces and allied Tasis Coalition drones struck Khartoum state, including the capital, in the first attack of its kind since January. The attack targeted oil refineries, power stations, and a fuel depot.

incidents.title: Raúl Castro makes public appearance
incidents.description: Raúl Castro, former leader of the Cuban regime and the Communist Party’s most powerful figure, made a public appearance at a military event on Sept. 5 alongside his grandson, Col. Raúl Guillermo Rodríguez Castro. His appearance shut down rumors circulating online of his death or critical illness.

incidents.title: Resistance disrupts resupply efforts by Myanmar regime
incidents.description: Myanmar’s oppositional Kachin Independence Army-led forces destroyed five boats in the ruling regime’s 30-boat flotilla destined for Kachin State with food, supplies, fuel, and personnel. This follows a previous resupply flotilla sent by the regime up the Irrawaddy River, of which only seven of the original 15 ships arrived in Bhamo township, a strategic stronghold in Kachin State. Resistance forces in Shegwu alleged the regime has used cluster bombs and indiscriminate airstrikes to provide cover for the flotilla.

incidents.title: Canada tariff $20 billion of U.S. goods
incidents.description: After Canadian tariffs on $20 billion of U.S. goods came into effect this week, Trump signed a number of executive orders banning imports of Canadian whey products, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, and motorbikes as of Sept. 29. The Trump administration also announced it would expand the scope of its tariffs on Canadian imports to include all-terrain vehicles and animal hides.

incidents.title: Mexican president, U.S. commerce secretary discuss USMCA
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick met virtually with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to discuss the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) ahead of a visit to Washington by Mexican Secretary of Economy Marcelo Ebrard for trade discussions.

incidents.title: Alternative for Germany (AfD) party wins statewide election
incidents.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the Saxony-Anhalt state election with 44% of the vote, defeating Chancellor Friederich Merz’s CDU but falling short of the required majority to form a government. Merz, who has called the AfD a “destructive force” with a migration policy that amounts to “ethnic cleansing of skilled workers,” postponed a planned call with Trump in the wake of the result, thought the exact cause remains unclear.

incidents.title: Indonesian wildfires top world carbon emissions
incidents.description: During the week of Sept. 1-7, Indonesia's wildfires released 19.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, making Indonesia the top source of fire emissions.

incidents.title: DRC launches $120 million reparations program for victims of Ugandan intervention
incidents.description: The Congolese government launched the first phase of collective reparations for communities affected by Uganda’s military activities in the DRC, allocating $120 million across Ituri, Tshopo, Haut-Uele, and Bas-Uele provinces. The money, part of the International Court of Justice’s $325 million reparations judgment, will be used to fund community projects in health, education, water access and economic recovery. Uganda has already transferred $260 million to the DRC.

incidents.title: Brent crude oil price exceeds $100
incidents.description: The benchmark Brent crude oil price breached $100 on Sept. 9, its highest level since late May, as markets reacted to the resumption of hostilities between the United States and Iran targeting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil shipments through the strait have dropped to under 2 million bpd at the same time that Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure are putting Red Sea export alternatives at greater risk.

incidents.title: Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats
incidents.description: Hungary expelled 10 Russian diplomats on Sept. 8. According to Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban, the envoys were engaged in unspecified “activities” that were "unacceptable for diplomats.”

incidents.title: Trump holds call with Putin on Ukraine peace efforts
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Sept. 8, offering significant trade deals for Russia in exchange for an end to the war in Ukraine, according to a statement from the Kremlin.

incidents.title: Kushner and Witkoff travel to Kyiv and Moscow for peace talks
incidents.description: White House adviser Jared Kushner and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the Ukrainian capital to discuss peace efforts on Sept. 8, before traveling to Moscow to speak with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

incidents.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group conducted combined drone and missile attacks against four cities in Saudi Arabia on Sept. 8, wounding at least 73 people. Saudi Arabia retaliated by bombing dozens of Houthi targets in Yemen. The attacks occurred during a simultaneous escalation of Houthi ground fighting against Yemeni government forces as the rebel group captured the coastal city of Mocha and the island of Perim in the Red Sea.

incidents.title: U.K., 11 other nations enact sanctions against Israeli settlers
incidents.description: The U.K., along with 11 other countries, enacted sanctions against exports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Following the move, Israel ordered the British consulate in East Jerusalem to be closed within 30 days and banned a dozen British officials from entering Israel. The other countries that announced sanctions alongside the U.K. were France, Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Ireland, Iceland, Poland, Spain, Portugal and Canada.

incidents.title: North Korea commissions second naval destroyer
incidents.description: North Korea commissioned its second naval destroyer, the Kang Kong, into service, joining the Choe Hyon which entered service in June. The destroyers are capable of launching both conventional and nuclear cruise missiles, and their entering service comes as leader Kim Jong Un is calling for a more reliable nuclear deterrent.

incidents.title: Canadian tariffs against U.S. come into effect
incidents.description: Canada enacted retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on over $20 billion of U.S. goods on Sept. 8. Among the increases were a doubling of the tariff on some resources critical for national security, such as steel, to 50%. Canada has announced a “dollar for dollar” increase to any new U.S. tariffs.

incidents.title: Chinese vehicle exports remain high; domestic sales fall
incidents.description: China’s vehicle exports remained strong in August, easing slightly from July, but remaining 77.5% higher than August of last year. Domestic sales have, however, remained low, with numbers falling for the 11th month in a row.

incidents.title: U.S. reportedly seeks greater access to Venezuelan minerals
incidents.description: The White House has sought greater U.S. access to Venezuela’s mineral resources as it expands its involvement in the country’s natural resource sectors beyond oil, according to anonymous sources quoted by Reuters. One source mentioned that the administration is also considering drafting an executive order on critical minerals as part of its approach to Venezuela’s mineral sector.

incidents.title: Iran deploys domestic security forces as fuel prices rise
incidents.description: Iran deployed Basij and other security forces to Tehran and other cities across the country as a planned fuel price increase went into effect Sept. 7. The price of gasoline doubled for individuals purchasing fuel outside of the authorized monthly ration.

incidents.title: India, China hold military talks
incidents.description: Indian and Chinese military commanders held two senior-level meetings along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh following recent tensions near Taksing, a remote border area where India and China have competing territorial claims. The meetings expand Sino-Indian engagement into the eastern sector and represent another step in efforts to stabilize the disputed border.

incidents.title: India, Sri Lanka deepen defense, maritime ties
incidents.description: Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh began a three-day visit to Sri Lanka on Sept. 8 with a senior defense and foreign affairs delegation focused on bilateral security and maritime cooperation. This supports India’s effort to deepen security ties in a neighboring state where New Delhi has competed with Chinese influence.

incidents.title: Canada, China hold defense meeting
incidents.description: Chinese and Canadian officials confirmed that the fifth defense coordination meeting between Canada and China took place on Sept. 4. The Canadian side reiterated its commitment to Canadian industries and said the meeting was held in support of deeper cooperation and communication at the functional level but didn’t include defense.

incidents.title: Trump calls for U.S. boycott of Bombardier
incidents.description: After U.S. President Donald Trump called for a boycott of Canadian jet manufacturer Bombardier, its Toronto-listed shares fell about 6% in trading. U.S. senators from Kansas, where the aerospace company has manufacturing facilities, pushed back against Trump’s call. However, the president announced that the United States market would be closed to Bombardier.

incidents.title: Sudan receives first visit from international mediation representatives
incidents.description: Representatives of the Quintet initiative, comprising the African Union, the United Nations, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development, the Arab League, and the European Union, arrived in Khartoum for a three-day visit to “pursue direct political consultations with Sudanese stakeholders on the ground” on a path to establish peace. This is the Quintet’s first visit to Sudan since the war began.

incidents.title: Indonesian military kills 4 West Papuan insurgents
incidents.description: Indonesia's military said it killed four insurgents while suffering no casualties in a skirmish with the separatists. This incident is part of the Damai Cartenz-2026 operation, a joint military-law enforcement offensive against separatist insurgents.

incidents.title: DRC deploys air power as AFC/M23 advances toward Walikale
incidents.description: The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo carried out airstrikes against AFC/M23 positions near the Masisi-Walikale boundary after the rebel coalition seized Humura and other localities and deployed additional fighters and ammunition along several routes leading toward Walikale. The renewed military activity, despite recent ceasefire-monitoring efforts, has triggered new civilian displacement as AFC/M23 presses toward strategically important routes in North Kivu.

incidents.title: Drone strikes in Tigray kill three civilians
incidents.description: Tigray regional television sources reported that a series of Ethiopian government drone strikes killed three civilians and injured four in the Hintalo District of southeastern Tigray on Sept. 8. District administrator Goytom Tesfay accused Addis Ababa of “deliberately targeting civilians.” The Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to the allegation.

incidents.title: Suspect in German electricity grid sabotage apprehended
incidents.description: A 48-year-old man suspected of carrying out several attacks on Germany’s electricity grid has been arrested. Authorities said the suspect was carrying explosives near a power plant in western Germany and noted that an explosive-rigged tent was discovered nearby

incidents.title: Indonesia restores flights to Java, Sumatra after volcanic eruption
incidents.description: Indonesian Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandi announced that eight airports in Java and Sumatra will resume operations after a two-day suspension amid the volcanic eruption of Anak Krakatau. The air traffic disruption affected civilian travel and foreign tourism.

incidents.title: Russia resumes bombardment of Kyiv after short pause
incidents.description: ussia resumed its bombardment of Kyiv on Sept. 9, following a temporary pause while U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential adviser Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, visited Kyiv on Sept. 8 to hold peace talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

incidents.title: Israeli bombardment kills at least 12 in southern Lebanon
incidents.description: Israeli bombardment in southern Lebanon killed at least 12 people on Sept. 7, further threatening the status of a U.S.-mediated peace agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

incidents.title: India approves major defense package
incidents.description: India’s Defense Acquisition Council approved roughly 1.1 trillion rupees ($13 billion) in planned military purchases, including helicopters, minelaying and mobile bridge systems, radar-jamming equipment, CBRN vehicles, and engines for naval ships. The government said about 98% of the purchases will come from Indian companies. The package is a part of India’s push to domestically manufacture more of its military equipment, especially as New Delhi tries to manage defense relationships with Russia, the United States, and other partners.

incidents.title: U.S.-Cuba negotiations stall
incidents.description: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez said his country has no active negotiations with the U.S. government and no plans for future talks. This comes as Cuba liberalizes its economy while U.S. officials intensify economic pressure against the island nation.

incidents.title: U.S. military reports fewer border drones following laser weapon use
incidents.description: U.S military officials said illicit drone activity in Texas’ Rio Grande Valley declined by roughly 75% after the implementation of a laser drone-targeting system. The military said it had intercepted 300 drones connected to cartels since the start of 2026, counting the 11 recently struck down by the laser system.

incidents.title: Houthis attack Saudi oil facility
incidents.description: The Yemeni Houthi rebel group struck Saudi Aramco’s oil facilities in Jizan on Sept. 7, the latest in a series of attacks targeting Saudi energy infrastructure along the Red Sea coast. The attack on the 400,000-barrel-per-day refinery came as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have elevated the facility’s strategic importance by pushing more Saudi energy exports toward Red Sea routes. Industry monitor Kpler recorded no refined product shipments from Jizan in August after earlier attacks disrupted refinery operations.

incidents.title: TPLF criticizes African Union mediator
incidents.description: The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) has questioned the impartiality of African Union Pretoria agreement representative Olusegun Obasanjo’s efforts to facilitate peace between the TPLF and Ethiopian federal government in the Tigray region. The TPLF stated that while it remains ready to pursue peace, the former Nigerian president’s approach “lacks neutrality [and] concrete proposals” and questioned his independence from Addis Ababa.

incidents.title: France to stop trade with Israeli settlements
incidents.description: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said in a statement on the X social media platform that France will “end trade” with Israeli settlements in the Palestinian Territories. Several other European nations announced similar decisions in individual and joint statements.

incidents.title: France announces more than $1.1 billion in emergency support for agriculture
incidents.description: France announced a new agricultural support package, worth more than $1.1 billion, that includes money for climate-related crop losses, tax breaks for hard-hit farms, and money to buy feed and seed.

incidents.title: Far right party victorious in Saxony-Anhalt election
incidents.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won 43.8% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, surpassing Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s center-right Christian Democratic Union (17.2%) and its junior coalition partner, the Social Democrats (9.3%), but falling short of an absolute majority. The AfD is considering a forming a coalition with the far-left populist Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht (BSW) to reach the majority needed to elect regional party leader Ulrich Siegmund as state minister-president.

incidents.title: China issues largest recapitalization in 20 years
incidents.description: China’s Ministry of Finance announced it would issue special bonds totaling $45 billion to eight financial institutions, including Industrial & Commercial Bank of China Ltd., Agricultural Bank of China Ltd., and People’s Insurance Company (Group) of China Ltd., as part of the country's largest recapitalization in 20 years. The bonds issuance is an attempt to bolster lending and comes as Chinese authorities have met several times over the past months to try and boost domestic consumption.

incidents.title: Myanmar, Vietnam prioritize joint defense initiatives
incidents.description: Vietnam and Myanmar formally elevated security to a pillar of their bilateral ties at the end of Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing’s state visit to Hanoi. Both parties expanded military training exercises, information sharing, military officer exchanges, and crime fighting initiatives, in addition to reaffirming the illegality of organizations from their countries using their territory to launch activities against the other.

incidents.title: Volcanic eruption disrupts flights in Indonesia
incidents.description: Ash from the eruption of Anak Krakatau in the western Indonesian archipelago disrupted air travel to Sumatra and Java. The eruption has affected transportation and tourism on Indonesia's most populous island.

incidents.title: Volcanic eruption disrupts flights in Indonesia
incidents.description: The eruption of Anak Krakatau, a volcano in the western part of the Indonesian archipelago, prompted the suspension of operations at eight of the country’s airports, including Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International, leaving about 170,000 travelers stranded. Ash plumes reaching up to 50,000 feet interrupted more than 1,500 flights.

incidents.title: Alberta separatist group releases Canadian secession transition plan
incidents.description: Alberta Transition Council released a 214-page report detailing the future of life in Alberta if the province secedes from Canada. Albertans will head to the polls on Oct. 19 to decide whether Alberta should remain or hold a second, binding referendum on the question. The plan addresses the legal and governmental framework of the Alberta-Canada relationship and acknowledges negotiations on debt, energy, and other assets.

incidents.title: Sudanese government accused of amassing chemical weapon arsenal
incidents.description: A Washington Post report alleges that the Sudanese government used chlorine intended for water purification to amass an arsenal of chemical weapons that have been tested in remote desert locations. The Post based the report on documents it acquired from unnamed third-country intelligence sources that include a list of targets where the toxic gas could be used. The Sudanese government denied the allegations and has reiterated an invitation for U.S. officials to inspect the facilities, invitations that have reportedly been declined. Separately, the United Nations Security Council is reportedly considering an expansion of an arms embargo to the entire country.

incidents.title: Diesel prices reach record high
incidents.description: Diesel prices averaged nearly $6 per gallon as the Iran war continues to limit U.S. energy imports, bringing the price increase to about 55% since the beginning of the war. Heating oil, derived from diesel production, has increased in price by nearly 70% over the same period.

incidents.title: Eni, PDVSA sign major Venezuelan oil development deal
incidents.description: Italian oil company Eni signed an agreement with Venezuela’s state-owned oil company PDVSA to develop the Junín 5 heavy oil project in the Orinoco Belt. Eni and PDVSA plan to invest about $1.5 billion annually in the project, with production expected to increase from roughly 12,000 barrels per day to 400,000 by 2030. Eni hopes to recover more than $2.3 billion owed by Venezuela through this project.

incidents.title: Brazil’s Supreme Court institutional crisis deepens
incidents.description: Justices Alexandre de Moraes and Andre Mendonça have sought major sanctions against each other in the fallout of a corruption scandal involving de Moraes and Banco Master CEO Daniel Vorcaro. Mendonça wants de Moraes to be suspended, while the court decides whether to investigate him, and de Moraes seeks a court investigation of Mendonça, who he accuses of using unauthorized proceedings to publicize federal police documents showing de Moraes’s and Vorcaro’s relationship.

incidents.title: Myanmar, Vietnam deepen ties over state visit
incidents.description: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing began his state visit to Vietnam with Viettel, one of Vietnam’s top telecom and defense companies. His first state visit to Vietnam since taking office is expected to yield cross-sector bilateral cooperation in automobiles, law enforcement, telecommunications, and defense.

incidents.title: Russia conducts weeklong bombardment of Kyiv
incidents.description: Russia conducted drone and missile strikes against several Ukrainian cities, with Sept. 3 marking its seventh consecutive day of bombardment in Kyiv.

incidents.title: Danish intelligence accuses Russia of upping sabotage efforts
incidents.description: The chief of Denmark’s counterintelligence agency PET said Russian intelligence operatives trying to recruit Danish citizens for a sabotage campaign against Danish defense industry targets amid a similar sabotage campaigns across Europe.

incidents.title: Clashes intensify between Yemeni government, Houthis
incidents.description: The al-Houthi rebel group killed at least 13 Yemeni government soldiers in clashes throughout the country on Sept. 3.

incidents.title: Chevron expands Venezuelan oil operations
incidents.description: Chevron announced plans to invest more than $7 billion in Venezuela over five years after receiving additional acreage in the Orinoco Belt. The company said it aimed to more than double its Venezuelan production to approximately 600,000 barrels per day.

incidents.title: U.S. strike in Iran kills at least 3 Iranian pilots
incidents.description: A U.S. strike in Iran this week killed three Iranian pilots, according to a statement from the Iranian government, which did not provide further details of the attack.

incidents.title: U.N. to aid Myanmar’s flood-stricken communities
incidents.description: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) authorized a free-to-use cargo transportation service as an emergency humanitarian response to extreme flooding in Myanmar’s Ayeyarwady region. A fleet of ships was made available to transport passengers, hygiene and sanitation products, and nutrition and food support alongside similar WFP humanitarian responses in the Sagaing region.

incidents.title: Economic reforms become law
incidents.description: Cuba’s national registry published 34 pages of new laws that convert parts of June’s 176 economic reform package into binding regulations. The new regulations aim to attract foreign investment, trade, and tourism as U.S. pressure and economic crisis on the island deepen.

incidents.title: Putin denies conscription plans
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Sept. 2 that rumors of a planned mass conscription were “complete nonsense.”

incidents.title: Russia formally accused in Leipzig airport attack
incidents.description: Germany, the EU, and NATO formally attributed an Aug. 4 drone attack on Germany’s Leipzig/Halle Airport to Russia.

incidents.title: Ukraine plans to shut down Russian airspace
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy vowed an escalated drone campaign that will “close” Russian airspace.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran exchange fire
incidents.description: The U.S. conducted multiple strikes inside Iran from Aug. 29 to Sept. 3, while Iran fired at infrastructure and U.S. bases in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Iraq.

incidents.title: Iran warns U.S. to prevent Israeli escalation in Lebanon
incidents.description: Iran warned the U.S. that it would retaliate if the Israel Defense Forces launched an offensive against the underground fortifications of southern Lebanon’s Ali al-Taher ridge, where Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps personnel are deployed with Hezbollah fighters. Hezbollah vowed to resume strikes into northern Israel if the ridge is attacked.

incidents.title: U.S. bombs wedding in Iran
incidents.description: A U.S. airstrike hit a wedding celebration occurring in a home in the southern Iranian city of Kuhestak on Sept. 1, killing at least five civilians and injuring dozens more.

incidents.title: Iran strike on oil tanker kills 2
incidents.description: Iranian forces struck a Saudi-owned vessel attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz on Sept. 2, killing at least two Filipino sailors.

incidents.title: Egyptian, Chinese presidents meet in Cairo
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in Cairo on Sept. 2 to discuss regional security concerns stemming from the U.S./Iran war and Chinese/Egyptian economic and security cooperation.

incidents.title: Australia, U.S. to deepen defense ties
incidents.description: Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles met with U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth in Washington, D.C., where they jointly stated that the U.S. would expand its force posture in Australia, increasing the number of U.S. troops in the country.

incidents.title: Chinese suppliers halt U.S. rare earth shipping
incidents.description: Some Chinese rare earth suppliers have not been shipping to the U.S. for fear of repercussions from China’s export controls authorities, according to a Reuters report based on anonymous sources. This comes despite repeated calls from the U.S. for Beijing to ensure smooth exports of rare earths in line with the bilateral agreement struck in South Korea last year. China has imposed sanctions on the U.S.-based Responsible Business Alliance in August, leading to these fears among Chinese suppliers.

incidents.title: Explosives found near German power substation
incidents.description: Following the discovery of several explosive devices near an electrical substation southeast of Berlin, German police are investigating the incident as a possible act of terrorism. Authorities suspect the incident was a deliberate attempt to target critical infrastructure.

incidents.title: EU delegation meets trade officials in Beijing
incidents.description: A delegation from the European Commission met with officials in Beijing for negotiations on trade revolving around China’s trade surplus. The EU has set an October deadline for imposing new measures to address the deficit, including new sanctions and investigations.

incidents.title: South Korean intelligence reports U.S./North Korea dialogue
incidents.description: South Korea’s National Intelligence Service has briefed the country’s parliament about increased “signs of dialogue” between the U.S. and North Korea, pointing to a renewed possibility of high-level talks between Pyongyang and Washington.

incidents.title: Sheinbaum’s approval rating at 69%
incidents.description: An El País poll showed Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum’s approval rating at 69%, 10% lower than in September 2025. Polling indicated that public safety is the biggest concern among Mexicans overall, and 27% of those who disapprove of Sheinbaum cite this as her administration’s main failure.

incidents.title: Brazil court orders regulation of AI use in political advertising
incidents.description: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) ruled in a 5-2 decision to explicitly define deepfakes in political advertising after a case involving opposition candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro generating a deepfake of his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. In a separate 4-3 decision, the TSE ruled against punishing Bolsonaro for AI use as the deepfake was not a political advertisement. It only appeared at a private event prior to his candidacy.

incidents.title: Electrical equipment stolen from Cuba’s seismological station
incidents.description: Unknown individuals stole solar panels, batteries, and other seismological equipment from Cuba’s Isle of Youth seismological station on Sept. 1, leaving it out of service. This comes amid a rise in electrical infrastructure theft across the country as the energy crisis deepens, driving more people to steal equipment for personal use or resale on the black market.

incidents.title: Mexico advocates for steel, auto tariff agreements with U.S.
incidents.description: Mexican Secretary of Economy Marcelo Ebrard met with U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick Sept. 2 during the G20 Innovation Ministerial to advocate for reduced steel and auto tariffs on Mexican imports.

incidents.title: DRC, Israel deepen strategic partnership
incidents.description: DRC President Felix Tshisekedi met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Isaac Herzog in Jerusalem, where they agreed to deepen cooperation in security and defense, agriculture and food security, water, health, infrastructure, energy, technology, training, and investment. The visit built on two memorandums signed July 27 establishing diplomatic training cooperation and regular political consultations, while Tshisekedi also explored Israeli investment in the Lobito Corridor. Israel had separately provided three tons of medical aid in July for the DRC’s response to the Ebola outbreak.

incidents.title: U.K. pledges £51 million for DRC Ebola response
incidents.description: The United Kingdom pledged $53.9 million to the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ebola response, bringing its total contribution to £78 million as the outbreak surpassed 6,000 confirmed cases. The package will support disease surveillance, infection prevention, frontline health workers, community engagement and other containment operations through partners, including the World Health Organization, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and humanitarian organizations.

incidents.title: EU nations willing to assist in Lebanon peace effort
incidents.description: European Commission Vice President Kaja Kallas said more than 10 EU nations are willing to train and advise the Lebanese armed forces as part of a U.S.-mediated peace deal in Lebanon. Kallas did not specify the countries in question.

incidents.title: Japan, Taiwan deepen tech cooperation
incidents.description: Japan and Taiwan have been deepening their cooperation in the AI and semiconductor sectors, with Japanese chipmaking suppliers Ajinomoto and Daikin Industries expanding their footprint in Taiwan.

incidents.title: France imposes levy on “ultra-fast fashion goods”
incidents.description: France imposed new taxes on high-volume, low-priced clothes. The taxes, which took effect Sept. 1, impact retailers such as Temu, AliExpress, and Shein and are based on the quantity of goods in the market and the ratio of the goods’ price to the cost to repair it. The duties will increase over time and will be capped at $22.60 per item in 2030.

incidents.title: Germany blames Russia for attempted drone attack
incidents.description: Germany formally accused Russia of perpetrating an Aug. 4 incident in which an explosive-laden drone targeted a cargo plane at the Leipzig/Halle Airport. Berlin ordered the closure of Moscow’s consulate general in Bonn and the Russian House cultural center in Berlin, summoned the Russian ambassador, and is working to extend EU sanctions and entry restrictions on Russian nationals entering the EU.

incidents.title: Berlin government data sold on black market
incidents.description: Berlin’s state government is refusing to pay a €2 million ($2.3 million) ransom to the hacker group Rhysida, which is selling data obtained during a recent cyberattack in a black-market auction. The group has been linked to numerous cyberattacks across Europe and the U.S.

incidents.title: Iran prepared to tap into foreign currency reserves
incidents.description: Iran is prepared to inject $2 billion worth of foreign currency reserves into its economy in an attempt to stabilize economic hardship, according to Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati of Iran’s Central Bank.

incidents.title: India signs Bishkek Declaration at SCO
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined other Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) leaders in signing the Bishkek Declaration, which condemns U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, opposes unilateral sanctions, and affirms Iran’s right to a peaceful nuclear program under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. India’s endorsement aligns New Delhi with the SCO position that challenges Western pressure on Tehran even as India seeks to manage its strategic relationship with the United States.

incidents.title: New foreign investment in Mexico slows
incidents.description: New foreign investment in Mexico dropped by 13% in the first half of 2026 compared to the first half of 2025 amid ongoing uncertainty around the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). Several business leaders told Reuters they are reevaluating their investments in Mexico, with some companies considering relocating operations to Asia.

incidents.title: Brazilian Supreme Court justice embroiled in corruption scandal
incidents.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes, vice president of Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court, has faced calls for removal after the release of text messages between Moraes and Banco Master CEO Daniel Vorcaro. Vorcaro allegedly sought legal advice from Moraes following a federal probe into Banco Master for fraud last November, disputing Moraes’s claim that the two did not have a close relationship.

incidents.title: Rumors of Raúl Castro’s declining health circulate
incidents.description: Unconfirmed claims are spreading on social media that 95-year-old Cuban leader Raúl Castro is severely ill or dead. Cuban officials have not commented on the rumors.

incidents.title: Nepal flood death toll surpasses 1,000
incidents.description: The death toll caused by the devasting Aug. 26 flash floods in Nepal has surpassed 1,000, and 4,000 people have been reported missing. A preliminary assessment by the U.N. Development Program indicates that the tragedy left at least ⁠2.2 million tons of debris.

incidents.title: U.S. tells Russia sanctions relief tied to end of war
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent told Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov that Russia would not receive further sanctions relief until it ends its war in Ukraine during a meeting between the two officials on the sidelines of a G20 Finance Minister Meeting in Ashville, North Carolina on Aug. 31.

incidents.title: U.S. envoys plan September visit to Ukraine
incidents.description: Zelenskyy held a phone call with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential adviser and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner on Aug. 31 to discuss their next trip to Kyiv, which is expected to take place sometime in September. Zelenskyy did not publicly confirm a date but described the call in constructive terms.

incidents.title: National dialogue recommends creation of Ethiopian “executive presidency”
incidents.description: At the conclusion of Ethiopia’s national dialogue on Aug. 22, delegates proposed constitutional reform to merge the offices of prime minister and president into a powerful executive presidency, appointed by a Parliament currently dominated by allies of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Critics of the government, which include opposition parties and regional militant groups, had already voiced opposition to the dialogue, calling it a regime legitimization tool.

incidents.title: Indonesia hosts U.S.-led military drills
incidents.description: The U.S.-led “Super Garuda Shield” annual exercises took place in Indonesia along with 15 other countries, focusing on securing shipping lanes and incorporating modern lessons learned with drone warfare. The drills come weeks after the U.S. reduced its participation in bilateral exercises with South Korea and Indonesia took part in military drills with China east of Taiwan.

incidents.title: China issues warning to Pacific Island Forum
incidents.description: Palau hosted this year’s annual Pacific Island Forum, which was highlighted by the absence of leaders from Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa, the Solomon Islands, and Kiribati, leading to concerns of Chinese interference. China further issued a warning of unspecified “consequences” following the participation of Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung. Concerns about China and Chinese missile tests featured heavily during the forum.

incidents.title: Fighting in DRC intensifies at South Kivu junction despite ceasefire process
incidents.description: Fighting between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, supported by pro-government Wazalendo armed groups and reportedly Burundian forces, and the Alliance Fleuve Congo/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) intensified around Point Zéro on the Fizi-Mwenga boundary. The fighting triggered significant displacement and humanitarian concerns days after a new ceasefire-verification mechanism began operating in the country’s east.

incidents.title: Barclays predicts Fed interest rate increases
incidents.description: U.S. brokerage firm Barclays said it expects the U.S. Federal Reserve to increase interest rates at least twice. The brokerage said Federal Reserve chairman's Kevin Warsh’s recent comments on interest rates were “notably hawkish.”

incidents.title: U.S. oil reserve falls to critical level
incidents.description: The U.S. Strategic Petroleum reserve is at approximately 290 million barrels, its lowest level since 1982, after years of releases to combat rising oil prices amid the Russia/Ukraine and Iran wars. That number is set to decrease further if the Trump administration releases 39 million more barrels as part of a March agreement with the International Energy Agency to help stabilize markets.

incidents.title: China pledges to accelerate investment opportunities
incidents.description: China agreed to increase the “investment potential” of industrial projects and urban renewal ventures during a rare meeting between the National Development and Reform Commission and multiple government bodies, including the ministers of industry and information technology, housing and urban-rural development, and transport. The Commission will accelerate the deployment of policy-based financing tools and local government special bonds for major construction projects. This comes as the economy has been struggling to meet its annual growth targets, leading to several recent meetings on increased government intervention.

incidents.title: Myanmar embassies restrict travel documents
incidents.description: Myanmar's military regime increased passport conversion, renewal, and processing restrictions for Myanmar nationals residing in Singapore, Thailand, Japan, Australia, and New Zealand. Citizens overseas are now subject to additional security screenings, two-month-long wait times for consular services, and nationals in Japan must return to Myanmar to renew their documents. Myanmar nationals in affected countries said they fear the restrictions will be used to monitor their activity abroad.

incidents.title: Mexican authorities seize cartel-bound firearms
incidents.description: Mexican Secretary of Public Security Omar García Harfuch said Mexican authorities seized 210 firearms in Nuevo León state bound for a cartel group after passing border inspections in both the U.S. and Mexico.

incidents.title: Indonesia’s West Papua faces famine risk after surprise frost
incidents.description: West Papua experienced an unexpected frost that caused severe crop failures, disrupting food supplies on the island’s central highlands, threatening the 15,000 people in the affected region with famine.

incidents.title: Hague orders India to uphold water treaty
incidents.description: The Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled that India must continue complying with the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, rejecting New Delhi’s argument that its suspension of the agreement removed the court’s authority over the dispute. India has refused to recognize the arbitration proceedings, intensifying tensions with Pakistan over control of shared water systems and adding a water security dimension to already strained bilateral relations.

incidents.title: U.S., Brazilian officials discuss tariffs
incidents.description: Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, Trade Minister Márcio Elias Rosa and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer agreed on Aug. 31 to resume tariff talks. The officials agreed to meet again to review progress on negotiations after a series of technical meetings scheduled for the coming weeks.

incidents.title: Members of Canada’s Liberal Party wins in byelections
incidents.description: Members of Canada’s ruling Liberal Party won three Aug. 31 parliamentary byelections by a wide margin, with each candidate winning over 50% of the vote. These wins indicate the strength of the Liberal Party in light of the U.S.-Canada trade war, especially in Quebec, which is home to industries such as aluminum, forestry, and dairy.

incidents.title: Saudi tankers hit near Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Two Saudi crude supertankers were hit with unknown projectiles while exiting the Strait of Hormuz on Aug.31, killing two people, in an attack that Saudi Arabia attributed to Iran. The tanker, which is owned by Bahri, Saudi Arabia’s national shipping company, was carrying about 2 million barrels of Saudi crude oil loaded at Aramco’s Juaymah terminal. The incident comes as Saudi crude exports fell to around 3 million barrels per day in August, their lowest level in at least nine years.

incidents.title: Assault leaves French LGBTQ+ activist hospitalized
incidents.description: In what Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire and LGBTQ+ rights organization STOP Homophobie have characterized as a homophobic attack, French police officer and activist Pierre Picavet was assaulted after leaving a bar in the Marais district of Paris. French police have the suspected attacker in custody.

incidents.title: Trump administration closes departments studying cyclospora
incidents.description: Two of the three research departments under the Department of Agricultural responsible for studying the spread of the parasite cyclospora have been closed by the Trump administration following Congress’ refusal to provide funding. The remaining department still operating faces a lack of staff.

incidents.title: India, Uzbekistan deepen ties
incidents.description: India and Uzbekistan elevated relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s state visit. The two sides set a $5 billion bilateral trade target for 2030, expanding cooperation on defense, nuclear energy, and critical minerals. They also advanced plans for a long-term arrangement to supply Uzbek uranium to India and discussed joint exploration and processing of critical minerals.

incidents.title: U.S. Executive order renames Lake Ontario
