incidents.description: United States President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario the Lake of America, effective immediately. Canadians, specifically Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford, have denounced the renaming.

incidents.title: General Motors approves investment agreement in Canada
incidents.description: Canadian union Unifor announced that General Motors has promised to invest over $720 million in Canadian Plants. The investments will support production for next-generation trucks, V8 engines, and wage increases. This agreement follows 25% U.S. tariffs on vehicles and a threat from U.S. President Donald Trump to raise that to 50%.

incidents.title: Germany’s Uniper, Norway’s Equinor sign 15-year natural gas import deal
incidents.description: Germany’s gas company Uniper has signed a 15-year agreement with Norway’s Equinor to import more than 30 terawatt-hours of natural gas per year from 2027 through 2041. The agreement follows Uniper’s July 29 long-term liquefied natural gas supply deal with Canada and supports the company’s efforts to diversify its gas imports amid energy shortages and high energy prices linked to the Iran war.

incidents.title: Ethiopia massing forces at Sudanese border
incidents.description: An analysis of satellite imagery by the Yale School of Public Health’s Humanitarian Research Lab (HRL) has identified a buildup of over 100 Ethiopian National Defence Force (ENDF) vehicles at a base in Asosa, near the country’s border with Sudan. The lab concluded that the movement of this equipment could signal an imminent ENDF-supported Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary group attack on the Sudanese government stronghold of Ad-Damazin in Blue Nile State. An attack in this region of Sudan would draw Sudanese army forces away from the main axis of conflict around El-Obeid.

incidents.title: Sudanese Otoro tribal chief accuses rebels of violating informal ceasefire
incidents.description: Otoro Paramount Chief Koko Al-Daqir Damjala accused the Sudan People's Liberation Movement – North (SPLM-N) of violating an informal ceasefire brokered by the Rapid Support Forces for the SPLM-N and Otoro tribal fighters. The fighters are accused of killing 28 people, looting stores and farms, and destroying a gas station. Hundreds protested the hostilities in the South Kordofan village of Kajoor Al-Shaabiya.

incidents.title: China removes two senior military officers
incidents.description: China fired two senior military officers, Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, from the Central Military Commission as part of a wider anti-corruption campaign, leaving just two active members on the seven-member commission. Zhang and Liu were also removed from their seats on the National Peoples’ Congress.

incidents.title: U.S., Venezuela reach major oil development agreement
incidents.description: The United States and Venezuela agreed to develop 17 Venezuelan oil fields containing approximately 65 billion barrels of proven reserves, with the United States receiving majority control of the venture’s output. Venezuela said the agreement would could attract more than $100 billion in investment and generate more than $209 billion in tax revenue for the state. The deal gives the United States 55% effective output from the new company, including an ownership stake and rights to purchase oil at cost, alongside 100-year development rights for the fields.

incidents.title: Russia to build nuclear plant in Myanmar
incidents.description: Russian nuclear company Rosatom is set to begin construction on Myanmar’s first nuclear power plant in 2027. The plant, which will be built near Nay Pyi Taw, will have a capacity of 110 megawatts upon completion.

incidents.title: Brazilian opposition presidential candidate promises to respect general election results
incidents.description: Brazil’s right-wing opposition presidential candidate, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, pledged to accept October’s general election results in an interview with TV Globo's Jornal Nacional. Bolsonaro has previously cast doubt on Brazil’s election integrity and electronic voting systems.

incidents.title: EU states push for use of frozen Russian assets to aid Ukraine
incidents.description: A group of EU states formed by Poland, Spain, Sweden, and the Netherlands is pushing for Brussels to revive a plan to use frozen Russian assets to aid Ukraine.

incidents.title: Taiwan lawmakers OK drone budget
incidents.description: A government drone-funding scheme was struck down in favor of a measure by the opposition in the Legislative Yuan, months after a proposed special defense budget was significantly reduced by the opposition Kuomintang. The government-proposed legislation would have designated the Ministry of National Defense as the main overseer of the project over the next five years, while the Kuomintang budget, which was approved, places the scheme within the Ministry of Finance’s purview. The money will be disbursed in yearly allocations over the next six years.

incidents.title: China, U.S. prepare for September summit
incidents.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue to discuss details on the upcoming summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in September. Wang stressed the need for the U.S. to “remove interference” and to keep the relationship stable.

incidents.title: Vietnam's National Assembly approves a joint nuclear plant with Russia
incidents.description: Vietnam’s National Assembly approved an agreement with Russia to jointly develop the Ninh Thuan 1 nuclear power plant, advancing the country’s first commercial nuclear project after Hanoi revived its nuclear energy program in 2024. The planned facility would use two Russian-designed VVER-1200 reactors with about 2,400 megawatts of combined capacity. Lawmakers also separated the wider Ninh Thuan program into independent projects for Ninh Thuan 1, Ninh Thuan 2, and approved a plan to resettle residents displaced by the development, removing legal obstacles that had complicated preparations for construction.

incidents.title: Thousands protest government corruption
incidents.description: Protesters gathered outside the Parliament building to demand a strengthening of anti-corruption penalties. Some protesters engaged in violence, setting a police post and two motorcycles on fire, blocking roads, and throwing rocks at police officers. Jakarta police arrested 322 people and are “gathering facts” related to an unspecified fatality.

incidents.title: CIA director visits Moscow amid Russian threat to Baltic states
incidents.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced trip to Moscow on Aug. 25 to warn senior Russian officials against escalatory action toward NATO allies, particularly Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Wildberries factory
incidents.description: A Ukrainian drone strike against a warehouse belonging to the Russian retail giant Wildberries on Aug. 26.

incidents.title: U.K. readies possible sanctions against Israeli settlers and senior officials
incidents.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is preparing to announce a ban on goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, as well as sanctions against senior Israeli officials, according to reporting from multiple British news outlets.

incidents.title: Iran and Oman reach deal over Strait of Hormuz passage
incidents.description: On Aug. 26, Iran and Oman announced a bilateral agreement to facilitate maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz. While the U.S. has yet to formally comment, its current force posture in the region prevents a deal from going into effect.

incidents.title: Board of Peace representative rebukes Israeli strikes in Gaza
incidents.description: Nickolay Mladenov, who was appointed by U.S. President Donald Trump as the high representative for Gaza on the Board of Peace, said Israel's repeated strikes in Gaza are jeopardizing the ongoing peace efforts while addressing the U.N. Security Council on Aug. 26. Mladenov also said Israel’s ongoing attacks “preserve” the status quo that led to the October 7 attacks by Hamas.

incidents.title: DOJ claims disruption of China-backed infiltration cyberattack
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Justice stated it had disrupted a hacking operation by Chinese network company Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company, whose past clients have included China’s Ministry of State Security. The Justice Department said the infiltration operation targeted the U.S. Senate, NASA, and other entities including the Department of Energy and the Federal Reserve. According to the department, these network attacks have been a regular occurrence since at least 2018.

incidents.title: China investigates Rocket Force corruption
incidents.description: The Chinese government has asked the public to report instances of corruption within the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force, following similar investigations made within China’s air force and cyberspace force in the past two years.

incidents.title: Venezuela enacts earthquake reconstruction law
incidents.description: Interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez signed legislation establishing requirements for rebuilding homes following the June earthquakes, including construction schedules and penalties for developers that fail to meet contractual or safety requirements. The government said 11,000 homes remained classified as high risk and that 3,000 new homes were under construction in the hardest-hit area.

incidents.title: Iran’s strategic fuel reserves run low
incidents.description: Iran’s strategic fuel reserves have reached “critically low” levels after weeks of drawdowns and a deficit created by the U.S. naval blockade against Iranian ports. The fuel shortage is expected to further inflame political division between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Iran’s security apparatus.

incidents.title: Iran and Oman reach deal over Strait of Hormuz passage
incidents.description: On Aug. 26, Iran and Oman reached a bilateral agreement to facilitate maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz. While the U.S. has yet to formally comment, its current force posture in the region would prevent the deal from going into effect.

incidents.title: DRC suspends universities in rebel-controlled cities
incidents.description: The DRC’s Ministry of Higher Education suspended academic activities for the 2026-2027 year at public universities in AFC/M23-controlled Goma and Bukavu after rejecting appointments made under rebel authority. Kinshasa also suspended the salaries of 48 higher-education employees accused of joining or accepting positions under AFC/M23, deepening the split between the parallel governance in eastern DRC.

incidents.title: Inflation rates in Ethiopia continue to rise
incidents.description: Ethiopia’s annual inflation rate rose to 15.3% in July 2026, an increase from 13.9% in June and 13.7% from August 2025. Government data shows that annual inflation had fallen to 9.7% in December 2025 before beginning to rise again, with larger price increases among non-food products. Ethiopia saw the largest increase among major economies on the African continent during Q1 and Q2 2026.

incidents.title: US announces 50% tariff on Canadian products
incidents.description: After trade pact negotiations fell apart, the United States announced a 50% tariff on a number of Canadian products, including dairy and liquor, and a 25% tariff on auto parts. In response, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled a list of 900 U.S. goods with an estimated worth of $27.6 billion that would be subject to reciprocal tariffs of 25% to 50%. The Canadian tariffs are expected to go into effect Sept. 8. Trump threatened further tariffs if a deal is not reached by January.

incidents.title: Iran and Oman reach deal on Strait of Hormuz transit
incidents.description: Iran said it reached an understanding with Oman on the concepts of a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz following weeks of negotiations over navigation in the waterway. The proposed route would be about 7 miles wide, with vessels entering and, in part, exiting through Iranian waters. Iranian officials said the arrangement would not amount to a full reopening of the strait, and key operational details, including when the corridor would begin functioning and which vessels would be permitted to use it, remain unclear.

incidents.title: Flash flood hits Nepal
incidents.description: Flash flooding across Nepal and the neighboring Tibetan region of China killed at least 160 people on Aug. 26 and left hundreds more missing, including large numbers of foreign tourists. In Nepal, the floods swept away at least 19 bridges and nearly 40 kilometers of roads and damaged villages and hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems. Climate researchers said an ice-and-rock avalanche from a glacier had likely blocked a tributary before releasing a sudden flood downstream; the same tributary has now experienced two major floods within 14 months.

incidents.title: U.K. to lobby Trump to bolster Ukraine’s air defense
incidents.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham intends to lobby U.S. President Donald Trump to provide Ukraine with air defense systems when he travels to New York for the U.N. General Assembly meeting in September.

incidents.title: Ukraine prepares new peace proposal
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine has drafted a one-page peace proposal based on U.S. and European input, intending for U.S. officials to present the proposal to Russia.

incidents.title: U.S. enacts new economic campaign against Iran
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent rolled out a series of sanctions against dozens of entities and threatened harsh economic consequences against any country engaging in trade with Iran. He also cautioned that any nation participating in money-laundering schemes with Iran would be cut out of the U.S. dollar system. Bessent said the U.S. is aiming to achieve the “economic asphyxiation" of Iran. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian retorted that the economic campaign “would not achieve anything.”

incidents.title: Rubio hints at temporary pause on strikes in Iran
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the U.S. is not planning additional airstrikes in Iran “for the time being” as the U.S. moves to escalate its hybrid campaign against Iran’s economy.

incidents.title: Trump sends Saudi nuclear energy deal to Congress
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump sent a proposed U.S./Saudi Arabia nuclear energy deal to the U.S. Congress for ratification within the next 90 days. Trump said Saudi Arabia must formally recognize Israel before the deal could take effect.

incidents.title: Syrian Democratic Forces agrees to dissolution
incidents.description: The Syrian Democratic Forces reached an agreement with the Syrian central government to dissolve the Kurdish-led organization as a separate entity and integrate, at least in part, into the Syrian army.

incidents.title: U.S., South Korea hold high-level call following scaled-down drills
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun held a call following last week’s scaling down of joint military drills. The conversation did not contain any joint commitment to the denuclearization of North Korea, a subject that had long been a key joint policy.

incidents.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects legal challenges to mail-in ballot executive order
incidents.description: The Supreme Court has ruled state governments do not have the legal standing to challenge U.S. President Donald Trump’s executive order to create a federal list of eligible voters. The order seeks to give the federal government the ability to disqualify voters it deems ineligible. The policy is expected to affect the acceptance of mail-in ballots, which the administration claims without evidence are often invalid.

incidents.title: Trump administration halts all immigrant visa applications
incidents.description: All immigrant visas have been paused as the White House reviews the application process. The policy shift comes alongside the announcement that visas for asylum seekers who enter the country for tourism or business purposes may be revoked.

incidents.title: China moves to expand anticorruption laws
incidents.description: During China’s held its 24th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress, a first reading of a proposed Anti-Cross-Border Corruption Law, aimed at expanding the Chinese Communist Party’s ability to combat corruption outside of its borders, was made.

incidents.title: U.S. eases Venezuela telecom sanctions while excluding Chinese firms
incidents.description: The U.S. Treasury Department issued two general licenses easing sanctions restrictions on Venezuela’s telecommunications sector, including transactions involving state-owned CANTV and mobile operator Movilnet. The licenses explicitly exclude transactions involving entities from China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba, as well as companies those countries own, control, or operate joint ventures with.

incidents.title: Iranian parliament moves to restrict access to foreign media outlets
incidents.description: The Iranian parliament advanced legislation that allows Iran’s Supreme National Security Council to categorize foreign media outlets as “foreign agents” and “hostile” to Iranian security. If approved, the legislation would provide a mechanism for Iranian security forces to exercise tighter control on the interactions of the Iranian public with international media.

incidents.title: India, China advance border talks
incidents.description: Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi agreed to continue negotiations toward a settlement of the countries’ disputed Himalayan boundary and maintain peace along the border. The talks mark improvement in bilateral relations despite recent military friction along the Line of Actual Control.

incidents.title: U.S. plans major increase in H-1B visa fees
incidents.description: The Trump administration proposed raising the fee for each new H-1B visa application to more than $100,000. Because Indian nationals and India-linked technology firms are major users of the program, the proposal could become another source of friction in U.S.-India economic relations and negatively affect a longstanding channel of skilled labor integration between the two countries.

incidents.title: Amnesty International Brazil finds social media election disinformation vulnerabilities
incidents.description: Amnesty International published the results of an experiment exposing Meta’s failures to moderate election disinformation through its Facebook Advertisements platform ahead of Brazil’s October presidential election. The experiment found that the platform accepted eight of 15 mock advertisements containing election disinformation, while moderators flagged the remaining seven for reasons unrelated to their content.

incidents.title: Canada announces domestic tariff relief support
incidents.description: The Canadian federal government announced a relief package of $7.5 billion to support businesses and workers that are impacted by the 50% tariffs that the United States imposed on Canada. This money will go toward expanding employment insurance benefits, raising the cap on non-payable loans to $3 million, and providing a $500 million liquidity stream for small- to medium-sized businesses that face cash-flow shortages.

incidents.title: Cuban president warns private sector against “illegal activities”
incidents.description: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned representatives of Cuba’s private sector against engaging in tax evasion, price gouging, and other profiteering practices that violate Cuban law in a meeting intended to foster greater dialogue between state and nonstate companies. Representatives from the food, energy, transportation, and agricultural sectors participated along with multiple high-ranking Communist Party officials

incidents.title: Sudan’s paramilitary force orders closure of markets and shutdown of satellite communication
incidents.description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) ordered the indefinite closure of all public markets and the shutdown of Starlink communications in Al-Nahud, West Kordofan. This coincides with the arrival of RSF reinforcements and continues the pattern of coercive control of towns under its control.

incidents.title: Sudan rebel and tribal groups clash, killing 27
incidents.description: The Sudan People’s Liberation Movement – North carried out ethnically motivated attacks that killed 27 people, including four children, in Otoro villages, according to the Sudan Doctors Network. This attack sparked another large wave of displacement toward Abu Hitan and Kadugli.

incidents.title: Railway cables severed near Stuttgart, Germany
incidents.description: Several railway cables were cut near the southwestern German city of Stuttgart, disrupting rail services and causing data failures for about 3 hours on Aug. 24. A specialist counterterrorism and state security unit is investigating the incident on suspicion of sabotage.

incidents.title: Vietnam's foreign minister to visit Myanmar
incidents.description: Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung made his first official state visit to Myanmar since the 2021 military coup, a month after Vietnam and Myanmar exchanged new ambassadors. He is expected to chair various commissions with his Myanmar counterpart and continue Vietnam’s posture of including Myanmar’s military-led government in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

incidents.title: Climate change on agenda for German government retreat
incidents.description: Amid this summer’s heatwaves, wildfires, and low river levels, German Chanceller Friedrich Merz’s CDU/CSU-led coalition is facing pressure from the Green Party, environmental activists, and the far-right Alternative for Germany over its climate policies. At the start of his Cabinet’s two-day retreat, Merz told reporters that Germany needs to “draw the long-term lessons from extreme situations such as this summer of heat” and must further curb climate change while adapting to the consequences.

incidents.title: Mexican governor leaves office a second time
incidents.description: Less than two days after reoccupying his position, Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya requested a second leave of absence after Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum indirectly criticized his return amid an ongoing U.S. investigation into Rocha’s alleged involvement in drug trafficking. On Aug. 25, Graciela Domínguez Nava, who was sworn in as the interim governor, said she will work with Sheinbaum to promote justice and peace in the state.

incidents.title: China, Indonesia commit to establishing code of conduct for South China Sea
incidents.description: During a visit by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Defense Minister Dong Jun, China and Indonesia agreed to continue work to establish a code of conduct between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to govern maritime issues in the South China Sea. They also discussed ways to enhance security and economic cooperation.

incidents.title: U.K. to boost Ukrainian domestic missile production
incidents.description: During a visit to Kyiv on Aug. 24, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged U.K. assistance for Ukraine in its domestic development of long-range missiles by sharing classified technical data for British weapons systems.

incidents.title: Israeli attacks in Gaza kill at least four Palestinians
incidents.description: Israeli attacks in Gaza on Aug. 24 killed at least four Palestinians, including two children.

incidents.title: U.S. lifts Syria’s terrorism sponsor designation
incidents.description: The U.S. lifted Syria’s “state sponsor of terrorism” designation on Aug. 24. The move lifts a significant hurdle to U.S. investment in Syria as Syrian President Ahmed al-Shaara seeks to stabilize and rebuild the country.

incidents.title: U.S. to impose overcapacity tariffs on China
incidents.description: Unnamed officials have said the Trump administration is preparing to impose 7.5% tariffs on Chinese imports over allegations of overcapacity. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer had previously touted the imposition, which he said would take longer to come into effect than the recently imposed forced labor tariffs.

incidents.title: Xi set to visit India for first time in seven years
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to visit India for the first time in seven years on Sept. 12 and 13 for the annual BRICS summit. While the visit has not yet been officially confirmed, both countries have worked to ease tensions following a deadly border clash in 2020.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions, UAE restrictions disrupt India-Iran trade
incidents.description: Indian exporters began seeking alternative trade routes to Iran after the United Arab Emirates suspended trade and financial transactions with Tehran, and Washington imposed additional sanctions. The measures threaten Indian rice, tea, and pharmaceutical exports, all of which have been transported through ports in Dubai in recent years.

incidents.title: Ceasefire monitors deploy to DRC under Qatar-led peace deal
incidents.description: Reuters reported the deployment of a joint ceasefire verification mission to Minembwe, South Kivu, to monitor violations between Congolese forces and the Rwandan-backed Alliance Fleuve Congo/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23). The deployment is the first operation of the monitoring mechanism established under the Qatar-mediated Doha peace process, moving the agreement from written commitment toward implementation.

incidents.title: Sudan downs drone originating from Ethiopian territory
incidents.description: Sudan’s Defense Ministry announced it had shot down a “hostile” drone over the Kurmuk area of Blue Nile State. Sudanese authorities alleged that the drone had been launched from Ethiopia but did not identify its operator, and there was no immediate response by the Ethiopian government. The airspace intrusion comes amid clashes between the Sudanese government and the United Arab Emirates-backed Rapid Support Forces in the Blue Nile Region.

incidents.title: Tornado causes widespread damage in French village
incidents.description: A tornado centered on the village of Pomas in southwestern France injured dozens, damaged hundreds of homes and left about 2,800 homes without electricity.

incidents.title: Poll shows Marine Le Pen leading presidential race
incidents.description: A Harris-Interactive-Toluna poll shows far-right National Rally candidate Marine Le Pen leading two leftist candidates ahead of presidential elections set for April 18, 2027. Far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon polls closer to Le Pen than center-left former prime minister Edouard Philippe.

incidents.title: Myanmar courts Belarusian investment, trade
incidents.description: After his state visit to Moscow, Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing traveled to Minsk, where he and Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko ratified nine cross-sector agreements, including credit frameworks and Belarusian shoe manufacturing in Myanmar. In addition to upgrading Myanmar’s Minsk consulate to an embassy, talks also touched on Myanmar’s potential integration into the Eurasian Economic Union to grow mutual access to markets.

incidents.title: Mexican authorities raid criminal network
incidents.description: Mexican federal authorities collaborated to conduct a simultaneous raid on 36 properties allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel in Hidalgo, Michoacán, and Jalisco. Mexico’s security ministry said authorities arrested 20 individuals during the operation and confiscated firearms, drugs, vehicles, and exotic animals.

incidents.title: Indonesia imposes beef price controls, plans subsidies
incidents.description: Indonesian Chief Food Minister Zulkifli Hasan announced that beef prices will be fixed at 142,000 rupiahs ($8) per kilogram, and that if prices rise more than 5%, the state and regional governments will subsidize prices. The price to import beef is rising due to Indonesia’s declining exchange rate.

incidents.title: Taiwan indictes 9 people for spying
incidents.description: Taiwanese prosecutors indicted nine people, including Nvidia and Super Micro employees, over an alleged scheme to send advanced AI servers to China in violation of U.S. technology restrictions. Prosecutors said documents for 130 servers falsely identified Taiwan as their final destination, while 74 were ultimately delivered to Chinese customers either directly or through intermediaries in Indonesia, Japan, and Hong Kong. Taiwanese customs stopped the delivery of the remaining 56 servers after detecting irregularities in the planned shipments. The indictments come as Taiwan has tightened controls intended to prevent advanced semiconductor technology from reaching China.

incidents.title: Sudanese civil society rejects proposal for talks
incidents.description: Anti-war coalitions and civil society groups rejected Sudanese Armed Forces Leader Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan's call for inter-Sudanese dialogue. They criticized the unilateral nature of the proposal and its focus on cementing the military in power, which they see as having no part in the peace process.

incidents.title: DRC, M23 agree to continue peace negotiations
incidents.description: Representatives of the DRC government met with counterparts from the M23 rebel group in Switzerland, where after five days of talks, they agreed to continue negotiations aimed at a ”comprehensive peace and conflict resolution” and to establish ceasefire monitoring systems. The talks and roadmap are in line with a 2025 U.S.-brokered framework.

incidents.title: Tigray calls for diplomatic efforts to halt escalation in northern Ethiopia
incidents.description: The Tigray Communication Affairs Bureau (TCAB) requested international diplomatic support to prevent renewed full-scale war with the Ethiopian federal government, saying recent attacks on civilians by Ethiopian forces have brought Tigray closer to major conflict. The TCAB claimed the Tigray government has consistently viewed negotiations as the only viable means of resolving political disputes.

incidents.title: Bali tourism threatened by disputed Zika virus outbreak
incidents.description: The U.S. Center for Disease Control issued a travel advisory warning after Zika cases were reported among travelers returning from Bali. Bali’s Tourism Office disputed the risk, with local health authorities documenting no cases of the virus.

incidents.title: Indonesia battles forest fires, arrests 72 in connection
incidents.description: Indonesian authorities arrested 72 individuals accused of illegally starting fires to clear land for farming. Indonesia has been fighting wildfires for several weeks, which have been made worse by a prolonged dry season caused by the El Niño phenomenon.

incidents.title: Large-scale water cuts ordered for western states
incidents.description: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation has announced that California, Nevada, and Arizona together must reduce their water intake from the Colorado River by approximately 1.25 million acre-feet (407 billion gallons) each year for the next two years.

incidents.title: Brazil’s president criticizes Russia, U.S. at campaign rally
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva denounced Russia’s war in Ukraine and said he was tired of hearing U.S. President Donald Trump’s boasts about having the biggest bombs at a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro. Lula, who is running for re-election, said Brazil does not want war and reiterated his government’s commitment to sovereignty in an appeal to nationalism.

incidents.title: Major failure cuts water to Havana
incidents.description: Cuban-run water company Aguas de La Habana, responsible for Havana’s water supply, announced an emergency shutdown of Havana’s water distribution system on Aug. 21 after a malfunction in its 78-inch pipeline. The breakdown left six municipalities in the city without water as Cubans face intensifying shortages of food, water, fuel, and medicine.

incidents.title: Chinese economy slows in early second half of 2026
incidents.description: Vice Finance Minister Liao Min stated that the government was preparing a new stimulus package to boost domestic consumption, including the subsidy of 1 percentage point of interest on eligible small-business loans, as July showed no signs of the economy growing.

incidents.title: U.S. and Brazil hold diplomatic phone call on tariffs
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva spoke by phone with the aim of restarting tariff negotiations between the nations. Lula emphasized the importance of negotiations while Trump suggested officials from both countries meet as soon as possible.

incidents.title: Canada/US trade talks collapse
incidents.description: Trade talks between the United States and Canada fell apart due to last-minute changes that Prime Minister Mark Carney described as “unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal.” by the Prime Minister Mark Carney.

incidents.title: Drone strikes on Tigrayan capital injure at least 13
incidents.description: Tigray People’s Liberation Front Bureau of Communications Affairs accused the federal government of carrying out two drone strikes near the regional capital of Mekelle on Aug. 20, resulting in at least 13 injuries, with conflicting reports on a death toll. This follows an Aug. 18 drone strike near the state capital that killed one and injured another. Previous drone attacks this year ascribed to the Ethiopian government have targeted Tigray’s borders, while these attacks near the center of the region signal a geographic expansion of hostilities after weeks of increasing tensions.

incidents.title: Myanmar, Russia deepen ties during state visit
incidents.description: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made his first state visit to Russia since taking office in April 2026, where he signed 12 trade and economic agreements with Russian President Vladimir Putin including oil refinery development in Myanmar's Dawei Special Economic Zone, nuclear power plant construction, and a geothermal plant. Through joint investment from Russian and Myanmar companies they are coordinating energy infrastruture to bypass Western sanctions.

incidents.title: North Korea fires 10 missiles into eastern sea
incidents.description: North Korea launched at least 10 ballistic missiles into the sea to the east of the Korean Peninsula, leading the South Korean presidential office to convene an emergency meeting. The launches come as South Korea and the U.S. substantially reduced their annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises.

incidents.title: China restricts aerospace exports to Taiwan
incidents.description: China has restricted and delayed exports of key components in the aerospace industry to Taiwan, including quartz, germanium, and neodymium magnets, leading to warnings from technology manufacturers about prolonged delays to their supply chains.

incidents.title: China, Indonesia agree to boost military and tech ties
incidents.description: Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi and defense minister Dong Jun travelled to Jakarta, where they agreed to bolster military cooperation and deepen work on AI, green energy, and fisheries. The deal will result in joint arms production, more joint drills, and cooperation in Indonesia’s critical minerals industry.

incidents.title: Chinese foreign minister visits South Korea
incidents.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi visited Seoul, where he discussed engagement with North Korea, warning South Korea not to take sides between China and the U.S. He also discussed the possible route towards a bilateral summit between South Korean President Lee Jae-myung and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

incidents.title: Iran executes man charged in January protests
incidents.description: Iran executed Qaem Hosseini, a foreign national accused of contributing to the deaths of Iranian security force personnel in the January 2026 popular uprisings.

incidents.title: Iran continues crackdown against January protesters
incidents.description: Four people arrested during the January 2026 popular uprisings face charges of “enmity against God” and corruption on Earth. The detainees are likely to face the death penalty amid an ongoing crackdown by the Iranian government against individuals involved in the protest movement.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan hold elections for parliment
incidents.description: On Sunday, Kazakhstan will hold initial elections for the Kurultai, the unicameral parliament established under its amended constitution, which took effect on July 1. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s ruling party, renamed from Amanat to Adilet, is expected to secure a majority of the vote, strengthening Tokayev’s mandate.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions target nine Cuban state entities, state-run outreach group ICAP
incidents.description: A new round of sanctions hit the Cuban mining, construction, and metals sectors, along with leadership of the Cuban Institute ​of Friendship with the Peoples, Havana’s foreign outreach organization. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused the group of infiltrating and radicalizing U.S. citizens on behalf of the Cuban regime.

incidents.title: Attackers burn Butembo health facility after Ebola case
incidents.description: Unidentified attackers set fire to a health facility in Butembo after authorities confirmed an Ebola case there, destroying equipment and forcing patients and health workers to evacuate. The attack further disrupts disease-control efforts in eastern DRC and reflects the persistent community resistance and misinformation that hamper contact tracing and treatment during the expanding outbreak.

incidents.title: Sudan's war fronts continue to shift and amplify cross-border involvement
incidents.description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) launched its most intense attacks on Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) positions in the border state of Blue Nile. These attacks have forced the SAF to withdraw and reposition in the towns of El Kurmuk and Geisan. It has been reported the RSF attacks are receiving logistical support routed through Assosa in neighboring Ethiopia.

incidents.title: Myanmar’s military chief visits Bangkok
incidents.description: Commander-in-chief and former spymaster of Myanmar’s armed forces Ye Win Oo met with his Thai counterpart nearly two weeks after President Min Aung Hlaing’s state visit. The topics discussed are speculated to concern border security and joint military coordination against ethnic armed organizations despite continuous pressure to demobilize from ASEAN.

incidents.title: Mexico considers imposing tariffs on Chinese products
incidents.description: Mexico is considering a U.S. request to impose tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from China, a move that would align Mexico’s economic positioning with the U.S. amid ongoing trade negotiations while supporting Mexico’s domestic manufacturing goals. While its Ministry of Economy said there is no set proposal to alter tariffs, the ministry continues to meet with businesses that could create a future tariff package

incidents.title: Students rally against government
incidents.description: Several hundred protesters gathered in Jakarta to decry what they describe as economic mismanagement and "decaying freedom" under the rule of President Prabowo Subianto. The University of Indonesia's student executive body organized the protests. Despite heated altercations between protesters and police, no violence was reported.

incidents.title: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister calls for elections
incidents.description: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a political rival of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, called for Ukraine to hold wartime presidential elections.

incidents.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange POWs
incidents.description: Ukraine and Russia completed the reciprocal exchange of 103 prisoners of war per side on Aug. 19.

incidents.title: Israel bombs Syrian airbase
incidents.description: Israel said it bombed a Syrian air base near Aleppo on Aug. 18, to prevent the suspected deployment of Turkish forces there.

incidents.title: UAE severs financial interactions with Iran
incidents.description: The United Arab Emirates announced Aug. 19 the suspension of all its commercial and financial interactions with Iran until further notice, citing new ballistic missile threats from Iran.

incidents.title: China begins base construction in South China Sea
incidents.description: Satelite imagery obtained by Reuters shows that China completed the first phase of construction of an island atop the disputed Antelope Reef in the South China Sea’s Paracels archipelago. The construction is expected to be used as a military base.

incidents.title: U.S.-South Korea drills reduced after Trump calls
incidents.description: The annual joint Ulchi Freedom Shield military drills between South Korea and the U.S. have been reduced by six days following a directive from U.S. President Donald Trump to reduce the U.S. role in the exercises. Trump said the exercises send a “hostile” signal to North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, with whom he said he has a good relationship. North Korea had previously stated that a continuation of joint drills would pose an impediment to engaging in bilateral talks with the U.S.

incidents.title: U.S. and Canada reach deal on tariff extension
incidents.description: Despite Trump’s announcement that the U.S. and Canadian governments had reached agreement on a trade pact and extended the deadline for the imposition of 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, negotiations continued over the details of a deal as the new deadline loomed

incidents.title: U.S. gross national debt reaches $40 trillion
incidents.description: The Department of the Treasury announced Aug. 17 that the U.S. national debt has reached a historic high of $40 trillion. That total reflects about $1.8 trillion added in the last fiscal year.

incidents.title: Venezuela sends 40% of oil output to United States
incidents.description: Venezuela is exporting more than 500,000 barrels of oil per day, about 40% of its total output of 1.25 million, to the United States, according to U.S. Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit.

incidents.title: Oil services firms seek to expand Venezuela’s drilling capacity
incidents.description: Oil services provider SLB and private equity firm Formentera Partners said they were working to reactivate drilling rigs in Venezuela or bring additional rigs into the country. Only two onshore drilling rigs were active in Venezuela at the end of July, while companies were working with the Venezuelan government to address obstacles to importing specialized equipment.

incidents.title: BRICS environment ministers reject EU Carbon Border Levy
incidents.description: At the 12th BRICS Environment Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi, ministers adopted a joint statement by consensus opposing the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), describing such measures as punitive and protectionist. India exports CBAM-covered goods including iron and steel, aluminum, and fertilizers to the bloc.

incidents.title: Brazil’s Supreme Court expands women’s protections
incidents.description: A decision by all 10 members of Brazil’s Supreme Court broadened the scope of a 2006 law that protects women from domestic violence. The law now applies to persecution, threats, and harassment from outside the home. Those charged under the law can be brought to trial without requiring a familial or sentimental connection to the victim.

incidents.title: Spanish airline Iberia extends its suspension of direct flights to Cuba
incidents.description: Spanish airline Iberia announced it will extend its suspension of direct flights to Cuba until June 2027, seven months beyond the initial date the company set in April. Iberia attributed the postponement to Cuba’s energy crisis and drops in demand as the humanitarian and economic situation on the island continues to deteriorate.

incidents.title: Trump administration scales back possible military intervention in Cuba
incidents.description: The U.S. strategy toward Cuba is shifting its focus away from military intervention toward ramping up sanctions and economic pressure to push the Cuban government toward negotiations with U.S. officials, Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed U.S. officials. This comes as the Trump administration faces pressure to strike a deal with Iran ahead of U.S. midterm elections.

incidents.title: Germany announces counterdrone research site
incidents.description: The German government has opened a drone security facility at the German Aerospace Center’s Cochstedt site in Saxony-Anhalt to research and test counterdrone technologies. The opening follows the discovery of an explosive-rigged drone of unknown origin on Aug.ustAugust 4th at the Leipzig/Halle airport, a key logistics hub for weapon shipments to Ukraine. Berlin continues to strengthen its ability to respond to hybrid threats.

incidents.title: Sudanese militants launch crackdown in opposition capital
incidents.description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), under the direct supervision of Gen. Muhammad “Hemedti” Dagalo, began its largest crackdowns in Nyala, South Darfur (the self-declared capital of the Tasis parallel government). This follows a wave of armed robberies, kidnappings of merchants and local leaders for ransom, ethnically motivated violence, and restrictions on Starlink communications.

incidents.title: Ukraine conducts large-scale drone attack against Moscow
incidents.description: Ukraine fired over 600 drones at Moscow between Aug. 18 and 19, marking one of the largest such strikes against the capital of the war. Russian officials have not reported any casualties.

incidents.title: U.K. pledges to stand with Ukraine after Russian threats
incidents.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the U.K. would stand with Ukraine “100%” after Russia threatened retaliation for its provision of drones that Ukraine has used to strike Moscow and other Russian cities.

incidents.title: Ukrainian casualties mount from Russian bombardment
incidents.description: Russian bombardment killed at least 10 people in Kharkiv on Aug. 18 and at least 15 more in Kyiv on Aug. 20.

incidents.title: Trump threatens to bomb Oman
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to bomb Oman over its bilateral negotiations with Iran to re-open the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: Israel kills at least six Palestinians in Gaza
incidents.description: Israel killed at least six Palestinians in Gaza, on Aug. 18, the day after Trump’s son-in-law and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner concluded talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

incidents.title: Trump threatens economic campaign against Iran trade partners
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump, who said no negotiations are currently taking place between Iran and the U.S., declared an “economic D-Day” against any nation conducting trade with Iran.

incidents.title: U.S. seeks to de-escalate tensions between Türkiye and Israel in Syria
incidents.description: U.S. Ambassador to Türkiye and Special Envoy to Syria Tom Barrack said the U.S. is working to establish a deconfliction mechanism between Türkiye and Israel following the recent Israeli bombing of a Syrian air base. Israel alleged Turkish troops were preparing to deploy to the base in the Aleppo region.

incidents.title: U.S. deports Mexican citizens to Honduras and Guatemala
incidents.description: Multiple Department of Homeland Security officials have reported that hundreds of Mexican nationals have been flown to Honduras and Guatemala in spite of the Mexican government's requests for their direct return. The officials said the rationale was to dissuade return immigration by sending the deportees much farther from the U.S. border.

incidents.title: U.S. oil producers sign contracts with Venezuela’s state oil company
incidents.description: Two independent U.S. oil producers signed production contracts with Venezuelan state oil company Petróleos de Venezuela, according to Venezuelan Oil Minister Paula Henao. The agreements would bring additional U.S. producers into Venezuela’s oil sector as the Trump administration seeks to increase the country’s production.

incidents.title: India, Armenia sign defense agreement
incidents.description: Indian Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and Armenian Minister of High Tech Industry David Tadevosyan signed a memorandum of understanding covering cooperation in research, development, innovation, and shared production in the defense industry during Singh’s visit to Yerevan, the Indian Defense Ministry stated. Armenia is India's largest export destination for military equipment, with deals estimated at about $3 billion since 2020.

incidents.title: Brazil’s president hails oil discovery near Amazon River
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva praised the discovery of an offshore oil field by the state-run oil company, Petrobras, about 110 miles from the mouth of the Amazon River. Lula addressed critiques of exploratory offshore oil drilling from environmentalists by framing the issue around economic growth and national sovereignty.

incidents.title: Trump pauses imposition of 50% tariff on Canada
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump extended the 50% tariff deadline on Canadian goods to August 20. The White House claimed that negotiators from Canada committed to concessions in trade negotiations, but Prime Minister Mark Carney did not specify concessions. Trump claims a deal could revive the Keystone XL pipeline project, which the Biden administration had previously blocked.

incidents.title: Substantial clean energy investment in Canada
incidents.description: If finalized, a $70 billion investment in clean energy will go toward expanding the Churchill Falls generating station, Gull Island hydroelectric project, transmission lines, and a 2,000-megawatt onshore wind energy project. This would represent the largest clean energy initiative in North America and could provide equivalent generating capacity for all homes in Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver combined.

incidents.title: Saudi state owned companies accelerate critical mineral extraction
incidents.description: A joint venture formed between state oil company Aramco and state-owned mining company Maaden will focus on accelerating mineral exploration and discovery as Saudi Arabia seeks to boost its role in the energy transition value chain. The new venture will concentrate on mapping and extracting hard rock mineral resources within a 182,000-square-kilometer (70,207-square-mile) region of the kingdom. Copper, in great demand for electric vehicle, energy storage, and power grid applications, is the principal target. Zinc, lead, and rare earth elements crucial to green energy technologies are secondary targets.

incidents.title: Deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC history
incidents.description: The death toll in the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed that of the country’s 2018–2020 epidemic. More than 2,300 people have died and more than 5,000 confirmed cases have been reported during the current outbreak. The record toll marks a significant deterioration in the public health crisis as insecurity, population movement, and gaps in disease surveillance continue to complicate containment.

incidents.title: Genomic study reveals increased resistance to antimalarial drugs among Ethiopians
incidents.description: A nationwide study published in the journal Nature Microbiology has revealed large-scale antimalarial drug-resistance within Ethiopians’ genomes, increasing government concern over the future effectiveness of artemether–lumefantrine, the country’s primary treatment for malaria. Malaria cases have been rising in the country since 2022. More than 4.7 million cases have been reported since January 2026, resulting in 918 deaths.

incidents.title: 15 Chinese companies make shortlist for Ethiopian airport construction, U.S. businesses absent
incidents.description: The United States is seeking to insert itself into Ethiopian Airlines’ $12.5 billion Bishoftu airport project after no U.S. companies made the 33-company construction shortlist. In July, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of Commerce for the Middle East and Africa Mark Mitchell said the U.S. is working to ensure American participation in the infrastructure project, but shortlist exclusion restricts avenues for Washington’s participation. In response, the U.S. has shifted its focus toward avenues beyond construction for involvement in the project.

incidents.title: Nearly 700,000 affected in government data hack
incidents.description: A hack of the French government’s tax and education ministries exposed the data of nearly 700,000 taxpayers and millions of students. The government is in the process of notifying affected parties, and French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held an interministerial crisis meeting regarding government digital security.

incidents.title: Russian warship spotted near German island
incidents.description: Russia’s Admiral Kasatonov, a warship armed with Zircon hypersonic missiles, sailed near Germany’s Fehmarn Island in the Baltic Sea. Its sighting follows recent Kremlin threats against British and EU vessels, heightening Berlin’s concerns over regional security.

incidents.title: Myanmar contracts sanctioned Russian company
incidents.description: Sanctioned software company Astra Group, which is licensed by Russia’s intelligence apparatus, was contracted to streamline Myanmar’s trade documentation system by creating a Single Window system. The resulting single portal would eventually connect to ASEAN’s Single Window, sparking security concerns. The deal is speculated to include the Astra Group’s tactical operating system, of which they provided high-level demonstrations in Nay Pyi Taw during June of 2026.

incidents.title: Russia provides wartime supply to Iran
incidents.description: Based on an official European document reviewed by NBC News, it reported that Russia is reportedly bolstering Iran’s war effort by shipping drone parts and munitions through the Caspian Sea.

incidents.title: China pressures Taiwanese lawmakers to block drone bill
incidents.description: The Taipei Times, citing an unnamed source, reported that the Chinese Communist Party is pressuring Taiwanese politicians to block a proposed bill aimed at funding drones for the military.

incidents.title: Gas prices raise inflation in Canada
incidents.description: Statistics Canada reported that the rebound of gasoline prices, due to increased conflict between the United States and Iran, pushed the country’s annual rate of inflation up to 3%. Peace talks eased inflation in June to 2.8%, but global oil prices are high again.

incidents.title: Nvidia to provide $105 billion dollars in data center construction
incidents.description: Nvidia agreed to provide a guarantee up to $105 billion in financial support for OpenAI’s lease of a large data center being developed by Softbank-owned SB Energy in Pike County, Ohio. Nvidia will also invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy and serve as the facility’s exclusive chip supplier. The site could eventually reach 8 gigawatts (GW) of capacity, with its first 800 megawatts expected to come online in 2028. SoftBank and SB Energy also plan to develop at least 10 GW of new power generation and invest $4.2 billion in regional grid infrastructure to support the project.

incidents.title: Petrobras discovers large oil deposit in Amazon
incidents.description: Brazilian state-owned oil company Petrobras confirmed the discovery of oil at the Morpho exploration well in Brazil’s Equatorial Margin, about 175 kilometers (108 miles) off the coast of Amapá. Drilling has reached roughly 3,000 meters below the seabed, with another 1,000 meters to go before the well is completed. Petrobras said it cannot yet estimate the volume of oil or the field’s production potential but expects to conduct further studies on the reservoir and its commercial viability once the well is completed around the beginning of September. The company has invested about $3 billion in its current exploration campaign in the region and has requested permits for additional offshore sites.

incidents.title: Colombia faces humanitarian crisis following 7.4 magnitude earthquake
incidents.description: Colombia faces significant economic losses in the wake of the 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck the western part of the country on Aug. 10. President Abelardo de la Espriella estimated Colombia’s immediate economic losses at 30 trillion pesos($9.58 billion), about 2% of the country’s annual gross domestic product. The quake damaged and destroyed numerous buildings and other infrastructure such as roads, bridges, and public utilities. The disaster initially knocked out 18% to 20% of the national electrical grid, but the country’s utility-scale solar PV plants escaped damage.

incidents.title: Kushner meets with Hamas and Israeli leaders
incidents.description: U.S. envoy Jared Kushner met directly with Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo on Aug. 16 and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Aug. 17, following Netanyahu’s recent rejection of Trump’s 15-point peace plan for Gaza, which Hamas had agreed to.

incidents.title: Aceh protesters demand independence
incidents.description: Large-scale protests in Aceh province centered around demands for independence from central government. The rally features chants of "Aceh has every right to be independent," and some protesters desecrated Indonesian national symbols and raised the Aceh nationalist flag.

incidents.title: Israel kills at least 11 Lebanese:
incidents.description: In a strike targeting a Hezbollah commander, Israel killed at least 11 people in southern Lebanon on Aug. 15, threatening a U.S.-mediated ceasefire after weeks of direct talks between Israel and Lebanon.

incidents.title: South Korea seeks closer ties with Japan
incidents.description: During a speech marking the 81st anniversary of South Korea’s liberation from Japanese occupation, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung called for deeper bilateral ties with Tokyo, stating that the foundations of trust for both countries have been established.

incidents.title: Brazil invokes economic reciprocity process against U.S. tariffs
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva triggered an economic reciprocity law mechanism in the wake of announced U.S. tariffs, saying he wanted to signal resolve. Lula reiterated that he does not want a fight with the U.S. but is “prepared to debate the defenceefense of Brazil anywhere in the world.”

incidents.title: French court strikes down under-15 social media ban
incidents.description: The French Constitutional Council ruled that a law banning minors under 15 from social media apps was unconstitutional, arguing it was a violation of their freedom of expression. The law was a signature fixture of French President Emmanuel Macron’s final term, and he has instructed the government to rewrite the law to comply with the court’s ruling.

incidents.title: López Obrador’s son claims U.S. cancelled his visa
incidents.description: In a public letter to U.S. President Donald Trump, Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, the son of former Mexican President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, claimed his U.S. visa was cancelled, arguing that the decision was politically driven as there is no evidence linking him to criminal activity. The Trump administration has previously revoked visas from other Mexican officials in its attempt to target corruption and cartel operations in Mexico.

incidents.title: Earthquake shakes Flores Island
incidents.description: An earthquake struck Flores Island south of Borneo in the Indonesian archipelago, killing 68 people and damaging critical infrastructure. Indonesian authorities and humanitarian organizations worked to distribute aid and restore essential services.

incidents.title: BP plans major Venezuelan offshore gas development
incidents.description: BP plans to develop the second phase of Venezuela’s offshore Loran gas field alongside a Qatari partner and two U.S. oil companies with ties to the Trump administration. The project would be one of the first large-scale foreign investments in Venezuela’s energy sector since the U.S. removal of President Nicolás Maduro in January.

incidents.title: Explosion kills 1 in Crimea
incidents.description: The detonation of an improvised explosive device inside a trash can in occupied Crimea reportedly killed a former Ukrainian service member who defected to Russia on Aug. 13. Ukrainian officials have not commented on the incident, while Russian intelligence officials confirmed that the man killed in the blast was in the Russian armed forces but did not provide additional details.

incidents.title: Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon threaten peace deal
incidents.description: Israel conducted airstrikes across southern Lebanon, threatening the implementation of a recent U.S.-mediated peace agreement.

incidents.title: Iraq prepares for departure of international forces
incidents.description: As Iraq prepares for U.S. and international forces to depart the country by the end of September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said he will pursue legislation to bring all arms in the country under state control.

incidents.title: Venezuelan government, opposition agree on judicial reform, frozen assets
incidents.description: Venezuela’s interim government and opposition representatives concluded their first round of talks with agreements to pursue judicial reform and seek access to frozen funds for earthquake recovery.

incidents.title: Ebola reaches sixth DRC province
incidents.description: Reuters reported that Congolese health authorities confirmed the first Ebola case in Bas-Uele after an infected motorcycle-taxi driver traveled from Haut-Uele to Buta and sought treatment at several health facilities before dying. The outbreak’s expansion into a sixth province broadens the geographic scope of the health emergency and further strains containment efforts as authorities struggle with contact tracing and limited infrastructure.

incidents.title: Putin threatens European commercial vessels
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened to seize European commercial vessels in retaliation for an ongoing European campaign against Russian shadow fleet exports.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy hints at plan to end war
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Aug. 11 that Ukraine and its allies have a plan to force Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war. Zelenskyy did not disclose any details but said that Ukraine has sent a proposal to U.S. negotiators.

incidents.title: U.N. says Israel advancing annexation of the West Bank
incidents.description: During an Aug. 11 brief to the U.N. Security Council, U.N. officials said Israel was nearing “de facto annexation” of the West Bank amid expanded settlement expansion and increased settler violence against Palestinians.

incidents.title: U.S./Iran talks stall
incidents.description: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that talks between the U.S. and Iran over ending hostilities are deadlocked, as U.S. President Donald Trump demanded that Iran pay compensation for war casualties.

incidents.title: Taiwan repels AI cyberattacks
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Ministry of Digital Affairs stated it had detected the use of artificial intelligence in Chinese-led cyberattacks against the island. Most attacks were “successfully handled” by Taiwanese authorities. The number of cyberattacks against Taiwan increased year-on-year in 2025 by 6%, and experts have warned that the use of AI will further increase their frequency and scope.

incidents.title: Putin visits disputed island near Japan
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin visited the Japanese-claimed island of Iturup, drawing strong protests by Tokyo. Ownership of the island, which is a part of what Japan calls the “Northern Territories,” was never formally settled between the countries after World War II.

incidents.title: India reiterates China border goals
incidents.description: India’s foreign ministry stated twice in a week that peace along its border with China was crucial to determining good bilateral ties. The disputed border remains a subject of tension following a deadly clash between border forces in 2020. The statements come ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi in September.

incidents.title: Leavitt to step down as White House press secretary
incidents.description: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said Aug. 12 she was departing from her role to focus on her family.

incidents.title: Iranian general says Tehran may prolong war
incidents.description: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Brig. Gen. Mohammad Reza Naghdi said during an Aug. 11 interview with PBS that Iran may draw out the war to outlast U.S. President Donald Trump’s time in office.

incidents.title: India, southern African nations begin trade talks
incidents.description: India signed an agreement with the Southern African Customs Union, a bloc made up of South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, and Eswatini, to open talks on a trade agreement to lower tariffs on selected goods. The signing revives a process that stalled after five rounds of talks held between 2002 and 2010.

incidents.title: Brazilian Supreme Court decision weakens deforestation protections
incidents.description: Brazil’s Supreme Court upheld state laws that deny tax incentives to farmers and companies that adhere to Brazil’s 2006 soy moratorium, a voluntary agreement to refuse to purchase soy grown on deforested Amazon land. The soy moratorium is credited with helping slow Amazon deforestation, but the ruling allows states to create tax incentives for farmers and companies that undercut the agreement.

incidents.title: Petition calls for U.S. ambassador to be removed from Canada
incidents.description: An online petition is calling for U.S. Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra to be declared persona non grata, a status which may strip him of his diplomatic status due to remarks denouncing the Canada-U.S. relations. The petition will be presented to the House of Commons later this year after passing a 500-signature threshold.

incidents.title: Houthi's strike an Egyptian cargo ship
incidents.description: Yemen’s internationally recognized government said a Houthi attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait killed 6 people and injured 10. The vessel was reportedly struck by three ballistic missiles, followed by an additional strike during rescue operations. The attack occurred amid renewed Houthi operations against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and it follows the group’s declaration of a blockade on Saudi-linked shipping and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

incidents.title: One-fifth of French nuclear fleet offline
incidents.description: A combination of extreme weather and a jellyfish invasion has forced 13 of France’s 57 nuclear reactors into partial or full shutdowns, including five of the six reactors at the Gravelines plant, the largest in Western Europe. The shutdowns are expected to last at least a week but are not expected to pose supply issues.

incidents.title: German government approves intelligence reforms
incidents.description: In response to recent hybrid attacks and security threats, the German government approved draft legislation to expand the powers of its federal foreign intelligence service. The bill, which still requires parliamentary approval, will allow German intelligence to conduct “hack-back” cyber operations that alter or delete data and will allow arms to be disabled during production.

incidents.title: Mexican former governor charged in mass kidnapping probe
incidents.description: Former governor of Guerrero Ángel Aguirre Rivero was officially accused Aug. 12 of ordering the destruction of evidence in the Iguala mass kidnapping case, in which 43 college students were abducted by cartel and police forces in 2014. Judge Mario Martínez Elizondo determined that Aguirre will remain in a maximum-security prison pending his conviction hearing.

incidents.title: Houthis conduct deadly attack in Bab el-Mandeb
incidents.description: Houthi attacks against international shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb killed at least six people on Aug. 11.

incidents.title: U.S. Navy disables ship in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: The U.S. Navy fired at and disabled a Panamanian-flagged ship attempting to circumvent the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz on Aug. 11. No casualties resulted.

incidents.title: China, Indonesia conduct drills east of Taiwan
incidents.description: China conducted naval drills off Taiwan’s east coast alongside an Indonesian warship, drawing strong condemnation from Taiwan. The People’s Liberation Army Navy has been conducting drills in the area since June, prompting concern from Washington.

incidents.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile
incidents.description: North Korea test-fired its second ballistic missile in a week out of the country’s Wonsan area off the east coast. The launch comes as the U.S. and South Korea are planning to hold military drills together.

incidents.title: Venezuela, Israel restore consular relations
incidents.description: Venezuela and Israel agreed to restore consular relations, reversing a 17-year break in ties.

incidents.title: Iranian supreme leader promotes hard-liners
incidents.description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a series of orders placing hard-line officials from the Iraq-Iran War generation in senior leadership positions within the Iranian security apparatus.

incidents.title: TPLF accuses Ethiopian government of drone strike on forces, school
incidents.description: The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) claimed that Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) drone strikes targeted its troops in southern Tigray, close to its regional border with Amhara. In an interview with AFP, TPLF Vice Chairman Amanuel Assefa called the strike “a serious escalation,” while the Ethiopian federal army has not yet commented on the accusations. Amanuel also claimed the drones hit a school, a claim AFP could not verify. The strike accusations follow large-scale artillery clashes between the TPLF and ENDF Aug. 1.

incidents.title: U.S. to negotiate tariffs with Brazil
incidents.description: The U.S. has agreed to hold discussions with Brazil after its appeal to the World Trade Organization (WTO) over separate tariffs of 25% and 12.5% on a slew of Brazilian exports. China requested to join Brazil’s appeal to the WTO because it was also subjected to the 12.5% tariff and cited economic concerns of these measures impacting Chinese exports in the U.S. market.

incidents.title: DRC health institute accounces over 2000 dead from Ebola
incidents.description: The country’s health institute reported that the death toll from the Ebola virus had reached 2,011, while the total number of confirmed cases reached 4,381 people across five regions. Since the current outbreak began in January, the virus has spread considerably faster than during previous outbreaks, as conflict, poor infrastructure, and weakened health services limited response.

incidents.title: Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces block Al-Mazroub
incidents.description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) imposed a blockade on Al-Mazroub, North Kordofan, blocking humanitarian aid and supplies amid a cholera outbreak. RSF soldiers reportedly seized large portions of the market and looted private homes. Al-Mazroub holds strategic importance in western North Kordofan because its road network connects the state to Darfur, making it a key staging ground for forces retreating from active combat zones.

incidents.title: Sudanese army repels rebels after attack
incidents.description: An alliance of the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North launched a heavy attack on the main market of Geisan in the Blue Nile region, looting shops and firing on civilians, according to local officials. They also attacked farmers in the field. The Sudanese Armed Forces eventually repelled the forces in the territory, which they recaptured from RSF control in June.

incidents.title: Thailand expands protections for Myanmar’s migrant workers
incidents.description: Following President Min Aung Hlaing’s visit to Bangkok, Thailand expanded its existing labor memorandum of understanding with Myanmar to provide migrants with equal access to governmental benefits and a protected working status until 2031. While this agreement provides pathways for legal immigration and protections against human trafficking, full access to benefits requires migrant workers to remit 25% of their pay to the regime.

incidents.title: Myanmar accepts foreign bid for natural gas extraction
incidents.description: Recent discoveries of gas fields off the coast of Myanmar prompted a Singapore-based subsidiary of Canadian Foresight Group (CFG) to begin offshore drilling operations by the end of 2026. Surveys of the fields projected them to be one of the largest in the world and able to satisfy 40% of the regime’s foreign currency earnings, which encouraged partnership between CFG and the sanctioned Myanmar Gas and Oil Enterprise.

incidents.title: Russian disinformation targets German elections
incidents.description: A Russian disinformation operation known as Matryoshka has amplified false videos and fabricated news reports depicting German news outlets, celebrities, and business leaders as supporting a redivision of Germany’s East and West ahead of September’s state elections in Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt, and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Designed to exploit regional divisions, the campaign comes as polls have shown Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany party, whose leaders advocate for stronger alignment with Moscow, holding leads or within competitive reach in all three states.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy claims North Korea increasing aid to Russia
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed that North Korea was preparing a new deployment of troops to Russia and that Russia used North Korean missiles in an attack against the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia that killed at least 9 people Aug. 11.

incidents.title: Ukrainian attack disrupts Russian grain exports
incidents.description: Ukrainian drone strikes forced the suspension of operations from two of Russia’s largest grain export terminals in Novorossiysk along the Black Sea and hit numerous Russian energy infrastructure and commercial sites.

incidents.title: Oman/Iran talks make progress
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baqei said bilateral negotiations with Oman over Strait of Hormuz transit were progressing positively.

incidents.title: Taiwan, Japan deepen semiconductor cooperation
incidents.description: Taiwan and Japan have announced they will be deepening their semiconductor partnership, with Sony Group and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. investing $6.3 billion in a joint venture to produce next-generation image sensor semiconductors.

incidents.title: Brazilian low-income household debts reach record high
incidents.description: The share of Brazil’s low-income households carrying debt reached a record high of 84.9% in July according to a nationwide survey by the National Confederation of Commerce. This is the fourth consecutive monthly high and tops the 82% debt rate of Brazilian families across all income groups.

incidents.title: Ethiopian peacekeepers withdraw from encircled Somali town
incidents.description: The African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) announced the withdrawal of Ethiopian troops from Burhakaba, even though the town remains surrounded by Al-Shabaab militants. The base had been operated by Ethiopia since 2014. The withdrawal and handover to the Somali National Army comes after the United States announced it would not continue to fund the AUSSOM mission past the end of its current mandate in December 2026.

incidents.title: Typhoon Dolphin forces over 1 million in eastern China to evacuate
incidents.description: Typhoon Dolphin forced the evacuation of more than 1 million people in eastern China. The tropical cyclone, the strongest storm to hit China this year, made landfall in Yuhuan, Zhejiang province, after hitting Japan and Taiwan.

incidents.title: Sudanese civil, political organizations move toward national dialogue
incidents.description: Gen. Abdul Fattah al-Burhan of the Sudanese Armed Forces) held private consultations with political and civil society groups on steps toward a national dialogue. The agreement explores proposals to drop charges against opposition leaders and to create a preparatory committee for the conference.

incidents.title: Myanmar nationals in U.S. lose protected status
incidents.description: An Illinois federal judge ruled against Temporary Protected Status designations for the 4,000 Myanmar nationals currently in the U.S., citing Myanmar’s December 2025 presidential election as evidence of situational improvement. Human rights groups in Myanmar and the U.S. warned of continued violence and instability in the country and are exploring further legal action.

incidents.title: 70,000 Canadian citizens petition for U.S. ambassadors removal
incidents.description: At least 70,000 Canadian citizens have signed a petition calling for the expulsion of U.S. ambassador to Ottawa Pete Hoekstra and to declare him a persona non grata. Signatories accused Hoekstra of interfering in Canadian domestic affairs and normalizing the Trump administration’s threats to annexing the country. The petition reached the threshold needed for the issue to be discussed in the House of Commons.

incidents.title: Heat wave underscores summer of extreme weather in France
incidents.description: Another heatwave moved through France, forcing 40,000 people into water. Ecology Minister Monique Barbut held a crisis meeting Aug. 12 related to the drought, in which she announced that this summer’s heatwaves could cost France between 10 billion to 15 billion euros ($11.5 billion to $17.3 billion).

incidents.title: EU levies tariffs on raw materials produced in Mexico
incidents.description: The European Union imposed a 24.1% antidumping tariff on Mexican terephthalic acid imports, a raw material produced in Mexico and South Korea used to make plastic. The tariff was levied to protect the localized production of this commodity within the EU, particularly in Spain, Belgium, and Poland.

incidents.title: Mexican Navy deploys troops in Mazatlán
incidents.description: The Mexican Navy deployed over 1,700 personnel to Mazatlán, Sinaloa, after the city recorded 36 deaths in July, its highest monthly homicide count this year.
