This deployment comes after 900 Mexican Army troops arrived in Mazatlán in late July to bolster security following sequential attacks in the city.

incidents.title: Indonesian rupiah gains on U.S. dollar
incidents.description: The rupiah, Indonesia's currency, gained value against the U.S. dollar on Aug. 10, partially reversing a monthslong slump. This came after President Prabowo Subianto nominated Destry Damayanti to serve as the Bank of Indonesia's next governor, easing currency markets after the abrupt resignation of the latter’s predecessor last month.

incidents.title: Taiwanese government to propose 16% defense budget increase
incidents.description: Taiwan’s government is expected to propose raising its defense budget for 2027 to $31 billion, a 16% annual increase. This comes several months after the government failed to adopt the full amount for a special defense budget after strong opposition in the Legislative Yuan.

incidents.title: China reduces imports from Germany
incidents.description: China’s trade surplus with Germany grew from $46 billion (€40 billion) in the first half of last year to $63 billion this year. China is also importing less vehicles from Germany as it seeks to reduce its reliance on imports. Germany’s automotive industry has struggled to keep up with competition from China, whose electric vehicle exports are a large contributor to the Chinese economy’s survival.

incidents.title: Indonesia deepens trade alignment with BRICS
incidents.description: In a meeting with trade representatives in Jaipur, India, Indonesia vowed to work with fellow BRICS states to eliminate trade barriers and to reform the WTO to support developing economies.

incidents.title: Modi, Vance discuss deepening ties
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. Vice President JD Vance discussed the India-U.S. strategic partnership during an Aug. 8 phone call, naming trade, security cooperation, advanced technologies, and exchanged assessments on global developments.

incidents.title: Canadian wildfire causes mass evacuations
incidents.description: British Columbia declared a state of emergency as a wildfire in the Bald Range started burning out of control and spread across 23,500 acres. The fire resulted in Canada’s largest evacuation this summer, with total evacuees reaching 20,000 people.

incidents.title: Türkiye, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia sign defense pact
incidents.description: Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense agreement referred to as the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on Aug. 7.

incidents.title: U.S. lost 23,000 jobs in July
incidents.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a net loss of approximately 23,000 jobs last month. The loss rate came as a surprise considering a Dow Jones report had forecast an 83,000 job gain. The unemployment rate stabilized at 4.1%, a decline from the 4.3% seen in prior months.

incidents.title: Ethiopian government detains chief of independent news site
incidents.description: The independent Ethiopian news site Addis Standard said Ethiopian government security forces detained and interrogated its editor-in-chief, Yonas Kedir, for 24 hours. Human rights groups said the action was part of a recent government campaign to target independent news outlets. Authorities revoked the Addis Standard's media registration in February, saying the site violated media ethics and posed an unspecified threat to "national interests."

incidents.title: DRC, AFC/M23 complete first detainee transfer under Qatar-brokered deal
incidents.description: Congolese authorities transferred 15 detainees to the Alliance Flueve Congo/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) through an operation facilitated by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The transfer is the first such release under the Doha Mechanism, a Qatar-mediated agreement signed by the two sides in September 2025.

incidents.title: U.S. searching for new Cuban leadership
incidents.description: Citing unnamed current and former U.S. officials, The New York Times reported that U.S. officials are searching for current or former Cuban officials who could replace Havana’s current leadership. The Trump administration directed its spy agencies to identify a Cuban counterpart to Venezuela’s interim president Delcy Rodríguez.

incidents.title: German company withdraws from US wind farm project
incidents.description: German energy company RWE will withdraw from its U.S. offshore wind projects after reaching a $1.2 billion settlement with the Trump administration. The company plans to redirect most of the funds toward natural gas investments, including $900 million for a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export terminal in Louisiana. According to RWE, the decision was driven by the Trump administration’s permitting restrictions, which left no viable path for developing the projects. RWE is the fifth company to reach such an agreement, signaling a broader shift in federal energy policy.

incidents.title: Indonesia, Brazil weigh trade deal
incidents.description: Indonesian Trade Minister Budi Santoso and his Brazilian counterpart, Márcio Fernando Elias Rosa, discussed a bilateral preferential trade agreement Aug. 7. This comes after unsuccessful Indonesian trade negotiations with Mercorsur bloc.

incidents.title: U.K. issues new sanctions against Russia
incidents.description: The U.K. issued a new sanctions package targeting Russian banks, companies, and shadow fleet vessels on Aug. 6.

incidents.title: Ukraine hits Russian oil refineries
incidents.description: Ukrainian drone strikes damaged two oil refineries in Russia’s Yaroslavl region, more than 400 miles from the Ukrainian/Russian border, on Aug. 6.

incidents.title: Trump signs executive orders targeting birthright citizenship
incidents.description: U.S. President Trump signed two executive orders targeting birthright citizenship. The first order expands the legal permissibility of declaring a child ineligible for birthright citizenship. The second seeks to end what the president calls “Birth Tourism,” where a pregnant woman travels to the U.S. for the explicit reason of getting the child U.S. citizenship.

incidents.title: Iranian President disputes death count from January protests
incidents.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in an interview released Aug. 5 that the reports of 30,000 to 40,000 killed in the January 2026 mass protest movement in Iran were exaggerated. However, Pezeshkian acknowledged that “thousands” had been killed, without specifying a number.

incidents.title: WestJet flight attendants go on strike
incidents.description: WestJet, the second-largest airline in Canada, went on a day long strike from Sunday, 8/2 to Monday, 8/3. Flight attendants were striking over compensation for groundwork, not just compensation for work done in-flight. A tentative deal has been reached with the airline that includes wage increases, increased time off, and higher allowances for food and uniforms.

incidents.title: DRC bans exports of copper, cobalt concentrates
incidents.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo prohibited exports of copper and cobalt concentrates in a bid to promote domestic mineral processing and retain more value from its mining sector. The ban took effect immediately, although the government said one-year export waivers could be granted under strategic circumstances.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions target Cuban military officials linked to Russia, China
incidents.description: The U.S. imposed sanctions targeting Cuban entities and corporations the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has accused of involvement in arms deals with China and Russia. The sanctions against eight Cuban individuals and five businesses are the latest escalation in the U.S. pressure campaign against the island.

incidents.title: China increases oil imports from Russia
incidents.description: China’s Sinopec has increased oil imports from Russia to offset the import shortages from the Middle East. Purchases of cheaper Russian oil have helped China to sustain relatively stable refinery throughput and capitalize on strong fuel export margins. Before the Iran conflict, nearly half of Sinopec’s crude imports came from the Middle East, with Saudi Arabia among its largest suppliers. Since then, Chinese purchases of Saudi crude have fallen sharply, dropping from around 20 million barrels in both March and April to just 2 million in August.

incidents.title: Russia kills at least 17 in Kyiv as Ukrainian air defense dwindles
incidents.description: Russian bombardment of Kyiv killed at least 17 people and injured over 120 on Aug. 5 amid the Ukrainian armed forces’ ongoing shortage of air defense munitions.

incidents.title: U.K. defense minister meets with Zelenskyy
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with British Defense Minister Wes Streeting in Kyiv on Aug. 5, where they discussed British aid to Ukraine’s air defense capabilities and other defense-related topics.

incidents.title: Drone carrying explosives found in German airport
incidents.description: A drone carrying explosive material was discovered and defused at Germany’s Leipzig/Halle airport, which serves as a major logistics hub for transporting military aid to Ukraine. Ukraine blamed Russia for the incident, while Russia has yet to officially comment.

incidents.title: Car bomb targets Russian drone producer
incidents.description: An Aug. 5 car bombing in a village within Russia’s Sverdlovsk region critically injured Vladimir Tkachuk, the head of a defense company that produces FPV drones.

incidents.title: Israel-Hezbollah fighting threatens peace talks
incidents.description: A flareup in fighting between the Israel Defense Forces and Hezbollah threatened the latest round of U.S.-mediated negotiations between Israel and Lebanon, which took place in Rome from Aug. 3-6. At least two Israeli soldiers were killed by an improvised explosive device while conducting operations in southern Lebanon on Aug. 5. Israel retaliated with airstrikes in the southern Lebanese town of Tebnine, killing at least one.

incidents.title: Israel escalates bombings in Gaza
incidents.description: Israel killed at least 20 Palestinians in Gaza between Aug. 1 and 2, threatening reported progress toward a disarmament deal with Hamas touted by U.S. President Donald Trump. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel will not agree to the deal, which would require it to withdraw from the “yellow line” in Gaza before Hamas disarms.

incidents.title: Oman, Iran advance Strait of Hormuz negotiations
incidents.description: Iranian officials reported meaningful progress in bilateral negotiations with Oman over control of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. has not publicly commented on the proposed deal, which would grant Iran authority to charge tolls for vessels traversing the strait.

incidents.title: China imposes retaliatory sanctions on U.S.
incidents.description: China announced a series of sanctions against U.S. companies and entities it accuses of aiding in the imposition of tariffs against forced labor practices of the Uyghur community in Xinjiang. These are companies that helped identify the origin of cotton in imported products and traced it back to the region, and include Applied DNA Sciences, Stratum Reservoir, Altana Technologies, Responsible Business Alliance, Verite Group and Human Rights in China.

incidents.title: U.S. expected to impose tariffs on polysilicon imports
incidents.description: The Trump administration is expected to impose a 15% tariff on imports of polysilicon products, notably used in solar panel production. If put in place, the tariffs would impact Chinese solar exports as the U.S. seeks to reduce its reliance on China’s dominance in the sector.

incidents.title: FBI chief hails new ties with Chinese, Russian law enforcement
incidents.description: U.S. Director of the FBI Kash Patel stated he has been forging new relationships with law enforcement entities in both China and Russia over the past year. Patel stated this was in the hopes of coordinating on mitigating fentanyl flows, electronic fraud, and child sexual exploitation.

incidents.title: Phillips 66 expands Venezuelan crude purchases
incidents.description: Phillips 66 said it has increased purchases of discounted Venezuelan crude oil as part of a strategy to expand its position in heavy crude markets. The increase has been supported by U.S. waivers that allow more shipments of Venezuelan oil; the waivers are expected to be extended.

incidents.title: Oman, Iran advance Strait of Hormuz negotiations
incidents.description: Iranian officials reported meaningful progress in bilateral negotiations with Oman over control of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. has not publicly commented on the proposed deal, which would grant Iran authority to charge tolls for vessels traversing the strait.

incidents.title: Argentina will not reciprocate Brazil’s diplomatic ties downgrade
incidents.description: Argentinian Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said Argentina will not act in response to Brazil recalling its ambassador to Argentina. According to Brazil’s Foreign Ministry, Brazil’s diplomatic presence in Argentina will remain downgraded until Argentinian President Javier Milei ceases referring to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as a thief and convict. Milei has repeated these insults in support of Lula’s challenger, right-wing presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, since July 25.

incidents.title: Indonesian economic growth tops 5%
incidents.description: According to official data from Statistics Indonesia, the economy grew by 5.29% during Q2 2026. The jump is primarily attributed to an increase in manufacturing productivity and a surge in household consumption.

incidents.title: Sheinbaum investigates fracking projects in northern states
incidents.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum investigated trial hydraulic fracturing projects in Coahuila and Tamaulipas designed to increase natural gas production. Sheinbaum modified her previous opposition to fracking, claiming that some methods have a lower environmental impact.

incidents.title: Congolese groups press U.N., EU for genocide tribunal
incidents.description: Congolese civil society organizations revived a 2024 memorandum calling on DRC President Felix Tshisekedi and its Parliament, the United Nations, the European Union, and the African Union to formally recognize atrocities committed in the DRC since the 1990s as genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes. The campaign calls for an international criminal tribunal, expanded victim reparations, and a national law on Genocost, a Congolese advocacy term linking genocide to the exploitation of the country’s mineral resources. The action could increase pressure for international accountability and intensify disputes over responsibility for the Congo wars and exploitation of Congolese minerals.

incidents.title: CIA creates covert Cuba task force
incidents.description: The CIA has established a secret task force centered on Cuba as the U.S. escalates pressure campaign against the regime, The New York Times reported, citing anonymous sources. The task force, composed of intelligence personnel, would enable the rapid direction of resources to the island, including human, financial, and technological assets.

incidents.title: Chinese miners reject claims of uranium-tainted cobalt
incidents.description: The Union of Chinese-owned Mining Companies in the DRC rejected allegations that cobalt from its member companies contained uranium levels above Congolese limits. Its response followed a Financial Times and Lighthouse Reports investigation that alleged repeated violations at the Tenke Fungurume copper-cobalt mine, operated by Chinese mining giant CMOC Group, raising concerns about the reliability of Congolese cobalt in global battery and electric vehicle supply chains.

incidents.title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Democratic primary
incidents.description: Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate; he will run against Republican former congressman Mike Rogers in November’s election. El-Sayed campaigned on a progressive platform that voiced frustrations with the mainstream Democratic establishment. After the election, Trump called El-Sayed a “Communist loser” and said his victory would help Rogers in the general election.

incidents.title: China produces record level of nuclear power
incidents.description: The world's nuclear power generation hit a record level in 2025, driven by unprecedented domestic expansion in China. The global nuclear power generation reached 2,845 terawatt-hours (TWh), an increase of 30 TWh from 2024. All this expansion was fueled by China, which contributed more than 34 TWh. China has tripled its nuclear power production in the last decade, closing the gap on the U.S.

incidents.title: Explosive found near Ukrainian aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport
incidents.description: Several aircraft were diverted after runway closures at Germany’s Leipzig/Halle Airport, where authorities found an explosive device near a Ukrainian aircraft. Shortly after the device was found, a diverted freight plane reportedly struck an unidentified object over the Leipzig area before landing safely in Hanover, where inspectors found minor damage to its nose.

incidents.title: Mexican social media influencer killed in Sinaloa
incidents.description: Cesar Gastelum, a Mexican social media influencer, was shot to death by two unidentified people as he livestreamed outside a restaurant in Culiacán, Sinaloa. Gastelum’s death occurred amidst ongoing violent conflict in Culiacán between competing factions of the Sinaloa cartel.

incidents.title: Iran suspected of cyberattacks in U.S. governor
incidents.description: Cyberattacks against water treatment and waste management facilities in at least 12 U.S. states have been reported as of Aug. 3. U.S. intelligence officials believe that Iran has directed the attacks according to reporting by multiple outlets. U.S. President Donald Trump said he doesn’t “think” Iran was behind the cyberattacks in Minnesota, instead blaming Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz.

incidents.title: North Korea considers ‘military options’ after Japanese missile test
incidents.description: Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, announced that North Korea would consider “military options” in response to Japan’s recent test firing of a U.S. Tomahawk cruise missile, accusing Japan of violating the Japanese Self Defense Force’s pacifist and defensive mandate.

incidents.title: Chinese chipmaker reports strong H1 profits
incidents.description: China’s top chipmaker, Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment China, stated it increased its profit for the first half of 2026 by 282% increase year-on-year based on unaudited figures. The AI and tech industry, along with heavy export numbers, have largely held the Chinese economy afloat as domestic consumption continues to remain low.

incidents.title: U.S. revokes visa to Brazil's ambassador
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration revoked the visa of Brazilian Ambassador to the United States Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti. The U.S. State Department said the action was in response to Brazil’s withholding approval of Trump’s newly appointed ambassador to Brazil, Daniel Perez, and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s blocking of visas for two senior State Department officials over election interference concerns.

incidents.title: Canadian wildfires ongoing
incidents.description: Wildfires in British Columbia are described as “explosive” and “dangerous” by wildfire officials due to dry lighting and hot temperatures worsening destruction. Hundreds of homes have been destroyed, and thousands of people have been ordered to evacuate.

incidents.title: Canada’s manufacturing sector expands
incidents.description: The S&P Global Canada Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index increased from 53.0 in June to 53.5 in July. This is the seventh month in a row that the index was above 50, indicating expansion, but an economist with S&P expressed doubt that growth would continue at this rate due to weak international demand, tariffs, and high energy costs.

incidents.title: 75 migrants die during attempt to enter Ceuta
incidents.description: At least 75 migrants have died following a wave of migration to the north African Spanish territory of Ceuta last week from Morocco, which saw more than 70,000 people come to Ceuta from Morocco in a single day, straining local authorities. While nearly all of them have since returned to Morocco, European Union interior ministers convened an emergency meeting where they endorsed a plan to further strengthen the bloc’s exterior borders, including through stronger cooperation with external partners.

incidents.title: Egyptian officials oppose new Ethiopian dam projects
incidents.description: Egyptian Irrigation Minister Hani Sewilam said Egypt would not allow Ethiopia to construct further dam infrastructure on portions of the Nile River upstream from Egypt. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) project has been a point of contention between the two countries since 2011, due to Egyptian fears that water flow changes would harm its agriculture. Ethiopia inaugurated the main dam of its GERD project in 2025 without a binding international agreement on management, and Ethiopia has recently signaled plans for three additional dams on the river.

incidents.title: Rhine hits record low
incidents.description: The Rhine River, one of Europe’s most important trade arteries from the North Sea to the Swiss Alps, has fallen to its lowest recorded level, with conditions expected to worsen in the weeks ahead. This summer’s heatwaves have lowered river levels throughout Europe, disrupting trade, forcing nuclear power plants to shutter, and exposing regional infrastructure vulnerabilities to drought.

incidents.title: Bombing in Moscow restaurant kills at least five
incidents.description: At least five people were killed in a Moscow restaurant when a hand-carried improvised explosive device detonated on Aug. 2. No party has publicly claimed responsibility.

incidents.title: Ukraine negotiator tapped as intelligence chief
incidents.description: Ukraine’s chief negotiator, Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine Rustem Umerov, will now also lead Ukraine’s foreign intelligence efforts. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made the decision amid an ongoing reshuffle of senior government positions.

incidents.title: Taiwan completes hypersonic missile design
incidents.description: Taiwanese officials confirmed that Taiwan has completed the design of a hypersonic cruise missile, known as the Ching Tien. It could enter the production stage as early as next year.

incidents.title: U.S. expresses concern with Chinese coast guard operations
incidents.description: The U.S. State Department expressed concern with Chinese coast guard operations off the east coast of Taiwan, which have been taking place since June. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated the U.S.’s position of not supporting any change regarding Taiwan’s status.

incidents.title: China increases soybean purchases form U.S.
incidents.description: Asian traders have revealed that Chinese trading companies have purchased at least 1 million metric tons of soybeans from the United States. Increased soybean purchases were a key demand from the U.S. during the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in May, and the current purchase increase comes ahead of a subsequent Trump/Xi summit scheduled for late September in Washington, D.C.

incidents.title: India’s Russian crude imports hit record high
incidents.description: India imported a record 2.8 million barrels per day (bpd) of Russian crude oil in July, or 55.5% of total crude imports of just over 5 million bpd. That is up from 2.73 million bpd in June, and Moscow’s share has more than doubled from 23.4% in January.

incidents.title: Indian ship sunk in Red Sea
incidents.description: The MSV Faize Noore Oliya, an Indian-registered vessel carrying 13 Indian crew members, was hit by a projectile while transiting the Bab el-Mandeb on Aug. 4, capsizing and sinking off the coast of Yemen. The Yemeni coast guard rescued all 14 people aboard. Yemen's government attributed the attack to the al-Houth rebel group, though there has been no public claim of responsibility.

incidents.title: Brazilian presidential election polls tighten
incidents.description: Polling indicates leftist incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is in a statistical tie with right-wing Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro preceding October’s presidential election. A Nexus/BTG Pactual poll showed that in a potential second-round runoff, Lula would receive 46% of the vote compared to Bolsonaro’s 45%.

incidents.title: Infrastructure growth continues in West Papua
incidents.description: Minister of Public Works Dody Hanggodo announced progress in constructing a road connecting Jayapura, the largest city on West Papua’s coast, to Wamena, the largest settlement in its internal highlands. A surge of infrastructure spending in the restive region is intended to economically integrate the remote highlands area by increasing public mobility.

incidents.title: Migrants arrested in Mexico following detention center riot
incidents.description: Two Venezuelan migrants being held at a detention center in Chiapas were arrested on charges of rioting. The migrants allegedly displayed hostile behavior that led to an uprising throughout the center after demanding their release, claiming that they had experienced abuse and had been held without access to external communication.

incidents.title: Myanmar's detained former leader makes rare appearance
incidents.description: Myanmar’s military regime allowed a meeting between State Counselor Aung San Suu Kyi, head of Myanmar’s National Democratic League, and representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross. This marked her first appearance since being put under house arrest following a 2021 coup.

incidents.title: Hungarian nuclear plant forced to reduce power output
incidents.description: Hungary's only nuclear power plant was forced to reduce power production due to record-low Danube River water levels caused by severe regional drought and heatwaves. The plant generates 40% of the country’s domestic electricity generation. The reduction caused output to fall to around 10% of normal capacity, with Prime Minister Péter Magyar warning that worsening conditions could force the plant to shut down completely.

incidents.title: Sudanese army chief announces full advance
incidents.description: Sudanese Army Chief of Staff Yasir al-Atta told allied fighters, including defected Rapid Support Forces (RSF) soldiers, that the army is advancing on all fronts and vowed to eliminate all RSF fighters and allies from Sudan by the end of 2026. Al-Atta told allied forces they can choose which front they want to fight on.

incidents.title: Presidential candidate claims targeting by Russia-linked groups
incidents.description: Left-wing member of the European Parliament and potential presidential candidate Raphaël Glucksmann claimed he’s been the subject of fake news stories spread by Storm-1516, a propaganda network tied to Russian intelligence, Le Monde reported. An anonymous source talking to Le Monde said Storm-1516 had targeted former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, who is also expected to run in next year’s presidential election

incidents.title: French court rejects Russian journalist’s appeal to stay in country
incidents.description: Russian TV commentator Xenia Fedorova, who had been ordered to leave France after being accused of promoting Kremlin propaganda, lost her appeal of the decision. Fedorova denounced the order as “censorship” and said she intends to challenge the decision.

incidents.title: Legal professionals push AfD ban
incidents.description: Over 1,000 legal professionals have signed a letter authored by the Republican Lawyers’ Association calling on the German federal government to ban far-right political party Alternative for Germany (AfD). The letter argues that AfD policies violate constitutional principles of human dignity and democracy, adding pressure as Germany’s Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution continues to investigate the party ahead of September’s state elections.

incidents.title: EU forces board Russian shadow fleet vessel
incidents.description: An Italian-led EU naval detachment boarded a Cameroonian-flagged Russian shadow fleet vessel on Aug. 2, in the Mediterranean Sea near Sicily. The European crew conducted a search but lacked authorization to seize the vessel.

incidents.title: Trump calls off attacks in Iran
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he called off planned strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure on Aug. 2 at the behest of U.S. allies in the Gulf.

incidents.title: Acting attorney general rescinds “Anti-Weaponization Fund”
incidents.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinded the Trump administration’s push for the Anti-Weaponization Fund following weeks of negotiations with U.S. Senate committee members.

incidents.title: Trump calls off attacks in Iran
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he called off planned strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure on Aug. 2 at the behest of U.S. allies in the Gulf.

incidents.title: Military announces offensive against West Papua separatists
incidents.description: In response to the killing of five construction workers by the West Papua National Liberation Army, the Indonesian military has announced increased patrols aimed at targeting the separatist presence from the Papuan Highlands. This comes amid growing violence and displacement associated with the West Papuan separatist conflict.

incidents.title: Cuba’s electric grid collapses
incidents.description: Cubans experienced their sixth nationwide blackout of the year on Aug. 2. This followed a partial blackout in the western region of the island on Aug 1. as power outages have become increasingly common.

incidents.title: Sudanese Armed Forces attack court building
incidents.description: The Sudanese Armed Forces said they control the entire El Obeid-Khartoum Export Road, which connects the capital to El Obeid and eases supply movement for the army. RSF forces retreated west toward rear cities and continued to target the corridor with drones.

incidents.title: Talks begin between Venezuelan government, opposition
incidents.description: Representatives of Venezuela’s ruling party and opposition began a new round of U.S.-facilitated talks focused on democratic reforms and the restoration of political rights following the U.S. capture of former President Nicolás Maduro. U.S. officials participated as facilitators, while the talks brought together members of the National Assembly and former opposition lawmakers.

incidents.title: India approves floating solar scheme
incidents.description: The Union Cabinet approved a roughly $533.2 million program to install solar panels with 5,000 megawatts of capacity mounted on reservoirs and other inland water bodies.

incidents.title: Myanmar builds jet fuel refinery with Chinese investment
incidents.description: An investigation by the Myanmar-focused media organization DVB has found that the Myanmar government’s efforts to restore the Thanlyin refinery, a producer of jet fuel, to join already-operating Thanbayarkan refinery, are being facilitated by Chinese investment. Both facilities are currently under repairs to support jet fuel production and domestic demand for petroleum products amid international sanctions. The necessary industrial equipment and accompanying foreign direct investment to make the fuel is coming from a combination of Chinese-based petrochemical companies and state-owned fuel production enterprises, the investigation found.

incidents.title: Sudanese Armed Forces claim control over major road
Fighting erupts in Tigray
incidents.description: Fighting between the Ethiopian government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) has broken out in western Tigray, with each accusing the other of having started the clashes. This fighting comes a week after the TPLF declared the 2022 Pretoria ceasefire agreement “effectively dead.”

incidents.title: IRGC conducts attacks in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claimed attacks against at least three vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz on July 29. No casualties were reported.

incidents.title: North Korea warns against U.S. force increase in Japan
incidents.description: Lt. Gen. Stephen Jost, ⁠commander of U.S. Forces Japan, stated to the media that the number of U.S. personnel stationed at headquarters had increased by 215 people since last year to improve coordination with regional allies. North Korean media picked up on the news and warned that the expansion would lead to a clash on the Korean peninsula.

incidents.title: India approves offshore oil exploration scheme
incidents.description: The Union Cabinet approved a national offshore oil and gas exploration program with an outlay roughly $9.5 billion, running through fiscal year 2030-2031. The government expects it to add more than 600 million metric tons of oil in reserves and cut dependence on imported crude and gas.

incidents.title: U.S./Iran mediation efforts continue in Islamabad
incidents.description: Negotiations between Iran and the U.S. are continuing under Pakistani mediation according to the Pakistani Foreign Affairs Ministry, despite a recent escalation of the conflict across the Middle East.

incidents.title: China vows to expand global trade ties
incidents.description: China’s Politburo stated it was aiming to expand trade ties globally as it continues to grapple with a slowing domestic economy that is held up largely by its dominance in exports. This comes as the U.S. recently imposed extra 12.5% tariffs on Chinese imports related to alleged labor malpractices.

incidents.title: China announces Central Committee fifth plenum
incidents.description: China’s Politburo announced it would hold its fifth plenary session in October to discuss “Party self-governance.” The meeting is expected to address anti-corruption campaigns and self-discipline, core values that Chinese President Xi Jinping has put at the forefront of his governance style. This approach has led to multiple Chinese Communist Party members being purged and sentenced.

incidents.title: U.S. conducts large-scale attacks across Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran over the period of July 29-30 in retaliation for IRGC missile strikes against U.S. forces in Jordan.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran mediation efforts continue in Islamabad
incidents.description: Negotiations between Iran and the U.S. are continuing under Pakistani mediation according to the Pakistani Foreign Affairs Ministry, despite a recent escalation of the conflict across the Middle East.

incidents.title: Brazil denies visas to two U.S. State Department officials
incidents.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced his government denied visas to two U.S. State Department officials expected to meet with right-wing presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, who is challenging him in October’s presidential election. Lula accused the U.S. of election meddling, an allegation the State Department previously denied as “baseless lies.”

incidents.title: Brazilian federal police to investigate president’s son
incidents.description: Brazilian Supreme Court justice André Mendonça authorized federal police to investigate Fabio Luis Lula da Silva, the son of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, over suspicions of alleged influence peddling and corruption on behalf of businessman Antonio Camilo Carlos Antunes. Fabio Luis denied allegations that he ⁠provided Antunes' businesses with access to Health Ministry officials, and Lula said he will not interfere in the probe.

incidents.title: U.S. Senate advances sanctions package against Russia
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate voted to advance new sanctions legislation against Russia, an effort championed by U.S. Sen. Lindsay Graham shortly before his death.

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia, U.S. forces jointly target PMFs in Iraq
incidents.description: Saudi Arabia joined the war against Iran by conducting joint bombings with the U.S. against Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) positions in Iraq, killing at least 30, after PMF units conducted drone attacks against Saudi energy infrastructure.

incidents.title: Israel and Hezbollah exchange fire in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel conducted artillery bombardment across southern Lebanon following a Hezbollah drone strike against an unmanned Israeli bulldozer, threatening a fragile U.S.-mediated ceasefire.

incidents.title: Drone hits energy infrastructure in Egypt
incidents.description: U.S.-owned energy infrastructure in Egypt was hit by a drone on July 29, although the attack remains unattributed as of July 30.

incidents.title: Taiwan conducts joint coast guard patrol with U.S.
incidents.description: The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) shared a photo of a joint patrol held by the U.S. and Taiwanese coast guards, who were conducting search-and-rescue operations and maritime law enforcement operations. While not their first joint patrol, this was the first time the AIT shared a photo of the operations so publicly.

incidents.title: China and Russia complete two-week-long naval patrol
incidents.description: The Chinese and Russian navies finished a two-week-long joint patrol that ended in Vladivostok in eastern Russia. Chinese news media described the patrols as a routine part of the countries’ annual cooperation plan.

incidents.title: Opposition supporters march for elections and Machado’s return
incidents.description: Hundreds of opposition supporters marched in Caracas to demand free elections and the return of opposition leader María Corina Machado on the second anniversary of the disputed 2024 presidential election. Protest organizers said a political transition required new elections with guarantees for all political forces.

incidents.title: U.S. weighs delaying French ambassador to Washington
incidents.description: The United States considered delaying France’s nominee for ambassador to Washington, Aurélien Lechevallier, after French criticism of the U.S. vote against renewing the mandate of U.N. human rights chief Volker Türk.

incidents.title: Cuba eases restrictions on private sector
incidents.description: Cuban leaders announced economic reforms to the private and trade sectors, removing 46 of the 125 restrictions on private enterprise and loosening restrictions on another 35 measures. These changes affect the oil sector, electric vehicle imports, wholesale trade, and medicinal sales on the island and come as the country’s economic and humanitarian crisis deepens.

incidents.title: Ukraine launches large scale drone attack against Moscow
incidents.description: Ukraine conducted an attack against Moscow utilizing at least 390 unmanned aerial vehicles on July 28. All drones were intercepted, according to Russian officials.

incidents.title: Conservative influencer reverses position on Ukraine
incidents.description: U.S. conservative influencer and informal Trump advisor Laura Loomer has reversed her position regarding Ukraine and has urged Trump to provide it with support following a visit to the country and meetings with senior Ukrainian officials.

incidents.title: Iran fires at U.S. forces in Jordan
incidents.description: Iran fired missiles at U.S. forces in Jordan on July 28 in a barrage intercepted by Jordanian forces. No casualties were reported. The U.S. retaliated by striking dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets in Iran.

incidents.title: PLA constructing Taiwan government building replicas
incidents.description: According to Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense, China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is constructing full-sized replicas of Taiwanese military and government buildings at its military training sites, including replicas of the Presidential Office Building. Previous reports indicated the PLA had built similar replicas of Japanese government buildings.

incidents.title: Taiwan detains Nvidia worker in chip-smuggling probe
incidents.description: Taiwanese authorities have detained an Nvidia employee as part of an ongoing investigation into the smuggling of advanced chips to China.

incidents.title: China rebukes overcapacity claims
incidents.description: China’s Ministry of Commerce released a document titled “China's position on the so-called issue of 'overcapacity,’” rebuking claims made by the EU and the U.S. that the Chinese Communist Party is encouraging a “dump” of industrial overcapacity onto international markets. This comes as the EU is preparing new tariffs against Chinese imports.

incidents.title: Trump administration to cut Medicare drug subsidy program
incidents.description: The Trump administration will end the subsidy program aimed at maintaining Medicare prescription drug prices at current prices in 2027. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz wrote that U.S. health care insurers have enough experience with Medicare to accurately price their products without further government assistance.

incidents.title: Iran publicly executes protesters
incidents.description: Iran on July 28 publicly hanged two men who had been involved in the January 2026 protest movement. Amirhossein Safari and Abolfazl Sepahi were accused of killing four Iranian security personnel during the protests. Human rights groups said that the guilty verdict against Safari and Sepahi was based on a forced confession, made under duress. The execution triggered small scale protests.

incidents.title: Peru swears in first female president
incidents.description: Peru swore in Keiko Fujimori as its first elected female head of state. Fujimori had narrowly defeated leftist Congressman Roberto Sanchez in a June runoff election. Her presidency marks an extension of right-wing governance of the country. She has vowed to forge stronger ties with the U.S. and touted a tough-on-crime stance.

incidents.title: Sheinbaum responds to U.S. criticism
incidents.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum responded to criticism from White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller that Mexico’s judicial, political, and legal systems are ineffective due to cartel presence and power. In a press conference, Sheinbaum contrasted Mexico’s decreasing crime rates with U.S. drug use, money laundering, and narcotics distribution, arguing that these issues require the full attention and accountability of the U.S. government.

incidents.title: Mexico to pay U.S. mining firm less than 1% of arbitration demand
incidents.description: After U.S. quarrying firm Vulcan Materials filed an international arbitration claim against Mexico after the state halted Vulcan’s limestone extraction operations in Quintana Roo, it was awarded less than 1% of the compensation it originally sought after the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes tribunal only recognized the closure of one property of a Vulcan subsidiary and dismissed the company’s other claims.

incidents.title: Ukraine attacks Iranian ship in Caspian Sea
incidents.description: Ukrainian forces struck an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea after claiming the ship was transporting Russian military supplies. The strike killed at least one crewmember.

incidents.title: Trump hosts Zelenskyy at the White House
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump hosted Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the White House on July 29. Zelenskyy, who described the meeting in positive terms, said he offered the U.S. support in drone defense in the Middle East and requested an emergency air defense package for Ukraine in anticipation of the coming winter.

incidents.title: Trump hosts Netanyahu
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump hosted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House on July 28 to discuss possible courses of action including diplomatic resolution and military escalation to end the Iran war.

incidents.title: China urges U.S. tariff removal
incidents.description: In response to the U.S.’s imposition of 12.5% tariffs on Chinese imports due to alleged forced labor, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce has urged the U.S. to remove them.

incidents.title: China warns U.S. against AI sanctions
incidents.description: China warned it would take retaliatory measures against the U.S. if Washington decides to impose sanctions on Chinese AI companies. This follows remarks made by U.S. officials claiming that China stole U.S. intellectual property related to AI.

incidents.title: China starts domestic DUV lithography machine manufacturing
incidents.description: China has started developing its own domestically built deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines, a key component in the supply chain of semiconductors. The move sent shares of Dutch lithography maker ASML tumbling, as it challenges its dominance in the DUV production. China’s machines are expected to be delivered to leading domestic semiconductor manufacturers by the end of the year.

incidents.title: Trump says U.S. collected $13 billion from Venezuelan oil sales
incidents.description: President Donald Trump said the United States had collected more than $13 billion from the sale of Venezuelan crude oil since U.S. forces captured former President Nicolás Maduro and assumed control of the country’s oil exports in January. Trump said the proceeds were being held by the U.S. government and used to fund the Venezuelan government’s operating expenses.

incidents.title: India tests long-range missile
incidents.description: India successfully carried out the first flight test of its domestically developed Kusha long-range surface-to-air missile on July 23, launching from a test range on Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast. India currently relies on Russia’s S-400 system for long-range air defense, a gap the Kusha program is meant to eventually close, though full deployment is still years away.

incidents.title: U.S. faces critical mineral shortfall
incidents.description: Domestic supply constraints and a huge disparity between domestic production levels and industry demand make it unlikely that U.S. companies will be able to meet a Jan. 1, 2027, deadline to halt imports of critical minerals from China, industry analysts warned. The Trump administration has made domestic production of critical minerals a national security priority and invested tens of billions of dollars in private industry in an effort to reduce China's control of the global critical minerals supply chain.

incidents.title: Sudan opposition leader gives commanders autonomy
incidents.description: Sudanese Rapid Support Forces leader Gen. Muhammad Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo Musa told field commanders they now have the authority to launch attacks without central orders. This comes after an “emergency” meeting of the RSF Defense and Security Councils where Hemedti warned of informants and unauthorized filming of the battlefield.

incidents.title: Mexican president cancels La Parota dam project
incidents.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced July 27 the cancellation of a proposed hydroelectric project on the Papagayo River in Guerrero, which will be replaced by radial wells to provide drinking water and energy to Acapulco. Sheinbaum explained that the dam cancellation was due to increased concerns about rural displacement and environmental damage disproportionately impacting indigenous communities.

incidents.title: Bank of Indonesia governor resigns
incidents.description: Perry Warjiyo resigned as Bank of Indonesia governor for what he said were personal reasons. After his resignation, the Rupiah lost value, deteriorating from 17,900 to 17,980 per dollar.

incidents.title: Increase in crop failures plague Indonesian farmers
incidents.description: The El Niño climate phenomenon is worsening water shortages in Java, Tenggara, and Sumatra, and in turn causing crop failures. Rice cultivation is particularly affected, threatening rising food prices in the months ahead.

incidents.title: Merz proceeds with Cabinet reshuffle
incidents.description: Ahead of September’s state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, and Berlin and after parliamentary group leader Jens Spahn’s July 18 resignation, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced July 24 a major cabinet reshuffle. After replacing Spahn with his Federal Chancellery head Thorsten Frei, Merz appointed Health Minister Nina Warken to Head of the Federal Chancellery, Carsten Linneman as health minister, Franziska Hoppermann to secretary general, and Stephan Bilger to replace Transport Minister Patrick Schieder.

incidents.title: Ethiopia inaugurates UAE-funded defense laboratory
incidents.description: Ethiopian Defense Minister Aisha Mohammed inaugurated a United Arab Emirates-funded laboratory at the Ethiopian Defense University. The AI, cybersecurity, and defense-focused research building was constructed under the Ethiopia-UAE bilateral development partnership.

incidents.title: Ebola death toll in DRC rises to 1,405
incidents.description: The death toll from the Ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reached 1,405 people, with more than 3,200 people infected, government data released July 26 showed.

incidents.title: Canada/U.S. bridge opens
incidents.description: The six-lane Gordie Howe Bridge that runs from Detroit, Michigan, to Windsor, Ontario, opened to the public on July 27. The goal of the Canadian and American governments is to limit the costs and expedite the process for trade and tourism.

incidents.title: ICE plans increase in deportations
incidents.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials are preparing for an expected increase in deportations targeting Haitian migrants whose work visas are set to expire following the termination of their legal status. The new wave of deportations comes on the heels of the June 2026 Supreme Court ruling allowing the Trump administration to revoke the Temporary Protected Status of nearly 360,000 Syrian and Haitian migrants.

incidents.title: Brazil recalls its ambassador to Argentina
incidents.description: Brazil’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that it will recall its ambassador to Argentina, Julio Bitelli, and conduct diplomatic relations at a chargé d’affaires level until Argentinian President Javier Milei ceases verbal attacks on Brazilian officials. On July 25, Milei called President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a “thief” and “delinquent” at a presidential campaign launch event for Brazil’s right-wing presidential challenger Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro in Sao Paulo. This downgrade of diplomatic relations marks the lowest point for Brazil-Argentina relations over the past four decades of close political and economic ties.

incidents.title: Sudan army chief directs forces to advance offensive
incidents.description: Commander-in-chief of the Sudanese Armed Forces Gen. Abedel Fattah Abdelrahman al-Burhan directed his forces to press the offensive to the border of the Central African Republic. Planning for other targets has been made, according to SAF commanders.

incidents.title: Myanmar junta, resistance forces clash outside the capital
incidents.description: Myanmar’s People’s Defense Forces, under the command of the exiled National Unity Government, took a regime military checkpoint outside the capital along the Naypyidaw-Magway highway. The fighting resulted in nine casualties for the regime and is the latest in a series of skirmishes across Magway region, where the military holds administrative centers while ethnic armed organizations hold rural corridors.

incidents.title: Myanmar's exiled government briefs members of Congress
incidents.description: Officials of Myanmar’s exiled National Unity Government visited the United States on July 24 to brief members of Congress in an event hosted by the Burma Research Institute. The briefing covered the ongoing cyber scam enterprises along the Myanmar-Thailand border, and proposed a strategic partnership between the U.S. government and the Steering Council for the Emergence of a Federal Democratic Union moving forward. Alongside the briefing were calls to release State Counselor Aung San Suu Kyi, formerly elected by Myanmar and an international symbol for the country’s humanitarian progress.

incidents.title: Indonesia, South Korea deepen partnership
incidents.description: At the ASEAN Foreign Minister's Meeting in Manila, Philippines, South Korea's Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and his Indonesian counterpart, Sugiano, signed an agreement to deepen trade, particularly in energy, and to increase defense cooperation, especially in the area of shipbuilding.

incidents.title: One dead, 29 injured in attack on Berlin pride event
incidents.description: An attack on Berlin’s St. Christopher’s Day, an LGBTQ+ pride event drawing an estimated 1 million people, left one dead and 29 injured. Police shot dead the suspected assailant, 21-year-old Abdul Ballot, a Berlin native with ties to Islamist extremist groups.

incidents.title: Wildfires rage in southwest France
incidents.description: The area around the city of Bordeaux and the Cap Ferret peninsula have been devastated by wildfires, with authorities ordering the evacuation of around 220,000 people. The proximity of the fires to the city raised the risk of broader economic disruption, specifically to the wine industry.

incidents.title: Indian education minister resigns
incidents.description: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned July 25 after weeks of demonstrations demanding his removal over leaked medical school entrance exams. The protests, organized by a youth movement called the Cockroach Janta Party, had spread from New Delhi to other major cities and intensified after police used tear gas and batons on students.

incidents.title: India responds to new 10% US tariff
incidents.description: India’s Commerce and Industry Ministry said that the country landed in the lower of four tariff tiers under the new U.S. Section 301 measures, a flat 10% duty compared to the 12.5% level facing competitors like China and Vietnam. India reaffirmed its commitment to concluding the broader bilateral trade agreement with Washington.

incidents.title: Sudan armed forces recapture city, kill RSF general
incidents.description: The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces recaptured the city of Bara from the RSF after heavy clashes and killed RSF commander Maj. Gen. Abdel Abakar. This gain opened a new supply corridor for the military to the city of El Obeid and further reduced threats to the capital.

incidents.title: Fano National Movement rejects national dialogue
incidents.description: The Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM), an ethnic rebel group that seeks increased protections for Ethiopia’s Amhara people, rejected the ruling Prosperity Party’s National Dialogue conference, describing it as a political exercise to feign legitimacy rather than truly address the country’s deepening ethnic conflict. The group advised Amhara communities to intensify their armed struggle against the federal government.

incidents.title: Canada’s weighs retaliation for U.S. tariffs
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that “everything is on the table” regarding how to respond to U.S. President Donald Trump’s 50% tariffs on dairy, cars, and alcohol. Some provincial premiers called for aggressive action, including limiting exports of vital goods such as potash and critical minerals.

incidents.title: U.S. imposes new wave of tariffs
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Commerce has imposed new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on more than 60 global trading partners, including China, the European Union, and the Philippines. The move comes on the day that the 10% tariffs imposed under Section 122 of the U.S. Trade Act expired. The current tariffs fall under Section 301, imposed for alleged forced labor conditions, and have the potential to stay in place much longer.

incidents.title: U.S. escalates bombing campaign in Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. military conducted its 13th consecutive day of bombing in Iran as of July 24. U.S. defense officials said a B-1 bomber was used in attacks on July 21, marking the first use of the aircraft against Iran since the U.S. resumed the high-intensity bombing campaign.

incidents.title: U.S. continues bombing campaign in Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. military conducted a 13th consecutive day of bombing in Iran as of July 24. According to U.S. defense officials, a B-1 bomber was used in attacks on July 21, marking the first use of the aircraft against Iran since the U.S. resumed a high intensity bombing campaign.

incidents.title: China halts dual-use exports to EU
incidents.description: China has banned the export of dual-use components to 14 entities in the EU as retaliation for the bloc’s latest sanctions package against Russia which targeted 14 China and Hong-Kong-based companies.

incidents.title: Venezuela notifies U.N. of ICC withdrawal
incidents.description: Venezuela formally notified the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC) after repealing its ratification of the Rome Statute. Foreign Minister Félix Plasencia and acting President Delcy Rodríguez said the court had become politicized and unfairly targeted Venezuela.

incidents.title: Sudan army chief vows to “eradicate” RSF
incidents.description: Gen. Abedel Fattah Abdelrahman al-Burhan, commander in chief of the Sudanese Armed Forces, vowed to “eradicate” the rebel Rapid Support Forces and any group supporting them, stating there would be “no place for the rebel militia.” His rhetoric essentially ruled out any return to past agreements as international mediation in the country’s civil war has stalled.

incidents.title: Myanmar's parliament rejects ASEAN plan
incidents.description: Myanmar's Union Parliament unilaterally rejected the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) plan, a framework for ending Myanmar’s civil war and facilitating its return to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. The rejection came days ahead of the ASEAN summit, where the regime’s Minister of Foreign Affairs U Tin Maung Swe contradicted the regime reasserting Myanmar’s commitment to the 5PC plan, harming the government's credibility with ASEAN.

incidents.title: OFAC sanctions 55 individuals, entities linked to CJNG finances
incidents.description: With cooperation from the Mexican Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, the U.S. Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control identified and sanctioned 39 individuals and 16 companies allegedly affiliated with the financial operations of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG).

incidents.title: U.S. lifts ban on Mexican cattle imports
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture announced it would lift a ban on Mexican cattle imports, which had proved ineffective at preventing the spread of the New World screwworm infestation into the United States. Halting imports increased U.S. beef prices while screwworm cases were still reported on Texas and New Mexico farms in June.

incidents.title: U.S. imposes 10% tariffs on Indonesia
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced he will impose 10% tariffs on multiple top trade partners, including Indonesia, ostensibly over concerns about coerced labor. This undermines the tariff reduction deal that the U.S. and Indonesia signed last year and threatens to reduce Indonesian exports.

incidents.title: Foreign minister concludes Africa tour
incidents.description: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul wrapped up his third trip to Africa this year after diplomatic visits to Mauritania, Nigeria, and South Africa. Wadephul’s tours are part of Berlin’s strategy to deepen political, economic, and security ties on the continent in response to U.S. protectionism and a broader pullback from multilateral cooperation.

incidents.title: U.S. businesses, African Union urge White House to rethink Ethiopia’s exclusion from AGOA
incidents.description: U.S. business groups, including the U.S. Grains and Bioproducts Council, joined the African Union in recommending that the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump to stop excluding African countries from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) if it wants to seriously compete with China in Africa. Ethiopia has been excluded from this program since 2022 due to human rights abuses and undemocratic practices.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions target Cuba’s GAESA
incidents.description: New sanctions targeting Cuba’s military conglomerate GAESA and the government’s overseas medical missions have gone into effect. The sanctions against nine entities and two individuals tied to the Cuban government are aimed at GAESA’s efforts to evade existing sanctions.

incidents.title: Rubio meets with Lavrov in Manila
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Minister of Foreign Affairs Sergei Lavrov met on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila on July 23 to discuss peace efforts in Ukraine. During the meeting, Lavrov told Rubio that it was “unacceptable” for the U.S. to continue facilitating arms shipments to Ukraine.

incidents.title: U.S. and Saudi Arabia reach nuclear deal
incidents.description: The U.S. and Saudi Arabia reached an agreement that will see the kingdom construct nuclear energy facilities with the help of U.S. companies and technology. Trump said the deal does not involve uranium enrichment and is contingent upon Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords. Senior Israeli officials swiftly condemned the deal.

incidents.title: Taiwan resumes indigenous submarine program
incidents.description: Taiwan resumed tests of its indigenous submarine prototype, the Narwhal, following a near two-month pause.

incidents.title: China conducts two-day drill in Taiwan Strait
incidents.description: China launched a two-day live-fire drill east of Dongshan Island off China’s Fujian province in the Taiwan Strait. The drill is not unusual for this time of year, during which Chinese forces seek to test equipment and personnel during harsher summer months.

incidents.title: China fires water cannons at Philippine vessel
incidents.description: A Chinese coast guard vessel fired water cannons at a Philippine fishing vessel near the disputed Scarborough Shoal, two days after both countries summoned their respective ambassadors to complain about previous similar incidents.

incidents.title: Bab al-Mandab strait sees increased attacks
incidents.description: The Red Sea attack on a Saudi oil tanker on July 23 claimed by the Iran-backed al-Houthis widened economic and security risks beyond the Strait of Hormuz. In the aftermath of the attack, the price of Brent crude spiked to around $100 per barrel amid growing concerns over disruptions to Gulf energy exports. Since the beginning of the war in February, Saudi Arabia had been rerouting most of its oil shipment to Red Sea ports via the East-West Pipeline. Attacks near the Bab al-Mandab now threaten this alternative export route, increasing risks for energy shipments to Asia.

incidents.title: Ukrainian drone strikes Russian oil refinery
incidents.description: Ukrainian drone strikes have damaged critical Russian oil refinery infrastructure, forcing Russia to import refined products from India, after more than 30% of its refining capacity was disrupted. Ukraine's drone strikes have shut down almost a third of Russia's oil refining capacity causing domestic gasoline and fuel shortages. This domestic fuel crisis in Russia has prompted the country to implement these emergency trade measures to secure foreign oil products.

incidents.title: U.S. imposes 12.5% tariffs on Brazil over forced labor concerns
incidents.description: The U.S. has imposed a 12.5% tariff on 38 countries, including Brazil, due to concerns relating to lax enforcement of forced labor bans within supply chains. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva rejected these tariffs as “arbitrary” and “unjustified,” and stated that while he is open to bilateral negotiations, Brazil may seek other markets for its exports.

incidents.title: Mexican mayor assassinated
incidents.description: Unidentified gunmen shot dead Valentín Lavín Romero, mayor of Temoa in Mexico’s Morelos state, a few months after he had survived a prior assassination attempt. He is the country’s 14th mayor to be assassinated since President Claudia Sheinbaum took office in 2024.

incidents.title: Iran bombs Jordanian Red Sea ports
incidents.description: Iran missiles and drones targeted commercial assets at ports in Jordan’s Red Sea coastal city of Aqaba. Jordanian defense officials said no casualties resulted as of July 24.

incidents.title: Houthis launch missile strike against Saudi oil tanker
incidents.description: Iran-backed al-Houthi forces launched missile and drone attacks against a Saudi oil tanker transiting the Red Sea near Jizan, marking the first reported strike on Saudi commercial shipping since the group declared its naval blockade against the kingdom. The vessel was reportedly struck and caught fire, although its crew was unharmed. The incident demonstrates the Houthis’ willingness to enforce their blockade threat through direct attacks, increasing security risks along Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea energy-export corridor.

incidents.title: Houthis escalate against Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: The Yemeni al-Houthi rebel group declared a blockade against Saudi ports, and the closure of the Bab al-Mandeb on July 20 and have since fired on Saudi vessels attempting to navigate the passage.

incidents.title: Quad foreign ministers meet in Manila
incidents.description: The foreign ministers from the Quad countries, the U.S., Japan, Australia, and India, met on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila, where they stressed the importance of upholding maritime security in the Indo-Pacific. Notably, the talks did not single out China, likely due to the upcoming summit between the U.S. and China. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio hinted at another meeting taking place in 2026, tempering fears of the White House’s disinterest in the forum.

incidents.title: U.S. judge sets Maduro trial date
incidents.description: U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein scheduled a trial for former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, on drug trafficking charges to begin June 1, 2027. Both pleaded not guilty and continued to challenge the legitimacy of the proceedings.

incidents.title: Rubio criticizes Iranian negotiators
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iranian officials “don’t seem to be serious” about peace negotiations despite U.S. willingness to strike a deal.

incidents.title: Rubio, Chinese counterpart meet
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit, during which both sides discussed preparations for the planned September summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington D.C. China has not yet released a statement on the talks, and Rubio had previously expressed concern about China’s conduct in the South China Sea.

incidents.title: India, U.S. advance trade and defense agreements
incidents.description: Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met in Manila to discuss developments in the Middle East and Indo-Pacific. They agreed to finalize key defense agreements and emphasized completing an interim bilateral trade deal.

incidents.title: Canada becomes Global Combat Air Programme observer
incidents.description: Canada became the first country to be granted exclusive observer status to the joint Global Combat Air Programme among Japan, the U.K., and Italy. The move represents a major endorsement of the program, which already has garnered interest by other countries, including Australia and Saudi Arabia, and is seen as the only credible alternative to U.S.- and Chinese-led sixth-generation aircraft programs.

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia signs nuclear deal with U.S.
incidents.description: The United States and Saudi Arabia reached an agreement on a 30-year civil nuclear program that includes provisions for potential uranium enrichment. The agreement positions U.S. companies to lead the development of Saudi Arabia’s civilian nuclear program, with Westinghouse’s AP1000 reactor expected to serve as the reference design. The reactor generates approximately 1.1 gigawatts of electricity, enough to power a midsize city or a large AI data center. After the agreement was announced, Trump added a condition that its implementation would be contingent on Saudi Arabia normalizing relations with Israel, although the discussion remains ongoing. The deal also faces review by the U.S. Congress.

incidents.title: Sudanese drone strikes Chad
incidents.description: A drone launched from Sudanese territory attacked Chad for the fifth time in recent months. According to a Chadian official, the attack injured two children and destroyed vehicles and shops.

incidents.title: West Papua separatists claim execution of 3 civilians, police officer’s death
incidents.description: A statement from the West Papua National Liberation Army (TPNPB)claims responsibility for the execution of three Papuan civilians, who they identified as informants for Indonesian authorities, They also claimed responsibility for the death of a police officer. The rising pattern of separatist violence threatens to destabilize Indonesian state control over West Papua.

incidents.title: French president refuses environmental minister’s resignation
incidents.description: French Environment Minister Barbut remained in government after President Emmanuel Macron refused her resignation. She submitted it after parliament approved a farm bill allowing the temporary reintroduction of two pesticides suspected of harming bees.

incidents.title: U.S. sends humanitarian aid to Cuba.
incidents.description: The U.S. State Department said it sent a humanitarian assistance flight to Cuba with the first tranche of a $100 million aid package as the Trump administration maintained pressure on the Cuban government to enact meaningful regime change. The shipment included food and hygiene kits for 700 families.

incidents.title: Cyclosporiasis outbreak reaches 41 states
incidents.description: An outbreak of the parasitic infection cyclosporiasis has now been reported in 41 states with over 4,100 confirmed cases and over 7,000 unconfirmed cased reported.

incidents.title: China and Philippines summon ambassadors
incidents.description: China and the Philippines each summoned the other’s ambassador following an incident around the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, during which a Philippine sailor was reportedly struck on the head by a member of the Chinese crew.

incidents.title: Trump threatens Iranian infrastructure
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iranian bridges and power infrastructure in retaliation for attacks against international shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: Taiwan reports new Chinese gray-zone tactics
incidents.description: Taiwanese defense analysts have reported that China tested two new “gray zone” tactics around Taiwan, including a Chinese helicopter flying parallel to the Taiwan Strait median line, as opposed to flying across it and back, as well as a joint helicopter-drone air patrol. The new tactics could simulate the types of reconnaissance patrols needed in anticipation of a larger air assault operation.

incidents.title: Iran considers increasing domestic fuel prices
incidents.description: Iran is considering an increase to the cost of gasoline at Iranian fuel stations amid worsening economic hardship, according to Reza Sepahvand, a spokesman for the Iranian parliament.

incidents.title: Opposition protests force suspension of Parliament
incidents.description: Indian opposition parties protested in Parliament and demanded the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the leak of medical school entrance exam papers affecting approximately 2 million students. The disruption forced Parliament to suspend its session as student-led demonstrations intensified into the largest youth challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.

incidents.title: South Africa to build new AI data centers
incidents.description: Officials in Cape Town, South Africa, have approved the development of two hyperscale data centers that would draw 174 megawatts of electricity, paving the way for a massive expansion of computational power in the country. This project represents one of the largest new electricity loads to be added to an African power grid. It also reflects the growing importance of reliable electricity supply in attracting large-scale AI and cloud computing investment, following recent improvements in South Africa’s power sector. As AI adoption accelerates, electricity infrastructure is becoming an increasingly important factor in investment decisions, with expanding AI capacity likely to influence long-term planning for electricity generation and transmission networks.

incidents.title: IDF begins to hand over territory to Lebanese army
incidents.description: The Israel Defense Forces have begun a limited handover of occupied Lebanese territory to the Lebanese army as part of a “pilot zone program” mediated by the U.S. Under the program, the Lebanese army will assume gradual control of territory in southern Lebanon currently occupied by the IDF on the condition that Hezbollah is denied access to those zones.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy fires top military commander
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy fired Commander-in-Chief of Ukraine’s Armed Forces Gen. Oleksandr Syrskii following a series of mass protests in Ukraine amid a reshuffle of its senior civilian and military leadership.

incidents.title: Indonesia reduces role in fifth-generation fighter program with South Korea
incidents.description: Indonesia has announced it will not pursue an agreement with South Korea to build fifth-generation KF-21 fighter jets in Indonesia. It nevertheless confirmed it is still interested in purchasing the fighter when it enters production.

incidents.title: At least 2,025 excess heat deaths in France attributed to heatwave
incidents.description: Reuters reported that the late-June record heatwave produced at least 2,025 excess deaths and overwhelmed parts of the French funeral sector.

incidents.title: Ethiopia, Djibouti nearer to establishing one-stop border post in Galafi
incidents.description: At a two-day European Union-financed workshop in Bishoftu, Ethiopia and Djibouti agreed on a joint roadmap for the implementation of the planned Galafi One-Stop Border post between the two countries. Harmonizing controls on border crossings at the trade corridor that facilitates 95 percent of Ethiopia’s import and export trade would shorten border clearance times for goods substantially when operational.

incidents.title: DRC strengthens Ebola surveillance measures
incidents.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo announced new 21-day monitoring requirements for first responders and other individuals returning from Ebola-affected areas. The policy establishes different monitoring procedures based on exposure risk to strengthen outbreak containment and align the country’s response with updated World Health Organization guidelines.

incidents.title: U.S. sends humanitarian aid to Cuba
incidents.description: A U.S. cargo flight delivered 700 food and hygiene kits in the first tranche of a $100 million U.S. direct assistance package to Cuban citizens. Catholic groups distributed the aid, which is intended to bypass the regime.

incidents.title: Brazil, U.S. in dispute over instant payment system
incidents.description: U.S. Trade Representative Jameison Greer cited Brazil’s Pix instant payment system as part of the justification for new 25% U.S. tariffs imposed on Brazilian goods. Pix, operated by Brazil’s central bank, has grown in popularity in recent years and raised alarms for U.S. private financial institutions for its potential to replace credit card transactions.

incidents.title: U.S. gas prices reach $4 per gallon
incidents.description: Average U.S. gasoline prices climbed to over $4 per gallon following renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran. Brent crude prices have also increased from around $72 per barrel at the beginning of July to around $100 per barrel. Meanwhile, commercial transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen by about half in recent weeks, while higher diesel prices point to broader transportation cost pressures.

incidents.title: Russia strikes civilian craft near Odesa
incidents.description: At least 10 people were killed when Russian fire struck a civilian commercial vessel in the Black Sea near Odesa on July 20.

incidents.title: Japan protests China live-fire drills
incidents.description: Japan issued a formal complaint against China following joint Chinese-Russian live-fire drills held July 19 near Okinotori Island. China disputed the complaint, claiming that Japan has no right to declare the waters around the island as part of its Exclusive Economic Zone.

incidents.title: Lionheart Capital nears oil investment
incidents.description: Lionheart Capital moved closer to a $400 million investment for a stake in a Venezuelan oil field, potentially marking one of the first major private investments in the country’s energy sector since the United States began easing sanctions.

incidents.title: Ukraine shuts down Russia grain exports from Sea of Azov
incidents.description: Russian grain exports from the Sea of Azov have effectively been shut down by Ukraine’s ongoing drone campaign, according to the economic research consultancy, SovEcon, which estimates Russia’s overall wheat exports are down nearly 30%.

incidents.title: Indian crew killed in missile strike
incidents.description: The Indian Ministry of External Affairs said four Indian nationals were killed when a Russian missile struck the commercial vessel MV Golden Leo as it departed Ukraine's port of Odesa. The ship carried 17 crew members, five of them Indian, alongside Syrian nationals. India condemned the attack and summoned a Russian diplomat to express “grave concerns.”

incidents.title: Lithuanian defense minister warns of Russian sabotage threat
incidents.description: Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas warned that Russian President Vladimir Putin is seeking to escalate sabotage operations in the Baltic states and Poland.

incidents.title: No China rare earth exports to Japan in June
incidents.description: Chinese customs data showed that no rare earth elements were exported to Japan during the month of June. This follows a similar lack of exports in May.
