The Japanese private sector had previously warned of increasing risk of supply chain disruptions if these restrictions continue.

incidents.title: U.S. announces start of Venezuelan democratic transition
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Venezuela’s democratic transition process would begin in early August as Washington continued managing relations with acting President Delcy Rodríguez’s government. Supporters of opposition leader María Corina Machado continued pressing for her return from exile and a transfer of power based on the disputed 2024 election.

incidents.title: Brazil announces AI investments from Chinese and U.S. companies
incidents.description: Brazil’s government announced it would invest $444.2 million into its artificial intelligence sector, split between U.S. and Chinese companies. Of those investments, $250.9 million will fund a supercomputing infrastructure project built by China’s Huawei Technologies and iFlytek, and a separate $190 million will go to a supercomputer project bid expected to be won by U.S.-based chipmaker Nvidia. Brazil’s government said the infrastructure is intended to build large language models and bolster its strategic autonomy.

incidents.title: Sudan faces new U.S. sanctions
incidents.description: New sanctions took effect over unresolved allegations that the Sudanese Armed Forces used chemical weapons against the Rapid Support Forces. Sudan’s Foreign Ministry rejects the penalties as “unilateral and illegal.”

incidents.title: Resistance forces profit from Myanmar’s mineral trade
incidents.description: The Stimson Institute reported that the Ta’ang National Liberation Army began large-scale rare earth mining initiatives throughout the territory it controls, just one instance of Myanmar’s many armed resistance forces extracting minerals for revenue. Access to the lucrative $1.4 billion minerals market has prompted these groups to seek foreign investment and provide China up to 40% of their rare earths.

incidents.title: WHO warns DRC’s Ebola response is falling behind
incidents.description: The World Health Organization warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continued to accelerate as insecurity, attacks on health facilities, and unidentified transmission chains hampered containment efforts. The warning underscored the growing humanitarian and public health challenges facing the eastern DRC.

incidents.title: U.S. report accuses Cuba of infiltration campaign
incidents.description: The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump released a report accusing Cuba of sponsoring espionage campaigns on U.S. soil that it claims have promoted left-wing extremism and protests for the past five decades.

incidents.title: Chinese military activity increases in June
incidents.description: Taiwanese coast guard officials noted an increase in Chinese military activity around the island in June, with a rise of Chinese government-affiliated vessel detection from 30 vessels in May to 55 in June. As such, Taipei is reportedly planning to increase drills simulating defense against an attack from the Pacific Coast.

incidents.title: New stimulus measures expected at next Politburo meeting
incidents.description: China’s Politburo members are expected to speed bond issuance at their next meeting to address weak domestic consumption and inject additional stimulus measures. This follows data from last week indicating that Chinese economic growth fell short of expectations by 0.3%.

incidents.title: Iran bombs Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, kills U.S. soldiers
incidents.description: Iran conducted attacks against Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain over the course of the week in retaliation for ongoing U.S. bombardment. At least 3 U.S. soldiers died in an Iranian attack in Jordan.

incidents.title: IMF approves emergency financing for earthquake response
incidents.description: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez announced that Venezuela secured $346 million in emergency financing from the International Monetary Fund to support humanitarian relief following the devastating Caribbean coast earthquakes. The funding provided immediate financial support for recovery efforts as the confirmed death toll surpassed 5,000.

incidents.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange bombardment
incidents.description: Russia conducted one of the largest single-day bombardments of the war against Kyiv on July 20, while Ukraine retaliated with an attack against Moscow that used over 400 unmanned aerial vehicles.

incidents.title: Interior minister raises threat level
incidents.description: Alexander Dobridt, German minister of the interior, told newspaper Welt Am Sonntag that the “increased volume of reporting and intelligence” has led him to raise the national threat level from abstract to high. Dobrindt pointed to an increase of identifiable attack plans regarding infrastructure, individuals, and institutions and urged Germans to prepare for the risk of terrorist attacks.

incidents.title: Sudanese government blames drop in Nile levels on Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
incidents.description: Sudan’s Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation blamed reduced discharge from the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam for a drop in Nile River levels, saying lower water levels have disrupted pumping stations that supply drinking water to areas of the country. Both Egypt and Sudan continue to push for a transnational and legally binding agreement on dam operation due to their position downstream of the project.

incidents.title: United States threatens to impose 50% tariffs on Canada
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump blamed Canada for being unable to control their wildfires, which began to impact American cities, and “unequal treatment “of U.S. cars, dairy, and alcohol. In retaliation, he announced a 50% tariff on these goods that will take effect in August.

incidents.title: U.S. tightens foreign student visa requirements
incidents.description: The U.S. is tightening the duration of visas issued to foreign students, journalists, and cultural exchange visitors. China urged the U.S. to withdraw the decision, calling it discriminatory.

incidents.title: Rial continues to weaken
incidents.description: The Iranian rial fell to a new low against the U.S. dollar this week, with $1 equaling nearly 2 million rial. According to Iran International, the official Iranian monthly minimum wage is now equal to $87.

incidents.title: DHS Secretary threatened state election officials
incidents.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin threatened state election officials who refuse to verify voter eligibility with a DHS-run database with prosecution. A federal judge previously ruled that the DHS database could not be used to determine election viability.

incidents.title: Myanmar, India to define official border for reasons of security
incidents.description: India and Myanmar are soon set to complete a boundary demarcation agreement for a long-disputed 1.2-mile stretch of the border between India’s Manipur state and Myanmar’s Kabaw Valley. Growing migration out of Myanmar and insurgent activity crossing the border prompted more recent discussions that are fraught with ethnic tensions and histories that span both sides of the border.

incidents.title: Indonesia bolsters strategic energy reserves with Russian crude
incidents.description: Indonesia's Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry will increase its imports of Russian oil to increase its strategic energy reserves. This supports its multiyear effort to insulate Indonesia from conflict-driven oil shocks.

incidents.title: France summons Russian diplomat
incidents.description: France summoned the Russian Embassy’s charge d’affaires to condemn malicious cyber activities it attributed to Russia, particularly the Federal Security Service’s Centre 16.

incidents.title: African Development Bank approves funding for $110 million Ethiopia wind project
incidents.description: The African Development Bank (AfDB) approved financing of up to $110 million for the construction of a 300-megawatt wind project in Ethiopia’s Somali region that would be the largest in the country. The project, operated by AMEA Power, is expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 1.39 million tons while providing 1,525 direct construction jobs and over 35,000 indirect jobs.

incidents.title: Brazil, neighboring states sign open skies agreement
incidents.description: Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Chile signed the South American Air Liberalization Agreement (ALAS) to build a single aviation market inspired by the European Union. Signatories will have 12 months to draft the common rules for implementing the agreement.

incidents.title: Kremlin says no “immediate prospects” for peace talks
incidents.description: Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov expressed gratitude to Türkiye on July 15 over willingness to facilitate peace talks between Russia and Ukraine, but he said that there are no "immediate prospects” of Russia re-engaging in the diplomatic process.

incidents.title: Israel conducts airstrikes in Gaza
incidents.description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least five Palestinians across the Gaza Strip on July 16.

incidents.title: U.S. and Taiwan announce joint drone production
incidents.description: The U.S. and Taiwan have agreed to work together to jointly produce the Mighty Hornet I drone, currently in use by the Taiwanese Marine Corps.

incidents.title: TSMC announces additional U.S. investment
incidents.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company confirmed it would be investing an additional $100 billion to the U.S. to build additional advanced chipmaking plants in Arizona.

incidents.title: Wildfires spread across Canada and U.S.
incidents.description: Active wildfire activity across Canada and the western United States continues to degrade air quality over large parts of North America. Smoke from hundreds of ongoing fires has spread into the U.S. Midwest, Northeast, and mid-Atlantic, prompting health advisories and disrupting outdoor activities. The persistence of the wildfire season has also heightened political tensions over cross-border environmental impacts and emergency preparedness.

incidents.title: U.S. plans military action against Cuba
incidents.description: Officials in the Trump administration said planners have drawn up possible scenarios involving a military operation against Cuba, including airborne operations. While discussions on possible military intervention have been ongoing, the officials said this should not be taken as an indication of whether Trump will attack the island.

incidents.title: Pentagon assessing options for military action in Cuba
incidents.description: CBS News reported that the Pentagon has been examining options for military action against Cuba, including an Army-led air assault. Military officials speaking on the matter emphasized this was not confirmation that any U.S. military campaign against the island was imminent.

incidents.title: Canada suspends immigration sponsorships
incidents.description: In an effort to make immigration influxes more sustainable, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada paused sponsorship applications through the remainder of 2026 and increased asylum eligibility criteria. The agency is processing 60,000 applications with wait times for decisions ranging from one to three years.

incidents.title: Latvian president warns of Russian sabotage campaign
incidents.description: Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics said he has received intelligence that Russia aims to conduct a sabotage campaign against infrastructure in Latvia, Lithuania, and other NATO member states.

incidents.title: China’s economic growth falls short of expectations
incidents.description: China’s second quarter economic growth slowed to 4.3%, short of its official forecast of 4.6% and the lowest growth rate in three years. While the Chinese economy has proved itself resilient to trade repercussions from the Iran war and is held up by strong AI demand, weak consumption levels domestically have had an overall negative net effect for the past couple of months.

incidents.title: U.S. resumes Iran port blockade
incidents.description: U.S. naval forces resumed a naval blockade of Iranian ports and fired on at least one commercial vessel attempting to circumvent it on July 15, disabling the ship.

incidents.title: India, U.K. trade deal takes effect
incidents.description: The India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement has come into effect, cutting tariffs on thousands of goods and expanding market access in both countries. The U.K. is scrapping duties on nearly 97% of its tariff lines immediately, while India is removing tariffs on 64% of its lines and phasing out another 21% over the next 10 years.

incidents.title: U.S. expands scope of strikes inside Iran
incidents.description: U.S. forces carried out an intensified series of strikes in Iran over the week, expanding the geographic scope of the campaign beyond the pattern established after the signing of the June 17 memorandum of understanding.

incidents.title: U.S. mediates talks between Lebanon and Israel in Rome
incidents.description: Lebanon and Israel completed their sixth round of U.S.-mediated negotiations in Rome. An anonymous U.S. official described the talks, aimed at facilitating a handover of territory occupied by the Israel Defense Forces to the Lebanese army, as “positive.”

incidents.title: India raises diesel, jet fuel export taxes
incidents.description: India increased export levies on diesel and jet fuel for the second half of July as renewed fighting between the U.S. and Iran constricts global fuel markets.

incidents.title: India approves $13.3B chip push
incidents.description: New Delhi’s Cabinet approved the expansion of its national semiconductor program, committing $13.3 billion in new funding. Information Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the funds will support chip design, manufacturing, and packaging capacity, building on the first phase’s $10 billion incentive allocation from December 2021.

incidents.title: U.K. and Spain remove border checks in Gibraltar
incidents.description: The EU and the U.K. have formally agreed to remove all border checks between Spain and the British-owned Gibraltar, bringing the territory into the EU’s Schengen area. Officials hailed the new labor and growth opportunities from the agreement, which will affect the approximately 15,000 people who cross the border daily for work.

incidents.title: U.S. imposes 25% tariff on Brazil
incidents.description: The U.S. announced it would impose a 25% tariff on a wide range of imports from Brazil following months-long investigations by the U.S. Trade Representative into unfair trade practices under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act. Exemptions to the tariff would be made for imports of beef, coffee, rare earths, energy products, and aircraft and aircraft parts. The tariff will go into effect on July 22 with an additional probe of forced labor, possibly resulting in an additional 12.5% tariff. Brazil has rejected the decision and allegations of trade malpractices.

incidents.title: Russia intensifies attacks on Odesa
incidents.description: Russia conducted several strikes against the port city of Odesa in response to Ukraine’s intensified campaign against Russian maritime shipping.

incidents.title: U.S. resumes Iran port blockade
incidents.description: U.S. naval forces resumed a naval blockade of Iranian ports and fired on at least one commercial vessel attempting to circumvent it on July 15, disabling the ship.

incidents.title: Myanmar regime, EAOs come to the table
incidents.description: In Thailand, ASEAN Special Envoy to Myanmar led negotiations between several regionally entrenched ethnic armed organizations and a regime-appointed committee to promote dialogue between the military and resistance forces. Myanmar’s exiled National Unity Government was not invited to the talks, which reflected ASEANs’ support of the regime’s 100-day Peace Plan.

incidents.title: Vietnam, Indonesia agree to increase annual trade
incidents.description: Indonesia and Vietnam agreed to a five-year plan that included a goal of increasing annual bilateral trade by $18 billion by 2028. This is a continuation of Indonesia’s longstanding objective of deepening economic integration with fellow members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

incidents.title: Attacks on German rail climb 7%
incidents.description: German rail networks were subject to 2,200 cases of sabotage, arson, dangerous interference and metal theft since the start of 2026, an internal Deutsche Bahn report revealed, marking a 7% year-on-year increase. . The rail operator said the acts caused over 220,000 minutes of delay in the first half of the year.

incidents.title: Canadian wildfires degrade air quality
incidents.description: Toronto had the worst air quality in the world due to the hundreds of wildfires burning across the country. An extreme heat wave is making conditions worse in Southern Ontario, where most of the smoke has accumulated.

incidents.title: EU bans gold imports from Sudan
incidents.description: The EU has banned gold imports from Sudan in an effort to reduce funding opportunities for the country’s civil war. Gold has been found to be a source of revenue both for the Sudanese Armed Forces and the rebel Rapid Support Forces. However, most of the gold is estimated to be smuggled out of the country before reaching major redistribution hubs such as the United Arab Emirates, and analysts warned that the sanctions may not be as effective without enforcement by these hubs.

incidents.title: Iran conducts strikes against U.S. partners
incidents.description: Iran conducted attacks against Syria, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan and threatened to deny maritime commercial access to the Red Sea in response to a resumption of U.S. military offensive action in its territory.

incidents.title: Houthis threaten Saudi Arabia after airport bombing:
incidents.description: Yemen’s al-Houthi rebel group has threatened a "siege" against Saudi Arabia following a July 13 attack against the Sanaa International Airport. While the Houthis attributed the attack to Saudi Arabia, the internationally recognized government of Yemen claimed responsibility, saying it was to prevent the landing of an Iranian plane.

incidents.title: U.S. Senate plans for sanctions targeting Russian oil, gas sales
incidents.description: A bipartisan group of U.S. senators revealed plans for legislation that will enact new sanctions and tariffs on the top importers of Russian oil and gas.

incidents.title: Shell seeks drilling services for Venezuela gas project
incidents.description: Shell began soliciting bids for drilling services for its Dragon offshore gas development, with four wells planned beginning in the second quarter of 2027. The contract remains contingent on a final investment decision.

incidents.title: U.S. confirms shipment of Nvidia H200 chips to China
incidents.description: U.S. Undersecretary of Commerce for Industry and Security Jeffrey Kessler confirmed to Congress that exports of Nvidia H200 chips to China were underway. This comes after a recent announcement that Chinese telecom company ZTE Corp was the latest one to receive U.S. approval to receive the chips. China had been holding off granting purchasing licenses to its companies but last week told some they could do so in limited quantities.

incidents.title: Ukrainian defense chief’s firing prompts protests
incidents.description: Protests broke out in Kyiv and other cities across Ukraine following the dismissal of popular Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The dismissal resulted from a falling out between Fedorov and Ukrainian armed forces Commander-in-Chief Gen. Oleksandr Stanislavovych Syrskyi and comes as the country’s parliament voted to dismiss Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko amid an ongoing Cabinet reshuffle.

incidents.title: Top Chinese official visits North Korea
incidents.description: Wang Huning, chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, visited North Korea three days after North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song visited Beijing. The countries have been increasing reciprocal visits and working on deepening bilateral ties.

incidents.title: Sudan rejects U.S.-brokered peace proposal
incidents.description: The Rapid Support Forces accepted a three-month humanitarian truce but rejected Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) demands to withdraw from captured territories. The proposal, presented by U.S. Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos, calls for a 90-day humanitarian truce, a political process, a comprehensive ceasefire, and the start of reconstruction. The SAF also disagreed with portions of the proposal calling for a gradual withdrawal of RSF troops.

incidents.title: Mexico files legal complaints with U.S. over ICE custody deaths
incidents.description: Following the deaths of at least 14 Mexican nationals detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) this year, Mexico has begun filing criminal complaints with U.S. state prosecutors. Mexico sent cease-and-desist letters to the detention centers where the deaths occurred, and its foreign minister has contacted the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.

incidents.title: Germany joins allies in expanding air defense for Ukraine
incidents.description: At the 37-member Coalition of the Willing meeting in Paris on July 13, German Chancellor Friedrich Metz pledged to expand air defense support for Ukraine, joining allies in unveiling a new 10-nation anti-ballistic missile-defense coalition. Merz said German support for Ukraine was for the sake of freedom throughout Europe.

incidents.title: Parliament reviews DRC’s military modernization plan
incidents.description: The National Assembly began closed-door deliberations on a new 2027-2030 military programming law designed to strengthen and professionalize the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The proposal prioritizes predictable defense funding, military modernization, intelligence capabilities, and troop training, signaling a shift toward longer-term defense planning in response to persistent insecurity in eastern DRC.

incidents.title: Cuba's electrical grid collapses
incidents.description: Cubans experienced a nationwide blackout for the third time in nine days and the fifth time in 2026. This comes as the humanitarian crisis on the island deepens amid an intensifying U.S. pressure campaign against the Cuban government.

incidents.title: Brazil threatens reciprocal tariffs on U.S.
incidents.description: Brazil has called U.S. tariffs unjust and politically motivated as it pursues legal avenues for reciprocal tariffs. Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Viera criticized U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for blaming previously stalled trade negotiations on the ego of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

incidents.title: France to grant Ukraine licenses for weapons production
incidents.description: France will grant Ukraine licenses to domestically produce a wide array of French-designed weapons systems, including cruise missiles, glide bombs, and air defense munitions, French President Emmanuel Macron said.

incidents.title: France takes nuclear reactors offline
incidents.description: Iraq, Syria, and the United States are considering reviving a 500-mile oil pipeline to Syria’s Mediterranean coast, aiming to reduce reliance on the Strait of Hormuz. The pipeline originally connected the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk to the Syrian coastal town of Baniyas but was shut down in 2003 amid the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq and has been offline ever since. It had a capacity of 300,000 barrels per day, which could be expanded to 1 million, according to Iraq’s ambassador to the United States, Nizar al-Khairallah. The pipeline would give Iraq an alternative export route, reducing its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, through which 95% of its oil exports pass.

incidents.title: EU buys record amount of LNG from Russia
incidents.description: The European Union imported a record amount of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Russia's flagship Yamal plant in Siberia during the first half of 2026. The European Union spent an estimated $6.82 billion to purchase 9.89 million metric tons of LNG in the first six months of the year, an 18% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The EU is set to ban long-term Russian LNG imports on Jan. 1, 2027.

incidents.title: Trump notifies Congress of military action in Iran
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump formally notified Congress that he is resuming offensive military action against Iran on July 14. U.S. forces carried out an intensified series of strikes over the week, expanding the geographic scope of the campaign beyond the pattern established after the signing of the June 17 memorandum of understanding.

incidents.title: Trump threatens Iranian infrastructure
incidents.description: On July 15, U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to destroy Iranian bridges and energy infrastructure if the country’s leaders do not agree to a peace deal by the following week.

incidents.title: France to enact sanctions over Russian cyber ops
incidents.description: French Foreign Minister Jean Noel-Barrot said that he plans to summon Russia’s ambassador and that France is planning to enact new sanctions after a recent cyber campaign conducted against France and at least 11 other countries that Jean-Barrot publicly attributed to Russian intelligence services.

incidents.title: Sudan gold trade sanctioned by EU
incidents.description: European Council approved sanctions targeting Sudan’s gold trade including an import ban and restrictions on routing the commodity through third countries.

incidents.title: ASEAN break no-contact with Myanmar’s regime
incidents.description: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations has resumed contact with the military junta in Myanmar for the first time since it took power in a 2021 coup. During a meeting of ASEAN foreign ministers in Bangkok, Myanmar Minister of Foreign Affairs U Tin Muang Swe said the country’s former leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, was in good health and reassured them she will be cared for while under house arrest. The group also reaffirmed its commitment to the original Five Point Consensus plan to bring stability and humanitarian assistance to Myanmar.

incidents.title: Data shows improvement in Michoacán security
incidents.description: The Michoacán government presented data showing that the “Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice” has reduced homicide and crime in the state. According to security official Marcela Figueroa’s report, the daily homicide rate in Morelia, Michoacán, has dropped by 46% since January 2025.

incidents.title: Ukraine to produce French missiles
incidents.description: French President Macron said France would license Ukraine to produce French cruise missiles for its own defense, deepening defense-industrial cooperation between Paris and Kyiv.

incidents.title: Tigray region leaders announce collapse of 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement
incidents.description: Leaders of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front in Ethiopia’s breakaway Tigray region stated that the Pretoria Agreement, which ended the civil war between itself and the central government in 2022, has collapsed. The group accused the government of drone attacks and military movements and stated it was ready to respond with force.

incidents.title: Wazalendo regain territory in DRC after clashes with AFC/M23
incidents.description: Fighting eased in parts of Masisi and Kalehe in the North Kivu province, after several days of combat between Wazalendo fighters and Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebels. Reports indicated that Wazalendo forces had retaken several localities, allowing some displaced residents to begin returning to their homes.

incidents.title: DRC eases pressure on mining companies
incidents.description: Democratic Republic of the Congo President Felix Tshisekedi instructed state revenue agencies to avoid aggressive enforcement actions against mining companies, saying unpredictable tax measures and asset seizures could discourage investment. The directive reflects the government’s effort to increase state revenue while preserving investor confidence in the copper and cobalt sector, a cornerstone of the Congolese economy. Reuters reported that the order followed recent tax disputes involving major mining companies, including Glencore.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions Cuba’s Ministry of Tourism, other state-run companies
incidents.description: A new round of sanctions imposed by the U.S. Treasury Department targeted Cuba’s Ministry of Tourism and state-run corporations in the energy, trade, and transportation sectors. This expands the target of U.S. sanctions beyond military-linked entities to Cuba’s economic sector.

incidents.title: Germany buys drones for Ukraine
incidents.description: Germany reportedly has paid for 50,000 one-way attack drones worth $103 million for Ukraine. Delivery of the drones to the Ukrainian government has begun and is expected to be completed before the end of this year.

incidents.title: Sen. Lindsey Graham dies
incidents.description: U.S. Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina died suddenly of an aortic dissection. The loss of Graham, an electorally safe candidate whose seat is now contested in the impending midterm elections, has destabilized the Republican congressional agenda.

incidents.title: Typhoon forces Chinese cities to evacuate
incidents.description: Typhoon Bavi hit Zhejiang province, China, with 89 mph winds, forcing nearly 2 million people to evacuate. Zhejiang has canceled 400 flights, halted dozens of trains, and suspended schools, employment, and outdoor activities. The typhoon previously hit the Philippines, Tawain, and Japan before reaching China.

incidents.title: U.S., allies reaffirm South China Sea ruling
incidents.description: The U.S., the Philippines, and a dozen other countries issued a joint statement reaffirming the 2016 decision by the Permanent Court of Arbitration that found China has no legal basis for its territorial claims in the South China Sea.

incidents.title: Sudanese court sentences RSF leaders to death
incidents.description: Rapid Support Forces leader General Muhammad Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo, his brothers, and 13 other allied tribal members were sentenced to death in absentia by a Port Sudan court under the authority of the country’s recognized government. The charges are on the assassination of West Darfur’s governor Khamis Abbakar in June 2023 and war crimes of genocide and crimes against humanity.

incidents.title: Ethiopia OKs Chinese company’s $4 billion purchase of Allied Gold Corp.
incidents.description: Ethiopia approved a $4 billion acquisition by Chinese mining firm Zijin Gold International of Allied Gold Corp.(AGC), opening the door for a large-scale gold mining project at the AGC’s Kurmuk Mine in western Ethiopia. That approval followed regulatory approvals by Canada, the United States, and several other African countries.

incidents.title: Iraq and U.S. consider repairing Syrian oil pipeline
incidents.description: Iraq, Syria, and the United States are considering reviving a 500-mile oil pipeline to Syria’s Mediterranean coast, aiming to reduce reliance on the Strait of Hormuz. The pipeline originally connected the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk to the Syrian coastal town of Baniyas but was shut down in 2003 amid the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq and has been offline ever since. It had a capacity of 300,000 barrels per day, which could be expanded to 1 million, according to Iraq’s ambassador to the United States, Nizar al-Khairallah. The pipeline would give Iraq an alternative export route, reducing its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, through which 95% of its oil exports pass.

incidents.title: Trump threatens Iran after threats of assassination
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to “decimate and destroy all areas of Iran” if there was an assassination attempt against him. Trump issued this threat after a written statement from Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei vowed to exact vengeance against Trump personally. The Iranian government has made calls for violence against Trump a routine part of its domestic messaging, including during Friday prayer. services.

incidents.title: Housing bill becomes law without Trump’s signature
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump allowed a contested bill aimed at lowering housing costs to become law without his signature. The enactment comes after months of negotiations during which Trump promised to veto the bill unless Congress passed a voter ID law that detractors claim amounts to voter suppression.

incidents.title: India and New Zealand deepen defense ties
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited New Zealand, where the two countries announced a new “strategic partnership” in defense and security as part of a broader deepening of ties. The partnership will see more frequent joint naval exercises and comes as India is looking to shore up ties with countries throughout the Indo-Pacific.

incidents.title: Indonesia's top anticorruption prosecutor resigns
incidents.description: Febrie Adriansyah, Indonesia’s chief anticorruption prosecutor, resigned after police seized $20 million in cash plus several kilograms of gold bars, some of which was found in his home. Prior to the raid, he was investigating the National Nutrition Agency, a signature initiative of President Prabowo Subianto marred by corruption allegations. Febrie’s arrest has divided Indonesian public opinion, with supporters questioning the motives behind the raid. Adriansyah has not been charged with a crime.

incidents.title: Iranian officials call for unity and vengeance
incidents.description: Iranian officials are using the themes of vengeance against U.S. President Donald Trump in domestic messaging meant to have a unifying effect on the Iranian population. Government officials have declared that Friday prayer services throughout the country will be referred to as “Fridays of Blood and Vengeance."

incidents.title: Iranians struggle to afford basic living expenses
incidents.description: Analysis conducted by the independent agency EcoIran estimated that millions of Iranian families still struggle to cover costs of food, rent and other basics because of dire rates of inflation, wartime conditions, and lack of adequate government subsidies.

incidents.title: Report: Cartel war hasn’t slowed fentanyl exports from Mexico
incidents.description: A recent report revealed that fentanyl shipments to the United States have remained stable despite an ongoing war within the Sinaloa cartel in Mexico. In the two years since the fracturing of the Sinaloa cartel following the capture of leader Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada in July 2024, the Mexican state of Sinaloa has recorded over 3,000 deaths, nearly tripling its previous annual homicide toll, due to ongoing conflict between cartel factions.

incidents.title: Cuba’s power grid suffers second collapse in a week
incidents.description: Cuba has experienced its second nationwide blackout of the week and its fourth of the year. Power outages have become increasingly common since January, when the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump imposed a blockade cutting off the oil imports.

incidents.title: Wildfires in Canada Spread
incidents.description: Pushed by gusty winds, three wildfires in Brunswick in British Columbia have grown to roughly 200 square kilometers. As firefighters struggle to gain control of the blazes, evacuations have proceeded and homes have been destroyed.

incidents.title: U.S. to grant Ukraine license to produce Patriot systems
incidents.description: While meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Ankara on July 8, Trump said the U.S. will grant Ukraine a license to produce its own Patriot missile systems.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Russian fuel storage facilities
incidents.description: Ukrainian drone strikes hit Russian oil platforms over 500 kilometers away from the Ukrainian-Russian border.

incidents.title: Putin orders fuel subsidies in Crimea
incidents.description: On July 8, Russian President Vladimir Putin directed the Russian government to provide fuel subsidies for Russian citizens in Crimea amid a sharp increase in prices because of Ukraine’s escalated drone campaign in the occupied territory. That same day, Russia enacted a month-long prohibition on diesel exports.

incidents.title: Iran attacks Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain
incidents.description: Iranian forces conducted long-range strikes against at least 85 individual targets in Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, and Bahrain, including U.S. military positions, according to a statement from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

incidents.title: U.S. delegation heads to Beirut
incidents.description: U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa said a U.S. delegation is expected to arrive in Beirut in the coming days to advance the implementation of a “pilot program” that will see the Israel Defense Forces turn over small pockets of Lebanese territory it currently occupies to the Lebanese army.

incidents.title: Iran holds funeral for Khamenei
incidents.description: Iran completed a weeklong state funeral and burial process for late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei that stretched across Iran and into Iraq. The funeral also featured several political rallies in which prominent Iranians called for the death of U.S. President Donald Trump.

incidents.title: Iran strikes US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait
incidents.description: Iran launched missile and drone strikes against U.S. military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait in response to a wave of U.S. airstrikes on Iran that were made after attacks on commercial oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. also canceled a license that Iran had been granted to sell oil.

incidents.title: Ukraine steps up attacks against Russian shipping
incidents.description: Ukraine intensified its strike campaign against energy targets and maritime shipping routes in and near Russian-occupied Crimea and against Russian shadow fleet vessels in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

incidents.title: AfD re-elects party leaders amid 50,000 protesters
incidents.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany party (AfD) held its two-day federal party conference in Erfurt with delegates re-electing Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla as co-leaders for the next two years. Police estimated around 50,000 demonstrators turned out for the conference in one of the largest anti-AfD mobilizations this year, as the party positions itself ahead of the September state elections.

incidents.title: Le Pen leads in presidential polls
incidents.description: Opinion polls showed far-right candidate Marine Le Pen leading the 2027 presidential field despite her EU embezzlement conviction, with surveys projecting her ahead in the first round and competitive or winning in run-off scenarios.

incidents.title: Bank of France foresees higher growth
incidents.description: The Bank of France revised its estimate for second-quarter growth upward to 0.2%, citing stronger June activity in services, industry, and construction despite disruptions imposed by this summer’s European heatwave.

incidents.title: Economic opportunities for Canada, Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney traveled to Saudia Arabia to discuss bilateral trade opportunities with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Both leaders are seeking to expand their influence in culture and economics.

incidents.title: Brazil tightens online betting advertising regulations
incidents.description: Brazilian Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that online betting companies must adhere to new strict advertising regulations. Health warnings and removal of claims that betting offers easy money are now required.

incidents.title: Trump says U.S. open to buying Ukrainian drones
incidents.description: During the NATO summit on July 8, U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. would consider buying Ukrainian drones. Trump also praised Ukraine’s defense industry, saying that it was “amazing” they could produce so many drones in wartime conditions.

incidents.title: Repeated Russian bombardments hit Kyiv
incidents.description: Russian bombardments of Kyiv killed at least 30 people between July 6 and July 8, while Russian strikes in the Black Sea city of Odesa killed at least four people on July 8.

incidents.title: Ukraine escalates campaign against Russian shadow fleet
incidents.description: Ukraine struck at least 21 Russian vessels, including 19 vessels associated with Russia’s shadow fleet, primarily in the Sea of Azov.

incidents.title: Trump says MOU with Iran is over
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said that the memorandum of understanding between Iran and the United States to end the war was “over,” and U.S. forces conducted two days of strikes against military targets inside Iran.

incidents.title: Iran conducts attacks in Strait of Hormuz; Trump threatens new blockade
incidents.description: Iran conducted a series of attacks against commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz on July 7. In response, U.S. President Donald Trump ordered airstrikes in Iran and threatened to reinstate a blockade of Iranian ports.

incidents.title: U.S. to lift state sponsor of terror designation for Syria
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump told Syrian President Ahmed al-Shaara on July 8 that he has decided to remove Syria’s designation as a sponsor of terrorism. The designation will officially be lifted following a 45-day review period by the U.S. Congress.

incidents.title: U.S. to lift sanctions on Türkiye, considers F-35 sales
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would lift sanctions on Türkiye while meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan during the NATO summit and that while he was undecided on the decision to sell F-35 fighter jets to Türkiye, he was “inclined” to do so.

incidents.title: China test fires nuclear-capable missile
incidents.description: China fired a nuclear-capable ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine. While the U.S., along with Japan and Australia, confirmed they had received advance warning of the test, they all criticized Beijing for the short notice, which the U.S. stated falls short of standards for nuclear countries.

incidents.title: ICE agents kill motorist in Houston
incidents.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers (ICE) killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujoa, a Mexican national, following a traffic stop in Houston. Statements made by an agency spokesman claim Araujo attempted to evade arrest, a claim also made to justify shootings in similar cases. Body cam footage has not yet been released, pending an FBI investigation.

incidents.title: Venezuela seeks sanctions relief as quake death toll rises
incidents.description: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez renewed calls for international sanctions on Venezuela to be lifted, arguing that access to frozen overseas assets would help finance earthquake recovery efforts. National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez said the death toll from the June 24 earthquakes had risen to 3,811, with 16,740 people injured and 17,907 displaced.

incidents.title: Trump says MOU with Iran is over
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said that the memorandum of understanding between Iran and the United States to end the war was “over,” and U.S. forces conducted two days of strikes against military targets inside Iran.

incidents.title: Japanese, Chinese vessels face off near disputed islands
incidents.description: A Japanese fishing boat clashed with two Chinese coast guard vessels near the disputed Senkaku/Diaoyu islands.

incidents.title: U.S. charges Indian gang leader
incidents.description: Federal indictments unsealed in Los Angeles charged Lawrence Bishnoi, the head of an Indian criminal gang currently incarcerated in India, and his North American deputy Satinderjeet Singh with directing the June 2023 murder of Canadian Sikh separatist leader Hardeep Singh Nijjar outside a temple in Surrey, British Columbia.

incidents.title: Graham Platner drops out of Maine Senate election
incidents.description: Democrat Graham Platner ended his campaign for U.S. Senate in Maine after a woman he previously dated accused him of sexual assault. At an emergency meeting following Platner’s resignation, the Democratic Party in Maine agreed to hold a convention to name a nominee in the race against Republican incumbent Susan Collins in November.

incidents.title: Iran conducts attacks in Strait of Hormuz; Trump threatens new blockade
incidents.description: Iran conducted a series of attacks against commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz on July 7. In response, U.S. President Donald Trump ordered airstrikes in Iran and threatened to reinstate a blockade of Iranian ports.

incidents.title: NATO pledges cooperation with Indo-Pacific partners
incidents.description: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte met with top officials from Australia, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea, also known as the Indo-Pacific Four (IP4), during the NATO summit in Ankara, Türkiye, where they pledged to expand cooperation in their defense industries and advanced technology development.

incidents.title: China to grant permission to purchase H200 chips
incidents.description: Chinese officials have told several Chinese companies, including ByteDance, Alibaba, and DeepSeek that they may soon receive permission to purchase Nvidia’s H200 chips from the U.S., marking a break in China’s policy of not wanting to rely on foreign tech imports. The U.S. had greenlit sales of the H200 chips to Chinese firms earlier this year, though no sales have since gone through due to stalling from Beijing.

incidents.title: Trump denies discouraging Machado’s return to Venezuela
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump denied reports that he had discouraged Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado from returning to Venezuela following the June 24 earthquakes. Trump said he had not told Machado to stay away and described her as “a good person” amid speculation that her return could challenge interim President Delcy Rodríguez.

incidents.title: Sudan armed forces recapture border town
incidents.description: The Sudanese Armed Forces recaptured the town of Kurmuk, close to the Sudanese border with Ethiopia, ending 3 ½ months of control by the Rapid Support Forces.

incidents.title: Myanmar presidential makes landmark Laos visit
incidents.description: President Min Aung Hlaing made his first state visit to Laos since taking elected office in April with a goal of deepening bilateral cooperation. The heads of state discussed shared regional concerns and deepened commitments to the Laos-Myanmar Joint Committee.

incidents.title: Ethiopia’s Abiy downplays threat of accused collaboration between regional rivals
incidents.description: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed played down the danger of any alleged alliance among Eritrea, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, and Sudan. Abiy told the Ethiopian Parliament that the government is improving its military capabilities to counter any threat such a partnership could impose.

incidents.title: Landslide kills three in Kerala
incidents.description: A landslide in India’s Kerala state killed at least three workers, injured seven, and left seven missing after 265 milimeters (~10.5 inches) of rain fell in 24 hours.

incidents.title: India, Indonesia sign missile deal
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto signed several agreements in Jakarta on July 7, including a defense contract for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile, an Astra missile deal, and memorandums of understanding covering critical minerals, agriculture, steel supply chains, and maritime security.

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia plans oil pipeline expansion
incidents.description: Saudi Aramco plans to expand the capacity of the East-West Pipeline, which connects the Abqaiq oil fields near the Arabian Gulf to the Red Sea port city of Yanbu. The crude oil pipeline, originally built in 1980 after the Iran-Iraq War, can transport up to 7 million barrels per day. It remains unclear whether the planned expansion would include upgrading the existing infrastructure or constructing a new pipeline. Neighboring Gulf countries could benefit from the project, especially those without the ability to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: Nine Pakistani police officers killed in Balochistan
incidents.description: Assailants killed nine police officers in Balochistan province. While no group claimed responsibility, Pakistani forces killed 15 members of the Pakistani Taliban in response. The incident comes after a May attack, attributed to the Balochistan Liberation Army, targeted a train carrying military personnel, killing 20, as well as cross-border drone strikes by the Afghan Taliban.

incidents.title: Bombs detonated in Damascus during Macron visit
incidents.description: At least two bombs were detonated in Damascus, Syria, on July 7 near a hotel where French President Emmanuel Macron was spending the night. At least 18 people were wounded in the attacks, which remain unattributed.

incidents.title: Netherlands, China discuss Nexperia ownership
incidents.description: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma hailed discussions with China over ownership of Chinese chipmaker Nexperia. His visit to China marks the first by a Dutch trade minister since 2018 and comes as the Netherlands is facing renewed pressure from the U.S. to further restrict Chinese access to advanced lithography machines from Dutch company ASML.

incidents.title: Ethiopia reports record export revenue
incidents.description: Ethiopia reported record earnings from exports for the fiscal year that ended July 7, claiming $10.7 billion in export revenue, which surpassed targets set by the government. Officials attributed the export growth to the expansion of the manufacturing sector and strong worldwide demand for Ethiopian agricultural goods.

incidents.title: Brazil's foreign minister warns of U.S. military intervention
incidents.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira warned Brazil’s Chamber of Deputies that the United States could unilaterally conduct military operations in Brazil. These fears have mounted following the White House’s May 29 designation of the criminal groups Primeiro Comando da Capital and Comando Vermelho as “foreign terrorist organizations.”

incidents.title: Japan warns of critical minerals shortage
incidents.description: Japan’s corporate and private sectors are warning of the heightened risks of critical minerals shortages as China shows no signs of easing its export restrictions against the country.

incidents.title: Armernian PM visits Russia
incidents.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan visited Yekaterinburg, Russia, to take part in an annual industrial exposition. The visit comes after Armenian elections in which Pashinyan’s party secured a victory on a pro-Western platform, beating the pro-Russian parties running for election. In response, Russia accused the West of interfering in Armenia’s elections and imposed import restrictions on Armenian products. Pashinyan said he hopes to develop further relations with Russia despite recent disagreements and rising tensions.

incidents.title: China, Russia hold naval drills
incidents.description: China and Russia launched a weeklong joint naval drill from the port of Qingdao, in China’s eastern Shandong province, emphasizing force assembly, harbor-based planning, and at-sea operations.

incidents.title: Mexican security forces kill 10 following attack on naval personnel
incidents.description: After an explosive device attack on a Mexican naval group monitoring water levels in Sinaloa left one dead and two injured, security forces forcefully prevented a second attack, resulting in the deaths of 10 assailants and the arrest of three others.

incidents.title: India and Indonesia deepen investment, trade, and defense integration
incidents.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed several economic and defense deals during Modi’s visit to Indonesia. India pledged to increase investments in Indonesian agriculture and critical minerals. In addition, Indonesia finalized a deal to buy cruise missiles from BrasMos, a joint Indian-Russian arms manufacturer.

incidents.title: IMF releases loan money to Ethiopia as fuel hikes, inflation blunt its impact
incidents.description: Money from the International Monetary Fund’s $464 million loan to Ethiopia is now flowing into the country’s coffers. However, policymakers have raised concerns that growing inflation and Middle East fuel chain disruptions will limit the benefit of the funds. This loan brought total IMF support for Ethiopia to roughly $2.65 billion.

incidents.title: Cuba’s electric grid collapses
incidents.description: Cuba’s energy grid collapsed for the third time this year as its fuel stocks dwindle following the deposition of Venezuela’s Nicolás Maduro and the subsequent U.S. oil blockade.

incidents.title: Canada to procure German submarines
incidents.description: Canada will procure up to 12 submarines from German shipbuilder ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced. Although the deal is still under negotiation, he indicated one submarine will be delivered by 2034, with a total of four being delivered by 2036.

incidents.title: Brazilian Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro to lobby Washington for tariff delay
incidents.description: Following a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods by the United States, presidential candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro plans to travel to the U.S. to urge the delay of these tariffs after the October election. Bolsonaro’s announcement comes as he tries to downplay his association with the U.S. presidential administration and unpopular tariffs on Brazil.

incidents.title: Wildfires spread across southern Europe
incidents.description: Wildfires spread across Portugal, Greece, and Spain, prompting large-scale firefighting operations and evacuations. Toxic smoke also affected parts of northern Greece, while strong winds and dry conditions continued to complicate containment efforts.

incidents.title: Venezuela marks Independence Day
incidents.description: Venezuela marked its 215th Independence Day as the country continued to respond to the deadly June 24 earthquakes. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez sought to project strength during a military ceremony, while critics accused the government of mismanaging the disaster response and slowing foreign aid.

incidents.title: Taiwan resumes “anti-communist” classes
incidents.description: In light of China’s increased military activity, the Taiwanese military is reintroducing “anti-communist” classes as part of its academic curriculum, lessons that had been on hold for the past 25 years.

incidents.title: OPEC+ increases oil production schedule
incidents.description: OPEC+ approved increasing output quotas by an additional 188,000 barrels per day for August as oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz had begun recovering after months of war-related disruptions. Although the group has raised quotas by nearly 800,000 bpd since April, oil production remains below prewar levels. Despite this, oil prices had fallen to around $72 per barrel after the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding, growing production outside of the Middle East, and diminished Chinese demand, prompting Iraq to demand higher production quotas.

incidents.title: Fiji, Australia sign defense agreement
incidents.description: Fiji signed its first ever defensive pact with Australia. Dubbed the “Ocean of Peace Alliance” it calls on both countries to come to the other’s aid if either is attacked. Australia has sought to curtail China’s influence in the Pacific.

incidents.title: Far-right group marches during D.C. Independence Day celebrations
incidents.description: The white supremacist movement Patriot Front held a march in Washington, D.C., during July 4 celebrations. No violence was reported during the march.

incidents.title: Indonesia increases military presence in West Papua
incidents.description: Indonesia has significantly increased the size of its military presence in West Papua in response an increase in separatist attacks, including a shootdown of a cargo plane and the killing of its pilot. This deployment has drawn protests from Catholic clergy and civil society groups worried about the risk of military violence against Papuan civilians.

incidents.title: Germany strikes weapons deal with U.S.
incidents.description: German Chancellor Frederich Merz told the Bundestag that Germany had struck a deal with the United States to purchase Tomahawk cruise missiles and ground-based Typhon launchers to be German-owned and operated.

incidents.title: China deploys coast guard to Taiwan’s east coast
incidents.description: China deployed coast guard vessels to waters east of Taiwan for the second time in two months. While the vessels stayed outside of restricted waters, the move constitutes an expansion of China’s patrolling zones, which Taiwan calls illegal and disruptive. The previous such patrol in June, launched in response to talks between Japan and the Philippines regarding their maritime boundaries, drew criticism from the U.S. and European countries alike.

incidents.title: Xi promotes officers
incidents.description: President Xi promoted two high-ranking military officers to general as the Central Military Commission seeks to fill in the vacancies left by recent purges amid an anti-corruption campaign.

incidents.title: Trump holds call with Putin
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on July 4 ahead of the NATO summit in Ankara, Türkiye. According to Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov, Trump offered to mediate a deal between Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to end the war. Ushakov described the call as constructive and “businesslike.”

incidents.title: Trump calls for new voter restriction law
incidents.description: In a July 4 speech, U.S. President Donald Trump called for a new round of voter verification laws that detractors claim are an attempt at voter suppression ahead of the midterm elections.

incidents.title: DRC opposition delays march protesting constitutional rewrite
incidents.description: Opposition coalition C64 postponed a planned demonstration against the revision of the Democratic Republic of the Congo Constitution after agreeing to consultations facilitated by Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye in his capacity as African Union chair. The delay temporarily reduced political tensions, while keeping constitutional reform at the center of national debate.

incidents.title: Iran warns against attacks during Khamenei’s funeral
incidents.description: Iran warned the U.S. and Israel of “harsh retaliation” if any strikes should occur against the state funeral of the former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, scheduled for July 2. st Status quo

incidents.title: IRGC clashes with Kurdish groups
incidents.description: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported killing five armed Kurdish militants during a firefight in northwest Iran on July 2.

incidents.title: India, Japan agree to expand cooperation
incidents.description: India and Japan agreed to deepen cooperation in artificial intelligence, metals, energy, defense, and economic security following talks between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in New Delhi. The countries also agreed to develop a joint roadmap on economic security as part of broader efforts to strengthen their strategic partnership.

incidents.title: Russia escalates bombardment of Kyiv
incidents.description: Russian overnight bombardment of Kyiv killed at least 20 people on July 2. Russian officials claimed that the attacks were retaliation for a series of recent Ukrainian strikes in Moscow.

incidents.title: Israel to sustain Syria, Lebanon and Gaza occupations indefinitely
incidents.description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said July 1 that Israel will maintain its occupations in Syria, Lebanon, and Gaza “indefinitely.” The comments follow recent Israeli incursions into Syria, beyond the territory it currently occupies.

incidents.title: U.S.-Iran talks conclude in Doha
incidents.description: Two days of talks between the U.S. and Iran concluded in Doha on July 2. Neither side cited meaningful progress following the indirect negotiations.

incidents.title: China halts iron imports from Australian firm
incidents.description: China Mineral Resources Group, the main iron ore purchasing company in China, has issued orders to its mills not to accept any deliveries from Australian mining company Fortescue. China is using Fortescue’s latest introductions of low-grade products to justify greater controls on the company’s exports.

incidents.title: BYD foreign sales increase year-on-year
incidents.description: BYD, one of China’s leading electric vehicle companies, reported a 5.5% year-on-year increase in total sales in June, largely due to high export demand countering low domestic sales.

incidents.title: Airplane crashes into Beijing tower
incidents.description: A small aircraft crashed into Beijing’s CITIC Tower, one of its tallest, killing the pilot and injuring 13 people near the site of the crash. The incident has raised questions about Beijing’s ability to enforce its citywide no-fly zone.

incidents.title: Families sue Maduro over extrajudicial killings
incidents.description: The families of five Venezuelan men filed a lawsuit in U.S. federal court alleging that former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro ordered their extrajudicial killings as part of a broader pattern of state violence. Maduro, who was removed from power by U.S. forces in January, is currently awaiting trial in New York on drug trafficking charges.

incidents.title: DRC takes U.N. Security Council presidency
incidents.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo assumed the rotating presidency of the U.N. Security Council for July. This comes as Kinshasa seeks to focus international attention on insecurity in Eastern DRC and the role conflict minerals play in sustaining armed groups.

incidents.title: West Bengal voter purge threatens welfare access
incidents.description: Millions of West Bengal residents removed from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision process risk losing access to government welfare benefits under the state’s Bharatiya Janata Party government. The voter revision exercise, which authorities said was intended to remove deceased, duplicate, and ineligible voters, disproportionately affected border districts and intensified political tensions over migration and citizenship.

incidents.title: Taiwan opposition party proposes drone funding plans
incidents.description: Taiwanese opposition Kuomintang outlined plans to allocate funding to the island’s drone industry, proposing approximately $7.5 billion over the next six years. This comes after the party recently opposed the full funding of a major government defense budget.

incidents.title: Supreme Court overturns campaign finance law
incidents.description: In a 6-3 decision , the Supreme Court struck down a 1974 campaign finance law that limits the amount of money a person or private entity can contribute to political campaigns.

incidents.title: Trump family earned $1.4 billion from crypto investment
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump made over $1.4 billion in crypto earnings over the last year, according to mandatory financial disclosure documents. . The documents also revealed that U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff has a controlling interest along with Trump in several crypto ventures.

incidents.title: Supreme Court upholds birthright citizenship
incidents.description: In a 5-4 decision, the U.S. Supreme Court declared an executive order issued by U.S. President Donald Trump that would have denied citizenship to some people born on U.S. soil illegal and unconstitutional..

incidents.title: U.S. drafts inverter import ban
incidents.description: A ban on imported solar and battery inverters is being drafted by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) due to cybersecurity and national security concerns. U.S. officials identified mysterious communication technologies in these devices, prompting concerns that China may use them to monitor or disrupt U.S. electricity infrastructure.

incidents.title: U.S. fuel reserve levels fall
incidents.description: U.S. commercial crude inventories have fallen by nearly 60 million barrels over the past 11 weeks, while the Strategic Petroleum Reserve has declined to 325.7 million barrels, its lowest level in over four decades. Meanwhile, oil prices declined, with Brent crude at $73.40, as the partial resumption of flows through the Strait of Hormuz reduced immediate supply concerns. Despite this, persistently low inventories leave the market with limited buffers against future supply disruptions and renewed geopolitical shocks.

incidents.title: India raises fuel export duty
incidents.description: India cut windfall taxes on diesel and jet fuel exports as global oil prices eased, while raising the export duty on gasoline. The diesel duty fell from 14 to 8.5 rupees (15 cents to 9 cents) per liter, and the gasoline export duty nearly tripled from 1.5 to 4 rupees per liter to protect domestic supply.

incidents.title: India crude imports reach record high
incidents.description: India’s crude imports reached a June record of about 5 million barrels per day, while Russian exports to India climbed to an all-time high of 2.6 million barrels per day. The surge reflected necessity more than choice, as the Strait of Hormuz disruption cut Gulf supplies and exposed India’s thin strategic reserves. Even as discounted Middle Eastern barrels return, the crisis reinforced Russia’s role as a strategic backup for India during future supply shocks.

incidents.title: Taiwan set to integrate air defense intelligence system
incidents.description: Taiwan’s military stated it was on track to fully develop and integrate a new air defense intelligence system, combining a missile defense program with a multiservice air defense intelligence system.

incidents.title: China, EU agree to October trade deadline
incidents.description: China and the European Union have agreed to set October as a deadline to “deliver on tangible results,” of their trade deal, according to trade commissioner Maros Sefcovic, including the creation of a joint platform to monitor trade flows and identifying areas of unfair trade practices.

incidents.title: China sanctions 20 Japanese companies:
incidents.description: China’s Ministry of Commerce added 20 Japanese entities to an export control list, whilst 20 more were added to a list allowing for increased scrutiny of traded goods. Beijing claimed the moves were in response to Japan’s “remilitarization” efforts.

incidents.title: AI demand boosts factory productivity
incidents.description: High demand in chips and AI-related products have driven up China’s factory productivity, countering the adverse effects on China’s economy from disruptions in the Middle East.

incidents.title: Earthquake toll surpasses 1,700
incidents.description: Venezuelan authorities confirmed that at least 1,719 people died and approximately 5,000 were injured following the June 24 earthquakes, while around 12,000 people have been displaced. Officials reported that seven states have been affected and that the United Nations and Venezuelan authorities agreed to procure 10,000 body bags amid expectations that the death toll will continue to rise.

incidents.title: India seeks exemption from EU scrap export restrictions
incidents.description: India has requested relief from planned European Union restrictions on scrap metal exports, warning that the measures could tighten supplies, increase costs, and undermine gains from a bilateral trade agreement. Under revised regulations, the EU will prohibit exports of nonhazardous waste to non-OECD countries beginning May 2027 unless exemptions are approved by November 2026.

incidents.title: Canada to receive Chinese EVs
incidents.description: Following through on a trade agreement signed earlier this year, China is set to deliver the first batch of 49,000 electric vehicles to Canada, which seeks to diversify trade away from the United States.

incidents.title: Russia declares state of emergency in Crimea
incidents.description: Russian officials in Crimea have declared a state of emergency as a result of Ukraine's escalated drone campaign against energy and infrastructure targets in the occupied territory.

incidents.title: Russia, Ukraine exchange POWs
incidents.description: Russia and Ukraine each exchanged 160 prisoners of war on June 26.

incidents.title: India launches anti-dumping investigations
incidents.description: India’s Directorate General of Trade Remedies initiated an anti-dumping investigation into hot-rolled steel imports from China, Japan, and Russia following complaints from major domestic producers that low-priced imports were harming the domestic industry. The investigation follows a sharp increase in Chinese steel exports to India, which more than doubled in April and reached their highest level in at least two years.

incidents.title: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of distillation
incidents.description: U.S. AI company Anthropic accused Chinese tech company Alibaba of copying its large language model through a “distillation” attack. Anthropic claims that this happened despite geographic restrictions that prohibit the company from operating its services in China.

incidents.title: Trump praises Zelenskyy
incidents.description: During a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at The Hague on June 24, U.S. President Donald Trump praised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, saying that he is “winning now” against Russia.

incidents.title: China-Japan flights decrease
incidents.description: Scheduled flights between China and Japan have decreased by 57% year-on-year during the peak holiday months of July and August, as bilateral tensions between both countries continue.

incidents.title: Power, water shortages continue in Iran
incidents.description: Power outages and water shortages persisted across multiple cities in Iran as summer temperatures reach a peak.

incidents.title: Trump says Erdoğan was positioned to go to war with Israel
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan was a “prime candidate” to go to war with Israel during the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran but that Erdoğan held back upon Trump’s request. The Turkish government has not officially responded to Trump’s comments.

incidents.title: Taiwanese vessel takes Iranian fire in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: A Taiwanese vessel attempting passage through the Strait of Hormuz reported taking fire on June 25, sustaining minor damage and reporting no casualties. According to unnamed U.S. officials, the projectile was fired by Iran. The vessel reported safely leaving the strait.

incidents.title: Europe embassies issue China warning
incidents.description: The de-facto embassies of the U.K., France, and Germany in Taiwan issued a joint statement of concern regarding China’s increased coast guard patrols near and around the island, in a rare break of silence and showcase of unity.

incidents.title: Ladakh protests resume
incidents.description: Residents of Leh and Kargil held demonstrations after talks between Ladakhi leadership groups and India’s Ministry of Home Affairs produced no breakthrough on demands for full statehood and inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.

incidents.title: India, U.S. conduct trade talks
incidents.description: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer concluded a three-day visit to New Delhi after meetings with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal on a first-phase bilateral trade deal. Both sides reported progress.

incidents.title: Trump refuses to sign housing bill
incidents.description: U.S. President Trump has canceled the signing ceremony for a recently passed bill that would fund new housing construction. While initially supportive of the bill, Trump refused to sign it into law as he pressed for a new voter ID law.

incidents.title: White House seeks $88 billion in supplemental funding
incidents.description: The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has sent Congress a request for a nearly $88 billion in supplemental funding in part to help replenish munitions expended during the Iran war and other military operational costs related to the conflict. The funding package also includes about $11 billion for aid to U.S. farmers and another $1.5 billion to fight the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

incidents.title: IDF surrounds underground Hezbollah complex
incidents.description: Thousands of Israeli soldiers have surrounded an underground complex housing dozens of Hezbollah fighters near Kfar Tebnit in southern Lebanon. Israeli officials said the militants are believed to be running low on food and water.

incidents.title: Powerful earthquakes strike Venezuela
incidents.description: Two earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 in magnitude, struck Venezuela, causing widespread structural damage and prompting evacuations across the region. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez said the earthquakes damaged infrastructure in multiple states, though authorities have not yet released casualty or damage estimates.

incidents.title: Chinese supercomputer beats U.S.
incidents.description: China’s National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzen unveiled its updated LineShine supercomputer, built with domestically sourced chips. LineShine was ranked at the top of the TOP500 biannual supercomputer speed ranking. This marks a milestone for China in the tech race as it surpassed U.S. capabilities for the first time in three years.

incidents.title: Iran denies Trump claims on nuclear inspections
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran has agreed to allow international inspectors access to its nuclear facilities “into infinity.” Iran denied the claim.

incidents.title: U.S. grants Iran temporary sanctions relief
incidents.description: The U.S. is granting Iran limited sanctions relief, to last for a 60-day period, as negotiations over the long-term fate of Iran’s nuclear program and other issues continue in Geneva.

incidents.title: Gas flaring reaches highest levels in six years
incidents.description: Instances of gas flaring reached their highest levels in six years according to World Bank data, mainly due to increases in Iran and Russia. Globally, about 167 billion cubic meters of natural gas worth $54 billion was burned off as waste in 2025, with Russia, Iran, and Iraq accounting for about half that total.

incidents.title: Alibaba sues U.S. government
incidents.description: China’s e-commerce giant Alibaba is suing the U.S. government following last week’s decision by the U.S. Department of Defense to add the company to its list of entities suspected of working with the Chinese military. The list contains approximately 188 companies.

incidents.title: Eight sentenced in immigration center shooting
incidents.description: Seven protesters have been sentenced to 30-70 years in prison on terrorism charges after they attended a protest where shots were fired despite having no involvement in the violence. Benjamin Song, who was convicted of firing a rifle that injured a police officer, received a 100-year sentence.

incidents.title: Indian Minister Jaishankar visits Mongolia
incidents.description: Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited Mongolia to review progress on the Mongol Refinery, backed with a $1.7 billion Indian investment and expected to be operational by 2028. Jaishankar also held talks with Mongolian Foreign Minister Battsetseg Batmunkh on bilateral cooperation.

incidents.title: Chinese aircraft carrier transits Taiwan Strait
incidents.description: China’s Fujian aircraft carrier sailed through the Taiwan Strait. This was the first mission of this kind to occur since April, and involved China’s most advanced vessel.

incidents.title: Russia considers banning diesel fuel exports
incidents.description: Russia is considering banning diesel exports, importing foreign fuel, and subsidizing gasoline prices to lower pump prices and inflation while stabilizing its energy market. These measures would be aimed at lessening fuel supply disruptions caused by the intense campaign of Ukrainian drone attacks targeting energy infrastructure. Direct government subsidies for imported fuel are also being considered.

incidents.title: Qatar investigates gas plant explosion
incidents.description: Qatari authorities are investigating the cause of a major gas plant explosion at Qatar's Barzan local gas supply station in Ras Laffan, the world's largest liquefied natural gas export hub, that killed 13 people and injured 66 others. Initial reports attributed the blast at the plant, which was being restarted after a monthslong maintenance shutdown, to an accident and not sabotage. The Barzan facility, which processes natural gas for Qatar's industry, water desalination, and electric generation. The Ras Laffan facility had been the target of Iranian attacks during the conflict with the United States and Israel.

incidents.title: India, China indicate normalization
incidents.description: The Indian Foreign Ministry described talks between Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on the sidelines of the BRICS National Security Advisers’ meeting in New Delhi as constructive and forward-looking. Both sides noted progress toward normalization of relations.

incidents.title: Ukraine threatens Belarus
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued an ultimatum giving Belarus a week to remove communications equipment from the Ukrainian-Belarusian border he said is being used to support of Russia’s war effort. Zelenskyy threatened Ukrainian action if the equipment remains. Russia responded by accusing Ukraine of threatening the Belarusian sovereignty.

incidents.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again
incidents.description: Iran said on June 22 that it was closing the Strait of Hormuz in response to continued Israeli attacks in Lebanon. U.S. officials disputed the claim that the strait was closed.

incidents.title: Taiwan’s China investments fall to new low
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs reported that the island’s investment into China has decreased to less than 1% of all foreign investments.

incidents.title: British PM Keir Starmer resigns
incidents.description: Keir Starmer announced he would resign as leader of the Labour Party government and as prime minister following the victory by former Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham in a special Parliamentary election.
