Burnham has voiced his ambitions of succeeding Starmer, and his victory follows a series of resignations by Starmer’s Cabinet, including the ministers of health, defense, and armed forces. Formal nominations for a successor to Starmer open July 9, with prospects high that Burnham will assume the leadership role without a challenge from his peers.

incidents.title: Indian minister Jaishankar addresses Jeju Forum
incidents.description: External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited South Korea, meeting Foreign Minister Cho Hyun to advance the countries’ Joint Strategic Vision covering semiconductors, AI, and critical minerals. Jaishankar also delivered the keynote address at the Jeju Forum for Peace and Prosperity.

incidents.title: Chinese steel demand decreases
incidents.description: China’s steel market has been experiencing a gradual decrease in demand, with exports still remaining strong while domestic consumption linked to the property market has been on the way down. This follows a broader pattern across the Chinese economy reflected across multiple sectors.

incidents.title: Russia bombs Ukrainian cities
incidents.description: Russia carried out strikes against cities across Ukraine.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Moscow and Crimea
incidents.description: Ukraine continued it campaign of strikes targeting Moscow as well as Russian energy infrastructure and industry targets both in Russian territory and in Russian-occupied Crimea.

incidents.title: Israeli bombardment in Lebanon continues
incidents.description: Continued Israeli occupation and bombardment of southern Lebanon threatened to derail ongoing U.S.-Iran peace negotiations. Israeli airstrikes killed at least 20 Lebanese on June 20, after another ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah went into effect.

incidents.title: Israeli leaders say IDF will remain in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on June 21 that Israel will maintain its occupation in Lebanon for “as long as necessary.” Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said that the Israel Defense Forces will not withdraw from Lebanon, despite reports of ongoing U.S.-mediated negotiations between Israel and Lebanon that aim to achieve a handover of territory to the Lebanese army in exchange for an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon.

incidents.title: Taiwan holds updated military drills
incidents.description: The Taiwanese military held five-day combat readiness drills this week, as part of efforts by the Ministry of National Defense to modernize training and incorporate new scenarios into its drills.

incidents.title: China sanctions U.S. minerals companies
incidents.description: China added two U.S. companies in the rare-earth sector – USA Rare Earth and MP Materials – to its export restrictions list in retaliation for U.S. sanctions placed last week against Chinese companies.

incidents.title: Far-right candidate wins election in Colombia
incidents.description: Far-right candidate Abelardo De La Espriella won Colombia’s presidential election with 49.66% of the vote. Sen. Ivan Cepeda came a close second with 48.70%. De La Espriella vowed to end all talks with rebel groups, reduce the size of the state, and expand the fossil fuel sector.

incidents.title: Venezuela prepares record sovereign debt restructuring
incidents.description: Venezuela is preparing to disclose approximately $240 billion in public debt, significantly above previous market estimates, as the country begins what could become the largest sovereign debt restructuring in history. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez aims to reach an agreement with creditors by the end of 2026 to restore Venezuela’s access to international financial markets.

incidents.title: Leaked message sparks debate in Tehran
incidents.description: A leaked message believed to be from Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei indicates that he approved the conditions of the memorandum of understanding with the U.S. despite personal reservations. The message, which has not officially been attributed to Khamenei, has sparked political debate within Tehran as hard-liners try to disavow the negotiation process.

incidents.title: Bolivian president mobilizes army against protesters
incidents.description: President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of emergency and mobilized the military against antigovernment protesters that have blocked major urban roadways for the past seven weeks. Protesters are demanding an end to austerity measures and a resumption of fuel subsidies. Paz’s government has asserted that the protests are aimed at destabilizing the country and of acting in support of former leader Evo Morales, who is currently in hiding after he was charged with human trafficking, an accusation he denies.

incidents.title: Kremlin open to dialogue with Europe
incidents.description: Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia is “open to dialogue” with Europe over peace negotiations in Ukraine but that it would not accept any ultimatums.

incidents.title: China considers indium export restrictions
incidents.description: China is stepping up its due diligence regarding indium exports, looking to add the element to its export list Beijing deems it critical for domestic industries. This follows the addition of indium phosphide to Beijing’s export list last year, a compound used among others in the semiconductor industry.

incidents.title: EU ponders Chinese EV tariffs
incidents.description: The European Commission is looking to impose tougher measures and tariffs against Chinese electric vehicle imports, targeting firms such as BYD, Chery and SAIC, as the bloc seeks to reduce its 360.6 billion euro trade deficit with China. The commission is also proposing a law that would require EU companies across multiple sectors to diversify the sourcing of key components.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran sign MOU
incidents.description: The U.S. and Iran electronically signed a memorandum of understanding on June 17 that calls for both countries to cease active hostilities toward each other, an end to Israel’s war in Lebanon, the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and the release of at least $300 billion worth of frozen Iranian assets. It also sets a timeline to begin nuclear negotiations that reach a deal within 60 days.

incidents.title: Israel seizes control of West Bank holy site
incidents.description: Israel seized administrative control of a shared Jewish and Muslim holy site in the West Bank in a violation of the 1997 Hebron Agreement.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Moscow oil refinery
incidents.description: Ukraine struck Russian energy infrastructure repeatedly over the course of the week including a large-scale attack against a major Moscow oil refinery, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelnenskyy declaring that Moscow “will burn.”

incidents.title: Pentagon initiates review of U.S. forces in Europe
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced a six-month review of the U.S. military’s presence in Europe, reiterating a demand that Europe take charge of its own defense. This follows recent reported cuts to the U.S. forces available during a crisis in Europe.

incidents.title: Ukraine threatens new drone campaign in Crimea
incidents.description: Ukrainian officials threatened to completely sever ground access from occupied Crimea to Russia with an escalated drone campaign.

incidents.title: G7 vows to reduce China minerals dependency
incidents.description: At this year’s G7 summit in France, leaders discussed a number of issues including the diversification of rare earth supplies from China. While there was unity between G7 partners on the need to reduce dependence on supplies from China, U.S. President Donald Trump praised Beijing for “remaining neutral” in the Iran war.

incidents.title: KMT leader visits U.S.
incidents.description: The leader of Taiwan’s Kuomintang, Cheng Li-wun, visited the U.S. on a two-week trip, meeting with think tanks, universities, and members of Congress. This comes two months after Cheng visited Beijing on a “peace mission” that resulted in some easing of restrictions by Chian against the island. It is unclear whether Cheng’s U.S. visit will yield any concrete results, given Washington’s push for increased Taiwanese defense spending, an issue usually opposed by the KMT.

incidents.title: ICE detainees transferred out of ‘Alligator Alcatraz‘
incidents.description: The Department of Homeland Security has announced all detainees from the infamous Florida based detention center have been moved to other facilities as hurricane season began. It is unclear whether the facility will reopen.

incidents.title: Modi, Zelensky meet at G7
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks on the sidelines of the G7 summit in France, with both leaders agreeing that India-Ukraine trade should return to where it stood before Russia’s 2022 invasion.

incidents.title: Telegram challenges India in court
incidents.description: The company operating the Telegram messaging app has filed a petition in a New Delhi court challenging the Indian government's order temporarily blocking access to the platform, arguing the measure is unconstitutional and an excessive restriction on free expression.

incidents.title: EU confirms India-EU FTA by 2026
incidents.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced at the G7 summit that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement will be formally signed before the end of this year, following a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and European Council President Antonio Costa on the sidelines. The two sides also committed to accelerating work on a separate bilateral investment agreement, deepening security and defense cooperation, and advancing the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.

incidents.title: Trump threatens to resume bombing if Iran nuclear deal fails
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened that the U.S. would resume offensive operations against Iran if an agreement regarding the fate of its nuclear program was not successfully reached within the 60-day period stipulated by a June 17 memorandum of understanding signed by both countries.

incidents.title: EU passes new anti-migrant law
incidents.description: The European Parliament passed a controversial law that would allow member states to speed the deportation of migrants who have no legal right to remain in the EU. The law also allows EU countries to set up “return hubs” or deportation centers outside of the EU, where migrants could be held indefinitely pending return to their countries of origin. The measure, backed by center-right and far-right lawmakers, would require formal approval by member states’ leaders before it could take effect.

incidents.title: Israel to continue occupations in Lebanon, Gaza, and Syria
incidents.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel will maintain its current territorial occupations in Lebanon, Gaza and Syria.

incidents.title: Trump and Zelenskyy meet at G7
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and other European leaders on the sidelines of the G7 summit held June 15-17 in France. Trump described his meeting with Zelenskyy as “very good” and made a number of statements urging peace between Russia and Ukraine, but did not signal that the U.S. would resume the diplomatic process it had pursued before the start of the Iran war. Trump also said that the war in Ukraine has “no impact” on the United States.

incidents.title: Canada announces new sanctions against Russia
incidents.description: At the G7 summit on June 16, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a new sanctions package against Russia that targets 162 individuals and entities primarily associated with Russia’s shadow fleet exports and defense industry.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran set to begin nuclear talks in Geneva
incidents.description: Negotiations over Iran’s nuclear program between the U.S. and Iran are scheduled to begin June 19 in Geneva.

incidents.title: China rebukes UK sanctions
incidents.description: China urged the United Kingdom to correct its “mistake” following London’s latest sanctions package, which included four entities in China for allegedly supplying military equipment to Russia.

incidents.title: U.S. holds off sanctions on DeepSeek
incidents.description: Reuters, citing unnamed sources, reported that the U.S. Commerce Department will delay adding Chinese AI companies, such as DeepSeek and CXMT, to its entity list in order to preserve good trade relations with China.

incidents.title: Chinese retail sales decline
incidents.description: Chinese retail sales declined by 0.6% in May compared with the same period last year, marking the first decline since the COVID-19 pandemic. The decline follows a pattern of weakening domestic consumption that has dampened China’s economy, which is held up by steady exports, though they, too, have experienced fluctuations over the past few months.

incidents.title: PDVSA, Repsol expand production in Venezuela
incidents.description: Venezuela’s state oil company, PDVSA, and Spain’s Repsol signed an agreement to expand crude oil and natural gas production in northwestern Venezuela. The agreement focuses on new exploration around Lake Maracaibo and could increase light crude production by about 20,000 barrels per day from the existing Petroquiriquire joint venture.

incidents.title: India, Estonia hold consultations
incidents.description: India and Estonia held their 13th round of Foreign Office Consultations covering trade, technology, defense, and digital infrastructure. Estonian officials identified India as a growth market for semiconductors and drones and positioned their country as an EU gateway for Indian firms.

incidents.title: Japanese company acquires Ukrainian drone makers
incidents.description: Japanese drone manufacturer Terra Drone will acquire two Ukrainian drone startups, WinnyLab and Amazing Drones. With the acquisition, the company would harness experience gained in the Ukraine war to sell drones to Japan, the Middle East, and Europe. Drones from both Ukrainian companies have successfully been used against Russian targets. Japan, which is seeking to modernize its defense capabilities, recently relaxed regulations on the foreign sales of lethal weapons.

incidents.title: Russia offers rare earth minerals to India
incidents.description: Russia has offered India access to the enormous Tomtor rare earth metals deposit in the Siberian Republic of Sakha (Yakutia). As a first step toward an agreement, Russia would process Tomtor ore samples and ship them to India for analysis. A finalized agreement would help India build a consistent supply chain for its electric vehicle, renewable energy, and defense sectors, a strategically important step for India to reduce its dependency on China. A deal would allow Russia, meanwhile, to attract significant international investment.

incidents.title: Venezuela, GE Vernova sign power agreement
incidents.description: Venezuela signed a memorandum of understanding with GE Vernova to modernize the country’s electricity grid. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the agreement aims to restore 1 gigawatt of generating capacity within two years and more than 5 gigawatts over four years.

incidents.title: Russia bombs historic cathedral in Kyiv
incidents.description: Russia continued its bombardment of cities across Ukraine, including a June 15 attack that set fire to a historic orthodox cathedral and Kyiv.

incidents.title: Report: China capable of striking Australia
incidents.description: An Australian think tank, the Lowy Institute, issued a report detailing how new Chinese intermediate-range ballistic missiles now had the capability to directly strike Australia, as the People’s Liberation Army continues to expand its arsenal.

incidents.title: Japan, UK tighten defense ties
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer in London, where both parties agreed to deepen economic and security cooperation. This comes as the UK has postponed funding for the Global Combat Air Programme, designed in partnership with Japan and Italy for the development of a sixth-generation fighter jet. Despite funding delays, both leaders reconfirmed their commitment to the program.

incidents.title: Senate postpones intelligence director confirmation hearing
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate postponed a confirmation hearing for Jay Clayton, U.S. President Donald Trump’s nominee for director of national intelligence after Trump instructed Clayton not to appear.

incidents.title: UN condemns use of drones in Sudan civil war
incidents.description: The United Nations decried the steady increase in casualties linked to drone attacks in Sudan this year. Figures from U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk indicated drone strikes between January and May killed over 1,000 people as the country’s civil war shows no signs of slowing. This comes as evidence of foreign involvement in the war, including drones and technological aid supplied by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Ethiopia to the Rapid Support Forces, has mounted.

incidents.title: Iran executes two protesters
incidents.description: Iran executed two men who had been arrested while protesting during the January 2026 civil unrest that swept the country, amid an ongoing domestic crackdown.

incidents.title: Trump demands voting overhaul be linked FISA renewal
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has insisted the proposed SAVE America Act be attached to any measure renewing the budget for the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA). The SAVE America Act would introduce a series of national voter ID requirements. Funding for FISA, which enables the U.S. government to monitor the communications of foreign nationals, recently expired for the first time since its introduction in 2008.

incidents.title: U.S. imposes sanctions on Cuban oil company
incidents.description: The U.S. government has imposed sanctions on Cuba's state-owned oil and gas corporation, Unión Cuba-Petróleo (Cupet), that prevent the company from accessing its assets in the United States and limit the Cuban government's energy trade. The move could deepen the island’s energy crisis, risking further restrictions on transportation, food storage, and electricity supplies for its residents.

incidents.title: Taiwan launches Chinese recruitment website
incidents.description: Taiwan’s National Security Bureau launched a website designed to facilitate disgruntled Chinese nationals to provide intelligence to Taiwan. The move follows recent similar tactics employed by the U.S., Israel, and the UK. China said it would take countermeasures against the site, calling the move revealing of Taiwan’s “confrontational mindset.”

incidents.title: U.S. strike kills Tren de Aragua leader
incidents.description: A strike directed by the U.S. Southern Command killed Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, known as Niño Guerrero, the leader of the Tren de Aragua criminal organization. The attack was conducted in coordination with the Venezuelan government.

incidents.title: China cuts crude oil imports
incidents.description: China cut crude oil imports by approximately 3 million barrels per day (bpd) during the Iran war, easing pressure on global oil markets. Its imports fell to approximately 7.8 million bpd in May from average levels of around 11 million bpd prior to the war. The country was able to manage the decrease by tapping existing reserves and cutting refined fuel exports, among other measures, increasing its ability to absorb external energy shocks.

incidents.title: U.S. strike kills Indian sailors in the Gulf of Oman
incidents.description: The U.S. navy struck an Indian-crewed oil tanker ship in the Gulf of Oman on June 10, killing three. An additional 21 crew members were rescued from the stricken ship. U.S. military officials said the vessel had attempted to bypass the U.S. blockade.

incidents.title: Ukraine drones damage bridges
incidents.description: Successive Ukrainian drone strikes have caused damage to numerous bridges linking the occupied territories of Kherson and Crimea. The attacks come as Ukraine initiates an intensified Ukrainian campaign against Russian logistical targets.

incidents.title: Iran re-closes Strait of Hormuz and exchanges fire with U.S.
incidents.description: Iran once again declared a full closure of the Strait of Hormuz on June 11. The closure follows a series of U.S. and Iranian strikes threatened the ceasefire agreement, including the downing of a U.S. Army Apache helicopter by Iran that prompted retaliation from the United States.

incidents.title: Iran strikes countries across the Middle East
incidents.description: Iran conducted strikes across the Gulf and against Jordan over the course of the week.

incidents.title: Israel may earmark $338 million for settlements
incidents.description: Israel is expected to approve the allocation of $338 million for West Bank settlement expansion.

incidents.title: U.S./Iran peace talks continue
incidents.description: Peace talks between the U.S. and Iran continued despite a series of strikes between the two countries, and Iranian barrages against Gulf states and Jordan. Anonymous Iranian officials reported that some progress had been made toward a political understanding, while reports circulated that a deal may be signed by June 14.

incidents.title: U.S. allocates annual Taiwan defense aid
incidents.description: The U.S. House Appropriations Committee issued its 2027 defense spending bill, which would allocate $2 billion for defense assistance and equipment replacement for Taiwan. The annual bill always provides some funds for defense of the island, as mandated by U.S. law; this year’s bill was announced after the Trump administration postponed a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan.

incidents.title: China sanctions Philippine defense minister
incidents.description: China sanctioned Philippine Defense Minister Gilberto Teodoro Jr. for making “erroneous remarks” and undermining Chinese interests. This comes after Teodoro stated he would like closer relations with Taiwan and worked with Japan on redefining maritime borders in the South China Sea.

incidents.title: Xi Jinping meets Kim Jong Un
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping visited North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Pyongyang this week. The visit marked the first time in seven years that Xi traveled to North Korea, with both countries pledging to improve ties across multiple sectors including high-level strategic communications, economic aid, culture, science, military. Unlike previous summits, North Korean denuclearization was not on the agenda.

incidents.title: Graham Platner wins Maine Senate primary
incidents.description: Progressive Democrat Graham Platner has won Maine’s U.S. Senate Democratic primary election. Platner will run against Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who has been in the Senate for nearly 30 years.

incidents.title: Erdoğan decries Israeli destabilization in Syria and Lebanon
incidents.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan said Israeli attacks in Syria and Lebanon were destabilizing the Mediterranean region and represent a direct threat to Türkiye.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions Chinese supporters of IRGC
incidents.description: The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control added 11 Chinese and Hong-Kong-based entities and individuals to its sanctions list, for their role in supporting the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

incidents.title: U.S. disrupts Chinese recruitment platforms
incidents.description: The U.S. Justice Department identified and seized 13 internet domains it says were used as fake consulting firms set up by Chinese intelligence to lure and recruit current or former U.S. officials.

incidents.title: Israel orders evacuation of major Lebanese city
incidents.description: Israel continued a high-intensity bombardment campaign in Lebanon despite recently agreeing to a U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal and ordered the evacuation of the city of Tyre.

incidents.title: Trump’s approval rating worsens on economy
incidents.description: A new Financial Times poll shows throughout May approximately 68% of registered voters now have a negative view of U.S. President Donald Trump’s handling of both the cost of living and the inflation crisis. This disapproval rating is 10 points higher than the April number for the same poll.

incidents.title: Venezuela releases 54 additional military political prisoners
incidents.description: The Venezuelan government authorized the release of 54 political prisoners, most of them military personnel linked to an alleged conspiracy against the government by military officers.

incidents.title: Modi reaches leadership milestone
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi reached 4,399 consecutive days in office, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru’s record for continuous elected service as prime minister. Foreign leaders extended their congratulations.

incidents.title: Meta, Reliance announce AI data center in India
incidents.description: Meta and Reliance announced a 168-megawatt AI data center leasing partnership in Jamnagar, Gujarat, that Reliance will build. Meta then plans to lease it, its first lease in India.

incidents.title: SLB signs agreement with Venezuela’s PDVSA
incidents.description: U.S. oilfield services company SLB signed a long-term agreement with Venezuela’s state oil company PDVSA to support the modernization and expansion of the country’s oil and gas sector. The agreement includes cooperation on exploration, field development, production, and the deployment of AI technology.

incidents.title: Pakistan strikes targets in Afghanistan
incidents.description: Pakistan launched a new wave of strikes in Afghanistan’s Khost, Kunar, and Paktika provinces, with Afghan authorities reporting 13 killed and 14 wounded. This resumption of violence follows several weeks of calm between both countries for the first time since Pakistan declared “open war” against Afghanistan in February, accusing Kabul of supporting militant groups.

incidents.title: Oil Tanker owners fear market crash
incidents.description: Oil tanker owners fear a market crash if the Middle East conflict ends and the Strait of Hormuz reopens, lowering shipping rates. The world's largest oil tanker owners earned $36 billion in the first quarter of 2026, breaking the 2022 record of $26 billion. Record earnings and war profits prompted shipowners to buy additional supertanker fleets. Owners’ main concern is that a big increase in ship orders and a diplomatic breakthrough will cause a massive vessel oversupply.

incidents.title: India questions U.S. over tanker strike
incidents.description: India summoned senior U.S. diplomat Jason Meeks after U.S. forces struck the Palau-flagged tanker Settebello in the Gulf of Oman. The vessel had 24 Indian sailors on board; 21 were rescued, and three were confirmed dead.

incidents.title: Stabbing attack at Northern Irish protest
incidents.description: Anti-immigrant protests in Belfast, Northern Ireland, turned violent following the stabbing of Stephen Ogilvie by Hadi Alodid, a Sudanese man who was granted a five-year permit to stay following his asylum request in 2023. Ogilvie suffered injuries to his eyes, and while his family called for calm and for the incident not to be used for divisive rhetoric, several prominent figures, including Elon Musk and far-right activist Tommy Robinson, made statements calling for increased protests against the U.K.’s immigration policies. The incident comes at a tense time in British public discourse, with anti-immigrant protests regularly occurring across the across the United Kingdom, despite official migration statistics showing an overall drop in migration to the country.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy meets with Nordic and Baltic leaders
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with Nordic and Baltic leaders in Estonia on June 9 following a series of accidental drone incursions into Baltic airspace.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy holds call with top U.S. negotiators
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described a call with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner on June 8 as “very positive.”

incidents.title: Florida based company to send oil to Cuba
incidents.description: A Florida-based trading company, Vanguard Energy, is poised to send Cuba 250,000 barrels of gasoline and diesel, the largest shipment of fuel to Cuba by the U.S. since the Eisenhower administration. The decision, approved by the Cuban government, awaits formal approval from the Trump administration. Vanguard Energy has specified that the shipment would be delivered to private-sector actors only, in line with White House directives, and comes as the island wrestles with an acute energy crisis due to the U.S.-imposed blockade.

incidents.title: EV sales surge in Philippines
incidents.description: Sales of electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrids have surged to record highs in the Philippines as rising fuel prices push consumers to consider alternatives to gasoline-powered vehicles. The Philippines imports 95% of its crude oil, exposing local drivers to global market volatility and worsening its energy crisis.

incidents.title: India fires at suspected Pakistani drone
incidents.description: Indian Army troops opened fire on a suspected Pakistani drone near the Line of Control in Poonch, Jammu and Kashmir. The drone reportedly returned toward Pakistan-administered Kashmir after troops fired on it.

incidents.title: Zojila Tunnel completed
incidents.description: India completed the Zojila Tunnel, connecting both ends of the strategic road tunnel linking Kashmir and Ladakh. The project is intended to provide access to Ladakh, including areas close to India’s disputed frontier with China.

incidents.title: Taiwan conducts defensive drills
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Army 10th Corps conducted live-fire drills in Taichung, using heavy artillery systems to mimic the repelling of a Chinese invasion, including the use of multiple launch rocket systems, self-propelled howitzers, and shoulder-launched rocket systems.

incidents.title: Trump signs new DHS funding bill
incidents.description: Congress recently passed a Department of Homeland Security funding bill that, if signed by President Donald Trump, would allocate $70 billion to the agency. The bill passed following months of gridlock primarily centering around the controversies surrounding the conduct of Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

incidents.title: Pentagon adds Chinese companies to watchlist
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Defense added several Chinese companies to its 1260H list, indicating a potential security risk due to their possible ties to the Chinese military. The move expands the U.S.’s mitigation strategy against “dual-use” technologies and includes companies such as BYD, Baidu, Huawei, and Alibaba.

incidents.title: French jet shoots down drone over Latvian airspace
incidents.description: A French jet conducting NATO security operations over Baltic airspace shot down a drone of undisclosed origin that entered Latvian airspace.

incidents.title: Russia says Ukrainian strikes have contributed to fuel shortage
incidents.description: Ukraine conducted numerous attacks against Russian energy and port infrastructure. The Russian Energy Ministry released a statement acknowledging that Ukrainian strikes have contributed to a fuel shortage in southern Russia and Russian occupied Crimea.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy meets with Russian billionaire in Kyiv
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that he met privately with Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich in Kyiv this past May to facilitate backdoor communication with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

incidents.title: Rodríguez, Erdoğan discuss energy, mining cooperation
incidents.description: Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Istanbul to discuss expanding cooperation in trade, energy, and mining. The two also discussed increasing bilateral trade and strengthening economic ties following.

incidents.title: Trump claims fraud in California primaries
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump made unsubstantiated claims that California’s primary election results were fraudulent. His claims centered around the idea of the tampering of mail-in ballots, which predominantly favor Democrats. These claims mirror similar unproven statements Trump made following the 2020 election.

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia lowers price of crude oil
incidents.description: Saudi Aramco lowered the price of its Arab Light crude for July for Asian buyers by $6 per barrel by reducing its premium from $15.50 to $9.50. The decision may reflect growing concern over softer regional oil demand, particularly in major importing markets such as China. It also suggests a more strategic use of pricing to preserve competitiveness and maintain export positioning in Asia.

incidents.title: Armenian Prime Minister wins election
incidents.description: Armenia held parliamentary elections this week, with the party of Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, the Civil Contract party, winning 64 out of 105 seats – enough to keep power but short of a supermajority. The result, which sidelined pro-Russian parties in the country, was hailed by French President Emmauel Macron as a positive step in policy alignment with the rest of Europe and will likely drive a continuation of Pashinyan’s diversification in foreign policy away from Moscow and efforts to normalize relations with Azerbaijan and Türkiye.

incidents.title: Israel continues Gaza bombardment
incidents.description: An Israeli airstrike in Gaza killed at least six people on June 8.

incidents.title: Chinese exports rise year-on-year
incidents.description: Chinese exports have risen by 15% year-on-year, with exports in May rising likely because orders were brought forward to avoid future pricing pressures related to rising energy costs from the war in Iran. However, e-commerce export profits for big online giants such as Temu and Shein have been contracting since last year’s tariff war with the United States.

incidents.title: EU announces new sanctions on IRGC
incidents.description: The EU enacted new sanctions against two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) officials and an IRGC unit for their involvement with curtailing freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: European leaders list conditions to end war
incidents.description: During a June 7 summit in London, the leaders of Ukraine, France, Germany, and the United Kingdom released a joint statement that listed five conditions required by Europe to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine. The leaders also discussed how Ukraine’s battlefield expertise and defense industry can be further incorporated into broader European security.

incidents.title: Taiwan stands off with Chinese coast guard
incidents.description: Taiwan deployed its coast guard to monitor and drive off Chinese coast guard vessels operating near Xiamen.

incidents.title: China confirms Xi visit to North Korea
incidents.description: Chinese state media Xinhua confirmed that President Xi Jinping would visit North Korea next week for June 8 and June 9 in a show of strong ties between the countries.

incidents.title: House votes to advance Russia sanctions and Ukraine aid bill
incidents.description: The U.S. House of Representatives voted to advance legislation that would enact new sanctions against Russia and provide military aid to Ukraine through the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative. The sanctions and military assistance are dependent on final votes in the U.S. House and Senate.

incidents.title: Zelenskyy writes open letter to Putin
incidents.description: On June 4, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy published an open letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin calling for face-to-face negations to end the war.

incidents.title: Israel to continue ground operations in Lebanon
incidents.description: On June 4, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel would continue its ground operations and territorial occupation in southern Lebanon, despite a conditional ceasefire agreed upon by Israel and Lebanon on June 3.

incidents.title: U.N. peacekeeper killed in Lebanon
incidents.description: A soldier deployed with a U.N. peacekeeping force was killed and two others were wounded by mortar fire in Lebanon on June 3. It has not been confirmed if the shelling was conducted by Israeli or Hezbollah forces.

incidents.title: Israeli bombings in Gaza
incidents.description: Israel killed at least nine Palestinians in separate airstrikes in Gaza on June 4.

incidents.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to conditional ceasefire
incidents.description: Israel and Lebanon agreed to a conditional ceasefire during U.S.-mediated talks in Washington, D.C., on June 3. The ceasefire is contingent upon the Lebanese army taking control of territory from Hezbollah. The agreement between Israel and Lebanon follows reports of significant tension between U.S. President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel’s offensive in Lebanon.

incidents.title: Khamenei warns of foreign exploitation of internal divisions within Iran
incidents.description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei released a message to the Iranian people on June 4, warning against attempts to create internal divisions within Iran, following the “defeat” of the United States and Israel on the battlefield. The message was read on behalf of Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since his appointment as supreme leader, following the death of his father and several family members in a joint U.S./Israeli strike.

incidents.title: Chinese EV's begin entering Canadian market
incidents.description: Chinese-made electric vehicles have begun entering [RI1] [ST2] Canada under a new trade arrangement that allows up to 49,000 Chinese EV imports annually. Under the agreement, imported vehicles will face a tariff rate of approximately 6%, significantly lower than the previous tariff exceeding 100%, which had largely restricted market access. Initial shipments include vehicles produced in China by Tesla and a limited number of Lotus models arriving through the Port of Vancouver. Although the quota currently accounts for less than 3% of Canada’s annual vehicle market, it may expand over time[RI3] [ST4] , as Canada seeks to lower EV costs and attract investment in its automotive and EV supply chains.

incidents.title: Trump to attend NATO conference in Ankara
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed that U.S. President Donald Trump will attend the upcoming NATO conference in Ankara this July.

incidents.title: Hungarian PM offers to host Russia/Ukraine negotiations
incidents.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar suggested Budapest could host future negotiations between Russia and Ukraine.

incidents.title: U.S. House passes war powers resolution to end Iran conflict
incidents.description: In the first concrete move from Congress to halt the Iranian war, the House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution that seeks to limit the U.S. President Donald Trump’s ability to prosecute the war. The passage of the resolution comes just weeks after U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson shut down a similar proposal.

incidents.title: Trump Says He’ll Nominate Todd Blanche for AG
incidents.description: President Donald Trump said he would nominate Todd Blanche, who became acting attorney general after Pam Bondi’s dismissal, to become her permanent replacement.

incidents.title: India receives fourth S-400 regiment from Russia
incidents.description: Russia delivered India’s fourth S-400 regiment, a long-range aerial missile defense system. This delivery brings India 80% of the way through a five-squadron contract signed in 2018 worth $5.5 billion.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran exchange fire; Iran strikes Kuwait
incidents.description: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire over the course of the week, testing a fragile ceasefire. U.S. forces claimed they conducted pre-emptive strikes in self-defense against Iranian forces preparing attacks and intercepted drone and missile launches by Iran against Gulf states. Iranian bombardment against Kuwait’s international airport killed at least one person.

incidents.title: DRC reopens major airport after Ebola outbreak
incidents.description: The DRC government has reopened Bunia airport in Ituri, the region hit hardest by the recent Ebola outbreak. The decision follows a recent trip by World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, who stated he saw signs of improvement in the region. The reopening would permit increased humanitarian assistance to fly in, although all passengers will still require extensive screening. Latest government figures place the number of confirmed Ebola cases at 321 and deaths at 48.

incidents.title: Rodríguez visits India as Venezuelan oil exports grow
incidents.description: Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez began a five-day visit to India aimed at strengthening bilateral ties as Indian purchases of Venezuelan crude continue to increase. India imported about 427,000 barrels per day of Venezuelan oil in May, making it the second-largest buyer after the United States, with Reliance Industries emerging as one of the largest purchasers.

incidents.title: Qatar rejects introducing transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Qatar opposed proposals by Iran and Oman to introduce permanent transit fees through the Strait of Hormuz but indicated that a temporary fee could be negotiable. The Qatari government said it would consider temporary charges aimed at supporting mine clearance and restoring navigational safety. However, the U.S. and Middle Eastern and European countries have pushed back against transit tolls through the strait over concerns that higher shipping costs could raise consumer prices and intensify disruptions to global energy and trade flows.

incidents.title: Rubio says Venezuela less of a threat to U.S.
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told U.S. lawmakers that Venezuela no longer represents the same national security threat to the United States that it did under former President Nicolás Maduro, citing reforms undertaken by the interim government over the past five months. Rubio said Venezuela remains far from a democratic transition, noting that conditions for free elections are still absent and hundreds of political prisoners remain in detention.

incidents.title: Venezuela requires energy firms to generate their own electricity
incidents.description: A draft of Venezuela’s new hydrocarbon regulations would require oil and gas companies to generate their own electricity rather than rely on the national grid. The proposed rules would also allow private firms to supply power to energy projects as the government seeks to attract investment despite ongoing electricity shortages and frequent blackouts.

incidents.title: China services activity rises to highest rate in months
incidents.description: China’s General Services Purchasing Managers’ Index, indicating the level of services activity, rose from 52.6 in April to 54.4 in May, the fastest rate in three months. This comes as recent numbers for overall productivity in the country stayed low.

incidents.title: U.S. proposes tariff increase
incidents.description: The office of the U.S. Trade Representative proposed [RI1] [MM2] tariffs ranging between 10% and 12.5% on more than 60 countries. The recommendation follows a series of trade investigations into imported goods allegedly produced with forced labor, per Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act. The office recommended 10% tariffs on the EU, Taiwan, the U.K., Canada and Mexico among others, while the 12.5% would apply to China, India, and Japan. Public comments can be submitted prior to the tariffs’ implementation, with the comment period set to end on July 6, and a public hearing expected on July 7.

incidents.title: U.S. sanctions target Iranian crypto exchange
incidents.description: The U.S. enacted new sanctions against Nobiex, an Iranian cryptocurrency exchange after a Reuters investigation revealed that the financial institution is used to finance Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps operations and sanctions evasion schemes.

incidents.title: Trump ends push for "Anti-Weaponization" fund
incidents.description: Following weeks of bipartisan backlash, Trump has ended his attempt to establish a $1.8 billion fund to help compensate individuals that faced legal prosecution[EC1] [MM2] including Jan. 6 rioters. Trump’s backing down comes after Republican members of congress refused to support his new Department of Homeland Security budget should the “Anti-Weaponization” fund go through.

incidents.title: Ethiopia's ruling party expected to win upcoming election
incidents.description: Ethiopia’s ruling Prosperity Party, led by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, is projected to win local and parliamentary elections held this week. Balloting was not held in Tigray[EC1] [MM2] province after the National Election Board of Ethiopia ruling that conditions were not favorable in light of the political turmoil following the 2020 civil war. Critics of the government have previously accused it of human rights abuses and oppression of dissidents.

incidents.title: Philippines, Vietnam agree to South China Sea stability
incidents.description: During a visit to Vietnam this week, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. struck an agreement with Vietnamese leader To Lam to elevate bilateral ties to an “enhanced strategic partnership,” stating that stability in the South China Sea was “nonnegotiable.”

incidents.title: Czech lawmaker visits Taiwan
incidents.description: Czech Senate President Milos Vystrcil visited Taiwan this week, leading a delegation of academic and business leaders. Beijing condemned the visit, urging the Czech Republic to take measures to curb the impact of the trip. Despite maintaining official diplomatic relations with Beijing, Prague has been deepening ties with Taiwan in recent years, including on semiconductor research and drone technology.

incidents.title: China EV maker plans first plant in EU
incidents.description: Chinese automaker SAIC unveiled plans to open its first EU-based plant in the Spain’s Galicia region. The initial investment would be around €200 million.

incidents.title: Ukraine extends reach of strikes
incidents.description: The Ukrainian armed forces are currently capable of striking Russian army logistics nodes in all Russian-occupied territory, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said June 1.

incidents.title: Russia bans jet fuel exports
incidents.description: The Russian government banned jet fuel exports [EC1] [RI2] until late November due to Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries, which have forced domestic oil refineries to decrease or stop production. This restriction is being implemented to maintain domestic fuel market stability.

incidents.title: U.S. considers expanded deployment of nuclear-capable aircraft in Europe
incidents.description: The U.S. is considering increasing the number of NATO countries that host bombers capable of deploying nuclear warheads as an attempt to bolster European confidence in U.S. security commitments to Europe. The U.S. is seeking to reduce its conventional capabilities on the continent.

incidents.title: Philippines seeks closer ties with Taiwan
incidents.description: Philippine Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro stated that Manila was seeking closer ties with Taiwan and neighboring allies to counter “nefarious plans” from China. He made the comments during the Shangri La Dialogue, as well as calling for a scaling up of relations short of full diplomatic recognition.

incidents.title: Russia bombards Kyiv; Ukraine strikes St. Petersburg
incidents.description: Russia continued its bombardment campaign against Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, killing at least 16 Ukrainians on June 3. The same day, Ukrainian drone struck oil infrastructure in St. Petersburg as Russia hosted the Saint Petersburg International Economic Forum.

incidents.title: China conducts coast guard patrols near Taiwan
incidents.description: The Chinese coast guard conducted “law enforcement” operations near Taiwanese waters following last week’s summit between Japan and the Philippines, during which both countries agreed to launch maritime delimitation talks.

incidents.title: Hegseth addresses Shangri-La Dialogue
incidents.description: During an address at the annual Shangri-La Dialogue, U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth called on allies to spend more on defense, at least 3.5% of their GDP, while stating that the U.S. remained in favor of equilibrium in the region. China did not send its defense minister to the forum for the second year in a row.

incidents.title: U.S. closes chip export loophole
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Commerce issued new guidance on the export of advanced chips, specifically targeting a loophole that saw chips and processors being shipped to Chinese entities located outside China. These entities have likely been importing the chips at scale despite official guidance from Beijing not to rely on chip imports from the U.S.

incidents.title: India rejects U.K. mediation in Nepal dispute
incidents.description: Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah suggested to Nepal’s parliament that the United Kingdom should attempt to resolve his country’s border dispute with India, an idea that India's Ministry of External Affairs rejected, saying no outside party should have any role in what New Delhi considers a bilateral matter.

incidents.title: India appoints new defense chief
incidents.description: Retired Lt. Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani was appointed as India’s chief of defense staff on May 31, succeeding Gen. Anil Chauhan.

incidents.title: Trump cancels call with Taiwan
incidents.description: Sources near the White House said President Donald Trump no longer intends to call Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te regarding the possibility of arms sales before Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit in September. This would further push back a potential $14 billion arms sale first proposed in January and follows Trump’s recent trip to Beijing, during which time Xi stated that Taiwan was a subject to be approached with extreme caution.

incidents.title: Russian drone strikes Romania
incidents.description: A Russian drone strayed into Romania from Ukrainian airspace and crashed into an apartment complex overnight on May 29. No casualties were reported.

incidents.title: China expands nuclear launch capabilities
incidents.description: China has been expanding its nuclear launch capabilities, including a buildup of mobile launch units and communication arrays, effectively strengthening Beijing’s second strike capability in case of a larger conflict with the U.S.

incidents.title: Trump pushes to extend Abraham Accords
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said in a social media post on May 26, that Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Pakistan, Egypt, and Jordan must join the Abraham Accords as a condition to end the war in Iran.

incidents.title: Japan establishes intelligence council across ministries
incidents.description: The Japanese parliament passed a law establishing a new National Intelligence Council, as part of a host of national security reforms planned by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Takaichi would chair the council, which would see enhanced integration of intelligence collection and sharing among Japanese organizations, as well as more robust safeguards against foreign espionage.

incidents.title: Japan, Philippines start intelligence sharing talks
incidents.description: Japan and the Philippines have agreed to start negotiations on classified intelligence sharing, which would, among other things, remove barriers to Japanese weapons system exports to the Philippines. Both countries have worked to enhance defense ties as Chinese aggression in the region has increased.

incidents.title: U.S. announces shift in green card application process
incidents.description: The White House has announced that the U.S. will now require green card applicants to apply for the cards from their countries of origin. Only those applicants facing “extraordinary circumstances” may be granted an exception as determined by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service officers reviewing individual cases. This change comes as a significant shift in longstanding U.S. immigration policy.

incidents.title: New Fed Chief’s first report shows rising inflation
incidents.description: Newly appointed Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh has released his first inflation report, which shows the highest inflation rate in the last three years. The report indicates that the already rising inflation rate has been exacerbated by the economic impact of the Iran war. The personal consumption expenditures price index shows a rise of around 1% in inflation since the beginning of the war.

incidents.title: U.S. prosecutors told to avoid Delcy Rodríguez investigations
incidents.description: The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly instructed federal prosecutors in Miami to avoid pursuing criminal investigations into acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez, who is reported to have been on the Drug Enforcement Agency’s radar for years. U.S. Justice Department officials said Rodríguez had never formally been under investigation or charged in the United States.

incidents.title: Russia agrees to joint nuclear project with Kazakhstan
incidents.description: During a visit by Russian President Vladimir Putin to Astana on Thursday, Russia and Kazakhstan signed a historic agreement to build Kazakhstan’s first nuclear power plant since the Soviet era. The deal calls for Russia to finance 85% of the project through its state nuclear corporation, Rosatom, with the plant projected to become operational by 2036. The deal reflects stronger economic cooperation between the two countries. Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev noted that Russia and Kazakhstan are jointly developing 177 projects worth nearly $53 billion, with 122 of them already operational.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran OK ceasefire extension
incidents.description: The U.S. and Iran agreed to a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension on May 29, pending approval from U.S. President Donald Trump. Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baqai acknowledged on May 25 that negotiations with the U.S. toward a permanent peace deal had advanced but said a final agreement was “not imminent.” On May 26, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the peace process with Iran would require a “few more days” to reach a permanent end to the war.

incidents.title: Poland, U.K. sign defense treaty
incidents.description: Poland and the United Kingdom signed a bilateral defense cooperation treaty May 27 intended to mutually strengthen both countries’ military and cyber defenses against Russia.

incidents.title: Ukraine prepares for possible drone campaign in Belarus
incidents.description: Ukrainian armed forces have identified 500 targets for a drone campaign inside Belarus according to Maj. Robert Brovdi, commander of the Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces. The target list is intended to serve as deterrence against a Belarus entry into Russia’s war against Ukraine.

incidents.title: Israel kills Hamas military chief
incidents.description: An Israeli airstrike in Gaza killed Hamas’ military chief Mohammed Odeh on May 27. Israel had killed Odeh’s predecessor 11 days previously

incidents.title: Canada buys military aircraft from Sweden
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced that the Royal Canadian Air Force would purchase a fleet of Saab GlobalEye surveillance aircraft from Sweden instead of from U.S. competitors. This follows recent pledges by Carney to diversify defense acquisitions away from the U.S. Canada is currently reviewing the planned acquisition of 88 F-35 jets from the U.S.

incidents.title: EU to increase tariffs against China
incidents.description: The EU’s industry commissioner, Stéphane Séjourné, told news outlets that the bloc would systematically increase tariffs and quotas targeting imports of Chinese chemicals, metals, and clean technology to safeguard European industries, which Séjourné claims threaten at least 29 million European jobs.

incidents.title: Dutch trade minister to visit China
incidents.description: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma will visit China in early July. Sjoerdsma was previously sanctioned by Beijing for his outspoken criticism of China’s treatment of Uyghurs, and his visit comes as both countries have been stuck in a dispute over ownership of Chinese chipmaker Nexperia, as well as export restrictions for advanced lithography machines from ASML.

incidents.title: U.S. Secretary Rubio visits India
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited India to shore up ties, as Indian officials expressed worries about U.S. President Donald Trump’s increased trade rapprochement with China. Rubio and his Indian counterparts signed a framework agreement on securing critical mineral supply chains, though other agenda items including a Quad-focused meeting did not yield substantive results with regards to China.

incidents.title: China's underemployment levels rising
incidents.description: China’s job market is experiencing a strain due to low supply of jobs and high demand, with analysts warning of under- and unemployment levels likely rising in coming months due to rising costs and AI adoption.

incidents.title: China wards off Dutch frigate in South China Sea
incidents.description: Chinese forces were dispatched to drive away the Dutch frigate HNLMS De Ruyter, which was operating near the disputed Paracel islands in the South China Sea. Beijing warned the Netherlands not to send military assets into its territory, while the Netherlands stated it was operating within the boundaries of international law, per a 2016 ruling from The Hague that rejected China’s claims to the islands.

incidents.title: Venezuela releases military officers jailed in 2017 Maduro coup allegations
incidents.description: Venezuela released eight army officers who had been imprisoned since 2017 on accusations of plotting to overthrow former President Nicolás Maduro in the so-called “Paratrooper Case.” The release was part of the broader wave of political prisoner releases that has continued since Maduro’s removal earlier this year.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran agree to tentative ceasefire extension
incidents.description: The U.S. and Iran agreed to a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension on May 29, pending approval from U.S. President Donald Trump. Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baqai acknowledged on May 25 that negotiations with the U.S. toward a permanent peace deal had advanced, but that a final agreement was “not imminent.” On May 26, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the peace process with Iran would require a “few more days” before a permanent end to the war could be reached.

incidents.title: Asian oil markets remain unstable as US strikes on Iran continue
incidents.description: Oil prices rebounded in Asian markets Thursday following reports of new U.S. military action against Iranian targets that raised further concerns over renewed instability in the Gulf. Brent crude rose above $96 per barrel and WTI exceeded $90 on Thursday, reversing earlier declines driven by diplomatic optimism. Falling U.S. crude inventories and continued uncertainty surrounding regional security and maritime energy flows also contributed to the upward price movement.

incidents.title: Trump unsatisfied with Iran peace proposals
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he was "unsatisfied" with the terms Iran has proposed so far in ongoing negotiations to secure a permanent end to the war. Among other demands, a major point of friction is the Iranian demand for access to billions of dollars of frozen funds in overseas financial institutions.

incidents.title: U.K. announces new sanctions against Russia
incidents.description: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper unveiled a new sanctions package on May 26 targeting illicit Russian finance networks and sanction-evasion schemes. The sanctions target 18 separate entities.

incidents.title: NATO strengthens Baltic defense with German, Dutch troops
incidents.description: NATO bolstered its rapid response capabilities in the Baltics by assigning a combined German-Dutch army corps (a ground unit consisting of 40,000-60,000 soldiers) headquartered in Germany to the defense of Latvia and Estonia in the event of a NATO security crisis.

incidents.title: Taiwan intelligence identifies Chinese disinformation accounts
incidents.description: Taiwan’s National Security Bureau said it identified more than 9,000 messages and posts on social media posted by nearly 100 accounts following the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The bureau said it did not flag regular messages of public debate, rather focusing on messages and accounts consistent with disinformation operations undertaken by the Chinese Communist Party.

incidents.title: North Korea conducts AI-guided missile test
incidents.description: North Korea tested a variety of weapons systems, including a short-range ballistic missile equipped with a “special mission warhead.” South Korean news agency KCNA further reported the integration of AI targeting and guiding systems as part of Pyongyang’s drive to modernize its military capabilities.

incidents.title: Taiwan apprehends suspected microchip smugglers
incidents.description: Taiwanese authorities apprehended three individuals suspected of smuggling advanced Nvidia microchips into China through Japanese ports. The smuggled goods include chips that the U.S. had barred from sale to China, separate from the H20 and H200 chips, which Washington has greenlit for Chinese purchase, but so far have not been sold.

incidents.title: Ken Paxton wins Texas primary
incidents.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton unseated longtime U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in the 2026 Republican primary. Paxton’s victory comes following an endorsement from U.S. President Donald Trump. While some Democrats who see Paxton’s divisive reputation as helping them in November’s midterms welcomed the news, it has been more than 30 years since a Democrat represented Texas in the U.S. Senate.

incidents.title: India, U.S. sign critical minerals pact
incidents.description: India’s Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed a critical minerals framework deal on the sidelines of the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi.

incidents.title: Bangladesh increases India border patrols
incidents.description: Bangladeshi border patrols have increased surveillance along parts of its border with India after accusing Indian authorities of forcing suspected undocumented migrants into Bangladesh.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan expands EU-China rail network
incidents.description: Kazakhstan’s national railroad operator, Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, said it was expanding its infrastructure aimed at increasing the flow of trade between the EU and China, as the war in the Strait of Hormuz has forced regional players to adapt their trade routes.

incidents.title: India, Canada push to conclude CEPA by November
incidents.description: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal met Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu in Ottawa, with both sides advancing the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) deadline from December to November 2026 and targeting bilateral trade of $50 billion by 2030, up from the current $17 billion.

incidents.title: Nvidia CEO to join Chinese university board
incidents.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated he has agreed to join the advisory board of China’s Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management. The board also includes Apple CEO Tim Cook as chair, as well as Elon Musk, Michael Dell, Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg.

incidents.title: Quad ministers meet in New Delhi
incidents.description: Foreign ministers from Australia, India, and Japan, and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met in New Delhi for the 11th Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, announcing three initiatives: the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration for the Indian Ocean, a $20 billion Critical Minerals Initiative Framework, and the group’s first joint infrastructure project: a port in Fiji.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran exchange strikes
incidents.description: U.S. forces conducted airstrikes against four missile sites in southern Iran on May 26, reportedly to pre-empt planned attacks against U.S. forces. The U.S. carried out additional attacks in Iran on May 28. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliated by attacking a U.S. base in Kuwait.

incidents.title: U.S. conducts airstrikes in Iran amid peace talks
incidents.description: U.S. forces conducted airstrikes against four missile sites in southern Iran on May 26, reportedly to pre-empt planned attacks against U.S. forces in the region. The attacks occurred amid a ceasefire, as Iranian negotiators traveled to Doha to continue negotiations to seek a permanent end to the war. The U.S. carried out additional attacks in Iran on May 28. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliated by attacking a U.S. base in Kuwait.

incidents.title: Israel escalates campaign in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the IDF to “increase the intensity” of its strikes against Hezbollah positions in Lebanon, despite a recent 45-day ceasefire extension with Lebanon. Following Netanyahu’s orders, the Israel Defense Forces announced numerous strikes, issued new evacuation orders for Lebanese civilians, and began to expand its ground operations beyond the “yellow line” in southern Lebanon. The IDF conducted an airstrike in Beirut on May 28, marking the first strike in the Lebanese capital in three weeks.

incidents.title: Ukraine pushes for EU to appoint a special envoy to Russia
incidents.description: Ukraine is encouraging the EU to appoint a special envoy to Russia, as part of an effort to reinvigorate peace efforts and to represent united European negotiations, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said.

incidents.title: Russian Minister Lavrov warns Rubio of bombing escalation in Kyiv
incidents.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Russia would continue its large-scale and “systematic” attacks against Kyiv, and that the U.S. should evacuate its diplomatic staff. Russia initiated an escalation of its bombardment against the Ukrainian capital with a large-scale strike on May 25, that involved the hypersonic Oreshnik missile, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The escalation follows recent Ukrainian drone strikes in Moscow.

incidents.title: Cyberattack hits Lithuanian data centers
incidents.description: A cyberattack targeting Lithuanian national data registers resulted in the leak of over 600,000 data entries. The Lithuanian government attributed the attack to a foreign country, but did not specify which. A Lithuanian politician blamed Russia but did not provide evidence.

incidents.title: China cracks down on overseas stock trading
incidents.description: China has added restrictions against the use of overseas platforms for stock trading. The move is the latest crackdown by Beijing to prevent capital outflow, and brokers’ stocks have tumbled following the announcement.

incidents.title: US energy storage capacity increased amid Iran war
incidents.description: During the first quarter of 2026, U.S. energy storage capacity installations increased at a record pace as the industry responded to grid stability concerns, increasing electricity demand, and the unpredictability of renewable energy sources. The Solar Energy Industries Association reported 9.7 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage capacity were installed during the quarter. This included 7.8 GWh in utility-scale deployment; 0.65 GWh in commercial and industrial applications; and 0.52 GWh in residential buildings. This represents a 32% increase from the same period last year.

incidents.title: Venezuelan inmates protest alleged abuse
incidents.description: Inmates at Venezuela’s Barinas prison staged a rooftop protest, burned mattresses, and demanded the removal of the prison director after accusing guards of shooting unarmed prisoners during a demonstration. Prisoners and relatives also alleged abuse, torture, and harsh detention conditions at the facility.

incidents.title: India pivots from Gulf crude
incidents.description: Indian refiners increased purchases from Venezuela, Brazil, Angola, and Nigeria as the Iran war continues to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Venezuela is on course to become India’s fourth-largest crude supplier in May.

incidents.title: UAE trains Colombian mercenaries to fight in Sudan
incidents.description: A new Human Rights Watch report revealed that UAE forces hosted Colombian mercenaries for training before those forces were transferred to Sudan to assist the Rapid Support Forces, which have been repeatedly reported to have committed widespread human rights violations. The report further implicated the UAE as a collaborator in these abuses, charges the UAE has repeatedly denied

incidents.title: Iran begins to restore internet access
incidents.description: Internet access is being incrementally restored in Iran following government-imposed blackouts during the U.S.-Israeli bombardment campaign.

incidents.title: Gunman opens fire at White House checkpoint
incidents.description: Twenty-one-year-old Nasire Best opened fire at a White House checkpoints on May 23, striking a bystander before law enforcement personnel fatally wounded him. Best, who had a history of mental health issues, previously had received notice to stay away from the White House, according to a law enforcement officials speaking to Reuters. No law enforcement personal were injured in the incident. Best later died in a hospital.

incidents.title: Chinese coast guard operates near Taiwan-controlled islands
incidents.description: Taiwan’s coast guard reported a Chinese coast guard vessel operating in the waters off of the Taiwanese- controlled Pratas Islands in the South China Sea. Taiwanese forces were separately dispatched to closely monitor a Chinese patrol near Taiwan. Taiwanese authorities have stated they were on heightened alert following the recent meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

incidents.title: In U.S., hunger strike for release of ICE detainees continues
incidents.description: U.S. Sen. Andy Kim and U.S. Rep. Rob Menendez of New Jersy visited the Delaney Hall detention facility in Newark, where several immigration detainees had reportedly launched an ongoing hunger strike. A Department of Homeland Security statement claimed “there is no hunger strike in Delaney Hall at this time.” However, comments made by the congressmen contradict those statements.

incidents.title: China sends 15,000 tons of rice to Cuba
incidents.description: Cuba has received 15,000 tons of rice from China as the island continues its standoff with the United States. The U.S. has not relinquished its energy blockade of the country as negotiations over Cuba’s governance continue. The shipment from China is the first of an expected total of 60,000 tons, the largest between the countries yet, according to China’s ambassador to Cuba. The U.S. oil embargo continues to subject much of the island to blackouts, with sources near the White House stating they were preparing for a possible regime collapse as early as this summer.

incidents.title: Japan, Philippines begin intelligence-sharing negotiations
incidents.description: Japan and the Philippines will begin formal negotiations to deepen their security agreements to include the exchange and sharing of classified information, marking the first such agreement Japan has signed with a Southeast Asian country.

incidents.title: EU expands Iran sanctions list
incidents.description: The EU expanded an existing sanctions framework targeting Iranians who the European Council accused of keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed and impeding freedom of navigation.

incidents.title: Upcoming Xi visit to North Korea
incidents.description: South Korea’s Yonhap news agency reported it received intelligence that President Xi will likely visit Pyongyang as early as next week. This comes as China has steadily been reshoring ties with North Korea, sending multiple officials and planning new joint infrastructure

incidents.title: Drone incursions in Latvian airspace
incidents.description: Latvia scrambled NATO jets on three consecutive days to respond to Ukrainian drone incursions into its airspace. Ukraine attributed the incidents to Russian interference. Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia would prepare an “appropriate” response to allegations that Ukraine planned to launch drone strikes into Russia from Latvian territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed the accusations.

incidents.title: ConocoPhillips says Venezuela oil reforms fall short
incidents.description: ConocoPhillips said Venezuela’s revised hydrocarbons framework remains insufficient to attract major foreign investment, arguing the government still retains excessive fiscal and contractual control of the sector.

incidents.title: Iranian Supreme Leader forbids removal of weapons-grade uranium
incidents.description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ruled out the possibility that Iran’s highly enriched uranium stockpile should be removed from the country. Its removal to a third-party country is one of the key U.S. demands in negotiations to end its conflict. Security escalation level

incidents.title: US charges former Cuban leader with murder
incidents.description: The U.S. charged former Cuban President Raul Castro with conspiracy to kill U.S. nationals related to the shooting down of two planes en route to Florida from the island in 1996. Washington has increased pressure against Cuba to accede to demands it make meaningful changes to its governance structure. President Miguel Díaz-Canel accused the U.S. of charging Castro without any legal foundation as a political maneuver. Russia released a statement vowing to provide “continued support” for the island.

incidents.title: WHO announces Ebola outbreak in DRC/Uganada
incidents.description: The World Health Organization categorized an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a “public health emergency of international concern.” A rare strain of the Ebola virus, known as Bundibugyo, has spread chiefly in the DRC’s Ituri province, where violence from the local Islamic State group as well as weak public health infrastructure have contributed to containment and treatment response shortfalls by health authorities. At least 139 deaths and almost 600 suspected cases have been attributed to the outbreak, although the long incubation period of the virus means the totals may be considerably higher

incidents.title: Taiwanese president pushes for new drone budget
incidents.description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te announced he would push ahead with new drone-focused budgets, despite opposition party maneuvers to block them

incidents.title: DOJ charges Raul Castro
incidents.description: Former Cuban leader and brother to Fidel Castro was charged by the DOJ with murder and conspiracy for his alleged involvement with a 1996 downing of two planes with American passengers. The charges come as a serious escalation in U.S.-Cuban tensions which have been building in recent months. The sudden accusation is similar to charges made by the U.S. to help justify the capture of Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro, fueling fears the U.S. may plan a similar operation in Cuba.

incidents.title: China bans Nvidia gaming chip
incidents.description: China banned its companies from purchasing Nvidia’s RTX 5090D V2 gaming chip last week, despite Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joining U.S. President Donald Trump in Beijing for his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Beijing continues to deny the import of Nvidia’s H20 and H200 chips, as it seeks to develop stronger technological independence for its supply chains.

incidents.title: India, Italy Elevate Ties
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni upgraded the countries’ bilateral relations to a special strategic partnership during their meeting in Rome, agreeing to annual leader meetings and a trade target of 20 billion euros by 2029, with a focus on defense, aerospace, clean technologies, and the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.

incidents.title: Chinese rare earth exports to Japan rise slightly
incidents.description: Shipments of Chinese rare earth magnets to Japan rose slightly by 2.5% in April following a slump period in March. Despite that, Japanese firms have issued strong warnings of rare earth shortages, with some companies not having received deliveries of magnets from China since November, as tensions between both countries continue.

incidents.title: U.S. forces board Iranian vessel
incidents.description: The U.S. military reported its forces boarded an Iranian-flagged oil tanker attempting to bypass a U.S. blockade in the Gulf of Oman. Following the interdiction, the vessel was redirected, according to U.S. officials.

incidents.title: US pauses Russian oil sanctions
incidents.description: U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on oil exports from Russia have been paused for another 30 days, allowing countries to buy oil and petroleum products transported by sea from Russia. The waiver extension comes as the Middle East conflict and the partial blockade of the Strait of Hormuz have contributed to rising oil prices.

incidents.title: EU planning new divestment regulations
incidents.description: As it continues to develop laws and regulations to reduce reliance on China, the EU is working on plans that would require European companies to buy critical components from at least three different suppliers based in different countries. China had previously expressed disappointment in the EU’s decision.

incidents.title: Putin visits Beijing
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, on the heels of U.S. President Donald Trump’s visit. Putin, who received similar red-carpet treatment as Trump, and Xi reaffirmed their ties and condemned the U.S.’s Golden Dome missile defense system, no major cooperation deals were signed. China further refused to provide concrete deliverables or timelines for Russia’s “Power of Siberia 2” pipeline.

incidents.title: Trump to discuss arms sales with Taiwan
