incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would discuss the pending $14 billion arms sale to the island that had been delayed due to his visit to Beijing with Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te. Beijing separately said it would not confirm a visit from U.S. Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby until it gains clarity on Trump’s decision.

incidents.title: China allegedly trained Russian soldiers
incidents.description: China hosted and trained around 200 Russian military personnel last year, including on the use of drones, European intelligence services told Reuters. China has repeatedly maintained its neutrality in the Ukraine conflict, despite aid to Russia in the form of supplies and funding

incidents.title: Rupee drops to record low
incidents.description: The value of the rupee fell to a record low at 96.96 per U.S. dollar, compared with the previous low of 96.6150. Since the Iran war began, the rupee has fallen over 6% as oil prices affect India’s economic outlook.

incidents.title: Venezuela expands legal protections for foreign oil investors
incidents.description: Venezuela’s oil minister said the country’s new hydrocarbons framework will allow international dispute resolution outside Venezuela, addressing a longstanding demand from foreign energy firms seeking legal certainty in a move aimed at encouraging greater foreign investment.

incidents.title: U.S./NATO relationship strains further
incidents.description: The White House plans to formally reduce the number of forces and capabilities it would commit to a security crisis in Europe, according to U.S. officials. The specifics of the plan are likely to remain classified, although Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby clarified that the U.S. nuclear umbrella would continue to extend to its European allies. U.S. Air Force Lt. Gen. and NATO Supreme Allied Commander Alex Grynkewich said he does not expect that the U.S. will withdraw additional troops beyond the 5,000 previously announced by Trump.

incidents.title: India-Nordic summit produces green technology strategic partnership
incidents.description: India and leaders of five Nordic countries elevated their bilateral relationship to a Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership. The joint statement called for accelerated cooperation on renewable energy, green hydrogen, carbon capture, and critical minerals. India and Finland also announced that they would jointly host the World Circular Economy Forum in Gandhinagar in September.

incidents.title: U.S. extends Russian oil sanctions relief
incidents.description: The U.S. granted a 30-day extension to a sanctions waiver on Russian oil shipments currently at sea, now set to expire on June 17.

incidents.title: Estonia downs Ukrainian drone
incidents.description: An Estonian jet shot down a Ukrainian drone that had strayed into Estonia airspace from Russia on May 19. The incident marked the first time a NATO pilot shot down a Ukrainian drone during the war.

incidents.title: U.S./Israeli plot to reinstall Ahmadinejad
incidents.description: An initial U.S./Israeli war aim in Iran was to free former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from house arrest in Tehran and reinstall him as the president of the country after killing most of Iran’s prewar senior leadership, according to unnamed sources cited by The New York Times. Various media outlets reported that Ahmadinejad, who was wounded in a strike on the first day of the war that killed the guards keeping him confined, had been briefed on the Israeli-designed operation. His whereabouts are unknown.

incidents.title: Rep. Thomas Massie loses House seat
incidents.description: In a significant win for U.S. President Donald Trump, U.S. Rep. Thomas Massie, one of his harshest critics , lost a Republican Party primary race to a Trump-backed candidate. Kentucky voters instead nominated Ed Gallrein, who is far more amenable to the president's agenda, to run in November’s general election. Massie earned Trump’s ire after he criticized the president's tax plan and his refusal to publish findings of investigations into disgraced financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

incidents.title: US pauses participation with Canada in Joint Board of Defense
incidents.description: U.S. Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby announced the U.S. would pause its participation in the Permanent Joint Board on Defense, a bilateral cooperation mechanism with Canada, citing insufficient progress from Canada to meet defense requirements. Among other achievements, the board, established in 1940, aided in the creation of the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD). Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously vowed to raise the country’s defense spending to 2%.of GDP.

incidents.title: Casualty count in Lebanon grows despite ceasefire
incidents.description: The number of Lebanese killed by Israeli strikes in the latest round of fighting surpassed 3,000 in the wake of numerous Israeli bombing operations in Lebanon, and ground clashes with Hezbollah, despite a recent 45-day extension of the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

incidents.title: Pakistan deploys to Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: Pakistan deployed at least 8,000 troops and 16 aircraft to Saudi Arabia, as part of a mutual defense treaty between the two.

incidents.title: Chinese economy slows to lowest point in 3 years
incidents.description: China’s overall economic growth slowed to its lowest point during the month of April since December 2022, with stagnating retail sales falling short of a 2% forecast. The slowdown comes despite the country’s recent record-high export levels, highlighting the urgency the Chinese Communist Party places on driving up domestic consumption.

incidents.title: Russia, Belarus begin nuclear drills
incidents.description: Russia and Belarus began joint military exercises in Belarusian territory on May 21. Russia has moved nuclear warheads into Belarus as part of the drills, according to the Belarusian Defense Ministry.

incidents.title: AI becomes Baidu’s largest income source
incidents.description: Chinese company Baidu hit a milestone as its AI businesses became the company’s largest source of revenue, with a 49% year-on-year increase, despite the company’s overall slight dip in income.

incidents.title: North Korea to reinforce southern border
incidents.description: Kim Jong Un called on his top military officers to reinforce its border with South Korea, reportedly using multidomain experience gained through deployments in Ukraine to bolster front-line units as tensions between Pyongyang and Seoul continue.

incidents.title: U.S./Iran negotiations continue
incidents.description: Iran said it was reviewing the latest peace proposal from the United States via Pakistani mediators, while U.S. President Donald Trump said he delayed planned strikes against Iran as he demanded the “right answers” from Iranian negotiators. Both Israel and the U.S. are positioned to resume offensive operations against Iran quickly.

incidents.title: Possible Iran sanctions relief
incidents.description: Iranian media sources have claimed the U.S. offered temporary sanctions relief for Iran’s oil sector as a part of ongoing peace negotiations. The U.S. has not confirmed the claim.

incidents.title: NextEra Energy to buy Dominion Energy
incidents.description: NextEra Energy, a major U.S. energy provider, announced plans to buy competitor Dominion Energy for $66.8 billion. Should this purchase go through, NextEra would become the globe’s largest electric utility by market value. The merger was prompted in part by the need to meet increased power demand posed by the U.S. data center boom.

incidents.title: White House pauses security pact with Canada
incidents.description: The Trump administration has decided to pause a World War II-era joint security arrangement with Canada. This decision comes after U.S. President Donald Trump accused Canada of insufficient military spending despite Ottawa’s pledge to increase its military budget to 5% of GDP over the next decade, further straining the U.S.-Canada relationship. U.S. combativeness with its NATO allies remains a fixture of recent U.S. foreign policy.

incidents.title: Possible Iran sanctions relief
incidents.description: Iranian media sources are claiming that the U.S. has offered temporary sanctions relief on Iran’s oil sector as a part of ongoing peace negotiations. The U.S. has so far not confirmed the authenticity of the claim.

incidents.title: U.S./Iran negotiations continue
incidents.description: Iran said it was reviewing the latest peace proposal from the United States via Pakistani mediators, while U.S. President Donald Trump said he delayed planned strikes against Iran as he demanded the “right answers” from Iranian negotiators. Both Israel and the U.S. are positioned to resume offensive operations against Iran quickly.

incidents.title: U.S. and China form boards of trade
incidents.description: Following last week’s summit with U.S. President Donald Trump, China said that it agreed to establish bilateral boards for trade and investment, while reaffirming its commitment to purchase aircraft, aircraft engines, and components from the U.S.

incidents.title: Tata Electronics, ASML sign semiconductor deal
incidents.description: India’s Tata Electronics and Dutch chipmaking equipment manufacturer ASML signed a deal to support India’s first commercial semiconductor fabrication plant, backed by Tata’s $11 billion investment. ASML will supply advanced lithography machines for manufacturing AI, automotive, and mobile chips at a plant in Dholera, Gujarat.

incidents.title: India, Sweden launch AI corridor
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. They leaders elevated Indian-Swedish ties to a strategic partnership and established the India-Sweden Technology and AI Corridor.

incidents.title: UAE nuclear plant struck by drones
incidents.description: The United Arab Emirates’ Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, was the target of an unclaimed drone attack. Barakah, the first commercial nuclear power facility in the Arab world, has a generation capacity of 5.6 gigawatts and supplies 25% of the UAE's electricity use. The attack caused an external generator at the 4 WEEKLY FORECAST MONITOR plant to catch fire, but did not cause injuries or radiation leaks. All four reactors are operating normally, according to UAE nuclear regulators and the International Atomic Energy Agency.

incidents.title: Ukrainian drone strikes in Moscow
incidents.description: A May 18 Ukrainian attack of over 500 drones killed at least three people in the Moscow area, according to Russian officials.

incidents.title: Israel expands occupations in Gaza, Syria, and Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel has expanded its territorial occupation of Gaza from approximately 53% of the Palestinian territory to 60% since the ceasefire deal with Hamas went into effect, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In total, Israel has expanded its regional territorial occupations since the October 7 attacks by 1,000 square kilometers in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria according to analysis by the Financial Times.

incidents.title: Drone hits Emirati nuclear power plant
incidents.description: An unattributed drone strike caused a fire at an Emirati nuclear power plant on May 17. Emirati officials have not publicly attributed the attack to Iran.

incidents.title: Venezuela deports former Maduro ally Alex Saab to U.S.
incidents.description: Venezuela deported Alex Saab, an ally of former President Nicolás Maduro, to the United States less than three years after his release in a Biden-era prisoner swap. Saab, long viewed as a key financial operative for the Maduro network, could now become a critical witness in U.S. proceedings against Maduro.

incidents.title: Modi announces five-nation tour
incidents.description: India’s Ministry of External Affairs announced that Prime Minister Narendra Modi will undertake a five-nation tour May 15-20 covering the UAE, Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and Italy. The UAE stop will focus on energy security and securing fuel supply chains amid the Hormuz crisis. The European stops will prioritize semiconductors, green hydrogen, AI, defense, and follow-up on the India-EU free trade agreement. The Norway stop marks the first visit by an Indian prime minister in 43 years and will include the third India-Nordic Summit.

incidents.title: UAE to build new oil pipline
incidents.description: The United Arab Emirates has accelerated development of a new oil pipeline that would bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The pipeline, with a completion date expected in 2027, is expected to be capable of carrying1.5 million to 1.8 million barrels per day, , effectively doubling the UAE’s export capacity through Fujairah. The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) aims to increase its production capacity to 5 million bpd by that time, an increase of roughly 1.1 million to 1.2 million bpd from current production levels. The country’s exit from OPEC will likely provide it with greater flexibility to expand output and support this production target. ADNOC also warned that full oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz may not return before 2027, projecting prolonged instability and disruption in regional energy markets.

incidents.title: Modi secures UAE petroleum reserve, LPG deals
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Abu Dhabi produced seven formal agreements, including a crude oil storage deal between India’s Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd. and Abu Dhabi National Oil Company; an LPG supply agreement; a strategic defense partnership framework; and $5 billion in UAE investment commitments. Modi also publicly condemned Iranian strikes on the UAE.

incidents.title: Large scale protests planned across the South
incidents.description: Democrats and civil rights activists across the south are planning a series of large-scale demonstrations to start in late May and go through the summer to advocate for fair voting rights following the Supreme Court ruling which narrowed the ability of the Voting Rights Act to protect access to voting.

incidents.title: Vessel seized in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: The British military reported that a vessel off the coast of the UAE had been seized and was being brought into Iranian territorial waters on May 14. The report did not identify the nationality of the ship’s crew or specify whether Iran had conducted the seizure.

incidents.title: Protests erupt in Cuba
incidents.description: Protests broke out in Havana on Wednesday against the government’s handling of the deteriorating power [KH1] [MM2] situation on the island. Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy said Cuba has exhausted its diesel and fuel[RI3] [MM4] oil supplies. This comes as the U.S. has reiterated its offer to send $100 million in exchange for “meaningful reforms” to the Communist system, sending CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Havana for a new round of negotiations on Thursday. The blackouts have impacted hospitals, schools, and government offices.

incidents.title: Israel and Lebanon begin new round of talks
incidents.description: Israel and Lebanon began a third round of direct peace talks mediated by the U.S. in Washington, D.C., on May 14, during which Israeli officials proposed a phased plan to achieve the disarmament of Hezbollah and increase political ties with the Lebanese government.

incidents.title: Latvian Prime Minister resigns
incidents.description: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Silina resigned on May 14, following the collapse of her coalition government. The series of events leading to her resignation was initiated by Silina’s firing of Latvian Defense Minister Andris Spruds after Latvian defense forces failed to intercept Ukrainian drones that flew into Latvian airspace from Russia. Following Spruds’ firing, his party withdrew support from Silina’s government.

incidents.title: Trump and Xi hail trade ties
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump travelled to Beijing, where he met with Chinese President Xi Jinping for two days of high-level talks on extending the trade truce that both parties agreed to last November. Both leaders hailed positive ties and an improved outlook for the future. Xi expressed interest in purchasing oil from the U.S. to make up for losses from Iran, and both sides pledged to identify low-risk products they can reduce tariffs on. While the U.S. hopes to get China more involved in stopping the Iran conflict, China signaled it wants the U.S. to change its stance on Taiwan.

incidents.title: China hits record trade numbers
incidents.description: Chinese imports and exports hit record numbers in the month of April, with a trade surplus of $84.8 billion in that time. The low level of imports highlights China’s ambitions to continue to wean off reliance on foreign products. While Beijing wants to spur on domestic consumption, its export-driven model still holds solid ground despite global trade disruptions.

incidents.title: Poland scrambles jets in response to Russian flight
incidents.description: Poland scrambled fighter jets and intercepted a Russian reconnaissance and surveillance aircraft over international waters in the Baltic Sea on May 14.

incidents.title: BRICS foreign ministers meeting held in New Delhi
incidents.description: India hosted the BRICS Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on May 14-15 in New Delhi in the runup to the BRICS summit in September. Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi attended despite ongoing UAE-Iran tensions, pressing members to navigate internal divisions on the war in Iran. He also called on BRICS members to condemn what he called U.S. and Israeli “unlawful aggression” against Tehran. The meeting agenda covered global governance reform and preparations for the September summit.

incidents.title: Japan reports large EV market value loss
incidents.description: Honda reported an annual loss of approximately $9 billion from its electric vehicles business, marking one of its most significant financial setbacks in decades. The company has indefinitely suspended its planned $11 billion EV and battery investment project in Canada, signaling a broader reassessment of aggressive electrification strategies among legacy automakers. This reflects wider challenges facing the global EV market amid slowing demand, rising costs, and intensifying competition

incidents.title: Iran to allow Chinese vessels to transit the strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Iran will allow some Chinese vessels to transit the strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Iranian news agency, Fars.

incidents.title: Keir Starmer faces pressure to resign after election loss
incidents.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer is facing a renewed wave of pressure to resign following heavy losses by the governing Labour Party in local elections across England, Scotland, and Wales. The defeats have surfaced divisions in his party, with nearly 90 members of Parliament urging him to resign and Secretary of Health Wes Streeting being the first of his Cabinet members to resign. The local elections saw big gains made by the far-right Reform party, as well as the leftist Green Party.

incidents.title: Israeli bombardment of Gaza increases
incidents.description: Israeli bombardment of Gaza has increased by 20% over the last five weeks going back to April 8, according to data gathered by the independent conflict monitoring group ACLED.

incidents.title: South Korea pledges to support U.S. in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: South Korea is reviewing plans to contribute to U.S. efforts to secure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, according to South Korean Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back, who clarified that South Korea will not conduct military operations in the strait.

incidents.title: U.N. official comments on political future of Hamas
incidents.description: U.N. Special Coordinator Nickolay Mladenov, the top U.N. official responsible for coordinating with U.S. President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace in Gaza, said he can envision a political future for Hamas in Gaza provided the group first disarms.

incidents.title: China expresses disappointment in EU
incidents.description: China stated it was “very disappointed” in the EU’s ambitions to restrict investment by Chinese companies. This comes as the EU is looking to pass stricter cybersecurity laws and looking to limit excessive reliance on foreign supply chains.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Russian oil infrastructure on Black Sea
incidents.description: Ukrainian drones struck Russian oil infrastructure on the Black Sea coast near the port of Taman on May 14.

incidents.title: Kevin Warsh confirmed as new Federal Reserve Chair
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate narrowly confirmed Kevin Warsh as the new chair of the Federal Reserve. Warsh is replacing Jerome Powell, whose eight-year tenure was marked by repeated clashes with the White House regarding the Fed’s independence

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia, UAE attacked Iran during war
incidents.description: Both Saudi Arabia and the UAE conducted retaliatory attacks against Iran alongside U.S. and Israeli forces, according to reporting from multiple media sources. Neither Saudi Arabia nor the UAE have publicly acknowledged the strikes.

incidents.title: Trump doubles down on proposal to make Venezuela the 51st U.S. state
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump renewed his suggestion that Venezuela could become the 51st U.S. state on May 13, posting a map of the country overlaid with an American flag after saying he was seriously considering the idea. Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez firmly rejected Trump’s suggestion.

incidents.title: Venezuela launches sovereign and PDVSA debt restructuring
incidents.description: Venezuela announced a comprehensive restructuring of its sovereign debt and the liabilities of state oil company PDVSA on May 13, aiming to secure substantial relief from what it described as unsustainable financial burdens.

incidents.title: Europe accepts Chinese bonds as collateral
incidents.description: European financial intermediary Euroclear has stated it plans to accept Chinese bonds traded in Hong Kong as an acceptable collateral, marking a potential win for China’s drive to internationalize the renminbi currency.

incidents.title: India, Russia in talks on critical minerals pact
incidents.description: India and Russia are in advanced talks on a preliminary critical minerals agreement covering exploration, processing, and technology, focused on lithium and rare earths. India’s Ministry of Mines has shared a draft with Russian counterparts, with a signing expected within two months. The pact aims to reduce India’s dependence on China’s dominance of rare earth processing.

incidents.title: U.S. mayor pleads guilty to being an illegal foreign agent
incidents.description: Eileen Weng, mayor of the Southern California city of Arcadia, agreed to plead guilty to one charge of acting as a foreign agent on behalf of China. FBI director Kash Patel commented that the FBI would move to “root out” any other such foreign influence in American institutions.

incidents.title: Chinese LNG imports recover after shortfall
incidents.description: Ship-tracking data shows China's LNG imports rebounding in mid-May 2026 after falling to an eight-year low in April. China imported 3.5 million tons of LNG in April, down 30% from the previous year and the lowest since 2018. LNG imports fell due to rising prices and reduced Middle Eastern supplies due to the ongoing conflict, Strait of Hormuz closure, and damage to Qatar’s LNG infrastructure damage. Attractive spot prices for LNG for the month of May have encouraged buyers to expand imports and prepare for summer peak power demand.

incidents.title: Qatar oil tankers cross through strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers crossed the Strait of Hormuz for the second time this week, carrying approximately 174,000 cubic meters of LNG bound for Pakistan. According to the report[KH1] [ST2] , the LNG cargo was sold under a government-to-government agreement and received approval from Iran. Pakistan has been in discussions with Tehran to facilitate LNG transit through the strait due to worsening domestic gas shortages since the outbreak of the war. Additional Qatari LNG shipments to Pakistan are expected in the coming days.

incidents.title: Iran expands area defined as Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Iran has expanded the area it defines as the Strait of Hormuz, according to Deputy Political Director of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy Mohammad Akbarzadeh. Iranian news agencies reported that the new area of operations described by Akbarzadeh encompasses 200-300 miles, up from 20-30 miles.

incidents.title: US threats towards Greenland drive up tourism
incidents.description: Following threats by the Trump administration earlier this year about annexing Greenland, U.S. officials have confirmed they had been holding high-level talks with Danish and Greenlandic counterparts about a deal that would see an increased U.S. troop presence on the island with the consent of all parties involved. While details remain scarce, talks indicate tentative plans to open three new U.S. bases on the island that could be designated as sovereign U.S. territory.

incidents.title: EU Sanctions Israeli West Bank Settlers
incidents.description: On May 11 the EU approved sanctions against Israeli settler leaders and political organizations as well as Hamas leaders.

incidents.title: Taiwan reveals tentative HIMARS plans
incidents.description: Taiwan has provided more details on its potential usage of the HIMARS systems it is purchasing from the U.S., stating they would be deployed to Penghu County and Dongyin Island to force a retreat of Chinese military forces.

incidents.title: U.S. imposes sanctions on Chinese satellite companies
incidents.description: Days before U.S. President Donald Trump’s trip to China, the U.S. Department of State imposed sanctions on three Chinee commercial satellite companies for their alleged role in supplying Iran with imagery used to conduct strikes against U.S. forces in the Middle East. China voiced strong opposition to the sanctions but has not yet taken retaliatory action.

incidents.title: China, U.S. arrest drug smugglers
incidents.description: Chinese and U.S. authorities arrested five individuals accused of trafficking drugs, both in the U.S. and in China. The arrests came in early April and are the latest sign of cooperation in stemming flows of fentanyl to the U.S., something the Trump administration placed a heavy priority on early in its second term.

incidents.title: Ceasefire violations in Russia and Ukraine
incidents.description: Russia and Ukraine accused each other of ceasefire violations and Russia carried out large scale attacks against Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.

incidents.title: Renminbi appreciates ahead of summit
incidents.description: The People’s Bank of China set the renminbi at its strongest level since 2023 this week ahead of the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. This likely signals not only a gesture of goodwill to the U.S., which has long accused China of undervaluing its currency, but also the potential easing of deflationary pressures and strong export competitiveness.

incidents.title: U.S. inflation reaches highest point in four years
incidents.description: The U.S. wholesale inflation reached 6% in April 2026, a figure not seen since 2022. The spike caused in part by rise in fuel prices amid the U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Bureau of Labor Statistics data reported by Bloomberg shows a 5% jump in gas prices in April, significantly slower than the 21% in the previous month.

incidents.title: Pakistan summons Afghan diplomat following attack
incidents.description: The Pakistani government summoned a senior Afghan diplomat following a suicide attack in Pakistan’s northwest border region that killed 15 police officers. Islamabad blamed Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan and accused Afghanistan of sheltering and aiding the group, an accusation the Taliban government in Kabul denies.

incidents.title: Modi urges Indians to cut fuel use and gold purchases
incidents.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly appealed to Indians to conserve fuel, avoid international travel, reduce gold purchases, and work from home as the Iran war pushed Brent crude to approximately $105 per barrel. India imports nearly 85% of its fuel needs and relies on the Strait of Hormuz for about 50% of its crude imports and almost all its liquefied petroleum gas. Opposition leaders immediately attacked the appeal as a sign of government failure.

incidents.title: China blocks Taiwan from WHO attendance
incidents.description: China stated it would not allow Taiwan to participate in the annual assembly of the World Health Organization starting next week. Taiwan stated it would still send a delegation over that would take part in meetings outside of the main summit.

incidents.title: Trump looks to suspend U.S. federal gas tax
incidents.description: Trump announced he will seek a suspension of the federal gas tax for an undetermined amount of time. This move, which would require congressional approval, comes after the U.S. Energy Information Administration reported the national average for gas has reached $4.45 per gallon.

incidents.title: Venezuela rejects ICJ jurisdiction in Essequibo dispute, defends claim to Guyana region
incidents.description: Venezuela reaffirmed on May 11 that it does not recognize the International Court of Justice’s authority in the dispute over the resource-rich Essequibo region, arguing the 1966 Geneva Agreement should determine sovereignty.

incidents.title: Trump rejects Iran peace proposal
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran, calling it “garbage” and saying that the ceasefire effort was on “life support.” Despite Trump’s rejection, U.S. Vice President JD Vance said he felt progress was being made toward a peace deal.

incidents.title: Iran executes alleged collaborator
incidents.description: Iran executed 29-year-old graduate student Erfan Shakourzadeh after accusing him of collaborating with the CIA and Mossad during the joint U.S./Israeli bombing campaign against Iran. Shakourzadeh denounced the charges prior to his execution as a “fabrication.” Iran has executed at least five of its citizens since the ceasefire began with the U.S. and Israel, all on similar charges.

incidents.title: Trump rejects Iran peace proposal
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran, calling it “garbage” and saying that the ceasefire effort was on “life support.” Among other conditions, Iran had demanded an end to Israeli operations in Lebanon and for reparations to be paid for war damages from the U.S. and Israel.

incidents.title: U.S. expresses disappointment in Taiwan defense budget
incidents.description: U.S. officials have voiced their disappointment in Taiwan’s latest defense budget, which was a reduced version of the initially proposed $40 billion to be used on procuring arms from the U.S.

incidents.title: Trump’s approval rating hits its lowest ever point
incidents.description: As the Iran war and its deleterious effects on the U.S. economy become more pronounced, a record high number of Americans now disapprove of U.S. President Donald Trump’s performance. A new Financial Times poll indicated the Trump tariffs and war with Iran are hurting the Republicans Party's midterm election prospects.

incidents.title: Qatar-mediated talks excluded Machado from post-Maduro transition planning
incidents.description: Reporting on May 10 indicated that Qatar-mediated talks between U.S. and Venezuelan officials before Nicolás Maduro’s capture did not include any role for opposition leader María Corina Machado in discussions over post-transition governance.

incidents.title: Putin, Trump comment on Ukraine war
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said May 9 that he thinks the war in Ukraine is “coming to an end” soon. On May 12, U.S. President Donald Trump also said that he thinks the war will end soon but noted that there is no understanding between himself and Putin that Russia will receive the entirety of Ukraine’s Donbas region as a condition to end the war.

incidents.title: Virginia Supreme Court rejects gerrymandered map
incidents.description: The Virginia Supreme Court rejected a new redistricting map that would have given increased congressional representation to Democrats. A private call between Democratic House members and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries indicated frustration with the court's ruling and a desire to continue seeking ways to flip two Republican seats in the state.

incidents.title: Israeli forces continue daily bombing campaign in Lebanon and issue new evacuation orders
incidents.description: Israeli forces sustained a wide-scale bombing campaign and issued civilian evacuation orders across southern Lebanon as Hezbollah conducted drone attacks in northern Israel and clashed with Israeli forces in southern Lebanon.

incidents.title: China confirms on-site technical support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor
incidents.description: China confirmed on May 10 that it provided on-site technical support to Pakistan’s air force during the May 2025 conflict with India, according to Chinese state media. India’s Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson responded on May 13 stating that “responsible nations must reflect on whether supporting attempts to protect terrorist infrastructure affects their reputation and standing.”

incidents.title: ASEAN leaders discuss joint energy projects
incidents.description: ASEAN leaders met last week and agreed to explore the development of a shared fuel reserve mechanism. The initiative aims to mitigate high oil prices and rising power costs during major geopolitical disruptions, such as the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., this year’s ASEAN chair, said the bloc should move beyond reacting to crises and instead strengthen its preparedness through existing regional mechanisms and institutions.

incidents.title: U.S.-led forces remove uranium from Venezuela
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Energy announced that the United States, United Kingdom, and Venezuela removed 13.5 kilograms of highly enriched uranium from a Venezuelan research reactor.

incidents.title: Russia warns foreign embassies in Kyiv
incidents.description: Russia’s Foreign Ministry released a message warning foreign embassies in Kyiv to pre-emptively evacuate their staff prior to Victory Day celebrations in Moscow, saying that Kyiv would face retaliatory strikes in the event of attacks in Moscow during the holiday.

incidents.title: U.S. and Ukrainian officials to meet in Miami
incidents.description: Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine Rustem Umerov is scheduled to meet with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in Miami to discuss peace efforts.

incidents.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills son of Hamas chief negotiator
incidents.description: An Israeli airstrike in Gaza on May 7 killed the son of the chief Hamas official negotiating with the U.S.

incidents.title: US supreme court rules Trump tariffs are unlawful
incidents.description: The U.S. Court of International Trade ruled that the 10% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration in February were unlawful. The ruling targets the universal tariffs imposed under Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act but has only blocked the tariffs affecting two companies that sued the administration over the issue, rather than a universal injunction.

incidents.title: Venezuela expands dollar sales to reduce inflation pressure
incidents.description: Venezuela’s government increased dollar sales and allowed the bolívar to depreciate in an effort to narrow the gap with the parallel exchange market and reduce inflationary pressure.

incidents.title: ShinyHunters cyberattack hits universities
incidents.description: A cyberattack claimed by the hacking group ShinyHunters disrupted the Canvas academic software platform used by thousands of schools and universities across the United States, Canada, Australia, and elsewhere. The outage affected an estimated 9,000 institutions during the end-of-year academic period.

incidents.title: Trump, Lula discuss U.S.-Brazil trade ties
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump met Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Washington to discuss strengthening trade relations and easing tariff tensions between the two countries. The meeting signaled a potential improvement in bilateral economic relations despite recent trade friction.

incidents.title: Trump says U.S., Iran near deal
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States and Iran were close to reaching an agreement after what he described as productive talks. Iranian officials said they were still reviewing U.S. proposals.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran exchange fire despite ceasefire
incidents.description: U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged fire despite the ceasefire remaining formally in effect. Neither side withdrew from the agreement following the incident.

incidents.title: General calls for deeper private sector military innovation
incidents.description: People’s Liberation Army Maj. Gen. Zhang Zhan, political commissar of the National University of Defense Technology, urged China to expand private-sector participation in military research. Zhang warned that U.S.-led efforts to limit China’s access to advanced technologies risk undermining the country’s long-term defense innovation capacity.

incidents.title: India marks Operation Sindoor anniversary
incidents.description: India held ceremonies marking the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor, the airstrikes on nine alleged terrorist infrastructure sites inside Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. The Indian Air Force commemorated the anniversary at precisely 1:05am, mirroring the timing of the original strikes. Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the armed forces' precision and resolve, calling it a defining moment in India's counterterrorism doctrine. SIPRI data published in April 2026 showed India's military spending rose 8.9% to $92.1 billion in 2025, elevating it to the world's fifth-largest military spender following the operation.

incidents.title: U.S., Philippines and Japan continue annual drills
incidents.description: The U.S., Japan, and the Philippines continued to hold their annual “Balikatan” military drills in the South China Sea. This comes as Japan considers potential military equipment transfers with the Philippines, made possible by recent decisions by Tokyo to allow the export of lethal weapons systems.

incidents.title: Internet blackouts in Russia's St. Petersbburg and Moscow
incidents.description: Russia has enacted internet blackouts in Moscow and St. Petersburg, citing security concerns related to Victory Day events.

incidents.title: Venezuela and Guyana attend hearings over Essequibo
incidents.description: Venezuela and Guyana are attending hearings in the International Court of Justice this week related to the disputed ownership of the Essequibo region, which is rich in resources including diamonds, oil, and timber. The dispute has been before the ICJ since 2019.

incidents.title: Guyana-Venezuela ICJ dispute over Essequibo intensifies
incidents.description: Venezuela argued at the International Court of Justice that the resource-rich Essequibo region was wrongfully taken during the colonial era and said the 1966 Geneva Agreement, rather than the ICJ, should determine ownership.

incidents.title: Sudan accuses UAE of recent drone strike
incidents.description: The Sudanese government accused Ethiopia and the UAE of responsibility for a recent drone strike against Khartoum International Airport that caused minor damage but no casualties. Sudan had accused both countries of conducting direct strikes against it earlier this year following drone launches from Ethiopian territory in March. Both the UAE and Ethiopia deny involvement in the incidents

incidents.title: Trump pauses Hormuz escort plan
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump halted plans to escort commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz because of concerns over Iranian drone attacks.

incidents.title: U.S. approves weapons sale to Ukraine
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of State approved a potential weapons sale to Ukraine worth $373.6 million.

incidents.title: Taiwan passes reduced special defense budget
incidents.description: Taiwan’s opposition parties have voted to pass a revised defense budget. The ruling Democratic Progressive Party has been trying to pass a $40 billion special defense budget for the past few months, a decision strongly supported by U.S. lawmakers. The new defense budget would amount to a lesser $25 billion.

incidents.title: U.S. Secretary of State suggests Israel-Lebanon peace deal is near
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said May 5 that a peace deal between Israel and Lebanon was "imminently achievable.”

incidents.title: EU seeks ban on Chinese renewable energy hardware
incidents.description: The EU has banned Chinese inverters from all EU-funded schemes in a first of an anticipated many directives as the EU attempts to limit its dependence on Chinese renewable energy hardware.

incidents.title: U.S. authorizes Venezuela debt restructuring process
incidents.description: The United States granted Venezuela permission to hire financial advisers and begin preparations for restructuring its sovereign debt and PDVSA liabilities.

incidents.title: Indiana primaries clear redistricting path
incidents.description: At least five Indiana Republican state senators who opposed U.S. President Donald Trump’s congressional redistricting plan lost primary races to Trump-backed challengers. The results strengthened support for a renewed Republican effort to redraw the state’s congressional map.

incidents.title: Nvidia CEO urges continued China chip competition
incidents.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said China should not have the most advanced U.S. semiconductors but urged Washington to allow U.S. chipmakers to continue competing in global markets, including China. Huang argued that U.S. technology firms strengthen U.S. exports and competitiveness through international market access.

incidents.title: India-Pakistan ceasefire reaches one-year mark
incidents.description: One year after the four-day conflict between India and Pakistan, the ceasefire continues to hold though tensions between the two remain high. Both countries emerged from the crisis claiming victory through selective narratives, enabling mutual de-escalation despite unresolved disputes. Hypernationalistic rhetoric in both countries and the unpredictability of non-state armed groups mean the risk of accidental escalation remains high.

incidents.title: Ukraine rejects ceasefire proposal after deadly Russian strikes
incidents.description: Ukraine rejected a temporary ceasefire proposal from Russia coinciding with Victory Day celebrations May 8-9, after Russian airstrikes killed at least 27 Ukrainians on May 5. Russia killed at least 13 Ukrainians on May 6 in a separate series of strikes.

incidents.title: India's BJP secures major electoral victory
incidents.description: The BJP secured a historic majority win in West Bengal’s state assembly elections, marking the first time the Hindu Nationalist party has governed the eastern state. The win ends 15 years of rule by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool Congress party (TMC) and removes one of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s most visible domestic critics from power. This result consolidates the BJP’s national dominance heading into the 2029 general election, where Modi is widely expected to seek a fourth term. However, the vote was contested amid opposition allegations that a pre-election voter roll stripped millions of likely TMC supporters of eligibility. A BJP governed West Bengal is expected to tighten migration policies, adding strain to an already difficult India-Bangladesh relationship

incidents.title: U.S. calls for Chinese actions ahead of summit
incidents.description: Ahead of next week’s scheduled U.S.-China presidential summit, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on China to escalate diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials also asked Beijing to increase efforts to repatriate Chinese nationals who are in the U.S. illegally.

incidents.title: Sweden arrests Chinese captain
incidents.description: The Swedish coast guard arrested the Chinese captain of a Syrian-flagged vessel with suspected ties to Russia operating in Swedish territorial waters.

incidents.title: North Korea removes reunification ambitions
incidents.description: North Korea formally amended its constitution to drop any mention of reunification with the South.

incidents.title: EU recommends Huawei ban
incidents.description: The European Commission, which is working on new cybersecurity laws, recommended that member states ban Huawei and ZTE infrastructure from the bloc’s connectivity nodes.

incidents.title: China bypasses US oil sanctions on Iran
incidents.description: In its first use of 2021 Blocking Rules, China is pushing back against recent U.S. sanctions targeting five Chinese refineries linked to Iranian oil imports. Beijing instructed the companies not to comply with U.S. sanctions, intensifying economic tensions between the two ahead of next week’s scheduled Trump-Xi meeting. The targeted refineries buy large amounts of discounted Iranian oil, helping Iran continue exporting crude despite U.S. sanctions. However, the country’s National Financial Regulatory Administration also advised Chinese banks against issuing loans for the sanctioned companies shortly after the non-compliance order.

incidents.title: U.S. and Iran exchange fire
incidents.description: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire on May 4 as Iranian forces targeted a U.S. destroyer in response to U.S. effort to break Iran’s Strait of Hormuz blockade. According to a statement from the U.S. Central Command, all incoming Iranian fire was intercepted, and U.S. naval forces destroyed six Iranian small boats in retaliation.

incidents.title: Iran attacks UAE with missiles
incidents.description: Iran targeted the UAE with at least 12 ballistic missiles on May 5, its first attack on the country since a ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran was announced April 8.

incidents.title: Supreme Court backs Louisiana redistricting plan
incidents.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Louisiana Republicans in a congressional redistricting dispute, allowing redrawn district boundaries to proceed.

incidents.title: Trump approval falls to lowest point of presidency
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump’s disapproval rating reached a record high of 62% in a new Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll, the highest level recorded for him in the survey across both of his terms.

incidents.title: Bharatiya Janata Party wins West Bengal elections
incidents.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party won West Bengal for the first time in the party's 46-year history, defeating the Trinamool Congress after a campaign marked by allegations of voter roll purges targeting Muslim and low-income voters. The BJP also retained Assam and Puducherry. In Tamil Nadu, actor Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party emerged as the biggest vote-getter, but fell short of a majority, disrupting DMK dominance. In Kerala, the Congress-led UDF returned to power. The results mark the BJP's post-2024 recovery and expanding presence across India's federal system.

incidents.title: U.S. withdraws troops from Germany
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would go “a lot further” after ordering the withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany. The German Defense Ministry said the U.S. has not canceled a Biden-era agreement to station a battalion of U.S. troops with long-range strike capabilities in Germany.

incidents.title: Japan and Australia fast-track minerals cooperation
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi concluded a three-day visit to Australia that saw both countries agree to prioritize and fast track projects related to critical minerals supply chains.

incidents.title: Israel issues new evacuation orders in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel issued new evacuation orders for population centers in southern Lebanon on May 6 and conducted an airstrike in Beirut on May 7 for the first time since agreeing to a U.S.-mediated ceasefire in April.

incidents.title: China ignores U.S. Iran Sanctions
incidents.description: China’s Commerce Ministry called U.S. sanctions against Chinese refiners that buy Iranian oil a violation of international law and has instructed the refiners to ignore them. At the same time, China’s National Financial Regulatory Administration advised its banks not to deal in loans with the sanctioned entities. The conflicting advice showcases Beijing’s balancing act between publicly defying the U.S. and avoiding additional economic damage.

incidents.title: Operation Project Freedom paused
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. campaign to guide commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, dubbed Operation Project Freedom, has been paused. This comes after Saudi Arabia denied the use of its airspace to U.S. aircraft supporting the operation.

incidents.title: Iran war drives up costs for automakers
incidents.description: Rising oil prices linked to the Iran conflict significantly increased operating costs for major U.S. automakers.

incidents.title: China blocks U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil buyers
incidents.description: China announced an injunction to prevent enforcement of U.S. sanctions against five Chinese refiners accused of purchasing Iranian oil. The U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctions barred the refiners from the U.S. financial system and targeted entities conducting business with them.

incidents.title: China demands EU drop Russia-linked sanctions
incidents.description: China has demanded that the EU remove its latest sanctions on Chinese businesses and individuals connected with the bloc’s latest sanctions package against Russia.

incidents.title: Taiwanese president makes surprise visit to Eswatini
incidents.description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te visited Eswatini, Taiwan’s only diplomatic ally in Africa, following a previously canceled trip due to pressure from Beijing. Following the surprise trip, Lai said Taiwan cannot be stopped from visiting its allies, and Beijing condemned his actions

incidents.title: Iran considers U.S. peace proposal
incidents.description: Iran is considering a peace proposal from the U.S. that would declare an immediate end to the fighting and set a timetable to discuss U.S. sanctions on Iran, freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. . U.S. President Donald Trump said that the current ceasefire still held, despite exchanges of fire between the U.S., Iran and the UAE.

incidents.title: U.S. issues sanctions warning
incidents.description: The U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control warned shipping companies they would face sanctions if they paid tolls to the Iranian government in exchange for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz

incidents.title: Global oil markets hit 113 dollars per barrel
incidents.description: Oil prices topped $113 per barrel on May 1, their highest level since the ceasefire in the Middle East was struck. Despite proposals to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a maritime chokepoint through which 20% of the globe’s oil flows, it remains largely obstructed, and regional oil production has fallen by more than half since the conflict began, intensifying concerns over supply risk once again. Prices are likely to remain elevated in the near term, with an upward bias if disruptions to the strait persist.

incidents.title: Spirit Airlines ceases operations
incidents.description: Spirit Airlines entered foreclosure amid rising fuel prices and mounting financial strain linked to broader energy market disruptions.

incidents.title: Oil producers resist White House pressure to boost output
incidents.description: Major American oil producers rebuffed White House pressure to rapidly increase production, limiting its ability to reduce domestic fuel prices.

incidents.title: DoD releases Ukraine aid package
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Defense released a $400 million aid package for Ukraine. The aid will be facilitated to Ukraine via the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative

incidents.title: Russia strikes Ukrainian cities
incidents.description: At least four Ukrainians were killed by Russian strikes in urban areas on April 29.

incidents.title: Russia proposes temporary Ukraine ceasefire
incidents.description: Russia proposed a temporary ceasefire to take place during May 9 Victory Day celebrations in Moscow. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he will seek clarification on whether the proposal is about “a few hours of security for a parade in Moscow or something more” before agreeing to the offer and responded with a proposal for a long-term ceasefire.

incidents.title: Ukraine waves off sanctions threat to Israel
incidents.description: Israel announced that it will not allow a Russian vessel carrying grain from occupied territories of Ukraine to unload in Haifa following threats of sanctions from Ukraine.

incidents.title: Lithuania open to joining U.S. operations in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda said that he is supportive of joining U.S. freedom-of-navigation operations in the Strait of Hormuz and is presenting a U.S. proposal to Lithuania’s State Defense Council

incidents.title: China increases Rare Earth Exports to U.S
incidents.description: Customs data showed that China has been increasing its exports of rare earths to U.S. aerospace companies in March

incidents.title: U.S. and Chinese officials meet ahead of summit
incidents.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of the upcoming China-U.S. presidential summit. Both officials exchanged complaints and demands in what was described as “candid” discussions

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela direct flights commence
incidents.description: U.S. and Venezuelan officials celebrated the arrival of the first direct commercial flight between the two countries in more than seven years.

incidents.title: Venezuela raises minimum wage and pensions amid inflation protests
incidents.description: Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez announced that minimum monthly income would rise to $240 and pensions to $70 as workers protested low pay and triple-digit inflation.

incidents.title: Rial falls to record low
incidents.description: Iran's currency fell to a record low against the U.S. dollar amid the continuing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian media reported the rial had lost around 15% of its value.

incidents.title: Iran threatens U.S. bases
incidents.description: Iran threatened to launch strikes against U.S. bases across the Middle East if the United States resumed military operations.

incidents.title: U.S. presses India to increase oil purchases
incidents.description: With the U.S. ending waivers on Russian and Iranian oil purchases and the Hormuz crisis tightening global supply, Washington stepped up pressure on India to convert its $500 billion energy pledge from the February trade deal into near-term commitments on U.S. crude purchases. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed the general license on Russian oil would not be renewed. High freight costs, refinery infrastructure incompatible with U.S. crude grades, and longer delivery times are among the key obstacles India faces in shifting away from Russian and Gulf supplies toward U.S. energy.

incidents.title: U.S. considers troop reduction in Germany
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. is considering a reduction of its troop presence in Germany, amid an ongoing diplomatic spat with senior German officials. German Chancellor Frederich Merz recently said that Iran was “humiliating” the U.S. in ongoing peace negotiations.

incidents.title: Canada recieves increased investment in oil production
incidents.description: Geopolitical instability in the Middle East is prompting several major oil and gas companies to shift investments to Canada, which they see as a more reliable alternative. For instance, Shell recently struck a deal to acquire Canadian energy company ARC Resources Ltd. for $16.4 billion. Other energy giants, including TotalEnergies, ConocoPhillips, Equinor, and BP, are assessing Canadian assets.

incidents.title: China Pressures Trump to Change Taiwan Language:
incidents.description: Ahead of the upcoming summit, China will likely ask Trump to change official language on Taiwan to include wording on the U.S. “opposing” Taiwanese independence rather than “not supporting” it

incidents.title: Taiwan Announces Coast Guard Reforms
incidents.description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te announced a plan to overhaul the island’s coast guard to adapt to China’s routine “gray zone” tactics around the island.

incidents.title: Democrats Urge Continued U.S. Tariffs on Chinese EVs:
incidents.description: A letter signed by 73 House Democrats and sent to Trump urges him to maintain tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports as the administration plans its upcoming summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in May

incidents.title: Trump and Putin hold phone call
incidents.description: A Kremlin official confirmed that Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump held a 90-minute phone call April 29 to discuss security matters related to Iran and Ukraine.

incidents.title: Pakistan strikes Taliban targets in Afghanistan
incidents.description: Pakistani troops struck Taliban outposts in Afghanistan as well as in its own Balochistan province. Afghan officials claim Pakistan has attacked civilian homes and a university near their shared border, killing seven people and wounding more than 80. Pakistan denies the claims. The developments come despite recent talks in which both sides agreed not to escalate their conflict

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela agreements advance oil and mining investment
incidents.description: White House officials traveled to Venezuela to announce agreements that could pave the way for foreign oil and mining companies to operate in the country.

incidents.title: Trump briefed on new Iran strike operations
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump received briefings from Adm. Brad Cooper, leader of the U.S. Central Command, on options to resume an offensive air campaign inside Iran, according to reporting from Axios and The Wall Street Journal.

incidents.title: Senate blocks limit on Trump war powers
incidents.description: The Republican-led U.S. Senate blocked a Democratic resolution that would have required congressional approval before U.S. President Donald Trump could take military action against Cuba. The procedural vote passed largely along party lines.

incidents.title: Huawei AI chip demand surges
incidents.description: Demand for Huawei’s Ascend 950 artificial intelligence chips surged following the release of DeepSeek’s V4 model, which runs on Huawei hardware. Major Chinese technology firms, including ByteDance, Tencent, and Alibaba, reportedly moved to secure new chip orders.

incidents.title: UAE withdraws from OPEC
incidents.description: The United Arab Emirates has announced its withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+ after nearly five decades of membership, signaling a major shift in global oil dynamics amid the ongoing conflict in Iran. The timing of the decision appears politically driven, reflecting growing tensions with Saudi Arabia and broader regional instability. Its exit removes a key source of spare capacity, around 13% of OPEC’s output, raising concerns about further fragmentation within the group. The short-term impact on oil prices is likely to remain limited given that oil production shortages amid the ongoing conflict have already tightened supply. However, over the medium term, the loss of coordinated spare capacity could increase market volatility and weaken OPEC’s ability to stabilize markets.

incidents.title: China Blocks Meta AI Acquisition
incidents.description: China ordered the reversal of an acquisition by Meta of the Chinese AI company Manus, following months of scrutiny by China’s regulatory agencies. Beijing cited concerns with technology transfer. This marks an escalation in the tech race between the U.S. and China and the first time that Beijing has ordered the unwinding of a completed capital acquisition.

incidents.title: China-EU EV Negotiations Continue
incidents.description: Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao met with heads of a German automaker group, where he said both sides had reached a “soft landing” in their ongoing discussion as the EU has expressed willingness to be flexible on its tariffs on electric vehicles from China.

incidents.title: US bill blocked bill that would have prevented escalation in Cuba
incidents.description: U.S. Senate Republicans blocked a Democratic-led bill to prevent Trump from utilizing military force against Cuba. This comes after Havana affirmed last week that negotiations with the U.S. are ongoing and proceeding in a professional manner

incidents.title: U.S. Imposes Sanctions on Chinese Oil Importers
incidents.description: The U.S. imposed sanctions on Shanghai-based Hengli Petrochemical, which the U.S. Treasury Department accuses of being one of the largest purchasers of Iranian crude oil. The U.S. warned other banks against aiding any Chinese purchases of Iranian oil, with the move coming just weeks away from a planned summit between Trump and Xi.

incidents.title: U.S. Gives U.N. Funding Conditions
incidents.description: The U.S. released a list of conditions it wants to see met before allowing the release of funds it owes to the United Nations, including limitations on China’s ability to influence the office of the Secretary General.

incidents.title: Guyana-Venezuela tensions rise
incidents.description: Guyana complained to Caribbean leaders after Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez wore a pin depicting the disputed Essequibo region as part of Venezuela.

incidents.title: Trump orders CENTCOM to prepare for extended Iran blockade
incidents.description: Trump is ordering CENTCOM to sustain an extended naval blockade against Iranian ports, as Trump claimed on Truth Social that Iranian officials told him that Iran is in a “state of collapse.”

incidents.title: U.S. rejects Iran peace proposal
incidents.description: Trump rejected the latest peace proposal from Iran, which reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. agreed to table nuclear negotiations to a later, unspecified date.

incidents.title: Trump feud with Jimmy Kimmel escalates
incidents.description: A public dispute erupted between U.S. President Donald Trump and late-night television host Jimmy Kimmel after a joke about Melania Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner.

incidents.title: IRGC expands wartime influence
incidents.description: Sources familiar with Iranian deliberations said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps expanded its influence during the war, reducing the authority of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

incidents.title: Trump orders extended Hormuz blockade
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump instructed aides to prepare for a prolonged blockade of the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Iran into accepting denuclearization.

incidents.title: China-Kyrgyzstan trade declines sharply
incidents.description: China’s trade with two Central Asian states declined during Q1 2026, with trade turnover between China and Kyrgyzstan falling from $6.1 billion to less than $4 billion year-on-year and trade with Turkmenistan dropping by $100 million to $2.2 billion over the same period. However, China’s overall trade with the five Central Asian countries climbed 15 percent to $24.6 billion.

incidents.title: U.N. General Assembly president visits India
incidents.description: U.N. General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock discussed global issues and multilateral cooperation with Indian leaders during a visit as India prepared to host the BRICS Foreign Ministers Meeting on May 14-15 under its chairmanship, reinforcing New Delhi's positioning as a key hub for multilateral diplomacy in 2026.

incidents.title: Russian African core attacked in Mali
incidents.description: The Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front and other al-Qaeda affiliated organizations attacked members of Russia’s Africa Corps, formerly known as the Wagner Group, in the northern town of Kidal, forcing the mercenary group to withdraw. Malian Defense Minister Gen. Sadio Camara was killed in the attacks.

incidents.title: U.S. Tank Shipment Arrives in Taiwan
incidents.description: The final shipment of 28 U.S.-made M1A2T Abrams tanks arrived in Taiwan, completing the delivery of 108 tanks approved in 2019.

incidents.title: Chinese Warships Spotted near Penghu Isl
incidents.description: Two Chinese warships were operating near the Taiwan-owned Penghu Islands in the Taiwan Strait.

incidents.title: U.S. and Philippines Continue Annual Drills
incidents.description: The U.S. and Philippines continued with their Balikatan military drills, simulating counter-landing operations in the South China Sea, along with forces from Australia, New Zealand, Japan, France, and Canada. China held combat readiness drills in response.

incidents.title: US invests 100 million in DRC mining sector
incidents.description: The U.S. is helping fund a $100 million initiative by the DRC’s General Inspectorate of Mines to set up a paramilitary unit to safeguard the country’s mining sector, which holds vast amounts of critical minerals vital to the supply chains of multiple industrial sectors. This marks a challenge to China, which holds a dominant mining position in the country, and follows last year’s partnership signed by the DRC and U.S. on cooperating on the sector

incidents.title: Putin hosts Iranian Foreign Minister
incidents.description: On April 27, Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Moscow for consultations on peace efforts with the U.S.

incidents.title: Trump criticizes latest Iran proposal
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump criticized Iran's latest peace proposal and said Iranian leaders appeared to be in a state of collapse.

incidents.title: Former defense ministers receive suspended death sentences
incidents.description: Former Chinese Defense Ministers Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu received suspended death sentences after military courts found them guilty of corruption-related offenses. Wei was convicted of accepting bribes, while Li was convicted of both accepting and offering bribes.

incidents.title: Industrial profits post strongest growth in six months
incidents.description: Profits at China’s industrial firms grew at their fastest pace in six months, adding to signs of continued economic recovery despite mounting external pressures. The increase came as producer prices returned to growth after a prolonged deflationary period, helping support industrial earnings.

incidents.title: India, New Zealand sign free trade agreement
incidents.description: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and New Zealand Trade Minister Todd McClay formalized a free trade agreement between their countries with an April 27 signing in New Delhi. The agreement grants 100% duty-free access for all 8,284 Indian export products into New Zealand. India offered tariff liberalization on 70% of tariff lines covering 95% of bilateral trade value. The deal is part of India's broader strategy of building Indo-Pacific trade architecture alongside free trade deals with the United Kingdom, European Union, United Arab Emirates, and Australia.

incidents.title: Australian foreign minister visits Japan
incidents.description: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong conducted an official visit to Japan, China, and South Korea on April 26-30 to secure Australia's jet fuel and energy supplies amid disruptions in the Middle East. Australia is a leading liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplier to both Japan and South Korea, while providing significant LNG supplies to China, though Chinese imports remain more diversified. At the same time, Australia's reliance on imported refined fuels highlights a structural vulnerability that these engagements seek to address.

incidents.title: Israel resumes Lebanon attacks north of Litani River
incidents.description: Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah continued in southern Lebanon despite a notional ceasefire agreement, as Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir said “there is no ceasefire” and that Lebanese infrastructure is not off limits. Israel resumed strikes north of the Litani River. Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed at least nine people on April 30, while a Hezbollah drone strike wounded at least 12 Israeli soldiers in northern Israel the same day.

incidents.title: U.S. eases sanctions for Maduro legal defense payments
incidents.description: The United States relaxed certain sanctions so Venezuela’s government could cover President Nicolás Maduro’s legal costs as he stands trial in New York on drug trafficking charges.

incidents.title: Suspect arrested in Secret Service shootout
incidents.description: Authorities arrested a 31-year-old man in connection with a shooting near the White House Correspondents’ Dinner with U.S. President Donald Trump in attendance.

incidents.title: Ukraine president signs military and trade treaty with Saudi Arabia
incidents.description: Zelenskyy arrived in Saudi Arabia on April 24 to meet with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and finalize agreements in the defense, energy and infrastructure sectors

incidents.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to three week ceasefire
incidents.description: Israeli and Lebanese agreed to a three-week ceasefire extension during a second round of direct peace talks in Washington, as Israeli forces continued to conduct strikes in southern Lebanon.

incidents.title: China places new sanctions on EU
incidents.description: China placed new export restrictions on dual-use items for EU-based defense firms that were involved in arms sales to Taiwan. This comes as the EU passed its latest round of sanctions against Russia, with some of them targeting Chinese firms the EU accuses of helping Russian war efforts.

incidents.title: Colombian president visits Venezuela
incidents.description: Colombian President Gustavo Petro met acting interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez in Caracas, becoming the first foreign leader to visit Venezuela since the U.S. capture of President Nicolás Maduro.

incidents.title: Justice Department drops Federal Reserve investigation
incidents.description: The Justice Department ended its investigation into the Federal Reserve after failing to find evidence of wrongdoing. The closure removed a politically sensitive inquiry involving a major U.S. institution.

incidents.title: U.S. soldier charged in prediction market case
incidents.description: A U.S. special forces soldier involved in the operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro was charged with using classified knowledge to place bets on the operation’s outcome through the Polymarket predictions market site. The case raised concerns over insider abuse of sensitive military intelligence.

incidents.title: Trump rules out nuclear strike
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he had no intention of using nuclear weapons against Iran.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran begin new Pakistan talks
incidents.description: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Pakistan for another round of negotiations with Iranian officials focused on extending the ceasefire.

incidents.title: Foreign automakers expand China partnerships
incidents.description: Foreign automakers showcased new models incorporating Chinese technology at a major industry exhibition in Beijing. Companies including Volkswagen and Nissan signaled plans to use Chinese-developed technology for both domestic and international markets.

incidents.title: BRICS meeting ends without joint statement
incidents.description: The BRICS MENA Deputy Foreign Ministers and Special Envoys meeting in New Delhi on April 24 ended without a joint statement after India blocked consensus language on Israel-Palestine. Indian Ministry of External Affairs officials sought to soften language criticizing Israel's bombardment of Gaza and Lebanon and to drop references to East Jerusalem as the future capital of a Palestinian state. MEA officials also sought to replace direct references to Israel with the less specific term “occupying power.” The impasse highlighted the tension between India's BRICS chairmanship ambitions and its strategic partnership with Israel.

incidents.title: India criticizes Trump social media repost
incidents.description: An unnamed Indian official described comments reposted by U.S. President Donald Trump on social media referring to India as a “hellhole” as “in poor taste” and at odds with the countries' relationship by an unnamed Indian official. The incident highlighted underlying tensions in the U.S.-India relationship despite the February trade agreement, reflecting Trump's unpredictable approach to foreign policy communications.

incidents.title: Germany proposes EU wide defense initiative
incidents.description: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius presented a defense realignment plan for Germany titled Responsibility for Europe, that outlines Germany’s plan to counter Russia’s security threat to the continent by modernizing its capabilities and increasing the number of its armed forces personnel by the mid 2030s.

incidents.title: 9 killed in Ukraine from Russia airstrike
incidents.description: At least nine people were killed by Russian strikes across Ukrainian cities on April 22, according to Ukrainian officials.

incidents.title: EU unfreezes 106 billion for Ukraine
incidents.description: A $106 billion EU loan to Ukraine was unblocked by Slovakia and Hungary after oil deliveries from the Druzhba pipeline that runs through Ukraine resumed April 22.

incidents.title: Taiwan sign 6 arms procurement deals
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense signed six arms procurement offers from the U.S., marking the latest advancement in U.S. arms sales to the island as Taiwanese lawmakers continue to stall the passing of a special defense budget.

incidents.title: China stockpiles oil
incidents.description: China had the largest oil stockpile of any other country as of December 2025, according to brief analysis report data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The estimated China’s strategic oil stocks reached 1.4 billion barrels by December 2025, ahead of the U.S. and Japan with 413 million barrels and 263 million barrels respectively.

incidents.title: Iran fires on three vessels in Hormuz
incidents.description: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired on three vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz and seized two of them on April 23.

incidents.title: Senate passes bill to reopen DHS
incidents.description: The Republican-led Senate passed legislation to reopen the Department of Homeland Security following a prolonged shutdown tied to disputes over funding for the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. The move restored core government services after weeks of political deadlock.

incidents.title: Iran seizes cargo ships in Hormuz
incidents.description: Iran seized two cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a suspension of strikes in the waterway.

incidents.title: Iran claims Hormuz toll revenue
incidents.description: Iranian Parliament Deputy Speaker Hamidreza Haji Babaei said Iran had begun collecting toll revenue from vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: H200 chip sales to China remain stalled
incidents.description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said Nvidia had not yet sold any H200 artificial intelligence chips to Chinese customers. Lutnick attributed the delay in part to difficulties obtaining approvals from Chinese authorities.

incidents.title: West Bengal elections draw record turnout
incidents.description: West Bengal's first phase of assembly elections drew a historic 91.58% voter turnout across 152 of 294 constituencies, despite ongoing controversy over the removal of approximately 9 million names from electoral rolls before voting began. Opposition parties led by the Trinamool Congress alleged the purge disproportionately targeted Muslim and low-income voters in border districts including Murshidabad and North and South 24 Parganas. The Election Commission defended the exercise as a cleanup of deceased and ineligible voters.

incidents.title: India, China compete for Russian oil supplies
incidents.description: With Hormuz-linked supply disruptions pushing Middle Eastern crude off the market, India and China competed more intensively than at any point in 2026 for June Russian oil cargoes. Indian and Chinese refiners both escalated outreach to Russian suppliers, with Indian state refiners seeking to lock in volumes following the brief lapse of the U.S. sanctions waiver earlier in the month. The competition highlighted India's continued energy security challenges despite the U.S.-India trade deal.

incidents.title: Pakistan rejects India’s Pahalgam attack allegations
incidents.description: Pakistan's Foreign Office formally rejected what it described as a campaign of baseless allegations by New Delhi seeking to link Islamabad to the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terrorist attack on its first anniversary. Pakistan called on India to refrain from rhetoric that could undermine regional stability and reiterated its offer to participate in an independent international investigation, which India has not accepted. The exchange underscored continued bilateral tensions.

incidents.title: Ukraine calls for summit with Putin
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy renewed calls for a direct summit between himself and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Ukrainian officials are seeking the help of Türkiye and other partners to facilitate the potential meeting. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Zelenskyy would meet Putin in any capital other than Moscow or Minsk. The Kremlin has yet to officially comment on the request.

incidents.title: Israel continues to attack Lebanon
incidents.description: Israeli forces continued to conduct strikes in southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces maintain a territorial occupation and continue to conduct ground operations despite an ongoing ceasefire agreement with Hezbollah that went into effect on April 16.

incidents.title: Israeli settlers kill 2 Palestinian children
