incidents.description: Two Palestinians, including a 14-year-old boy, were killed by Israeli settlers when they opened fire at a Palestinian school in the West Bank on April 22.

incidents.title: China deploys navy near Japan
incidents.description: China’s Eastern Theater Command deployed a group of vessels to the Western Pacific, including a destroyer. On their return, they passed through the Yonaguni-Iriomote Waterway near Japan’s Okinawa prefecture as tensions escalated between both countries.

incidents.title: Flights between Japan and China drop sharply
incidents.description: Flights between China and Japan fell sharply in March, with 2,691 flights being cancelled as bilateral relations continue to fall.

incidents.title: Taiwanese minister visits disputed islands
incidents.description: Taiwanese Ocean Affairs Council Minister Kuan Bi-ling visited the Itu Aba island in the South China Sea, to witness coast guard drills in the disputed Spratly Islands. This marks the first time in seven years that a Taiwanese minister visits the island, which Taiwan claims as its own.

incidents.title: Eswatini cancels trip with Taiwan president
incidents.description: Taiwan cancelled a planned trip for President Lai Ching-te, who was meant to fly to Eswatini this week. Taiwan and the U.S. have accused China of pressuring other African countries to close off their airspace for the flight, which Beijing denies.

incidents.title: Pro-Russian candidate wins in Bulgaria
incidents.description: Pro-Russian former Bulgarian President Rumen Radev’s Progressive Bulgaria party won the country’s parliamentary election, securing 130 out of 240 seats. Radev has refused to condemn Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and his victory was welcomed by Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov. The far-right Revival party also secured 12 seats, increasing the likelihood of the country stalling EU policies against Russia.

incidents.title: US refuses to sell H200 chips to China
incidents.description: Commerce Department Secretary Howard Lutnick stated that the U.S. had not yet sold any H200 Nvidia chips to China, despite the sale being greenlit earlier this year. Lutnick stated that Chinese firms were not getting authorization by the Chinese government to purchase the chips, as China continues to place a strong priority on developing technological self-reliance.

incidents.title: South Korea increases energy cooperation with Japan
incidents.description: South Korean trade minister Yeo Han-koo stated that South Korea should increase its energy cooperation with Japan in light of increased energy volatility and uncertainty from the Iran war

incidents.title: Boeing to make delivery to China
incidents.description: Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg stated that the company was ready to deliver on a long-awaited order from China, expressing his hopes that Trump will facilitate the deal as soon as possible.

incidents.title: US captures 3 Iranian tankers
incidents.description: The U.S. maintained its naval blockade of Iranian ports and intercepted at least three Iranian- flagged oil vessels in waters near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka.

incidents.title: Virginia advances new congressional redistricting plan
incidents.description: Virginia secured enough support to move forward with a new congressional redistricting map ahead of the 2026 midterms.

incidents.title: China-Japan flight cancellations increase
incidents.description: Flight cancellations between China and Japan increased in March amid ongoing political tensions between the two countries. Nearly half of scheduled flights were canceled, with additional reductions expected during the May 1-5 Labor Day holiday period.

incidents.title: US set to export more oil to Asian markets
incidents.description: The United States is projected to export a record 5.44 million barrels of crude oil per day in April, with a significant share directed toward Asian markets. This marks a sharp increase compared to earlier in the year, when U.S. crude exports to Asia averaged approximately 1.11 million barrels per day in January and 1.21 million barrels per day in February. The surge reflects shifting global trade flows, largely driven by the ongoing Middle East conflict and resulting disruptions to production and exports from key Gulf suppliers.

incidents.title: EU sanctions Russian government emploees
incidents.description: The EU enacted sanctions against two Russian nationals involved in Kremlin propaganda and disinformation campaigns.

incidents.title: Israel airstrike kills 7 civilians
incidents.description: Israeli airstrikes killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza on April 21

incidents.title: US and Cuba hold talks
incidents.description: The Cuban government has confirmed that it held negotiations with U.S. officials in Havana. The Cuban Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated the talks were conducted with “respect and professionalism” and that Cuba’s top priority was to remove the U.S. oil blockade. This comes after a shipment of Russian oil was allowed to dock at the island. While Trump had previously alluded to military action, Cuban officials have confirmed that U.S. officials have repeatedly come to the island in April for negotiations.

incidents.title: Virginia passes gerrymandered house map
incidents.description: Voters in Virginia approved a heavily gerrymandered map of the state’s U.S. congressional districts, which could flip up to four seats in midterm elections to the Democratic Party. The campaign was heavily backed by Democratic leadership in Washington, D.C. The election followed similar results [RI1] [MM2] from California and Utah.

incidents.title: Japan removes limit on lethal weapons exports
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi approved the removal of restrictions on lethal weapons exports, marking a major change in the country’s defense policy. Takaichi had previously touted reforms to the constitution including on the Self Defense Force’s role and capabilities.

incidents.title: US extends ceasefire indefinitely
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump indefinitely extended the U.S. ceasefire with Iran at the request of Pakistani mediators, who continue to push for another round of direct talks between the U.S. and Iran in Islamabad. Iran declined to participate in a planned diplomatic summit with U.S. Vice President JD Vance this week, citing the ongoing U.S. naval blockade

incidents.title: U.S. crude exports reach record highs
incidents.description: The United States recorded record crude oil export volumes as domestic production surged amid global energy disruptions.

incidents.title: US hold military drills with Asian allies
incidents.description: The U.S. and Philippines will be leading this year’s annual Balikatan military drills between April 20 and May 8. Other countries joining the drills include Canada, France, New Zealand, Australia, and Japan. Tokyo will be sending 1,400 troops, marking a sharp increase compared to last year’s 150.

incidents.title: Oil prices near 100 dollars a barrel
incidents.description: The ongoing U.S./Israel conflict with Iran and uncertainty over the status of the Strait of Hormuz has led to a huge increase in the price of oil around the world. The price of a barrel of Brent crude increased to around $99.78[EC1] [MM2] on Apr. 22, while the price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate rose to $94.36.

incidents.title: China sails aircraft carrier through Taiwan Strait
incidents.description: China sailed its Liaoning aircraft carrier through the Taiwan Strait two weeks after the leader of Taiwan’s opposition Koumingtang party visited Beijing for a peace mission.

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela direct commercial flights resume
incidents.description: American Airlines began selling tickets for flights between Caracas and Miami, marking the return of the route after several years of suspension.

incidents.title: Venezuela opposition urges accelerated elections
incidents.description: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado said she expects to return to Venezuela before the end of 2026 and urged the United States to accelerate plans for elections.

incidents.title: Venezuela discusses electricity shortages with Siemens, GE
incidents.description: Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez said her government was in talks with Siemens and General Electric to address severe electricity shortages in Zulia state.

incidents.title: U.S. launches tariff refund process
incidents.description: The United States began implementing a refund mechanism for companies impacted by tariffs later ruled unconstitutional by the U.S. Supreme Court. The move provided financial relief and reduced pressure on affected industries.

incidents.title: North Korea tests new ballistic missile
incidents.description: North Korea launched ballistic missiles, marking the fourth time this past month that Pyongyang conducted such a test.

incidents.title: China to sign energy agreement with Turkmenistan
incidents.description: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang visited Turkmenistan to attend the groundbreaking of the fourth phase of the Galkynysh gas field, the second-largest natural gas field in the world. In this new phase, an additional 10 billion cubic meters of natural gas will be produced annually and shipped to China via the China-Central Asia pipeline network. A contract was signed April 16 between Türkmengaz and CNPC Amudarya Petroleum Company Ltd., for construction, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure for natural gas production.[RI1] [MM2]

incidents.title: China, Turkmenistan deepen energy cooperation
incidents.description: China and Turkmenistan expanded cooperation in the energy sector as Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang attended the launch of a major gas field project and signed new agreements. Ding also met with Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov to discuss broader bilateral cooperation.

incidents.title: Iran fires on Indian ships in Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps vessels fired on two Indian-flagged ships attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, during a period when Iran had briefly reopened the waterway before reimposing restrictions. India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri expressed deep concern to Iranian Ambassador Mohammed Fathali over the incident. While no crew member was hurt, some cargo was damaged. The incident exposed India's acute vulnerability to the Iran-US conflict given its heavy dependence on Gulf energy imports.

incidents.title: Iran war disrupts India’s steel, energy imports
incidents.description: The Iran war's disruption of the Strait of Hormuz has cascaded into India's steel and energy sectors. Capesize freight rates rose from $9.80 to $12.20 per metric ton within weeks, directly raising the landed cost of metallurgical coal and iron ore. Around 20-22% of India's metal scrap imports from West Asia were disrupted. India's supply of crude oil and liquefied natural and petroleum gases remained vulnerable, with 230 loaded oil tankers stranded inside the Gulf at the height of the blockade. Steelmakers raised domestic prices to protect margins as input costs climbed.

incidents.title: IMF and World Bank restore ties with Venezuela
incidents.description: The International Monetary Fund and World Bank announced they were resuming ties with Venezuela under its interim leadership after relations were cut in 2019.

incidents.title: Trump says Iran deal may be near
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said a deal to end the war with Iran could be close and identified reopening the Strait of Hormuz and extending the ceasefire as key issues under discussion.

incidents.title: Russia kills 16 in airstrike
incidents.description: Russia conducted a large-scale drone and missile attack against Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro killing at least 16 people during the overnight period of April 16. Both Russia and Ukraine accused each other of violating a 32-hour ceasefire over the weekend of Orthodox Easter.

incidents.title: Lebanon begins ceasefire
incidents.description: A U.S.-mediated 10-day ceasefire in Lebanon began at midnight April 17. In the lead-up to the ceasefire agreement, the White House hosted direct talks between Israel and Lebanon on April 14. U.S. President Donald Trump said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun would speak directly on April 16. Following Trump’s statement, Aoun conditioned direct talks with Netanyahu on a ceasefire deal.

incidents.title: DRC expands copper exports
incidents.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s state mining company, Gécamines, has expanded its copper commitments to the United States to 500,000 metric tons, a fivefold increase in sales from a previous deal made in January. The deal will channel mining output into direct exports, giving Kinshasa more control over how its copper is marketed and sold.

incidents.title: ICE acting director Todd Lyons resigns
incidents.description: Acting Immigration and Customs Enforcement director Todd Lyons resigned amid backlash over immigration enforcement operations and mounting scrutiny of agency conduct.

incidents.title: Pentagon reportedly increases Cuba invasion planning
incidents.description: Reports indicated U.S. military planning for a possible invasion of Cuba had intensified amid deteriorating bilateral tensions.

incidents.title: China’s economic growth exceeds expectations
incidents.description: China’s economy grew 5% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, exceeding analyst expectations. Strong export performance helped offset continued weakness in domestic demand.

incidents.title: Russia will sell more oil to China
incidents.description: Following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on April 15, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that Russia is prepared to increase its energy exports to China.

incidents.title: Israel kills 8 Palestinians
incidents.description: At least eight Palestinians were killed by Israeli attacks in Gaza on April 16.

incidents.title: US deploys aircraft carrier to Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. is deploying the aircraft carrier U.S.S. George H.W. Bush and several accompanying warships to the Middle East amid the ongoing ceasefire with Iran. The 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit, which includes around 4,500 Marines, is expected to arrive in the region near the end of April.

incidents.title: China bloacks Phillippine vessels in South China Sea
incidents.description: China deployed a floating barrier at the entrance of the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, effectively blocking access to Philippine vessels. The move follows declarations last year made by Beijing unilaterally declaring the Shoal as a nature reserve, which the Philippines say is a pretext for occupation.

incidents.title: Taiwan to reopen budget talks
incidents.description: Following last week’s visit by the leader of Taiwan’s opposition Kuomingtang party to Beijing, Taiwanese lawmakers are set to resume talks on passing the proposed special defense budget.

incidents.title: U.S. eases sanctions on Venezuela’s central bank
incidents.description: The United States eased sanctions on Venezuela’s central bank, signaling improving ties with the interim government.

incidents.title: Trump threatens to remove Fed chief Powell
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would consider removing Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chair if he refused to step down voluntarily.

incidents.title: U.S., Iran weigh ceasefire extension
incidents.description: U.S. and Iranian negotiators discussed extending the ceasefire by two weeks to allow additional time to resolve outstanding issues in peace talks.

incidents.title: China considers solar equipment export restrictions
incidents.description: Chinese officials held preliminary discussions on possible restrictions of exports of advanced solar manufacturing equipment to the United States. The move could affect investment plans and supply chains tied to solar technology production.

incidents.title: Ukraine holds defense talks with Norway
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy conducted a series of diplomatic meetings across Europe, where he signed defense cooperation agreements with Norway, Germany, and Italy. Spain and Belgium pledged a combined $2.35 billion defensive aid package to Ukraine on April 14.

incidents.title: Russian increases oil sales due to Iran war
incidents.description: Russian oil export revenue increased from $9.75 billion to $19 during March as a result of a temporary reprieve in U.S. sanctions due to the impact of the Iran war. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant said on April 16 that the U.S. would not extend the sanctions waiver.

incidents.title: Indonesia holds military talks with US
incidents.description: The U.S. and Indonesia announced they are working on elevating their defense partnership to a Major Defense Cooperation Partnership, which would among other things allow U.S. jets to use Indonesian airspace.

incidents.title: Russian oil exports increase
incidents.description: Russian oil exports surged from $9.75 billion in February to $19 billion in March. The increase was mainly driven by the U.S. Treasury’s decision to lift sanctions for 30 days to stabilize global energy markets during the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. decision not to extend the temporary waiver is likely to curtail further economic gains for Russia, and continued Ukrainian drone strikes further compound that pressure by degrading the country's energy infrastructure.

incidents.title: China increase tech independence from US
incidents.description: Chinese chipmaker YMTC is expanding semiconductor manufacturing to become self-sufficient as the U.S. considers increasing chipmaking tool export limits, with one new plant set to be complete this year and two more being planned. Together, the plants would more than double YMTC’s production capacity.

incidents.title: Sudan's army conducts widespread drone strikes
incidents.description: The Sudanese Armed Forces conducted five drone strikes in the southern Darfur region, killing two people and injuring 56 others. As the war enters its fourth year and shows no signs of abating, the U.N. Human Rights Office said casualties from the conflict have increased in 2026, with at least 500 deaths between January and March from drone strikes alone.

incidents.title: Rodríguez calls for lift of sanctions
incidents.description: Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez called on the United States to fully lift sanctions that have strained the country’s economy, saying recent limited licenses were insufficient.

incidents.title: Venezuelan diaspora survey shows moderate intention to return
incidents.description: A UNHCR survey found that just over one-third of Venezuelans living across Latin America would consider returning home if conditions improve, with family reunification as the main motivation.

incidents.title: China’s export growth slows amid war disruptions
incidents.description: China’s export growth slowed sharply in March as higher energy and transportation costs linked to the Middle East conflict weighed on global demand. The slowdown highlighted China’s continued reliance on overseas markets to support economic growth.

incidents.title: U.S. DOD considers taking Cuba by force
incidents.description: Officials at the U.S. Department of Defense have reportedly been increasingly planning for possible military contingencies to take Cuba by force, though both countries have asserted that negotiations on the island’s leadership are ongoing. In the Pacific[RI1] , the DoD has continued its campaign against small boats it alleges are carrying drugs to the U.S., with U.S. forces killing five boatmen last Sunday. The Trump administration seems to be ramping up its military posturing, demanding that domestic civilian automakers [EC2] [MM3] start contributing to defense tech production as well

incidents.title: EU will provide 105 billion dollar loan to Ukraine
incidents.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated on April 13 that the EU will seek to move forward with a $105 billion loan to Ukraine, following the electoral defeat of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

incidents.title: Israel continues war in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel continued ground and air operations inside southern Lebanon, as the IDF announced that its forces have nearly fully encircled the Lebanese city of Bint Jbeil.

incidents.title: US and Iran hold peace talks
incidents.description: The U.S., Israel, and Iran maintained the two-week ceasefire that began April 8. While direct negotiations between the U.S. and Iran in Islamabad on April 12 failed to secure a permanent peace deal, talks are ongoing to extend the ceasefire, according to unnamed Middle Eastern government officials cited by the Associated Press. Meanwhile, senior Pakistani officials met with Iranian counterparts in Tehran to push for further direct talks with the U.S.

incidents.title: US holds military drills with Asian allies
incidents.description: The United States held joint military drills spanning four days in the South China Sea along with Australia and the Philippines for the second time this year. China held navy exercises of its own in the South China Sea during the same timeframe, accusing the Philippines of undermining peace in the region.

incidents.title: The Phillippines discovers Chinese plot to sabotage navy
incidents.description: Officials in the Philippines said they had discovered cyanide bottles on Chinese shipping vessels in the disputed Second Thomas Shoal, accusing China of wanting to sabotage local maritime life, which could affect food supplies for Philippine navy personnel operating in the area.

incidents.title: Hungary elects new Prime Minister
incidents.description: Péter Magyar, leader of Hungary’s Tisza party, won a landslide victory in last week’s election, winning a supermajority in Parliament. The victory marks a significant blow for the Trump administration, which had spent a significant amount of time endorsing Orbán, as did many other European far-right leaders. Magyar has vowed to replace many domestic officials appointed by Orbán, urged President Tamas Sulyok to resign, and vowed to work closely with the EU and NATO, notably in releasing assistance funds for Ukraine.

incidents.title: India launches startup fund 2.0
incidents.description: The Indian government formally launched Startup India FoF 2.0 with 10,000 crore rupee ($1.6 billion) to move capital toward tech, advanced manufacturing, and early growth firms.

incidents.title: China and Phillippines cooperate on oil extraction
incidents.description: The Philippines warned that any cooperation with China on gas and oil exploration in the South China Sea would have to be strictly within the bounds of its constitution and its sovereignty. This comes as preliminary exchanges on the subject have been started between both countries, with little progress reported so far.

incidents.title: KMT leader meets with Xi Jinping
incidents.description: Following Kuomingtang leader Cheng Li-wun's visit to Beijing last week, China said it would resume direct flights to Taiwan and imports of Taiwanese aquaculture products, as well as promote more cross-strait relations, though commentators have noted this may be a ploy to subvert the governing DPP’s authority and create more friction on the island.

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia restores oil facility to operation
incidents.description: Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline has resumed full operations after sustaining damage during the Iran conflict. The pipeline serves as the kingdom's only export route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, through which Saudi Arabia can reroute its entire 7 million barrels per day of oil exports. At the height of the disruption, the attack had reduced pipeline throughput by approximately 700,000 barrels per day.

incidents.title: U.S. blockades Hormuz
incidents.description: The U.S. has enacted a naval blockade against Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships that are not traveling to or from Iranian ports will not be subject to the blockade

incidents.title: China resumes limited Taiwan exchanges
incidents.description: China announced plans to restore some connections to Taiwan, including a resumption of suspended direct flights and imports of Taiwanese aquaculture products. Beijing also said it would explore creating a long-term communication mechanism with Taiwan’s Kuomintang.

incidents.title: Jaishankar meets UAE president
incidents.description: India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar met UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi for talks centered on regional stability and bilateral coordination.

incidents.title: China to supply Iran with air defense systems
incidents.description: U.S. intelligence officials warned that China was preparing to supply Iran with air- defense systems within the next few weeks. Trump stated he had requested that China not do so, threatening any country that supplies Iran with weapons with immediate 50% tariffs. This comes as the U.S. declared its own blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, raising questions over what a confrontation between U.S. and Chinese ships looks like.

incidents.title: U.S. inflation reaches four-year high
incidents.description: Consumer prices rose to their highest level in four years as prolonged conflict with Iran pushed energy and supply costs higher.

incidents.title: Chinese oil tankers transit Hormuz
incidents.description: Two Chinese supertankers carrying crude oil appeared to transit the Strait of Hormuz following the announcement of a ceasefire between the United States and Iran. The oil was not of Iranian origin, and their passage marked one of the busiest days for oil shipments through the waterway since the conflict began.

incidents.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to 1 day ceasefire
incidents.description: Russia agreed to a Ukrainian proposed Orthodox Easter ceasefire beginning at 4 p.m. local time on Saturday April 11 and ending at midnight on Sunday.

incidents.title: US threathens to resume war
incidents.description: U.S. forces in the Middle East remain postured to resume offensive operations should the ceasefire collapse or if a permanent peace deal is not reached by April 22. In a social media post, Trump threatened that the “shootin'” will resume “bigger, and better, and stronger than anyone has ever seen before” if Iran does not concede to demands from Washington.

incidents.title: Venezuela approves mining regulation reform
incidents.description: Venezuelan lawmakers approved a bill to regulate the mining sector as the government seeks to attract foreign investment to resource-rich but crime-affected southern regions.

incidents.title: Federal judge blocks Pentagon press restrictions
incidents.description: A federal judge blocked the Pentagon’s attempt to restrict journalist access to the press pool, preserving media access to defense coverage.

incidents.title: Iranian delegation arrives for Pakistan talks
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher arrived in Islamabad for mediated talks with a U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance.

incidents.title: India’s ISRO completes drop test
incidents.description: India’s space agency ISRO carried out the second integrated air drop test for the Gaganyaan crew module at Sriharikota, testing recovery systems under flight conditions.

incidents.title: Uk and Norway conduct military patrol
incidents.description: Norway and the U.K. conducted a weeks-long joint operation to deter Russian submarines operating near undersea infrastructure in the North Atlantic.

incidents.title: NATO Secretary General meets with Trump
incidents.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte held a closed-door meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House on March 8, following recent threats from Trump to withdraw the U.S. from NATO. On April 9, Trump continued to publicly criticize NATO’s lack of support to the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

incidents.title: Taiwan's National Secruity Director warns about China
incidents.description: Taiwan’s National Security Bureau Director-General Tsai Ming-yen gave a speech warning of China’s increased efforts to infiltrate Taiwan’s security establishment through the recruitment of rank-and-file personnel rather than just mid-level officials, as has previously been the case.

incidents.title: US and China summit set to take place
incidents.description: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that the relationship with China was stable and that the upcoming summit in May between Trump and Xi was on track.

incidents.title: Venezuelan police block wage protests
incidents.description: Workers, retirees, and union leaders marched in Caracas demanding higher wages and pensions but were blocked by police from reaching the presidential palace.

incidents.title: ConocoPhillips sends scouting team to Venezuela
incidents.description: ConocoPhillips said it was sending a small team to Venezuela to assess oil and natural gas opportunities after leaving the country in 2007 when its assets were nationalized.

incidents.title: Trump attacks NATO allies over Iran war support
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump publicly criticized NATO allies for refusing to more actively support the U.S. military campaign against Iran.

incidents.title: ICE agents shoot California man during confrontation
incidents.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in California shot a man authorities said attempted to weaponize his vehicle during an encounter.

incidents.title: Iran rejects nuclear restrictions
incidents.description: Atomic Energy Organization of Iran head Mohammad Eslami said Iran would not accept restrictions on its nuclear program and rejected U.S. and Israeli demands for denuclearization.

incidents.title: Xi urges military loyalty campaign
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on senior military officers to deepen ideological discipline and maintain loyalty to the Communist Party. The remarks followed an ongoing anticorruption campaign within the armed forces.

incidents.title: Russia and Ukraine express support for Iran ceasefire
incidents.description: Russian and Ukrainian senior leaders spoke in favor of the two-week ceasefire agreement between the U.S., Israel and Iran. Zelenskyy recently met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Shaara and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to discuss defense cooperation amid the Iran war.

incidents.title: Russia continues to hammer Ukrainian energy supplies
incidents.description: In the hours following the announcement of the two-week ceasefire in the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, numerous Gulf states reported attacks from Iran and Israel conducted a rapid series of airstrikes in Lebanon that killed at least 303 people.

incidents.title: Taiwan stockpiles energy
incidents.description: The Taiwan Semiconductor Industry Association (TSIA) called on the government to stockpile helium and liquified natural gas, both materials used in semiconductor manufacturing which have been disrupted by the war in Iran. TSIA also backed the reopening of the island’s nuclear power plants, though that will be a several year-long process

incidents.title: Trump puts 50 percent tariff on Iran allies
incidents.description: Trump said April 8, that any country supplying Iran with arms will be targeted with 50% tariffs

incidents.title: Chinese envoy meets with North Koreans
incidents.description: China’s foreign minister Wang Yi will visit North Korea next week for the first time since 2019.

incidents.title: Afghan/Pakistan agree to ceasefire
incidents.description: China’s Foreign Ministry said that following mediation efforts from Beijing, both countries had agreed not to further escalate their conflict and to explore comprehensive solutions for a peace agreement. While Afghanistan released a statement affirming the statement, Pakistan has not yet commented on the talks.
incidents.url: China says Afghanistan and Pakistan agree to explore comprehensive solution in peace talks | Reuters

incidents.title: Hungary to hold elections
incidents.description: The country is gearing up for its parliamentary election on Sunday, with current projections placing the opposition party Tisza on track to win a two-thirds parliamentary majority, a result that would unseat Viktor Orban’s ruling Fidesz party. Tisza’s leader, Peter Magyar, has campaigned on an anticorruption platform, vowing to bring Hungary in line with EU policies, with his potential victory marking the first step for the EU to unlock 90 billion euros in assistance funds for Ukraine
incidents.url: Hungary's Tisza party seen winning two-thirds majority in parliament, Median projection shows | Reuters

incidents.title: Israel kills 303 civilians in airstrike
incidents.description: In the hours following the announcement of the two-week ceasefire in the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, numerous Gulf states reported attacks from Iran and Israel conducted a rapid series of airstrikes in Lebanon that killed at least 303 people.

incidents.title: Venezuela promises wage increase amid inflation concerns
incidents.description: Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez urged workers to remain patient as her government works to stabilize the economy and promised a May 1 wage increase designed to avoid triggering inflation.

incidents.title: Iran and US agree to ceasfire
incidents.description: The U.S., Israel and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire beginning April 7. The agreement narrowly avoided a severe escalation of U.S. military operations, with Trump threatening that “a whole civilization will die tonight” just hours before.

incidents.title: US vice President pleads efforts to sign peace deal with Iran
incidents.description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance will lead U.S. diplomatic efforts to achieve a permanent peace deal with Iran at a summit meditated by Pakistan, scheduled for April 11.

incidents.title: Iran drone strikes Saudi pipeline
incidents.description: An Iranian drone struck a major Saudi pumping station and pipeline. Saudi Aramco declined to provide details on the extent of the damage.

incidents.title: India’s clean power capacity boost
incidents.description: India’s renewable electricity generating capacity surpassed 280 gigawatts, including almost 150 gigawatts of solar generation. The country now ranks third in the world in installed renewable capacity, comfortably ahead of its Paris accord pledge.

incidents.title: Indian Reserve Bank holds rate steady
incidents.description: The Reserve Bank of India left its policy rate unchanged at 5.25% and lifted its inflation outlook, citing higher crude price assumptions and the economic uncertainty created by war in the Middle East.

incidents.title: Russia sends oil to China
incidents.description: Russia has exported its first liquified natural gas shipment to China since November, using the Arc-class tanker Vladimir Rusanov to ship gas from the Yamal peninsula in ⁠the Arctic, which used to export gas mainly to Europe.

incidents.title: ICE kills alleged gang member
incidents.description: Agents from the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Agency (ICE) killed Carlos Ivan Mendoza Hernandez, an alleged member of the 18th Street Gang who was wanted in El Salvador, after he allegedly tried to run over an officer, just weeks after Congress passed a funding bill for the Department of Homeland Security that excluded funding for ICE operations. Separately, ICE data showed that its operations at U.S. airports have been expanding, with 800 arrests made between January 2025 and February 2026, largely aided by the Transport Security Administration sharing the records of over 31,000 passengers with ICE.
incidents.url: ICE agents shoot man in California during vehicle stop

incidents.title: China reduces dependency on US food
incidents.description: China’s agricultural sector has been diversifying its food sources for livestock, as China is hoping to wean itself off U.S. soybean imports, which have been the center of bilateral trade disputes over the past year.

incidents.title: Trump links NATO hostility to Greenland dispute
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said his frustration with NATO stemmed partly from allied opposition to U.S. annexation ambitions involving Greenland.

incidents.title: Trump issues new threat
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that an entire civilization would die if Iran did not make a deal. The statement came after weeks of failed peace talks and escalating violence.

incidents.title: China insulated from fertilizer shortages
incidents.description: China’s reliance on coal-based urea production helped shield its agricultural sector from global fertilizer disruptions linked to the Iran conflict. Analysts said Beijing may still limit exports to maintain domestic supply and control prices.

incidents.title: India industry delegation visits China
incidents.description: Indian officials and auto industry executives traveled to China to seek more reliable access to rare earth magnets and electric vehicle components, fields where Chinese firms dominate.

incidents.title: Ukraine reclaims territory
incidents.description: Ukrainian army chief Oleksandr Syrskyi claimed Ukraine has recaptured 185 square km of territory in the country’s east and south since January.

incidents.title: Japan holds talks with Iran
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated she was arranging summit talks with Iran, aiming to contribute to peace-making efforts in the ongoing conflict.

incidents.title: Taiwan opposition leader visits China
incidents.description: Kuomintang Chair Cheng Li-wun traveled to China as part of what she described as a peace mission amid renewed efforts by Beijing to promote reunification. The visit occurred during a period of heightened Chinese military pressure on Taiwan.

incidents.title: KMT leader visits Xi Jinping
incidents.description: The leader of Taiwan’s Kuomintang (KMT) opposition party, Cheng Li-wun, visited the Sun Yat Sen memorial in Nanjing as part of her multi-day “peace mission” to China. The visit culminated with a joint press conference, where Chinese President Xi Jinping said he would not tolerate any moves for Taiwanese independence. The move comes amid increased pressure by the U.S. for Taiwanese lawmakers to pass a supplemental defense budget, something the KMT has repeatedly blocked, with Cheng skipping talks on the subject with her visit.

incidents.title: Gunfire investigation near White House
incidents.description: The U.S. Secret Service investigated reports of overnight gunfire near Lafayette Park across from the White House while U.S. President Donald Trump was in residence. No injuries were reported, no suspect was found, and security in the area was increased.

incidents.title: India’s auto dealers warn of disruptions
incidents.description: India’s auto dealers warned that the Middle East conflict could soon disrupt vehicle supplies and dispatches as raw material costs rose. The industry signal showed the conflict spilling beyond energy into manufacturing and distribution chains.

incidents.title: US envoys arrive in Kyiv for peace talks
incidents.description: A senior U.S. delegation led by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, and U.S. Sen. Lindsay Graham is expected to arrive in Kyiv for talks with Ukrainian counterparts later this month.

incidents.title: South Korea secures energy protection deal
incidents.description: South Korean Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol met with representatives of the Gulf Cooperation Council, asking them to ensure a steady flow of fuel to South Korea while ensuring the safety of Korean vessels near the state.

incidents.title: China provides data to Iran about US equipment
incidents.description: Chinese firms, some of which have links with the People’s Liberation Army, have been using open source data to make social media posts detailing the location and nature of U.S. equipment in the Middle East amid Iran’s strikes across the region.

incidents.title: Iran to close Hormuz again
incidents.description: Iran reclosed the Strait of Hormuz in response to Israel’s large-scale April 8 attack in Lebanon.

incidents.title: Trump considers broader Cabinet purge
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly weighed additional Cabinet removals following recent senior dismissals.

incidents.title: US threathens EU to send help in Iran or face arms reductions
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to end arms shipments to Ukraine unless U.S. European allies participate in U.S.-led military operations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to anonymous sources cited by the Financial Times.

incidents.title: China maintains oil restrictions
incidents.description: China is expected to maintain restrictions on refined fuel exports through April, with only limited volumes, estimated at 150,000 to 300,000 metric tons of diesel, jet fuel, and gasoline potentially allowed for select Southeast Asian countries amid ongoing discussions.

incidents.title: Japan's Tomahawk missiles may be delayed
incidents.description: Japan’s orders of U.S.-made Tomahawk missiles, slated for delivery in 2028, may be delayed as U.S. forces are prioritizing the use of the missiles in their operations against Iran.

incidents.title: Iran strikes UAE/Kuwait oil facilities
incidents.description: Iranian drone and missile strikes disrupted the operations of major energy infrastructure in the UAE and Kuwait. An attack on the Habshan Gas Complex, the UAE’s largest natural gas plant, caused a fire that led to its shutdown. Drone attacks in Kuwait caused fires and serious damage at the Mina Al-Ahmadi Refinery and destroyed crucial Kuwaiti civilian infrastructure, including power generation and water desalination plants in the south.
incidents.url: Iran War: Abu Dhabi Halts Operations at Habshan Gas Facility After Attack - Bloomberg

incidents.title: Trump threatens Iranian infrastructure
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to strike Iranian civilian infrastructure, including bridges and power plants, if Iran refused U.S. ceasefire terms. Trump indicated the United States was prepared to expand its target set beyond military facilities.

incidents.title: Iran shoots down U.S. aircraft
incidents.description: Iranian forces shot down an A-10 Warthog and an F-15E fighter jet. U.S. forces rescued two of the three pilots while Iranian forces searched for the remaining pilot.

incidents.title: China investigates Politburo member
incidents.description: Chinese authorities placed Ma Xingrui, former party secretary of Xinjiang, under investigation for alleged violations of law and party discipline. The probe marked another high-profile case in Chinese President Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption campaign.

incidents.title: Ukraine denies Russia has captured city
incidents.description: Ukrainian officials have denied claims from Russian officials on April 1 that the Russian army has captured the entirety of Luhansk Oblast. Russian forces have occupied nearly all of Luhansk since 2022

incidents.title: UK hosts conference to reopen Hormuz
incidents.description: British Foreign Minister Yvette Cooper hosted a virtual summit of 35 nations on April 2, with the intention of exploring ways to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. did not participate in the summit

incidents.title: Taiwan builds new defences
incidents.description: Taiwan stated it would strengthen its defensive capabilities on its Pratas Islands, which have seen increased frequency of Chinese “gray zone” harassment

incidents.title: China detains Panama vessels
incidents.description: China has been detaining Panama-flagged vessels in China following a recent Panama court ruling against Hong Kong-based port operator CK Hutchison. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has condemned the seizures and state he looks forward to cooperating with Panama.

incidents.title: Iran fire salvo of missiles at Gulf States
incidents.description: Iran continued to fire missile and drone salvos against Israel and Arab Gulf states throughout the week, while Trump said during an April 1 national address that the U.S. will continue its bombing campaign for the next “two to three weeks” and bring Iran

incidents.title: Iran allows Phillippines ships to pass through Hormuz
incidents.description: Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro spoke with her counterpart in Iran and received assurances that Iran would allow Philippine-flagged vessels to safely pass through the Strait of Hormuz, including fuel tankers.

incidents.title: Trump fires Bondi
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi amid reported dissatisfaction over her handling of Justice Department files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and failed prosecutions involving the president’s political opponents. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche was named acting attorney general.

incidents.title: Indian defense exports hit record
incidents.description: India’s defense exports reached a record 384.24 billion rupees, about $4.1 billion, in the fiscal year ending March 2026, a jump of more than 62% from the previous year, reflecting the government’s effort to scale up domestic arms production and expand weapons sales abroad.

incidents.title: India’s government waives petrochemical duties
incidents.description: The government said key petrochemical inputs would receive a temporary full customs duty exemption during the Middle East crisis.

incidents.title: US considers withdrawing from NATO
incidents.description: Trump told a reporter from The Telegraph that he is considering withdrawing from NATO over lack of European support for the U.S. war in Iran

incidents.title: Israel kills Hezbollah leaders
incidents.description: Israeli officials claimed that more than 40 Hezbollah operatives, including a senior commander, were killed by Israel Defense Forces airstrikes against dozens of targets on April 1.

incidents.title: UAE and US prepare for joint operations
incidents.description: The United Arab Emirates is preparing to join the United States in operations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to anonymous UAE officials cited by the Wall Street Journal.

incidents.title: US citizen kidnapped by Iranian backed miltia
incidents.description: An American journalist was kidnapped by the Iranian-backed Iraqi militia Khataib Hezbollah in Baghdad on April 1.

incidents.title: China send navy into Tsushima strait
incidents.description: Five Chinese naval vessels, including three destroyers, crossed the Tsushima Strait between South Korea and Japan in response to Japan’s deployment of Type 25 long-range surface-to-ship guided missiles and hypervelocity gliding projectiles capable of striking Chinese mainland.

incidents.title: US lawmakers visit Taiwan
incidents.description: A bipartisan delegation of U.S. lawmakers visited Taiwan, urging Taiwanese lawmakers to pass a defense spending bill held up by opposition parties

incidents.title: KMT leader visits China
incidents.description: The leader of Taiwan’s opposition KMT party, Cheng Li-wun, visited China at the invitation of President Xi Jinping, with an intended aim of promoting peace and reconciliation.

incidents.title: US reopens DHS
incidents.description: United States: House Republicans have agreed to pass a bill that would resume funding for the Department of Homeland Security while excluding Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol. Speaker of the House Mike Johnson stated that funding would resume in the next few days through the appropriations and reconciliations processes. House and Senate minority leaders hailed the decision that would end seven weeks of a government shutdown, which had caused long delays at U.S. ports of entry.

incidents.title: US and Venezuela sign new mineral deal
incidents.description: United States/Venezuela: The U.S. Treasury Department issued general licenses related to Venezuela’s critical mineral and oil sectors, dictating the conditions for mineral supply acquisition and investment. The licenses exclude any transactions from Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, and China, with China already calling for a general lifting of sanctions instead. This comes as the U.S. Embassy in Caracas resumed operations for the first time since January.

incidents.title: U.S. lifts sanctions on Rodríguez
incidents.description: The United States lifted sanctions on acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez, removing her from the Treasury Department’s Specially Designated Nationals list.

incidents.title: Spain tightens immigration pathway for Venezuelans
incidents.description: Spain announced it would end a program allowing Venezuelans to regularize their legal status through humanitarian residence permits.

incidents.title: Trump attends Supreme Court birthright case
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to attend oral arguments at the Supreme Court, appearing during proceedings over his executive order to end birthright citizenship.

incidents.title: Iran expands security checkpoints in Tehran
incidents.description: Iranian authorities recruited teenagers to join paramilitary patrols and conduct vehicle searches at security checkpoints across Tehran. The measures continued despite concerns that checkpoints could become targets for U.S. airstrikes.

incidents.title: China plans fuel export ban extension
incidents.description: China was expected to extend its ban on refined fuel exports into April while considering limited exemptions for some Southeast Asian countries. Discussions covered small volumes of diesel, jet fuel, and gasoline shipments.

incidents.title: India grants SEZ duty relief
incidents.description: New Delhi allowed goods from special economic zones to be sold more easily into the domestic market through temporary customs duty relief to decrease internal supply strains as trade disruptions build up.

incidents.title: Japan and Indonesia cooperate on trade
incidents.description: Japan and Indonesia have made plans to coordinate on energy security as the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran squeezes Asia's oil and gas supply. Indonesia supplies half of the world's thermal coal for electricity generation and is a major liquefied natural gas exporter to Japan. Indonesia will assist in replacing Qatari and Gulf gas shipments and increase the supply of coal. Japan will use more coal-fired power plants to offset Middle East war-related disruptions to LNG imports. The collaboration will also include critical minerals, rare earths, and nuclear energy.

incidents.title: Russia rejects ceasefire
incidents.description: Russia rejected Ukraine’s March 30 offer of a ceasefire over the April 16 Orthodox Easter holiday.

incidents.title: French President visits Japan
incidents.description: French President Emmanuel Macron visited Japan, where both countries agreed to strengthen cooperation in securing rare earth supply chains.

incidents.title: EU provides more assests to Ukraine
incidents.description: Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas said the EU will provide Ukraine with $92 million of frozen Russian assets.

incidents.title: China buys more US oil
incidents.description: China has reportedly increased its purchases of U.S. crude oil and liquified natural gas, as China-bound tankers are headed to Corpus Christi, Texas, to load up nearly 600,000 barrels per day scheduled to be delivered to Chian in April, as the war in Iran continues to strain Asian energy markets.

incidents.title: Rubio calls for patience on Venezuela’s democratic transition
incidents.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Venezuela would require a transition period followed by free and fair elections while emphasizing that the process would take time.

incidents.title: Venezuela opposition leader meets with Rubio
incidents.description: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado held a closed-door meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to discuss restoring institutions, organizing elections, and attracting foreign investment.

incidents.title: U.S. gas prices surge after Hormuz disruption
incidents.description: Average domestic gasoline prices topped $4 per gallon after disruptions linked to the Strait of Hormuz crisis. This is the first time since the 2022 Russia invasion of Ukraine that U.S. gas reached that level.

incidents.title: China, Pakistan propose Iran ceasefire
incidents.description: China and Pakistan proposed a peace plan that included reopening the Strait of Hormuz and implementing a ceasefire between the warring parties. U.S. President Donald Trump said talks with Iran were continuing.

incidents.title: Trump says Iran war could end soon
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said the war with Iran could be nearing an end as U.S. objectives approached completion. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said direct talks with Iranian officials were possible.

incidents.title: Chinese ships transit Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Three Chinese ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz after coordination with relevant parties, according to China’s Foreign Ministry.

incidents.title: India’s export credit relief extended
incidents.description: India’s central bank extended export-credit relief through June 2026, as a result of stress from the Middle East crisis.

incidents.title: Chip assembly plant opens in India
incidents.description: Kaynes Semicon opened a chip assembly and test plant at Sanand in Gujarat, an outlay of around 33 billion rupees set to churn out several million chips a day. The plant joins a growing cluster of state backed semiconductor projects.

incidents.title: Russia provides oil to Cuba
incidents.description: The U.S. allowed a Russian oil tanker to bypass its blockade and deliver its cargo to Cuban ports on March 30. Trump said he had “no problem” with the shipment

incidents.title: US openly considers invading Iran
incidents.description: Trump is considering a ground operation to seize and remove at least 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium inside Iran, according to an anonymous U.S. government source cited by the Wall Street Journal. Such an operation would likely take several days at minimum. Trump has also publicly weighed options to seize Iran’s Kharg island through an amphibious landing.

incidents.title: China reopens airspace to North Korea
incidents.description: China has resumed Air China flights to North Korea, conducting its first commercial flight to Pyongyang in six years as both countries seek to deepen ties.

incidents.title: Iran maintains embassy will remain in place in Lebanon
incidents.description: Iran said its ambassador will remain in place in Lebanon despite being recently declared persona non grata by the Lebanese government.

incidents.title: Trump threatens to destory Iranian energy infrastucture
incidents.description: Trump threatened to destroy all of Iran’s energy infrastructure if a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is not reached. Oil prices have risen about 60% to $113 to $116 per barrel since the conflict began, as of March 31

incidents.title: Spain closes airspace for US aircraft
incidents.description: Spain has denied use of its airspace to U.S. aircraft involved in the Iran war, which Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has described as “illegal,” amid broad pushback from traditional U.S. allies in Europe over the joint- U.S./Israeli operations.

incidents.title: Iranian drone attack hits port of Dubai
incidents.description: An Iranian drone attack caused a fire on the Kuwaiti oil tanker Al Salmi, as it was anchored at the Dubai port. The tanker was loaded with 2 million barrels of crude oil from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait for delivery to China

incidents.title: Chinese factory activity returns to expansion
incidents.description: Economists projected that China’s manufacturing sector returned to expansion in March after two months of contraction. Strong export demand supported industrial activity despite concerns about supply chain disruptions linked to the Iran conflict.

incidents.title: Ukraine strikes Russian port with drones
incidents.description: A Ukrainian drone strike hit the Russia’s Baltic port of Ust-Luga on March 29. Ukraine recently has ramped up the frequency of its attacks against Russia’s Baltic maritime infrastructure.

incidents.title: China sanctions Japanese official
incidents.description: China imposed sanctions against Keiji Furuya, a Japanese lawmaker and aid to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, for his repeated visits to Taiwan, which Beijing considers collusion with “Taiwan independence forces.”

incidents.title: Pakistani Reiterates Interest in US/Iran/Israel Talks
incidents.description: Pakistani Foreign Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar reiterated that Pakistan is willing to facilitate talks between the U.S. and Iran, as Pakistan and China presented a peace initiative that includes an immediate ceasefire and a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has claimed that the U.S. is negotiating “directly and indirectly” with Iran, while Iranian officials have denied that negotiations are taking place.

incidents.title: China conducts military exercises
incidents.description: The Chinese air force, navy, and coast guard conducted patrols around the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea.

incidents.title: North Korea tests new missile
incidents.description: North Korea held a test for a solid-fuel engine that reportedly could give North Korean missiles the ability to reach U.S. mainland, though experts debate the feasibility of that capability.

incidents.title: No Kings protests expand across U.S.
incidents.description: Thousands of demonstrations took place across the United States as part of the third round of coordinated No Kings protests against the Trump administration, with opposition to the Iran war among the major drivers of mobilization.

incidents.title: India Navy maritime war game
incidents.description: The Indian Navy held a tabletop crisis exercise at its Kochi warfare center, an event it tagged IMEX TTX 2026, working through scenarios with partner navies.

incidents.title: China and Phillippines make energy deal
incidents.description: The Philippines have resumed high-level talks with China on possible energy exploration cooperation in the South China Sea, marking the first such talk after a year-long pause since January 2025.

incidents.title: EU buys more Algerian oil
incidents.description: As the Middle East war disrupts global energy flows, Europe is turning to Algeria as a potential replacement for gas supplies from the Gulf. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni visited Algiers on Wednesday in an effort to increase gas imports from Algeria, and a Thursday visit to Algiers by Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares resulted in the countries looking to raise gas deliveries to Spain by 10%.

incidents.title: Ukraine and Suadi Arabia sign tech agreement
incidents.description: Ukraine and Saudi Arabia have signed a cooperation agreement focused on defense and technology industry investment. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy unveiled the deal during an unannounced trip to Saudi Arabia on March 26.

incidents.title: China stations aircraft near Taiwan
incidents.description: China has stationed old J-6 fighter jets, repurposed as attack drones, at six air bases in Fujian and Guangdong provinces near the Taiwan Strait, offering Beijing a cheaper strike method if it chooses to attack Taiwan.

incidents.title: Russian energy targets are hit by Ukraine
incidents.description: The Ukrainian military is targeting critical Russian energy infrastructures after the U.S.-Israel war with Iran prompted the easing of sanctions on Russian oil in response to global energy shortages. Ukrainian drones attacked one of the largest Russian oil refineries northeast of Moscow, the Kirishi refinery, and the Ust-Luga and Primorsk export terminals on the Baltic coast

incidents.title: Senate passes DHS budget ending shutdown
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate approved a budget deal reopening the Department of Homeland Security after a prolonged shutdown tied to disputes over immigration enforcement. The agreement restored key federal services and reduced immediate governance disruption.

incidents.title: India clears arms purchases
incidents.description: The Defence Acquisition Council cleared military procurement proposals worth about $25 billion, including air-defense systems, transport aircraft, drones, and more S-400 units. The package indicated the continued force buildup against pressure from China and Pakistan.

incidents.title: India eases China procurement rules
incidents.description: New Delhi relaxed some restrictions on state-run purchases of critical equipment from China, reducing approval burdens for select suppliers.

incidents.title: India absorbs oil shock
incidents.description: Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri said the state was taking on part of the crude oil price jump instead of pushing the full increase onto households.

incidents.title: Modi meets ministers on fuel
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi convened chief ministers to coordinate fuel distribution and inflation management as the conflict in the Middle East strained imports and logistics.

incidents.title: Drone hits Turkish crewed ship carrying Russian oil
incidents.description: A drone struck a Turkish-crewed vessel operating under the flag of Sierra Leone carrying Russian oil in the Black Sea on March 26. The attack took place just outside of Turkish territorial waters, 33 kilometers from the Bosphorus.

incidents.title: US puts hold on new strikes against Iranian energy
incidents.description: The U.S. extended a pause on attacks against Iran's energy facilities until April 7, as U.S. President Donald Trump reported “productive” talks with Iranian officials

incidents.title: South Korea open up monitary reserves in light of Iran war
incidents.description: The South Korean government announced it would deploy a supplemental $16.6 billion budget to help ease the economic repercussions of the Iran war.

incidents.title: U.S. inflation reaches OECD high amid war fallout
incidents.description: U.S. inflation climbed to the highest level among OECD countries as economic consequences from the Iran conflict intensified. Rising fuel and supply costs increased domestic economic strain.

incidents.title: Pentagon develops new Iran strike plan
incidents.description: Two U.S. officials said the Pentagon was developing a new operation designed to deliver a final blow to the Iranian military. The planning reportedly included consideration of a possible ground campaign.

incidents.title: Trump extends Hormuz ultimatum
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump extended a deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and allow additional time for diplomacy. Trump also warned that the United States could target Iranian energy infrastructure if negotiations failed.

incidents.title: U.S. considers 10,000-troop deployment
incidents.description: The Pentagon considered sending up to 10,000 additional troops to the Middle East as peace talks with Iran continued. Officials said the deployment would provide military planners with additional options if negotiations failed.

incidents.title: China chip industry accelerates
incidents.description: Chinese semiconductor executives said the country’s chip industry was growing faster than expected as artificial intelligence infrastructure demand increased. The growth was driving higher capital spending and capacity expansion across the sector.

incidents.title: China mulls easing bank ownership rules
incidents.description: Chinese regulators considered relaxing shareholding restrictions for some major bank investors. The proposed move aimed to broaden capital-raising options for commercial banks facing economic pressure.

incidents.title: Iran opens passage to Indian shipping
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said vessels linked to India, China, and Russia would still be allowed commercial passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: Russia halted oil exports from two major Baltic Sea ports
incidents.description: Russia halted oil exports from two major Baltic Sea ports on March 25, following Ukrainian drone strikes.

incidents.title: UK seizes Russian oil tankers
incidents.description: U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer has authorized British armed forces to board and seize Russian shadow fleet vessels

incidents.title: Ukraine attends peace talks in US
incidents.description: U.S. and Ukrainian officials coordinated on peace talks in Miami from March 21-22, for the first time since the start of the U.S./Israeli war with Iran. Zelenskyy said on March 24 that the U.S. has conditioned security guarantees to Ukraine on Kyiv’s ceding the entirety of the Donbas region to Russia.

incidents.title: Taiwan gets permission to buy US arms
incidents.description: Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo said Taiwan received a letter of guarantee from the U.S. regarding the planned $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan indicating that the deal will likely be formally approved in May following Trump’s trip to China.

incidents.title: US and China agree on date for talks
incidents.description: The Trump administration has confirmed new dates for a summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, which will likely take place on May 14-15. This follows previous statements by the White House that Trump wanted to wait until the end of the Iran war to visit Beijing.

incidents.title: US deploys airborne division to Middle East
incidents.description: The U.S. ordered the deployment of at least 2,000 more soldiers from the 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East. The location and the mission of the deployment has not been specified by DoD officials.

incidents.title: Pakistan opens negotiations between US and Iran
incidents.description: Pakistan opened indirect lines of communication between the United States and Iran. The U.S. presented Iran a 15-point ceasefire proposal to Iran. While details of the proposal have not confirmed by the White House, some of the conditions include the removal of enriched uranium, the abandonment of the enrichment program, limitations on ballistic missile production, and the cessation of support to Iran’s regional proxy network, according to anonymous officials from Middle East states cited by the Washington Post. Iran rejected that proposal and submitted a counterproposal via Pakistani intermediaries.

incidents.title: U.S. recovers Venezuelan gold reserves
incidents.description: U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said the United States recently recovered $100 million worth of gold from Venezuela after visiting the country with oil and mining executives.

incidents.title: Venezuela appoints intelligence chief as defense minister
incidents.description: Venezuela’s longtime intelligence chief Gustavo González López, who has been accused of overseeing torture and repression, was appointed defense minister as acting President Delcy Rodríguez consolidated control over the military.

incidents.title: Iran insists Lebanon be included in peace talks
incidents.description: Iranian officials have informed the U.S. via intermediaries that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire deal with the U.S. and Israel.

incidents.title: Poll shows rising U.S. concern over Iran war
incidents.description: An AP-NORC poll found that 59% of Americans believed recent U.S. military action against Iran had gone too far, while the share of Americans highly concerned about affording gasoline rose from 30% to 45%.

incidents.title: Chinese vessel transits Hormuz
incidents.description: A Chinese-owned liquefied petroleum gas carrier transited the Strait of Hormuz during the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. The voyage followed Iranian statements promising safe passage for vessels not linked to countries Tehran considers enemies.

incidents.title: Israel attacks Iranian port
incidents.description: Israel bombed a port on the Iranian Caspian Sea coast that is believed to facilitate the delivery of weapons and supply deliveries from Russia to support the Iranian war effort.

incidents.title: Israel announces plan to occupy South Lebanon
incidents.description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Israel intends to occupy Lebanese territory up to the Litani River, as Israel continued its bombing campaign across Lebanon and conducted ground operations in the south near the Israeli-Lebanese border.

incidents.title: Lebanon expells Iranian envoys
incidents.description: Lebanon declared Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Reza Sheibani persona non grata and expelled him from the country over Iran’s support for Hezbollah

incidents.title: US blocks Russian ship from entering Cuba
incidents.description: The United States has formally stated that the Russian oil tanker heading toward Cuba with 700,000 barrels of crude will not be permitted to deliver its cargo to the island. This comes despite temporary sanctions easing measures on Russian oil put in place by the U.S. Treasury in an effort to calm markets. The Russian delivery is likely a test by the Russian government to put pressure on the U.S.’s resolve, according to knowledgeable sources quoted by Politico. Meanwhile, U.S. suppliers have been delivering oil to Cuba’s private sector, with 30,000 barrels delivered since February. While this represents a fraction of Cuba’s energy needs, documents obtained by Reuters suggest the volume is likely to keep growing. Former Cuban President Raul Castro and current President Miguel Diaz-Canel said they have been in negotiations with the U.S. regarding the island’s energy shortage.

incidents.title: China maps undersea areas near Taiwan
incidents.description: China has reportedly conducted an extensive undersea mapping and monitoring operations over the past two years in preparation for possible naval conflict with the U.S. The mapping operations have spanned the Pacific, Indian, and Arctic oceans.

incidents.title: China conducts military exercises
incidents.description: China conducted large-scale naval live-fire exercises, for the first time involving two newly commissioned Type-055 destroyers, which the People’s Liberation Army Navy hopes will increase their combat capabilities in the Eastern Theater Command, which oversees operations near Taiwan and Japan.

incidents.title: Japan downgrades China in diplomatic handbook
incidents.description: Japan is expected to downgrade its relationship with China in its upcoming 2026 Diplomatic Handbook following increased tensions with Beijing over comments on Taiwan made by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. This follows a separate event in which an active duty officer of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces breached the Chinese Embassy in Tokyo, for which Beijing has demanded strong repercussions.

incidents.title: China sees more investment in green energy
incidents.description: Stock prices for Chinese renewable energy companies have risen as investors anticipate a surge in global demand for green energy due to the oil shock caused by the Iran war. Since the conflict began, investors have bought shares in Chinese solar, wind, electric vehicle, and battery manufacturers. China's renewable energy sector will benefit from expected increased export demand, as well as increased official support and investment.

incidents.title: Taiwan restarts nuclear reactors
incidents.description: State-owned Taiwan Power is moving ahead with proposals to start the process of reopening the island’s nuclear power stations. President Lai Ching-te approved the restart despite opposition to nuclear power by his ruling Democratic Progressive Party, which had led the successful effort to phase out Taiwan’s nuclear power sector. Two plants, Guosheng and Maanshan, will likely be restarted under the plan.

incidents.title: Venezuela opposition pushes oil privatization
incidents.description: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado called for the full privatization of the country’s oil industry in a speech to energy executives and investors.

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela dialogue delegation announced
incidents.description: Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez said her government would send a diplomatic delegation to Washington to begin a new phase of talks with the United States.

incidents.title: Iran war continues on both sides
incidents.description: The U.S. and Israel continued their bombing campaign across Iran, as Iran continued to fire missile and drone salvos targeting Israel and the Gulf states throughout the week of March 21-27.

incidents.title: U.S. deploys 82nd Airborne to Middle East
incidents.description: The U.S. 82nd Airborne Division joined other American forces deploying to the Middle East. The deployment came as U.S. President Donald Trump suggested a deal could soon end the war.

incidents.title: Iran leaves door open to negotiations
incidents.description: Iranian officials criticized the terms of a U.S. proposal to end the war but stopped short of rejecting it outright. The response left open the possibility of further negotiations between the two sides.

incidents.title: China tests new destroyers
incidents.description: Two newly commissioned Chinese Type 055 destroyers conducted their first live-fire training after joining the People’s Liberation Army division responsible for Taiwan and the East China Sea. The exercise simulated high-intensity combat missions.

incidents.title: Jaishankar, Rubio discuss energy security
incidents.description: Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the Middle East conflict and wider energy-security concerns.

incidents.title: Explosion occurs in Ukrainan city
incidents.description: An IED explosion in the Ukrainian city of Bucha near Kyiv wounded two police officers on March 23. The attack was orchestrated by Russian intelligence agents, according to Ukrainian authorities.

incidents.title: India puts new tariffs on China
incidents.description: India is considering imposing antidumping tariffs on viscose filament yarn imports from China.

incidents.title: Ukraine makes accusation that Russia gives assisstance to Iran
incidents.description: Zelenskyy claimed that Ukraine has “irrefutable evidence” that Russia is providing Iran with intelligence to aid its war effort against the U.S. and Israel, while Russia is providing drones to Iran, according to an unidentified western intelligence official cited by the

incidents.title: Australia signs trade deal with EU
incidents.description: The EU signed a trade deal with Australia after eight years of negotiations. The deal will see a removal of most tariffs on each other’s imports, including Australian critical minerals, while keeping quotas on EU imports of Australian agricultural products.

incidents.title: US to pay French energy company to stop building windfarm
incidents.description: The Trump administration has said it will pay French energy giant TotalEnergies $1 billion to halt development of offshore wind farms off the U.S. East Coast. In turn, TotalEnergies agreed to invest that money in U.S. natural gas and oil projects. The company also promised not to build any new offshore wind projects in the U.S.

incidents.title: US confrims new DHS secretary
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate confirmed the appointment of Sen. Markwayne Mullin as the new head of the Department of Homeland Security by a 54-45 vote. He will succeed Kristi Noem, who has been reassigned. This comes as lawmakers approved financing most of DHS’s operations with the exception of the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, while Trump signed a separate order to fund the Transportation Security Administration following weekslong disruptions to the country’s airports.

incidents.title: India recommends duties on Chinese yarn
incidents.description: India’s Directorate General of Trade Remedies recommended anti-dumping duties on imports of viscose rayon filament yarn from China. The proposed duties would apply to a type of artificial fiber widely used in textiles.

incidents.title: Modi says energy supply secure
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told the Lok Sabha that India’s energy position remained manageable despite the war, citing steps taken to protect fuel availability and shipping.

incidents.title: India seeks duties on Chinese yarn
incidents.description: India’s trade remedies body recommended anti-dumping levies on filament yarn made from viscose rayon and brought in from China, an artificial fiber common in textiles.

incidents.title: Russia captures village in Ukraine
incidents.description: Russian forces reported the capture of a small village in the Sumy region, as Ukrainian officials claim that Russia has initiated a springtime ground offensive along the front lines in Ukraine.

incidents.title: Iran to allow Japanese ships in Hormuz
incidents.description: Iran has stated it was prepared to allow Japanese ships to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Japan has stated it could consider deploying its minesweeping capabilities to the strait after a ceasefire is reached.

incidents.title: China to buy more from US and EU
incidents.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang told the China Development Forum in Beijing that China will aim to open the country’s economy to more imports of high-quality goods from the U.S. and EU, as well as other trading partners. This follows China’s ambitions to shift toward a more consumption-based economy.

incidents.title: 64 people killed in Darfur
incidents.description: At least 64 people were killed in strike on a hospital in the country’s Darfur region. The rebel Rapid Support Forces blamed the Sudan Armed Forces for the strike while the SAF officially denied the attack. SAF officials speaking anonymously said the strike had been intended to hit a nearby police station. The conflict is entering its third year, with an official death count of 40,000, though aid groups estimate a likely higher toll.

incidents.title: Chinese premier pledges wider market access
incidents.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang said China would further open its economy to foreign companies and pursue more balanced trade with global partners. Li also said Beijing would import more high-quality foreign goods and expand trade opportunities.

incidents.title: Industry group backs mitigation steps
incidents.description: The Confederation of Indian Industry said the government was moving quickly to cushion the Iran war’s impact through energy sourcing and shipping measures, reflecting coordination between policymakers and business.

incidents.title: Trump threatens to deploy ICE to airports
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said that if the Democrats did not agree to fund the Department of Homeland Security, he would deploy Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to airports.
