His threat was issued at the height of spring break travel season amid delays and long wait times at airports across the country.

incidents.title: Modi speaks with Iran president
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, condemned attacks on critical infrastructure, and stressed the need to keep sea lanes open.

incidents.title: Venezuela replaces military leadership
incidents.description: Acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez said she had replaced all senior military commanders following the U.S. abduction of President Nicolás Maduro.

incidents.title: U.S. weighs attack on Kharg Island
incidents.description: Reports indicated the United States was considering attacking or invading Iran's Kharg Island to force the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Sources familiar with Pentagon planning said Iranian drones could continue disrupting shipping even if the island were seized.

incidents.title: IRGC spokesman killed in airstrike
incidents.description: A joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike killed Ali Mohammad Naini, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps deputy of public relations and a prominent spokesman for the organization, according to Iranian state media.

incidents.title: U.S. seeks Chinese fentanyl convictions
incidents.description: A U.S. official said Washington welcomed recent Chinese arrests related to illicit fentanyl trafficking but wanted Beijing to pursue seizures and convictions. Chinese state media had announced a new campaign targeting traffickers.

incidents.title: CIA claims Iran is getting targetting data from Russia
incidents.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe said Iran is seeking targeting data from Russia against U.S. forces in the Middle East, during a congressional hearing on March 18.

incidents.title: South Korea considers buying oil from Russia
incidents.description: South Korea is reportedly exploring the possibility of buying oil and naphtha from Russia for the first time in three years. Other countries, including the Philippines and Thailand, have indicated similar plans as the conflict in Iran is inflicting a heavy toll on Asian oil supplies.

incidents.title: Japanese PM meets with Trump
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met with Trump in Washington, their second meeting since a positive hailing of ties in October. The leaders agreed to cooperate further on joint development of rare earth elements and strengthening their supply chains, while also reiterating commitments made by Japan to invest in U.S. critical industries. Both countries further issued a statement opposing any unilateral change to the status quo with Taiwan. While Trump said he expected Japan’s help in resolving the conflict in Iran, he did not publicly push Takaichi for military involvement

incidents.title: Japan and France discuss cooperating in Space
incidents.description: Japan and France are exploring new ways to enhance cooperation on space defense, including sharing satellite data, following a recent visit by French Maj. Gen. Vincent Chusseau to Japan.

incidents.title: Trump denies role in South Pars strike
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected accusations that the United States attacked Iran's South Pars gas field and instead blamed the Israeli air force. Qatar also denied involvement in the attack.

incidents.title: China approves Nvidia H200 chip sales
incidents.description: Chinese authorities approved Nvidia’s sale of H200 artificial intelligence chips to domestic customers, according to sources familiar with the matter. The approval opened the door for Nvidia to resume sales of a key chip in the Chinese market.

incidents.title: India rolls out insurance support package
incidents.description: India rolled out an insurance-support package worth about 4.97 billion rupees, or $52.7 million, for shipments exposed to conflict-affected Middle East routes. The scheme was meant to offset war-risk premiums and keep smaller exporters from losing orders.

incidents.title: Spain sends 1.2 billion defence package to Ukraine
incidents.description: Spain announced a $1.2 billion aid package for Ukraine, focused on expanding defense industry cooperation

incidents.title: Russia captures village in Sumy
incidents.description: Russian forces claimed the capture of a village in Ukraine’s Sumy region on March 17

incidents.title: EU offers financial and tech support to Ukrainian pipelines
incidents.description: The EU has offered financial and technical support to Ukraine to repair a pipeline that delivers Russian crude to Hungary in an effort to persuade Hungary to relent on its legislative block on EU aid initiatives to Ukraine. Hungary is lobbying the EU to relieve sanctions on Russian and Belarusian fertilizer exports.

incidents.title: Trump openly considers ground invasion of Iran
incidents.description: Trump is weighing options of deploying thousands of additional American troops to support the war effort against Iran, according to unnamed U.S. government officials cited by Reuters. The sources did not indicate what the objective of the deployment would be.

incidents.title: China offers LNG to Taiwan
incidents.description: China offered to export liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Taiwan to ensure adequate energy security. Taiwan rejected the offer, with government officials stating the move is part of efforts by Beijing to unify the island and mainland through cognitive warfare. Taiwan currently imports no energy from China and had previously mentioned securing LNG stockpiles from multiple sources, including the U.S., that would last until at least June

incidents.title: Israel kills key Iranian officials
incidents.description: Israeli strikes killed numerous key Iranian officials, including Intelligence Minister Esmail Khatib, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Ali Larijani, and head of the Basij forces Gen. Gholamreza Soleimani during the week of March 16-20.

incidents.title: Malaysia void trade agreement with the US
incidents.description: The Malaysian government has stated it considers its trade agreement with the U.S. “null and void” following the recent U.S. Supreme Court decision to strike down Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs. Washington had previously urged its trading partners to honor the terms of the deals despite the ruling.

incidents.title: India investigates Chinese chemicals
incidents.description: India’s Directorate General of Trade Remedies opened an anti-dumping investigation into imports of ethyl chloroformate from China, following allegations in the industry that China was selling the product at unfairly low prices.

incidents.title: U.S. eases sanctions on PDVSA oil sales
incidents.description: The U.S. Treasury Department eased sanctions to allow American companies to conduct limited business with Venezuelan state oil firm PDVSA as part of efforts to boost global oil supply during the Iran war.

incidents.title: Israel attacks oil facility in Persian Gulf
incidents.description: Israel conducted airstrikes March 18 against energy infrastructure in the South Pars, an offshore gas reservoir in the Persian Gulf that extends into the territorial waters of Qatar and Iran. Iran retaliated by firing on the energy infrastructure of various Gulf states, including Qatar. Trump claimed on social media that Qatar had no knowledge of or involvement in the attacks and claimed that Israel would not conduct another attack in the South Pars unless Iran attacked Qatar.

incidents.title: Pentagon seeks $200 billion to fund Iran war
incidents.description: The Pentagon requested a major congressional funding package to increase production of weaponry linked to the Iran conflict.

incidents.title: Ukraine sends drone operators to Gulf states
incidents.description: Ukraine deployed 201 drone specialists to the Middle East to assist Gulf states in their counter-Iranian drone efforts, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

incidents.title: Ukraine and UK sign new defense production agreement
incidents.description: Ukraine and the U.K. signed a defense agreement on March 17, focused on drones and defense industry cooperation.

incidents.title: Turkiye offers to hold peace talks between Russia and Ukraine
incidents.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan told Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov that Türkiye is ready to host new rounds of negotiations, although Washington has not signaled a high-level willingness to engage.

incidents.title: Israel deploys troops into Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel committed additional troops to its ground operations in southern Lebanon and conducted numerous airstrikes across Beirut, including a strike in central Beirut that killed at least 10 people on March 18. Over 900 people have been killed and over 1 million displaced in Lebanon since March 2. Hezbollah has consistently conducted rocket attacks into northern Israel since March 2, although no Israeli fatalities have been reported

incidents.title: Trump asks to delay Xi Jinping summit
incidents.description: Trump formally asked to delay the planned summit with President Xi Jinping by a month, placing the new date to the end of April, in light of the developing situation in Iran. Prior to the request, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in Paris, where trade relations were dubbed as stable by officials present. Both sides are also reportedly exploring the establishment of a “Board of Trade” that would see political barriers lowered in sensitive sectors, though details still remain scarce.

incidents.title: Pakistan continues its air campaign in Afghanistan
incidents.description: Pakistan continued its airstrike campaign against Afghanistan, this week striking a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul, resulting in at least 75 killed, many of whom were adolescents. The latest strike brings the total death count to 274 people since Islamabad declared “open war” against the Taliban regime. Efforts by China to mediate the conflict so far have failed to deliver concrete results, and the U.S. has given its approval to Pakistan’s right to self-defense in light of its conflict with terrorist groups. A Taliban spokesperson has stated the regime would retaliate

incidents.title: Iran rejects any attempts to reach peace resoultion
incidents.description: Iran’s newly appointed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has rejected ceasefire proposals presented by two intermediaries to the Iranian Foreign Ministry, according to an unnamed Iranian official cited by Reuters. Details of the proposed terms and the identity of the intermediaries are not publicly available. Khamenei vowed to bring the U.S. “to their knees.”

incidents.title: U.S. counterterrorism chief resigns over Iran war
incidents.description: National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent resigned from his position. Kent posted on social media that Iran posed no imminent threat to the United States and said the war began because of pressure from Israel and its American lobby.

incidents.title: Iran reports senior IRGC leaders killed
incidents.description: Iranian acting Minister of Defense Majid Ebn-e-Reza announced the deaths of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps security head and the leader of the IRGC's Basij militia as the United States and Israel continued targeting Iranian leadership. Iran responded by firing missile salvos into Israeli territory.

incidents.title: China fuel export ban may tighten Asian supply
incidents.description: China’s ban on diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel exports was expected to worsen fuel shortages across Asia. The restriction came as Gulf refineries and shipping routes faced disruption from the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

incidents.title: Indian Parliament passes appropriation bill
incidents.description: Parliament approved the 2026 Appropriation Bill, completing a key stage of the budget process as the government prepared for mounting external strain.

incidents.title: NATO leaders condemn Israel for invasion of Lebanon
incidents.description: A joint statement from the leaders of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, and the U.K. called for the prevention of a “significant ground invasion” of southern Lebanon by Israel

incidents.title: US bloackade around Cuba cripples power grid
incidents.description: Cuba’s electricity grid collapsed on Monday, causing widespread blackouts as the U.S. oil blockade against the island continues to hold. In response, Russia has sent over 700,000 barrels of oil on a sanctioned tanker, which is currently en route to the island. Despite negotiations reportedly still taking place, Trump refused to rule out military operations against the island, stating that he would “have the honor of taking Cuba,” while U.S. officials have stated that Trump wishes to remove President Miguel Díaz-Canel from power before leaving it to Cubans to ensure adequate governance

incidents.title: Board of Peace meets with Hamas Officials
incidents.description: Representatives of Trump’s Board of Peace met with Hamas officials in Egypt to safeguard ceasefire implementation in Gaza from the regional fallout of the war in Iran.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan amends constituion
incidents.description: A referendum on constitutional reform overwhelmingly passed, with 87% of votes in favor amid a 73% voter turnout. As a result, the country will abolish its bicameral legislature and replace it with a unicameral parliament. The referendum also enshrines Kazakh as the official state language, as opposed to a language on official footing with Russian. Critics of the reformed constitution claim it grants more power to the presidency and risks enabling government crackdown on dissenting voices. The legal changes are set to be implemented in the summer.

incidents.title: EU energy ministers plan for how to avoid power loss from US war with Iran
incidents.description: EU energy ministers are developing emergency energy measures to protect consumers from rising gas and oil prices from the U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Benchmark gas prices in Europe have increased by more than 50% to between $101 and $108 per barrel as of March 18. Ministers are exploring potential solutions to mitigate surging energy prices and interruptions to supplies of oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) that have resulted from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Short-term measures include increasing the supply of carbon emission permits to lower the cost of electricity, financial relief, and price controls, while long-term measures include reducing reliance on fossil fuels imports and accelerating renewable energy and nuclear projects.

incidents.title: Top UAE oil producers close down amid US-Iran war
incidents.description: The U.S.-Israel war with Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz led UAE national oil company ADNOC to shut down production, reducing UAE oil output by more than half. The UAE's port of Fujairah, which is a significant oil bunkering and storage hub, was the target of an attack by a drone, which caused ADNOC to cease oil loading operations. By March 16, the UAE's daily crude production dropped from nearly 3.56 million barrels in February to approximately 1.5 million barrels per day.

incidents.title: Venezuela seeks return to Mercosur
incidents.description: Venezuela announced plans to seek full membership in Mercosur after previously being suspended in 2017 over the political crisis under former President Nicolás Maduro.

incidents.title: Trump attemps to mobalize NATO against Iran
incidents.description: Trump called on U.S. NATO and European allies to form a joint naval force to contribute to security operations in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran’s Islamic Revolution Guard Corps declared the strait closed. No U.S. allies have yet agreed to enter into the proposed coalition.

incidents.title: India’s trade gap narrows
incidents.description: India’s February trade deficit narrowed, but officials warned that the escalating Middle East crisis was already complicating shipments, insurance, and energy security.

incidents.title: Belgium offers to mediate end to Ukraine war
incidents.description: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever called for Europe to end the war in Ukraine, normalize relations with Russia, and regain access to cheap energy. Belgian Foreign Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Maxime Prévot publicly distanced himself from De Wever’s comments.

incidents.title: China enters Taiwanese airspcae
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported renewed incursions into its air-defense identification zone by the Chinese military following a recent lull in such operations for the first time in four years. China further sent a coast guard ship into Taiwan’s Dongsha coral island, a disputed landmark in the South China Sea, likely to test Taiwan’s reaction time.

incidents.title: China develops new semiconductor chips
incidents.description: China-based Hua Hong Group, the country’s second-largest chipmaker after Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), announced it was in the final stages of installing a 7-nanometer chip-making process in its Shanghai-based plant. SMIC had up until now been the only Chinese company capable of developing the 7-nm chips, which are necessary for training advanced AI models. The equipment used for the process in Hua Hong’s case has not been disclosed, and while Hua Hong is reported to have worked in close collaboration with Huawei, details on how it achieved the breakthrough are unclear.

incidents.title: DPRK fires missiles into Sea of Japan
incidents.description: North Korea launched more than 10 ballistic missiles into the sea during joint military drills between the U.S. and South Korea. This comes as Trump expressed a renewed desire last week to organize a summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

incidents.title: U.S. Embassy reopening in Caracas
incidents.description: The United States said it had reopened its embassy in Caracas after a seven-year closure, marking a major step in restoring diplomatic relations with Venezuela.

incidents.title: US forces prepare to invade Kharg island
incidents.description: U.S. forces conducted significant bombings against Iranian positions on Kharg Island, while U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to target energy infrastructure on the island if Iran did not agree to re-open the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: Meta to cut 10,000 jobs in 2026
incidents.description: Facebook parent Meta announced a second round of mass layoffs, causing the tech industry to brace for a significant economic downturn. Tech companies have laid off more than 290,000 workers since the beginning of 2022.

incidents.title: India seeks safe passage for ships
incidents.description: India worked to secure transit for more vessels stranded around the Strait of Hormuz after some ships were allowed through.

incidents.title: U.S. launches trade investigations
incidents.description: New investigations conducted under Section 301(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 into 60 economies are being launched to determine whether those governments have curbed imports of goods produced with forced labor.

incidents.title: Mojtaba Khamenei threatens Hormuz shipping
incidents.description: New Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Iran would attack any ship in the Strait of Hormuz to pressure global powers into ending the war against Iran. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu responded by threatening Iran's new government and its leaders.

incidents.title: Iran strikes Gulf states
incidents.description: Iran struck multiple Gulf states with missile and drone attacks. The attacks followed comments from new Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei that any country hosting a U.S. military base would be considered a valid target, while the United States said it struck targets on Kharg Island.

incidents.title: Trump assails Iranian leadership
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump disparaged Iran's recently assassinated leader and government while defending U.S. and Israeli strikes against the country. Iranian sources said the war had killed more than 2,000 people as Trump cited Iran's human rights record to justify the campaign.

incidents.title: China passes ethnic identity law
incidents.description: China approved a new law promoting a shared national identity among the country’s ethnic minority groups. The law, enforced starting on July 1, will mandate that Mandarin be the language of instruction in schools.

incidents.title: India pauses U.S. trade talks
incidents.description: India deferred plans to close an interim trade arrangement with the United States after Washington’s tariff regime changed and new probes were opened.

incidents.title: Russian envoy meets with Steve Witkoff
incidents.description: Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev met with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner in Florida on March 11 to discuss the possible easing of U.S. sanctions against Russia, to offset the impact of the war in Iran on oil prices. Russia has made $6.9 billion in fossil fuel revenue as a result of fallout from the war in Iran on global energy markets, according to data analysis from the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air

incidents.title: Iran attacks Dubai
incidents.description: Iranian fire hit vessels off the coast of Dubai and Iraq and oil infrastructure in Bahrain on March 12

incidents.title: Taiwan passes bill to buy HIMARS
incidents.description: Taiwan’s three political parties came together in a rare show of agreement to authorize the acceptance of a U.S. sale of HIMARS systems to Taiwan, which must be authorized by Taiwan’s Legislative Yuan and signed before March 26 to ensure timely delivery of the system, along with other weapon systems. This comes as U.S. pressure for Taiwanese lawmakers to pass a special defense budget have increased over the past weeks, and as fears are growing in the Indo-Pacific that the U.S.’s attention in the Middle East is drawing defensive weapons away from the region.

incidents.title: South Korea invests heavily in American industry
incidents.description: The South Korean National Assembly approved the legislation required to green-light the $350 billion investment in the U.S.’s strategic industries agreed upon last year. Trump had previously threatened to increase tariffs against Seoul for not ratifying the agreement fast enough.

incidents.title: Afghan/Pakistani war continues
incidents.description: The countries have continued to exchange strikes after Pakistan declared “open war” against Afghanistan in late February, with Kabul claiming Pakistani strikes killed four civilians on March 12. The death toll has continued to rise, with U.N. data placing it at 56 killed, while Kabul and Islamabad place the number at 95, in both cases a majority of deaths being civilians. The Chinese ambassador to Pakistan met with Pakistani leadership, conveying strong words from Xi to cease hostilities, resulting in a slight easing of military efforts by Islamabad, according to Pakistani officials.

incidents.title: U.N. says human rights abuses continue in Venezuela
incidents.description: A U.N. fact-finding mission reported no signs of meaningful structural reforms to improve Venezuela’s human rights situation despite the removal of President Nicolás Maduro in January.

incidents.title: Colombia-Venezuela meeting canceled
incidents.description: Venezuela and Colombia announced the cancellation of a meeting between acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez and Colombian President Gustavo Petro on border security and potential gas exports.

incidents.title: Iran proposes conditions for peace
incidents.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian laid out three conditions that Iran requires to end the war with Israel and the United States. Pezeshkian said in a post on social media, “The only way to end this war—ignited by the Zionist regime & US—is recognizing Iran’s legitimate rights, payment of reparations, and firm int’l guarantees against future aggression.”

incidents.title: Jaishankar consults Indonesia on Middle East conflict
incidents.description: External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar discussed the Middle East conflict and its regional implications with Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono.

incidents.title: Russian factory is destroyed by Ukrainian missile
incidents.description: Ukrainian forces used British-provided Storm Shadow missiles to strike a factory in Russia’s Bryansk region that produces missile guidance systems components. Escalation level

incidents.title: US conducts trade investigations into partners
incidents.description: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced on Wednesday that the Trump administration was opening two new trade investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The investigations are probing for forced labor and excess industrial capacity and would target trade with China, the EU, Taiwan, and Mexico among others.

incidents.title: Israel Conducts airstrikes in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel conducted numerous airstrikes in Beirut and across southern Lebanon as the IDF expanded its ground campaign in the south. Hezbollah escalated its bombardment of northern Israel and engaged in clashes with Israeli ground forces. More than 700,000 people have been displaced.

incidents.title: Nepal holds democratic elections
incidents.description: The Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) secured a majority victory in the country’s first elections since last year’s youth-led protests, winning 125 out of 165 parliamentary seats. The party’s victory marks a substantial shift for the country since the abolition of the monarchy in 2008, which marked a period of more pro-China political stances. The RSP was congratulated by representatives from India, China, and the U.S., suggesting a more balanced approach to the country’s relations moving forward

incidents.title: China and North Korean reopen passanger train service
incidents.description: China and North Korea are resuming passenger train service between Beijing and Pyongyang that had previously closed due to Covid six years ago. The move comes as China seeks to increase infrastructural cooperation with North Korea since the leaders of both countries met several times last year.

incidents.title: U.S. seeks extradition of Maduro ally Alex Saab
incidents.description: The United States negotiated the extradition of billionaire businessman Alex Saab, a close associate of former President Nicolás Maduro facing a sealed corruption indictment in Miami.

incidents.title: Iran attacks tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Iran attacked three oil tankers attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz and warned that oil prices could reach more than $200 per barrel. Iranian forces also continued rocket and missile attacks against targets across the Middle East.

incidents.title: Chinese vehicle sales post sharp decline
incidents.description: China’s vehicle sales fell 15.4% year-over-year in February, marking the steepest decline in two years. Domestic demand weakened despite continued growth in vehicle exports.

incidents.title: Putin and Trump hold talks
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone call on March 9 to discuss possible resolutions to the wars in Ukraine and in the Middle East, according to statements from the Kremlin and the White House. The U.S. gave no signal it intended to resume bilateral talks with Ukraine or pursue trilateral talks that had been proposed prior to the start of the U.S./Israeli war in Iran.

incidents.title: US and Israel continue air campaign against Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. and Israel escalated their air campaign inside Iran, conducting the heaviest day of strikes yet on March 10. Part of the ongoing U.S. air campaign is focused on strikes against Iranian naval vessels to prevent Iran from mining the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: Japan deploys new anti-ship missiles
incidents.description: Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara stated Tokyo was readying the first deployment of domestically produced long-range land-to-ship missiles to Camp Kengun in Japan’s southwestern Kumamoto prefecture. Kihara did not provide more details other than the timeline for deployment was slated for the end of the month.

incidents.title: US continues restrictions on Cuba
incidents.description: Trump has signaled that his administration is still pursuing pressure tactics on Cuba, claiming that his plans may include a “friendly takeover” of the government. He also confirmed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was continuing negotiations with the Cuban government and that people involved in the discussions have stated that a possible deal was on the table, one focused on energy and including a possible offramp for President Miguel Diaz-Canel

incidents.title: Canada increases oil production to offset loss from Iran war
incidents.description: LNG Canada in British Columbia has increased its LNG production amid threats to global energy supply from the U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Japan, South Korea, and the Philippines are among the Asian countries that have benefited from LNG Canada's increased exports and production, which have reached almost full capacity at 14 million metric tons per year.

incidents.title: Iran fires missiles against Israel and Gulf states
incidents.description: Iran fired numerous missile salvos against Israel and the Gulf states as Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps vowed to prevent oil exports from the region. U.S. President Donald Trump threatened further escalation if Iran blocked oil shipments.

incidents.title: U.S. destroys Iranian mine-laying vessels
incidents.description: U.S. forces destroyed 16 Iranian mine-laying vessels, according to the U.S. military. U.S. officials said Iran was attempting to mine the Strait of Hormuz to disrupt global oil traffic, while CNN reported that dozens of Iranian-made mines had been laid throughout the strait.

incidents.title: Chinese exports exceed expectations
incidents.description: China’s exports surged 21.8% during the January-February period, far exceeding market forecasts and driven by strong electronics demand. The performance put the country on track for another record trade surplus, barring wider disruption from the Iran war.

incidents.title: Ukraine conducts counteroffensive
incidents.description: Ukrainian forces are engaged in a counteroffensive in Ukraine’s southern Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions according to Ukrainian Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi, who reported the re-capture of at least 285 square kilometers of land previously under Russian occupation.

incidents.title: China plans to build pipelines to Russia
incidents.description: Amidst the Iran war, China included the plan for two natural gas pipelines to import gas from Russia, raising debate on whether the “Power of Siberia 2” pipeline project was being fast tracked, and Russia/China relations growing stronger

incidents.title: South Korea introduces a price cap on oil
incidents.description: Amid soaring oil prices, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed to introduce a price cap on domestic fuel prices

incidents.title: Canada announced it will still allow TikTok
incidents.description: Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly said that the country would allow TikTok to continue operating in Canada after completing a national security review. This comes after Prime Minister Mark Carney visited China to reset relations with Beijing a couple of weeks ago.

incidents.title: Consumer prices rise; factory deflation eases
incidents.description: China’s consumer prices rose at their fastest pace in more than three years while factory deflation moderated further. Economists attributed the increase largely to stronger holiday spending and higher energy prices.

incidents.title: Rupee falls to record low
incidents.description: The Indian rupee fell to a record low and equity markets declined as higher oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict increased concerns over energy imports.

incidents.title: China opposes regime change in Iran
incidents.description: Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi told a news conference that China firmly opposes any efforts to seek regime change in Iran.

incidents.title: Taiwan and Japan discuss collective secruity
incidents.description: Taiwanese Premier Cho Jung-tai visited Japan, as both nations shore up relations in light of ongoing economic pressure by China against Japan for its declared support of Taiwan.

incidents.title: Japan invest in the US
incidents.description: As part of the agreed upon $550 billion investment by Japan into the U.S., Japan Display is looking to potentially play a role in strengthening the U.S. military’s display technologies. These systems have traditionally been reliant on Chinese display technologies, while Japanese manufacturers were largely driven out through fierce competition.

incidents.title: China agress to still hold talks despite Iran war
incidents.description: Despite declaring the U.S.’s actions in Iran as “unacceptable,” China is unlikely to cancel the upcoming summit between President Trump and President Xi, seen largely as an opportunity to maintain the current bilateral relationship without escalating tensions further

incidents.title: Blast at U.S. Embassy may have been terrorism, police say
incidents.description: An overnight explosion caused minor damage to the U.S. embassy in Oslo, with Norwegian police saying the incident may have been an act of terrorism. No injuries were reported.

incidents.title: China advances brain-computer interface plans
incidents.description: A leading Chinese brain-computer interface expert said the technology could enter practical public use in China within three to five years. Beijing elevated brain-computer interfaces to a core future industry in its new five-year plan.

incidents.title: Iran war disrupts global oil prices
incidents.description: The U.S.-Israel war with Iran has caused a major global energy shock, with crude oil price surges, supply disruption, and liquefied natural gas (LNG) volatility. Refinery shutdowns and export restrictions due to the Strait of Hormuz’s closure have begun to impact crude oil processing and regional supplies, causing operational disruptions. The price of crude oil has jumped by 42% to just under $93 per barrel, as of March 13. Oil exports from some of the world's leading producers, such as Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, and the United Arab Emirates, have been threatened.

incidents.title: U.S. gas prices surge 14%
incidents.description: Average U.S. gasoline prices rose to $3.41 per gallon after crude oil prices rose to their highest levels since 2023. As U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran continue, oil exports from the region have been curtailed.

incidents.title: Xi warns military over corruption
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping warned the military against protecting corrupt or disloyal officials. Xi made the remarks to People’s Liberation Army and People’s Armed Police Force delegates during China’s annual parliamentary session.

incidents.title: Trump fires DHS head Kristi Noem
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump fired U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem and announced U.S. Sen. Markwayne Mullin as her replacement.

incidents.title: China seeks Hormuz shipping access
incidents.description: China held talks with Iran to secure safe passage for crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The discussions came as the U.S.-Israeli war disrupted one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

incidents.title: Japan wants to hold military drills with US
incidents.description: Japan has been in talks with NATO to potentially take part in the alliance’s Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) initiative, possibly allowing Japanese startups to use NATO’s testing infrastructure for military and dual use technologies, including AI and quantum computing, marking the first non-NATO country to make use of the program.

incidents.title: China Increases defense budget
incidents.description: China held its annual National People’s Congress (NPC), or “two sessions,” during which the Chinese Communist Party gave its final approval for the country's next Five-Year Plan. The plan includes a 7% increase in military spending, with Chinese Premier Li Qiang vowing to crack down on Taiwanese separatist activities.

incidents.title: China stops military exersises
incidents.description: Taiwanese authorities reported a halt in Chinese military activity around the island for the past week, marking a substantial break from past years. Reuters further reports that military activity has fallen 46.5% compared with the same period last year. Possible reasons for this may be the upcoming Trump-Xi summit, diplomatic posturing by Beijing, or a lack of a functioning command structure following recent purges within the Chinese government

incidents.title: Talks to be help between Ukraine/Russia/US
incidents.description: Trilateral negotiations among Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S. that had been set to take place in Abu Dhabi this month were postponed due to the regional fallout of the war in Iran. While both Istanbul and Geneva had been floated as possible alternative meeting locations, Zelenskyy said there was a lack of "necessary signals” from the U.S. that negotiations should resume at this time.

incidents.title: China increases it's military budget
incidents.description: China held its annual National People’s Congress (NPC), or “two sessions,” during which the Chinese Communist Party gave its final approval for the country's next Five-Year Plan. The plan includes a 7% increase in military spending, with Chinese Premier Li Qiang vowing to crack down on Taiwanese separatist activities.

incidents.title: Japan holds talks with NATO
incidents.description: Japan has been in talks with NATO to potentially take part in the alliance’s Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) initiative, possibly allowing Japanese startups to use NATO’s testing infrastructure for military and dual use technologies, including AI and quantum computing, marking the first non-NATO country to make use of the program.

incidents.title: China ends military activity around Taiwan
incidents.description: Taiwanese authorities reported a halt in Chinese military activity around the island for the past week, marking a substantial break from past years. Reuters further reports that military activity has fallen 46.5% compared with the same period last year. Possible reasons for this may be the upcoming Trump-Xi summit, diplomatic posturing by Beijing, or a lack of a functioning command structure following recent purges within the Chinese government

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela diplomatic relations restored
incidents.description: The United States and Venezuela agreed to restore diplomatic relations, marking a major shift after years of hostility between the two countries.

incidents.title: Iranian drone hits airport in Azerbaijan
incidents.description: An Iranian drone struck the airport in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic of Azerbaijan. The Azerbaijani government condemned the attack and called for accountability from Iran.

incidents.title: China lowers growth target
incidents.description: China lowered its 2026 gross domestic product growth target to 4.5% to 5%, the lowest target since 1991. Officials cited weak domestic demand and a volatile international trade environment.

incidents.title: Natural gas supplies tighten
incidents.description: State-run GAIL warned it could reduce natural gas supplies after disruptions to liquefied natural gas imports from Qatar affected deliveries.

incidents.title: Modi opens Raisina Dialogue
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Raisina Dialogue while External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar held meetings with counterparts from several countries.

incidents.title: Ukraine deploys advisors to gulf states
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced he is deploying Ukrainian military and intelligence specialists to assist Gulf states defend against Iranian missile and drone strikes. The U.S. and at least one Gulf nation are currently negotiating the purchase of Ukrainian-made

incidents.title: Russia threatens to cut off gas for Europe
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin publicly floated the idea of cutting off Russian gas exports to Europe to take advantage of expected shortages of liquefied natural gas due to the war in Iran, to take advantage of expected shortages of liquified natural gas due to the war in Iran by diverting those supplies to the open market..

incidents.title: US oil drillers face shortages due to Iran conflict
incidents.description: US fracking industry is facing a new face of outages and shortages as a result of Iranian closure of strait of Hormuz

incidents.title: Iran attacks Gulf states
incidents.description: Iran retaliated against the U.S.-Israeli attacks by striking energy and civilian infrastructure in Gulf states, as well as U.S. military bases and diplomatic posts across the region.

incidents.title: Hezbollah fires missiles at Israel
incidents.description: Hezbollah fired rockets into Israeli territory on March 3, prompting Israel to bomb Beirut and escalate the scope and intensity of its ongoing air campaign across Lebanon. Israeli ground forces also seized additional Lebanese territory south of the Litani River.

incidents.title: Iran fires missiles at Turkey
incidents.description: NATO air defenses intercepted an Iranian ballistic missile that had entered Turkish airspace on March 4

incidents.title: Nvidia stops selling advanced chips to China
incidents.description: Top U.S. chipmaker Nvidia has halted production of its H200 artificial intelligence chip, which had been approved by U.S. regulators for sale to China. The company instead has reportedly shifted production at its facilities at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) to its new Vera Rubin AI platform. This move comes as both Washington and Beijing have signaled that the U.S. may tighten export controls of the H200, with U.S. lawmakers debating a possible limit of sales to individual Chinese companies to 75,000 chips apiece. Meanwhile, Chinese-based Huawei Technologies is set to unveil a new supercomputer model that reportedly equals Nvidia’s hardware. The recent approval of China’s next Five-Year Plan, which emphasizes accelerating efforts toward tech independence, may also have factored into the decision.

incidents.title: US intiates Kurdish insurgency in Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. is considering initiating a CIA-backed Kurdish insurgency inside Iran. The purpose of the proposed campaign, according to an unnamed U.S. official cited by various media outlets, would be to create conditions for a popular uprising against the Iranian government

incidents.title: US lifts some oil restrictions on Cuba
incidents.description: The Trump administration has made exceptions to its oil embargo of Cuba, allowing private businesses to buy Venezuelan oil, as long as it does not end up going to government-owned entities. Small businesses and humanitarian organizations will be among the entities permitted to request oil deliveries, potentially stabilizing the deteriorating humanitarian situation on the island. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called for a reorganization of the island’s economy, to which the private sector plays only a minor role

incidents.title: Iranian navy blocks strait of Hormuz
incidents.description: Iranian naval forces have effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, with a senior IRGC official threatening that any ship attempting to navigate the waterway will be fired upon.

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela gold export agreement signed
incidents.description: Venezuela’s state-owned mining company signed a multimillion-dollar agreement to sell up to 1,000 kilograms of gold for delivery to U.S. markets.

incidents.title: U.S., Venezuela talk energy, mineral cooperation
incidents.description: U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum met with acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez to discuss cooperation on the country’s energy and mineral sectors.

incidents.title: US torpedos Iranian ship
incidents.description: A U.S. submarine torpedoed an Iranian destroyer in the Indian Ocean off the Sri Lankan coast on March 4.

incidents.title: US congress does not pass bill to limit Iran war
incidents.description: Congress rejected a pair of bipartisan resolutions that would have limited Trump’s authority to continue with the war in Iran without congressional oversight. A resolution introduced in the Senate was rejected in a 5347 vote a day after the House shot down a similar measure that could have halted further U.S. military action in Iran without congressional approval. Separately, Trump announced he has fired Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem following several days of questioning by both Republican and Democratic lawmakers. 3 WEEKLY FORECAST MONITOR NEW LINES INSTITUTE Trump nominated U.S. Sen. Markwayne Mullin, a Republican representing Oklahoma, as her successor.

incidents.title: Senate blocks effort to restrain Trump Iran war powers
incidents.description: The U.S. Senate rejected legislation aimed at limiting U.S. President Donald Trump’s authority to continue military action against Iran.

incidents.title: Top Politburo officials absent from political meetings
incidents.description: Two senior Chinese officials, Gen. Zhang Youxia and Ma Xingrui, were absent from China’s top annual political meetings amid an ongoing anti-corruption campaign.

incidents.title: Gulf gas shortages reduce fertilizer production
incidents.description: Disruptions to natural gas supplies from the Gulf reduced output at Indian fertilizer plants as feedstock shortages affected urea production.

incidents.title: US considers limiting Tencent in US
incidents.description: he Trump administration is weighing options to limit Chinese company Tencent’s stakes in major U.S. video game groups, citing national security risks, as the U.S. seeks to bolster its leverage ahead of March’s summit.

incidents.title: US treatens Cuban leader
incidents.description: Federal prosecutors reportedly have warned Venezuela’s interim leader, Delcy Rodriguez, that she could face U.S. prosecution if she does not continue to comply with the Trump administration’s demands, Reuters reported. U.S. government officials have denied the report. Rodriguez, who has not been charged or indicted, could face corruption and money laundering charges related to the handling of funds from state-owned oil company PDVSA between 2021 and 2025, the report said. Several members of Venezuela’s interim government are under U.S. indictment. One of the key U.S. demands of Rodriguez is to continue to help prosecute other high-ranking Venezuelan government officials.

incidents.title: US-Middle east oil imports drop due to Iran war
incidents.description: Disruptions caused by the U.S.-Israel war on Iran have caused oil and natural gas production stoppages in Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar. Iraq, the second-largest OPEC+ producer, has trimmed production by half to 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) in light of storage and transportation bottlenecks. Saudi Aramco’s Ras Tanura refinery, capable of processing more than 500,000 bpd of crude, was shut down after a drone strike. Qatar, which provides about 20% of global liquefied natural gas supplies, halted production due to attacks on LNG installations. The Strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of global oil and LNG supplies transit, was closed amid Iranian attacks against shipping using the waterway.

incidents.title: India looks for alternative energy sources
incidents.description: India is looking for alternative energy supplies due to the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, through which the country normally imports approximately 50% of its crude oil supply. The government’s strategic reserve is estimated to hold a 25-day supply of oil. Indian LNG reserves, meanwhile, may be exhausted in only a few days after Qatar, its largest supplier, stopped production as its facilities suffered damage from retaliatory Iranian attacks. Up to 85% of India’s LNG imports pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

incidents.title: US kills Iranian leader
incidents.description: The U.S. and Israel began a war with Iran, killing Khamenei and numerous senior officials from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in a sustained air campaign that began Feb. 28.

incidents.title: EU attempts peace talks with Iran
incidents.description: The EU will pursue “all diplomatic efforts” to reduce tensions in the Middle East, according to EU Commission spokesman Anouar El Anouni.

incidents.title: US considers limiting tencent in US
incidents.description: The Trump administration is weighing options to limit Chinese company Tencent’s stakes in major U.S. video game groups, citing national security risks, as the U.S. seeks to bolster its leverage ahead of March’s summit.

incidents.description: Defense secretary Pete Hegseth has ended its military contract with AI company Anthropic. The move comes shortly after the AI start up refused to create a AI model that could operate military assets without direct human oversight.

incidents.description: Trump tells Delcy Rodriguez she may face prosecution if she does not comply with US demands

incidents.description: The Trump administration is preparing a potential criminal indictment against acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez as part of efforts to increase leverage over Caracas, Reuters reported.

incidents.title: Venezuela oil exports surge
incidents.description: Venezuela significantly increased oil exports in February, shipping about twice as many barrels as in January after the Trump administration took control of the country’s crude sales.

incidents.title: Iran floats peace deal with US
incidents.description: Iranian intelligence agencies reached out to the CIA through indirect backchannels to negotiate an end to the war a day after the U.S. and Israel began a high intensity air campaign inside Iran, according to The New York Times. White House and U.S. intelligence officials declined to comment.

incidents.title: U.S. shale producers unable to offset Iran war oil shock
incidents.description: U.S. shale oil producers warned they could not increase production quickly enough to address supply disruptions caused by the Iran conflict, with industry leaders saying meaningful output increases would take months. Producers said high prices alone were insufficient to justify rapid drilling expansion given cost concerns and depleted drilling inventory.

incidents.title: China opens annual Two Sessions
incidents.description: Thousands of delegates gathered in Beijing for China’s annual Two Sessions political meetings. Leaders were expected to finalize a new five-year plan focused on technological self-sufficiency, trade, and economic growth.

incidents.title: India and Japan discuss rare earth cooperation
incidents.description: India and Japan opened discussions on joint rare earth exploration projects in Rajasthan as both countries sought to diversify supply chains away from China.

incidents.title: Chip assembly plant opens in Gujarat
incidents.description: Kaynes Semicon opened a semiconductor assembly and testing facility in Gujarat, expanding India's domestic semiconductor manufacturing capacity.

incidents.title: US reps to visit China
incidents.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will meet Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng next week in preparation for the Trump-Xi summit. Both sides confirmed that the summit is still on schedule despite the war with Iran

incidents.title: India and Canada sign trade deal
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney signed multiple new trade and cooperation deals in the Indo-Pacific. In talks with India, both countries pledged to boost cooperation on trade and supply chains, marking a formal reset of their relations after several years of tension. Carney also signed a deal with Australia on critical minerals and vowed to boost “middle power” cooperation

incidents.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will meet Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng next week in preparation for the Trump-Xi summit. Both sides confirmed that the summit is still on schedule despite the war with Iran.

incidents.title: Ukraine takes 9 towns in ongoing operation
incidents.description: Ukrainian forces have recaptured at least nine settlements in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region during an ongoing counteroffensive, Zelenskyy said.

incidents.title: India and Canada sign trade deal
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney signed multiple new trade and cooperation deals in the Indo-Pacific. In talks with India, both countries pledged to boost cooperation on trade and supply chains, marking a formal reset of their relations after several years of tension. Carney also signed a deal with Australia on critical minerals and vowed to boost “middle power” cooperation

incidents.title: Huawei unveils artificial intelligence supercomputer
incidents.description: Huawei demonstrated its Atlas 950 SuperPoD artificial intelligence supercomputer overseas for the first time, claiming it could rival Nvidia’s offerings. The system links thousands of Huawei Ascend processors for artificial intelligence computing.

incidents.title: India and Canada relaunch trade negotiations
incidents.description: India and Canada agreed to revive trade negotiations and reached a uranium supply understanding as part of a broader improvement in bilateral relations.

incidents.title: China commissions new guided missile ships
incidents.description: Open-source photographs have revealed the People’s Liberation Army’s navy has possibly commissioned two new Type 055 guided-missile destroyer into the East Sea Fleet, indicating possible new ambitions for a “blue water navy” capable of operating beyond the first island chain.

incidents.title: China lauches new naval assets
incidents.description: Open-source photographs have revealed the People’s Liberation Army’s navy has possibly commissioned two new Type 055 guided-missile destroyer into the East Sea Fleet, indicating possible new ambitions for a “blue water navy” capable of operating beyond the first island chain.

incidents.title: FBI investigates Austin shooter
incidents.description: U.S. authorities investigated whether the gunman who killed two people and wounded 14 others in Austin’s Sixth Street entertainment district was motivated by the U.S. military campaign in Iran. Police killed the suspect at the scene.

incidents.title: U.S. strikes expand across Iran
incidents.description: U.S. Central Command said U.S. forces had attacked more than 1,000 targets across Iran since the conflict began on Feb. 28, 2026. The strikes hit military sites, strategic bases, communications systems and command units, while the United States said three servicemen died and five more were wounded in combat.

incidents.title: China condemns strikes on Iran
incidents.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi condemned the U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran and called for an immediate ceasefire and renewed negotiations. Wang also criticized the killing of Iran’s leader and efforts to pursue regime change.

incidents.title: Pakistan/Afghanistan conflict continues
incidents.description: The Afgan/Pakistani conflict shows little signs of stopping as bombing continues into it's second week.

incidents.title: China monitors AUKAS exersises
incidents.description: A Chinese Ministry of Defense spokesperson stated the country's forces were on “high alert” in the South China Sea following last week’s U.S-led drills with Australia, the Philippines, and Japan.

incidents.title: China condems US strike on Iran
incidents.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran “unacceptable” as the Chinese Communist Party spoke with several governments, including Russia’s, and offered itself as a peace mediator. China relies on Middle Eastern oil supplies, which have been disrupted by the ongoing war. The attacks on regional export infrastructure puts pressure on China, raising the stakes ahead of the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at scheduled for the end of March.

incidents.title: Pakistan declares war on Afghanistan
incidents.description: Fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan continued following last week’s declaration of “open war” by Islamabad. Attempts by Saudi Arabia and Qatar, among others, to mediate the conflict have been unsuccessful. The Afghan government reported a failed attack by Pakistani forces targeting Bagram air base, while Pakistan continued an airstrike campaign against targets in Kabul. Separately, Pakistani forces have been deployed outside U.S. diplomatic facilities in light of ongoing strikes against Iran

incidents.title: US eases restrictions on Cuba
incidents.description: The Trump administration has made exceptions to its oil embargo of Cuba, allowing private businesses to buy Venezuelan oil, as long as it does not end up going to government-owned entities. Small businesses and humanitarian organizations will be among the entities permitted to request oil deliveries, potentially stabilizing the deteriorating humanitarian situation on the island. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called for a reorganization of the island’s economy, to which the private sector plays only a minor role

incidents.title: Russia calls for peace in Iran
incidents.description: The Russian Foreign Ministry called the U.S./Israeli war in Iran a “preplanned and unprovoked” act of aggression and called for de-escalation. Putin characterized the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in a targeted strike as an “assassination.” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow is in “constant contact” with Iranian leadership, although Moscow has not taken action to aid its ally in Tehran

incidents.title: China on "high alert" after US drills
incidents.description: A Chinese Ministry of Defense spokesperson stated the country's forces were on “high alert” in the South China Sea following last week’s U.S-led drills with Australia, the Philippines, and Japan.

incidents.title: China condems US strikes on Iran
incidents.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran “unacceptable” as the Chinese Communist Party spoke with several governments, including Russia’s, and offered itself as a peace mediator. China relies on Middle Eastern oil supplies, which have been disrupted by the ongoing war. The attacks on regional export infrastructure puts pressure on China, raising the stakes ahead of the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at scheduled for the end of March.

incidents.title: Chinese military raises South China Sea alert
incidents.description: China’s Ministry of National Defense said the People’s Liberation Army remained on high alert in the South China Sea following joint patrols by the United States, Australia, Japan, and the Philippines. Beijing warned that outside attempts to stir tensions would fail.

incidents.title: India issues Kuwait security advisory
incidents.description: India issued a travel advisory urging its nationals in Kuwait to exercise caution as regional security conditions deteriorated.

incidents.title: Pakistan declares war on Afghanistan
incidents.description: Pakistan has declared “open war” against Afghanistan, after it conducted a series of airstrikes against alleged terrorist targets against the country, killing at least 20 people including women and children. The Taliban’s defense ministry condemned the attack, stating it was conducted against civilian areas in Nangarhar and Paktika provinces. Pakistan stated it had previously identified and confirmed seven terrorist encampments linked to Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and Islamic State-Khorasan, both of which had claimed responsibility for recent attacks in Pakistan. A Taliban government spokesperson has announced it would carry out “large-scale offensive operations” against the Pakistani military along the countries’ border.

incidents.title: U.S.-Venezuela tanker seizure effort expands
incidents.description: The U.S. Justice Department filed a complaint to seize a sanctioned tanker and nearly 2 million barrels of oil intercepted off Venezuela’s coast, marking the first formal move to take ownership of vessels detained under the crackdown.

incidents.title: Trump tells agencies to halt using Anthropic
incidents.description: After Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei made clear that he would not agree to allow the Pentagon to use his company’s AI products for mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons, U.S. President Donald Trump ordered administration agencies to cut ties with the company. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said he designated the company a supply chain risk and barred defense contractors from using Anthropic AI.

incidents.title: China removes military lawmakers
incidents.description: China removed nine military representatives from the National People’s Congress as President Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption campaign continued. The officials included several senior commanders.

incidents.title: China holds drills in the South China Sea
incidents.description: China conducted a patrol in the South China Sea in response to joint military drills by the U.S. and the Philippines, accompanied for the first time by Japanese troops.

incidents.title: North Korea makes offer to US
incidents.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un stated that if the U.S. recognizes North Korea as a nuclear power on equal footing and withdraws its “hostile policy” against Pyongyang, there should be no reason for the countries not to get along

incidents.title: US and Iran hold nuclear talks
incidents.description: The U.S. and Iran held a third round of indirect negotiations in Geneva on Feb. 26. Iranian officials insisted that only nuclear issues are on the table and that Iran will not compromise on its conventional weapons programs.

incidents.title: Cuba kills 4 Americans in speedboat
incidents.description: The Cuban coast guard opened fire against a U.S.-registered speedboat that entered its territorial waters off the northern coast, killing four of the 10 passengers. The U.S. government said the individuals on the boat were Cuban nationals in exile with previous criminal histories. Russia, a Cuban ally, accused the U.S. of provoking the incident, but the Trump administration denied involvement in or knowledge of it, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio stating the U.S. would conduct its own independent investigation before commenting further.

incidents.title: Venezuelan oil resale licenses approved
incidents.description: The U.S. Treasury Department said companies could seek licenses to resell Venezuelan oil to Cuba’s private sector, a step intended to help ease the island’s fuel shortages.

incidents.title: Hungary send troops to boarder
incidents.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban deployed soldiers to protect energy infrastructure after accusing Ukraine of planning sabotage operations in Hungarian territory

incidents.title: Poll shows support for deportation, not ICE tactics
incidents.description: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 61% of Americans supported deporting unauthorized immigrants, including 92% of Republicans and 35% of Democrats. The same poll found broad disapproval of the administration’s enforcement tactics, including the use of masked agents during immigration operations.

incidents.title: India and Israel deepen defense cooperation
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli officials agreed to expand defense cooperation and continue working toward a bilateral free trade agreement during Modi's visit to Israel.

incidents.title: US warns of small reserves of rare earth elements from China
incidents.description: U.S. aerospace and semiconductor firms have warned of dwindling rare earth supplies, particularly of yttrium and scandium, despite China announcing its resumption of rare earth exports in October 2025.

incidents.title: US data centers may cause power disruptions
incidents.description: U.S. electrical infrastructures' inability to keep up with large-scale AI data center spending may slow U.S. tech companies’ AI dominance. Aspirations for the advancement of artificial intelligence in the U.S. may be limited by delays in grid expansion, grid capacity limits, generation shortages, and regulatory restrictions. PJM Interconnection, the largest U.S. power grid operator, warned of power supply deficits over the next few decades due to demand increases. By 2027, the U.S. system may lack capacity and reserves, causing blackouts. AI companies are shifting their focus to independent power generation (natural gas, renewable energy, and nuclear) to keep up with the boom.

incidents.title: DRC withholds shipments of cobalt to international markets
incidents.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has considerably agitated international markets by imposing restrictions on cobalt exports in response to an oversupply and falling prices. The DRC, which produces 70% of the world’s cobalt, set new cobalt export quotas at 96,600 metric tons annually for 2026 and 2027, 48% lower than the amount set for 2024. The DRC’s aim is to increase global market control, improve local value creation, and reduce the low-cost supply.

incidents.title: Ukraine holds talks with US and Russia
incidents.description: Zelenskyy expressed optimism that a trilateral summit among the U.S., Ukraine, and Russia that is set for March will pave the way for an eventual meeting of himself, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S. President Donald Trump

incidents.title: CIA seeks Iranian informants online
incidents.description: Central Intelligence Agency social media accounts posted apparent instructions in Farsi for how Iranians could safely contact the agency to share information. The recruitment effort came as U.S. forces continued to build up in the Gulf of Oman.

incidents.title: Nvidia has yet to sell H200 chips to China
incidents.description: A U.S. Commerce Department official told a House committee hearing on export controls that Nvidia had not sold any H200 artificial intelligence chips to Chinese customers.

incidents.title: Russia accuses US of escalating war
incidents.description: Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peksov said “direct intervention” by the United States and European nations in Ukraine has turned the war into a wider conflict between Russia and Western nations

incidents.title: US threatens Iran with attack
incidents.description: The U.S. continued to threaten direct military intervention in Iran amid a significant buildup of military assets in the region. Iran warned that even a limited operation from the U.S. would be met with a "ferocious" response.

incidents.title: Iran buys anti-ship munitions from China
incidents.description: Iranian officials worked to close an arms deal with China for the acquisition of advanced anti-ship missiles, according to unnamed sources cited by Reuters.

incidents.title: Israel threatens Lebanon
incidents.description: Israeli officials warned the Lebanese government that it would strike civilian infrastructure in Lebanon, including Beirut’s international airport, if Hezbollah should attack Israel in the event of a war between the U.S. and Iran.

incidents.title: Mass protests in Iran
incidents.description: Student protests resumed across Iranian university campuses on Feb. 21 for the first time since the Iranian government violently suppressed mass nationwide protests in January. Basij forces clashed with the protesters in response, although the current reaction from the Iranian government appears to be limited in comparison to January, according to early reports.

incidents.title: US creates social media profiles to undermine Iranian power
incidents.description: The CIA is conducting a Farsi-language social media campaign aimed at encouraging defections inside the Iranian government, which includes instructions on how to access secure virtual communication channels with the U.S. intelligence agency.

incidents.title: China adds ban on certain rare earth elements to Japan
incidents.description: China has implemented an export ban on 20 “dual-use” rare earth materials to Japan, following up on an announcement made last month, as well as adding a further 20 materials on a “watch list” that will slow trade. This marks the latest escalation in China’s feud with Japan over the latter’s relationship with Taiwan.

incidents.title: German chancellor travels to China
incidents.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met with Chinese Premier Li Qiang and Xi, with both sides vowing to strengthen economic cooperation and China vowing to purchase 120 Airbus aircraft from Germany

incidents.title: Cuban security personnel leave Venezuela
incidents.description: Hundreds of Cuban security personnel, including soldiers, intelligence agents, and bodyguards, began departing Caracas after decades of deployment under the Caracas-Havana alliance.

incidents.title: US Supreme Court rules Trump tariffs illegal
incidents.description: Following last week’s decision by the Supreme Court to invalidate the “liberation day” tariffs, Trump signed an executive order imposing a flat tariff of 10% on all global trading partners, saying that it was required in order to address the trade deficit the U.S. has with other countries. Trade data has shown that despite the tariffs, the trade deficit rose last year by 2.1% compared to 2024. Trump invoked Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act to impose the current tariffs, which are set to expire after 150 days without congressional approval.

incidents.title: Trump global tariffs take effect
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump’s new 10% global tariffs took effect after the Supreme Court blocked many of his broader import taxes, with the administration invoking Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act to impose the levy for up to 150 days without congressional approval. Trump later said he could raise the tariff to 15%, though no formal directive had been issued.

incidents.title: Iran nears Chinese missile deal
incidents.description: Sources familiar with talks between Iran and China said the two countries were nearing a deal for Chinese-made supersonic antiship missiles to be sold to Iran. The sources said the negotiations began more than two years earlier and continued as U.S. forces built up near Iranian waters.

incidents.title: EU imposes sanction on Russia
incidents.description: The EU imposed sanctions against eight individuals in Russia for human rights.

incidents.title: US withdraws from Syria
incidents.description: U.S. forces are conducting a “conditions-based” withdrawal from bases in Syria as a security handover is underway between the U.S. military and the Syrian army. The withdrawal is expected to take at least one month.

incidents.title: Ukraine regains land in assualt
incidents.description: Ukraine has reclaimed 800 square kilometres of territory from Russian forces in the southeastern Dnipropetrovsk region since the end of January, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

incidents.title: Taiwan holds new military exerises
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Huadong Defense Command will conduct live-fire exercises March 24-27 in Taitung County, with intended aims being improving command skills, firepower coordination, and airspace control measures.

incidents.title: US restricts Nvidia chips to go to China
incidents.description: The U.S. assistant secretary for export enforcement, David Peters, acknowledged that none of Nvidia’s advanced H200 chips have yet been sold to Chinese customers, citing guardrails in the export process

incidents.title: Large scale violence breaks out in Mexico
incidents.description: Violence erupted across multiple regions of Mexico following a U.S.-assisted operation by Mexican armed forces, resulting in the death of the leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), Nemesio “El Mencho” Rubén Oseguera Cervantes. More than 70 people died during the operation to capture him, and following his death, cartel members attacked multiple infrastructure sites, including an airport in Jalisco, with intervention by armed forces resulting in the death of 25 members of the Mexican national guard and 30 suspected CJNG members. The cartel warned of further violence.

incidents.title: Venezuela gives amnesty to 2,200 people
incidents.description: About 2,200 people were released from Venezuelan prisons or had legal restrictions lifted under a new amnesty law, ruling party lawmaker Jorge Arreaza said.

incidents.title: Armed man killed outside Mar-a-Lago
incidents.description: Secret Service agents fatally shot a man discovered within the secure perimeter of U.S. President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort in Palm Beach, Florida. The man, later identified as Tucker Martin of North Carolina, was found with a shotgun and gas can.

incidents.title: Iran campus protests spark police clashes
incidents.description: Ongoing protests at several Iranian universities led to skirmishes with police. The unrest occurred as the United States continued its military buildup in the Gulf of Oman and both governments remained in talks over Iran's nuclear program.

incidents.title: China less likely to purchase U.S. soybeans
incidents.description: Analysts said China appeared less likely to complete another major purchase of U.S. soybeans following the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision on tariffs. The outlook reduced expectations for expanded agricultural trade between the two countries.

incidents.title: Ukraine investigates explosion in Lviv
incidents.description: Zelenskyy said a Security Service of Ukraine investigation into a Feb. 22 improvised explosive device attack in Lviv that killed one person and injured 25 was a sabotage operation orchestrated by Russian intelligence.

incidents.title: Venezuelan foreign minister demands U.S. release Maduro
incidents.description: Venezuelan Foreign Minister Yvan Gil demanded at the U.N. Human Rights Council that the United States immediately release former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and first lady Cilia Flores, framing their abduction as a political abduction.

incidents.title: U.S. halts tariff collections after Supreme Court ruling
incidents.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection said it would stop collecting tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act following the Supreme Court’s ruling that the duties were illegal. The customs agency said it would disable all tariff codes associated with Trump’s prior IEEPA-related orders.

incidents.title: Australia sails ship through Taiwan strait
incidents.description: Australia sailed an Anzac-class frigate through the Taiwan Strait in a freedom of navigation operation.

incidents.title: Iran university protests continue
incidents.description: Antigovernment protests continued at universities across Iran after beginning in January. BBC footage showed a protest march moving through the campus of Sharif University of Technology in Tehran and later showed a skirmish between protesters and government supporters.

incidents.title: Australian warship transits Taiwan Strait
incidents.description: An Australian naval frigate sailed through the Taiwan Strait, prompting monitoring by the Chinese military. Beijing reiterated its claim over the waterway and has frequently objected to foreign naval transits.

incidents.title: United States signals temporary tariff on India
incidents.description: The White House indicated India would face a temporary 10% tariff after the U.S. Supreme Court invalidated emergency tariffs previously imposed by the Trump administration.

incidents.title: US Supreme Court rules Trump tariffs illegal
incidents.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the International Emergency Power Act (IEEPA) under which the Trump administration imposed its “Liberation Day” tariffs against most of the U.S.’s global partners, did not grant the president authority to do so. This marks a significant loss for the administration’s foreign and trade policy strategy.

incidents.title: Trump to travel to China
incidents.description: The White House confirmed that Trump will travel to China from March 31 to April 2 to meet with Xi, where talks on trade are expected to be at the front of the agenda following the U.S. Supreme Court’s annulation of reciprocal tariffs last week.

incidents.title: Modi holds bilateral meetings during artificial intelligence summit
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met multiple foreign leaders on the sidelines of the India AI Impact Summit to discuss technology, investment, and broader cooperation.

incidents.title: Moldova and Ukarine investigate assassination
incidents.description: Moldovan law enforcement officials announced a joint investigation alongside their Ukrainian counterparts of ongoing assassination plots by Russia’s FSB intelligence agency against prominent Ukrainian officials

incidents.title: US-Indonesian trade deal signed
incidents.description: The U.S. signed a new trade deal with Indonesia that would set U.S. tariffs on Indonesian imports at 19%, 13 points lower that current rates, as well as grant tariff exemptions on several products, including palm oil.

incidents.title: India opens MILAN 2026 naval exercise
incidents.description: Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated the multinational MILAN 2026 naval exercise at Visakhapatnam with participation from dozens of navies.

incidents.title: India targets domestic rare earth production
incidents.description: Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy said India aimed to begin domestic production of rare-earth permanent magnets by the end of 2026. The initiative was intended to reduce dependence on foreign suppliers for a strategic technology input.

incidents.title: India hosts artificial intelligence summit
incidents.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi and promoted India as a leader in global artificial intelligence governance. The event brought together foreign leaders and technology executives.

incidents.title: Algeria opens new pipeline to EU
incidents.description: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced that construction would begin on the long-delayed the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP). The 4,200-kilometer pipeline, when completed, would have a total capacity to transport 30 billion cubic meters of natural gas per year. The strategically significant infrastructure project will boost regional and continental energy connectivity. It will connect Algeria, which serves as a gas export hub to Europe, through Niger to gas fields in Nigeria, the source of production. The pipeline would help Europe meet gas demand as it continues to diversify away from Russian supplies after the latter’s invasion of Ukraine.
