The pipeline could meet 7 to 10% of EU gas consumption and diversify the Southern Corridor.

incidents.title: Ukraine sanctions Belarussian President
incidents.description: Ukraine unveiled a new round of sanctions against Belarussian President Aleksandr Lukashenko that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as retaliation for "facilitating the killing of Ukrainians.

incidents.title: German chancellor travels to China
incidents.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will travel to China next week, where he stated he will aim to secure “strategic partnerships” with Beijing.

incidents.title: AI company opens new data center in US
incidents.description: Green energy company Zeo Energy Corp and AI data center developer Creekstone Energy Co. have signed a memorandum of understanding regarding the construction of 280 megawatts of solar and long-duration storage capacity to supply Creekstone's Millard County data center development. When complete, the data center campus in Utah will be one of the largest in the U.S. with an estimated capacity of 10 gigawatts. The campus will be powered by multiple energy sources, integrating solar and storage (molten salt or compressed CO2 systems) with a natural gas-fired power plant and next-generation nuclear power.

incidents.title: Russia and Iran hold naval drills
incidents.description: Russia and Iran announced joint naval drills in the Gulf of Oman and the Indian Ocean this week

incidents.title: Japan joins US military exercises
incidents.description: Japan will join the bilateral U.S.- and Philippines-led Salaknib military exercises, sending 300 elite troops to take part in the annual drills. The move comes amid rising tensions between China and Japan as Tokyo seeks to increase its defensive readiness.

incidents.title: US builds up forces for impending attack on Iran
incidents.description: The U.S. continued its military buildup in preparation for a possible sustained bombing campaign against Iran. U.S. President Donald Trump made numerous threats of intervention against the Iranian government.

incidents.title: International Monetary Fund urges China to cut subsidies
incidents.description: The International Monetary Fund urged China to reduce state subsidies for industry, arguing that support for key sectors remained unusually high. The fund estimated subsidies equaled about 4% of China’s gross domestic product.

incidents.title: Radio Free Asia resumes China broadcasts
incidents.description: Radio Free Asia resumed broadcasting into China after funding cuts previously forced the outlet to halt operations.

incidents.title: Ukraine aquires German made drones
incidents.description: Ukraine’s HUR intelligence agency claimed Russia is acquiring German-made parts for its drone supply through a complex sanctions evasion scheme in Europe that involves front companies and third countries.

incidents.title: Hezbollah rejects disarm proposal
incidents.description: Hezbollah rejected a disarmament proposal by the Lebanese government, which called for the Iranian-backed militant group to disarm within four months.

incidents.title: US deploys new missile systems to the Philippines
incidents.description: The U.S. unveiled plans to deploy additional missile systems to the Philippines despite warnings from China. The U.S. had deployed its mid-range Typhon missile systems to the Philippines in 2024, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

incidents.title: Taiwan discusses budget crisis amid US pressure
incidents.description: Taiwan’s top lawmakers have pushed deliberations on its special defense budget to the top of the agenda following pressure from U.S. lawmakers who expressed concern about the slow pace of deliberations.

incidents.title: US exports to China fall by 8 percent
incidents.description: Trade data from the Port of Los Angeles shows that exports to China fell 8% in January to reach its lowest monthly output in the past three years.

incidents.title: US accuses China of conducting nuclear tests
incidents.description: Assistant Secretary of State Christopher Yeaw accused China of conducting undisclosed nuclear tests, citing reports of an “explosion” near the Lop Nor test grounds in Western China in 2020. The Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty Organization said there was insufficient data to properly assess the nature of the blast.

incidents.title: Car bomb kill 11
incidents.description: The Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan militant group claimed responsibility for a vehicle-borne attack that killed 11 security personnel and one child at an army base in the country’s northwest. This follows an attack by the Islamic State earlier this month that killed 30 at a mosque in Islamabad, leading to speculation of renewed terrorist threats on multiple fronts

incidents.title: Russian forces encircle Pokrovsk
incidents.description: Russian forces north of the key Ukrainian logistics hub of Pokrovsk are intensifying their efforts to encircle the city, according to reports from the Ukrainian army

incidents.title: Ukraine and Russian talks end without result
incidents.description: Two days of direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine in Geneva ended inconclusively on Feb. 18. Zelenskyy described the results of the U.S.-mediated summit as insufficient, noting that progress was made over the monitoring mechanism of a potential ceasefire but not over the future control of the Donbas region. Zelenskyy reiterated that Ukraine will not cede land it currently holds and stated that another round of talks is currently being scheduled. U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said there was “meaningful progress” and senior Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky described the talks as “difficult but businesslike.”

incidents.title: US blocks trade to Cuba
incidents.description: As U.S. pressure on Cuba mounts, the island has faced an increasingly difficult situation, from power disruptions affecting health care services to trash building up in the streets. Trump has reiterated his warnings to Cuba to make a deal and to “make changes” to the regime, without specifying an exact outcome. Trump also confirmed that Rubio is in discussions with Cuba’s government, while deeming a military operation akin to the one against Venezuela in January “unnecessary.” In a separate incident, U.S. forces boarded a sanctioned oil tanker in the Indian Ocean as part of its efforts to control Venezuelan oil, though there was no indication that the tanker was placed under formal U.S. control.

incidents.title: Israel is expected to begin land seizure in west bank
incidents.description: The Israeli government is imminently expected to begin a “land registration process” in the West Bank that would allow Israeli forces to seize land currently owned by Palestinians if the owners in question are unable to legally prove ownership.

incidents.title: China grants visa free travel to UK-Canadaian citizens
incidents.description: China has added Canada and the U.K. to its list of countries whose citizens can enter China without a visa following recent meetings between the three countries aimed at thawing relations

incidents.title: US and Iran conduct talks in Oman
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reported progress in ongoing Omani-mediated negotiations with the U.S. in Geneva, while unnamed U.S. officials cited by various news agencies were dismissive of the talks and claimed the U.S. military would be prepared to strike Iran as soon as Feb. 21

incidents.title: China cracks down on investment influencers
incidents.description: Chinese regulators launched a crackdown on aggressive influencer marketing of investment products. Officials said the campaign aimed to reduce speculative behavior amid a technology-driven stock market rally.

incidents.title: Israeli airstrike kills 11
incidents.description: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza killed at least 11 Palestinians.

incidents.title: Israel strikes targets in Lebanon
incidents.description: Israel conducted multiple airstrikes in southern and eastern Lebanon

incidents.title: Iran signals openness to nuclear compromise
incidents.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Deputy Director for Economic Diplomacy Hamid Ghanbari said the United States and Iran were actively pursuing a mutually beneficial agreement as weekslong negotiations continued. The talks centered on the decadeslong dispute over Iran's nuclear program.

incidents.title: Indian and Canadian foreign ministers meet
incidents.description: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand met Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference. The officials discussed trade, technology, energy, and broader bilateral cooperation.

incidents.title: US-Israeli agreement to push Iran not to sell oil to China
incidents.description: Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, where he agreed that the U.S. would increase economic pressure on Iran by working to reduce Iranian oil exports to China.

incidents.title: China sets African import tariffs to zero
incidents.description: China announced it would implement zero tariffs on imports from 53 African countries with which it maintains diplomatic relations beginning May 1. Beijing also pledged to expand market access for African exports.

incidents.title: Iran continues to talk with the US about nuclear proliferation
incidents.description: While Iran is open to negotiating uranium enrichment levels with the U.S., restrictions on ballistic missile programs and support to regional proxies are “non-negotiable” according to , Ali Shamkhani, secretary of Iran’s Defense Council.

incidents.title: Japan seizes a Chinese fishing vessel
incidents.description: Japanese authorities seized a Chinese fishing vessel and arrested its captain after he attempted to dodge an inspection while operating in Japanese waters.

incidents.title: US sets new tariff on Chinese minerals
incidents.description: The U.S. finalized its decision on new tariffs on graphite imports from China, following an investigation into unfair trade practices, resulting in countervailing tariffs of 67% and an antidumping duty of 93.5%. These tariffs, which are separate from the “Liberation Day” tariffs that are facing scrutiny in the U.S. Supreme Court, are expected to be put in place by the International Trade Commission in March.

incidents.title: Indian tech companies discuss AI construction
incidents.description: A recent AI Impact Summit in New Delhi bolstered India’s ambitions to raise its global tech profile. India’s government emphasized the conference as the “first-ever global AI summit hosted in the Global South,” attracting top executives of major tech and AI companies to discuss issues including employment, sovereign AI, and global policymaking. Attendees included OpenAI’s Sam Altman, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, and Bill Gates, among others.

incidents.title: Iran protest crackdown death toll rises
incidents.description: Iranian activist groups attributed more than 7,000 deaths to violent government crackdowns against protest movements as of this week. The violence also complicated Iran's foreign policy as Tehran struggled to reach a compromise with the United States.

incidents.title: Chinese provinces cut revenue forecasts
incidents.description: Chinese provinces lowered their budget revenue expectations for 2026 as the prolonged property downturn continued to strain public finances.

incidents.title: Russia atta ks Kiev with ballistic missiles
incidents.description: Russia carried out numerous bombings against cities across Ukraine, including the use of hypersonic Kinzhal missiles in Lviv

incidents.title: US-Taiwan sign new tariff treaty
incidents.description: Taiwan and the U.S. signed a new trade agreement that reduces U.S. tariffs on all imports from the island to 15% in exchange for preferential access of U.S. exports to Taiwan. This places Taiwan at similar tariff rates to South Korea and Japan.

incidents.title: China agress to buy more US agricultural products
incidents.description: Asian traders have reported that China has increased its orders of U.S. sorghum to 2.5 million metric tons over the past three months. This has been driven both by Chinese pledges to import more agricultural products from the U.S. and diminishing domestic supplies.

incidents.title: China agrees to allow EV makers to sell independently in EU
incidents.description: China’s Ministry of Commerce has agreed to let Chinese electric vehicle makers negotiate their pricing and sales independently with the European Union rather than as a whole.

incidents.title: China has lowered tariffs on EU dairy products
incidents.description: China has lowered tariffs on dairy products from the European Union to a maximum of 11.7% from the previous range of 21.9% to 42.7% after an 18-month anti-dumping investigation. These tariffs are set to remain in place for five years starting Feb 13.

incidents.title: 300,000 people in Odessa lose power during war
incidents.description: Nearly 300,000 people in Odesa are without power and running water as a result of Russian bombardment of the city’s and region’s energy infrastructure.

incidents.title: Xi praises anticorruption campaign
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping publicly praised the military’s recent anticorruption campaign, describing it as revolutionary. Xi said the armed forces had been strengthened through the crackdown.

incidents.title: UK provides over 200 million dollars in new military equipment to Ukraine
incidents.description: British Defense Minister John Healy announced that the U.K. has committed $205 million to provide Ukraine with U.S.-made weapons and munitions through the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List

incidents.title: ICE end operations in Minnosta
incidents.description: Border czar Tom Homan announced the White House would end its aggressive immigration enforcement campaign in Minnesota, citing increased cooperation by local law enforcement. Details of the policy shift remain scarce beyond Homan’s pledge to no longer deploy new federal agents to the state. The Department of Homeland Security may still face a partial funding freeze from Congress following continued debate on the department’s involvement in law enforcement activities

incidents.title: Ukraine and US agree to hold peace talks in Miami
incidents.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine accepted an invitation from the U.S. to attend peace talks in Miami on Feb. 17-18. Zelenskyy noted that Russia has not yet committed to sending a delegation.

incidents.title: US decides not to seize Iranian oil tankers
incidents.description: The U.S. has decided against seizing additional Iranian oil tankers during ongoing nuclear negotiations in the interest of preventing destabilization to global markets and Iranian retaliation, possibly including the mining of the Strait of Hormuz, according to U.S. officials cited by the Wall Street Journal.

incidents.title: Trump says talks with Iran will continue along with Israel
incidents.description: Trump “insisted” that negotiations with Iran will continue, following a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House on Feb. 11. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said both the U.S. and Iran are prepared to compromise and reach a deal over uranium enrichment but cautioned that expanding demands to restrict Iranian missile programs and regional proxies would risk “another war.”

incidents.title: Russian foreign minister says he will continue to remain in the START treaty
incidents.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Russia will continue to abide by the limits previously set by the expired START nuclear weapons treaty so long as the U.S. does the same. While negotiations for a new nuclear arms control treaty between the U.S. and Russia are ongoing, U.S. President Donald Trump rejected an initial offer from Russian President Vladimir Putin to extend the terms of the START treaty by one year. Trump said he would prefer to negotiate a “new and improved” deal

incidents.title: France considers new tariffs on CHina
incidents.description: A French government strategy report called on the European Union to consider imposing a 30% blanket tariff on all Chinese goods to counter cheap imports from China. Chinese state-affiliated social media accounts have already warned that such a move could result in reciprocal tariffs or trade investigations into French wine imports.

incidents.title: Japanese prime minster Takaichi secures victory
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi secured an electoral victory after her party won a two-thirds majority in the lower house of parliament. Following the results, Takaichi said at a news conference she was ready to engage in discussions on constitutional reform, including on the role of the Self Defense Force.

incidents.title: Leaked US docs claim the US is planning to send extra equipment to Taiwan
incidents.description: Sources close to Trump have revealed that the administration is preparing a large arms sale to Taiwan that would include Patriot air defense missile systems. This comes shortly after a reported call between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping during which Xi had warned the U.S. to tread carefully in regards to arms sales to Taiwan.

incidents.title: Iran rejects missile program talks
incidents.description: Ali Shamkhani, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader, said Iran was unwilling to negotiate over the country's missile capabilities. Shamkhani made the comments shortly after talks between the United States and Iran broke down without a substantive agreement.

incidents.title: Israeli soliders kill 8 civilians in Gaza
incidents.description: Israeli forces killed at least eight Palestinians in Gaza amid reports that Israel is preparing for a ground offensive to force the disarmament of Hamas, according to sources cited by the Times of Israel.

incidents.title: Ethopia has been foujd to have trained RSF members
incidents.description: A Reuters investigation found that Ethiopia has been training members of the Sudanese Rapid Support Forces (RSF) rebel group in a training camp allegedly co-financed by the United Arab Emirates. Located in Ethiopia’s western region of Benishangul-Gumuz, the camp held as many as 4,000 RSF fighters in early January undergoing military training, in addition to other Sudanese rebel groups and Ethiopian nationals. Other infrastructure expansion efforts have also been reported, including the enlargement of the nearby Asosa airport, which officials say they want to refurbish as a drone operation center

incidents.title: EU report concludes they are losing ground to China in green energy
incidents.description: Executives in Europe’s green hydrogen industry warned that they could begin losing ground to Chinese competitors. Unless the electrolyzer business for green hydrogen production grows rapidly with public support, it will follow the solar sector's lead, where Chinese manufacturing costs dropped and Europe relied heavily on imports. China manufactures 60% of hydrogen electrolyzers worldwide and has huge cost advantages due to its massive manufacturing scale.

incidents.title: EU Vice President prepares list of demands for Russian withdrawl
incidents.description: Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas said the EU is preparing a list of concessions that it will demand from Russia regarding its war in Ukraine, in an effort to unify European diplomatic efforts.

incidents.title: SMIC warns of chip shortages
incidents.description: Chinese chipmaker Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. warned that surging demand for memory chips had pushed the industry into crisis conditions. Company executives said customers were increasingly overbooking orders amid supply shortages.

incidents.title: US and Armenia agree to cooperate on nuclear energy
incidents.description: U.S. Vice President JD Vance met with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Armenia, where both countries agreed to cooperate in the civil nuclear sector. This agreement paves the way to potentially replace Armenia’s only Russian-built nuclear power station, Metsamor, as it seeks to diversify energy trade away from Russia and Iran. While an official choice has not yet been made, this cooperation agreement comes on the heels of a preliminary peace agreement with Azerbaijan brokered by the U.S. as well as the creation of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, heavily involving the U.S. in Armenia’s energy-related decisions.

incidents.title: Russia attacks new range of Ukranian cities
incidents.description: Russian forces are intensifying their ground campaign against the Ukrainian city of Pokrovsk in Donetsk. The Ukrainian army maintains a foothold in the northern part of the city, according to Ukrainian defense officials.

incidents.title: China urges banks not to cooperate with US
incidents.description: Chinese financial regulators have urged Chinese banks to limit the purchase of U.S. government bonds due to perceived risks of market volatility. The call does not apply to the Chinese state’s holdings of U.S. Treasuries and comes on the heels of several statements made in recent weeks by the Chinese government stating ambitions for the renminbi to become a global reserve currency.

incidents.title: US tightens pressure on Cuba with oil cut off's
incidents.description: The Trump administration has been increasing pressure on Cuba, cutting off Venezuelan oil shipments to the island, leading to the Cuban government warning of fuel shortages for stopover airplane transits as the country rations its reserves. This will notably affect longer flight paths, including those from Russia and Canada, both of which support Cuba’s tourism industry. Other domestic services have been impacted, including public transport and the banking sector. China, has pledged to do what it can to help Cuba, though it has not specified publicly how it would do so, while Russia said it planned to send oil as part of humanitarian aid to the island

incidents.title: Israel signs bill allowing Israeli citizens to purchase more land in the west bank
incidents.description: On Feb 8, Israel’s security cabinet approved a decision to “dramatically” reduce bureaucratic hurdles for Jewish Israeli citizens to purchase land in the West Bank. President of the Palestinian Authority Mahmoud Abbas called for a “firm response” from the U.S. in opposition to the measures.

incidents.title: China critic Jimmy Lai sentenced
incidents.description: A Hong Kong court sentenced media entrepreneur Jimmy Lai to 20 years in prison under national security legislation. The case marked the conclusion of Hong Kong’s largest national security prosecution to date.

incidents.title: US plans to deploy nuclear powered subs in Australia
incidents.description: A new Wall Street Journal report stated that the U.S. is planning to strengthen its naval posture in the Indo-Pacific by deploying up to four nuclear-powered submarines to the Australian HMAS Stirling naval base in 2027. This deployment would be consistent with the established goals under the trilateral AUKUS agreement.

incidents.title: US deploys rotational forces in the Phillippines
incidents.description: The U.S. Army confirmed that it had established a rotational presence in the Philippines in July 2025. This establishes a stronger footing for the branch in an area normally dominated by the Navy and Air Force, as the U.S. seeks to bolster its presence in the South China Sea.

incidents.title: China restricts offshore yuan stablecoins
incidents.description: China introduced new rules prohibiting individuals and companies from issuing offshore yuan-linked stablecoins without regulatory approval. Officials said the measures were intended to protect monetary stability.

incidents.title: Tesla recruiting new staff
incidents.description: According to senior executives, Tesla is recruiting new staff to support founder Elon Musk’s goal of becoming the largest manufacturer of solar energy components in the United States. Tesla is implementing Musk's vision to set up 100 gigawatts of domestic solar production.

incidents.title: China conducts military exercise in South China Sea
incidents.description: The People’s Liberation Army conducted “combat readiness patrols” with air and naval assets near the disputed Scarborough Shoal, days after the U.S. and Philippines conducted joint drills in the region.

incidents.title: Singapore buys 4 F-35B fighters
incidents.description: Singapore is set to receive four F-35B fighter jets from the U.S. by the end of the year, based on an order placed in 2019. This will mark the first batch of F-35s out of a total of 20 that are slated to be delivered by 2030 and will place Singapore as the fourth country in the Indo-Pacific to operate the jets after Australia, Japan, and South Korea.

incidents.title: Russia companies are forced out of Venezuela
incidents.description: Russian companies are being “openly forced out” of Venezuela as part of a U.S. pressure campaign, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said

incidents.title: US-Russia talks close in on START continuation
incidents.description: U.S. and Russian officials in Abu Dhabi are “closing in” on an extension of the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START) according to unnamed sources cited by Axios. START, which officially expired on Feb. 5., capped the quantity of each nation's strategic nuclear weapons at 1,550

incidents.title: US and Russia agree to resume bi-lateral military talks
incidents.description: Ukraine, Russia, and the United States conducted two days of trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Feb. 4 and Feb. 5. Following the talks, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the summit as “constructive”, and Russian Special Envoy Kirill Dmitriev cited “positive movement forward.” Prior to the talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff hosted Russian Special Envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Florida on Feb. 3, for talks that Witkoff described as “productive and constructive.”

incidents.title: China refuses to sign Start treaty with US and Russia
incidents.description: The New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired this week, with Trump stating he was open to renewing it provided China signed onto it as well. Beijing called the expiration regrettable but has rebuffed the offer to join the treaty.

incidents.title: Russo-Ukraine POW swap conducted in UAE talks
incidents.description: As a result of negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Ukraine and Russia conducted a POW exchange of 314 personnel each on Feb. 4. The deal would marked the first such exchange in the last five months

incidents.title: US signs new trading block with global powers
incidents.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance hosted officials from European, African, and Asian countries in Washington to sign on to a new trading bloc with the aim of stabilizing the supply chains and costs of critical minerals. Representatives of Greenland and Denmark were not present at the meeting despite the ongoing debate about access to Greenland’s natural resources, and China stated it opposes the meeting and bloc

incidents.title: US and China have productive discussion of Taiwan
incidents.description: Trump stated in a Truth Social post that he and Xi discussed Taiwan in a phone call, marking the first publicly acknowledged bilateral discussion on the topic. Xi reportedly warned Trump to be “prudent” regarding arms sales to the island.

incidents.title: Iran seizes two oil tankers
incidents.description: The IRGC seized two oil tankers along with their foreign crews on Feb. 5, claiming that the vessels were carrying over 1 million liters of “smuggled fuel.” The nationalities of the crewmembers have not been identified.

incidents.title: Oman hosts US-Iran talk about Nuclear power
incidents.description: Oman hosted talks between the U.S. and Iran over Iran’s nuclear program on Feb. 5 in Muscat. The talks followed a series of threats by Trump to conduct military operations against Iran, along with the deployment of significant U.S. naval and air assets to the region. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian instructed Iran’s lead diplomats to conduct “fair and equitable” negotiations

incidents.title: Russia bombs Ukrainian Cities
incidents.description: Russia conducted bombings against numerous Ukrainian cities. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers had been killed since the beginning of Russia’s invasion in 2022 and noted that there were “a large number of people missing

incidents.title: Putin holds conference call with Xi Jinping
incidents.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin held a Feb. 4 call with Chinese President Xi Jinping to deepen bilateral cooperation following an announcement from Trump that India had agreed to cease purchases of Russian oil as part of a new trade deal with the United States

incidents.title: EU lauches trade investigation into Chinese company
incidents.description: The European Union initiated a trade investigation into Goldwind Science and Technology, a Chinese wind turbine maker, for possible unfair subsidies by the Chinese government. China reacted by decrying “protectionist” policies by the bloc

incidents.title: Ukraine President Acusses Putin of ceasefire violation
incidents.description: Russia resumed its bombardment campaign against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, following a weeklong pause at Trump’s request.

incidents.title: American deploys destroyer after Iran tries to board US tanker
incidents.description: On Feb. 3, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval forces approached and threatened to board a U.S. flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, the U.S. military deployed the USS McFaul, a guided-missile destroyer, and unspecified U.S. Air Force assets to provide the tanker with a security escort.

incidents.title: US maintains export block on H200 chips to China
incidents.description: Exports of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China are still on hold as the process needs to pass security inspections by the U.S. departments of defense, state, and energy before any export licenses can be approved. This follows the directive from Trump, who approved the sale and export of the chips provided an adequate security check is conducted

incidents.title: US-India trade deal reached
incidents.description: Trump announced that the U.S. had reached a new trade deal with India. In his post, he stated that India had agreed to reduce its purchases of Russian oil, which will now result in U.S. tariffs on Indian products falling to 18%. The Indian government has confirmed that an agreement was met but has not commented on the situation regarding Russian oil.

incidents.title: American F-35 shoots down Iranian drone
incidents.description: On Feb. 3, an American F-35 pilot shot down an Iranian drone that "aggressively approached” the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea, according to a statement from U.S. Central Command

incidents.title: Jordan prohibits US or Iran from using their airspace
incidents.description: Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, that Jordan will not be a “battleground” in a potential conflict between the U.S. and Iran and that Jordan will not allow the U.S. to use its airspace to support a possible attack against Iran

incidents.title: Qatar expands oil production to meet demands of AI data centers
incidents.description: Qatar Energy CEO Saad al-Kaabi warned that increased electrical demand from AI and data centers, Asian fuel demand growth, and European gas needs might turn a projected worldwide liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply surplus into a deficit by 2030. New LNG production capacity and export infrastructure drives the 2026–2029 global LNG supply surplus. The U.S. is set to double its capacity by 2029, and Qatar is expanding its north field to boost output by 85% by 2030. The U.S. and Qatar account for 70% of the 300 billion cubic meters per year of additional world LNG liquefaction capacity predicted by 2030.

incidents.title: America conducts airstrikes against ISIS tagets in Syria
incidents.description: U.S. military forces deployed to U.S. Central Command carried out a series of airstrikes against ISIS personal and weapons depots in Syria from Jan. 27 to Feb. 2

incidents.title: EU attempts to expand imports of CRM as renewable target falls short
incidents.description: The EU's efforts to diversify its imports of critical raw materials (CRM) for energy transition has failed, according to a report from the European court of auditors. The EU aims to reach net-zero emissions by 2050 and produce 42.5% of its energy from renewable sources by 2030. The EU needs more critical minerals for energy transition and climate targets. A more diversified import portfolio, more domestic production, and better and sustainable resource management could guarantee a steady supply of critical materials, such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper, and rare earth elements. According to the report, the European Union's efforts to diversify CRM imports did not seem to be successful in producing meaningful outcomes, largely due to high energy costs of setting up processing facilities, as well as strategic partnerships with third countries not delivering as planned. EU officials met in Cyprus this week to discuss the implementation of the bloc’s new “RESourceEU,” which they hope will accelerate their diversification and implementation efforts.

incidents.title: America ends its blockade on Venezuela oil after fall of Maduro
incidents.description: Following the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro by U.S. forces, the U.S. ended its blockade against oil shipments out of the country, resulting in oil exports nearly doubling from December to January. The U.S. Treasury granted export licenses to Trafigura and Vitol, two Venezuelan traders, leading to January’s exports amounting to 800,000 barrels per day, compared to December’s 480,000 bpd. The Treasury department further authorized U.S. businesses to work with Venezuelan oil producer PDVSA, though individual licenses are still in the process of being granted.

incidents.title: Syrian army deployed into Hasakah
incidents.description: The Syrian army deployed forces to assume security responsibilities in the city of Hasakah, under observation from and in cooperation with Kurdish forces, as part of a deal to integrate the Kurdish militias and institutions into the central Syrian government.

incidents.title: Baloch Liberation army conducts attack in Southern Pakistan
incidents.description: The Baloch Liberation Army conducted a series of coordinated bombings and gun attacks across Balochistan on Feb. 1, killing 50 people. An intervention by Pakistani security forces led to the deaths of nearly 150 militants.

incidents.title: Israeli bombing kills 56 Palesinians
incidents.description: Israeli forces in Gaza killed at least 56 Palestinians during a series of bombings on Jan. 31 and Feb. 4 after clashes between Hamas and the IDF

incidents.title: Partial gov shutdown ends after 4 day standoff
incidents.description: The federal government reopened Tuesday after a four-day partial shutdown. Democratic lawmakers had refused to fund the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) after Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents fatally shot two U.S. citizens in Minnesota, while hardline conservatives pushed for a vote on a controversial voter identification bill. Pressure from the White House swayed some Republican lawmakers, who were followed by more than 20 U.S. House Democrats, and a bill that provides two weeks of stopgap funding for DHS passed 217-214. The Trump administration vowed to take a “softer touch” on immigration enforcement, as Trump’s border czar Tom Homan announced that 700 federal law enforcement officers were being removed from Minnesota, leaving approximately 2,000 in the state.

incidents.title: China arrests senior CCP offical for corruption
incidents.description: China’s Central Commission for Discipline Inspection stated it was investigating Wang Xiangxi, a senior official within the Chinese Communist Party, for “serious violations of discipline and law.” Three lawmakers with ties to the Chinese defense industry were also removed from their position, following last week’s ousting of the Central Military Commission’s vice chair

incidents.title: Syrian government and Syrian Democratic forces (SDF) sign cease fire
incidents.description: The Syrian government and the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) have declared a ceasefire after reaching an agreement to integrate SDF forces and institutions into the central Syrian government

incidents.title: British PM makes new policy agreement with China
incidents.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer met with Xi, and both leaders agreed to push for a “more sophisticated” relationship with increased communications on matters of common interest. China subsequently granted access to British pharmaceutical and energy companies to its market while reducing tariffs on imports of British alcohol. The meeting marks a diplomatic win for Beijing as it seeks to position itself as a stable alternative power to the United States

incidents.title: Trump admin imposes tariffs on any country exporting to Cuba
incidents.description: Trump signed an executive order designating Cuba as an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to the U.S. and declared a national emergency, citing the support that Cuba offers to “adversaries in the Western Hemisphere.” Trump stated he would impose tariffs on imports from any country that supplies Cuba with oil, leading to condemnation from Russia and China.

incidents.title: Ukraine and Russia Describe Constructive Direct Talks
incidents.description: Ukrainian and Russian officials both described direct talks held in Abu Dhabi from Jan. 23-24 as “constructive” ahead of a second round of direct talks scheduled for Feb. 1. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said there has been a “qualitative change in the composition” of Russia’s negotiators.

incidents.title: Ukrainian Membership to EU is Not Possible According to German Chancellor
incidents.description: Ukrainian membership in the EU in 2027 is “not possible” and “out of the question,” according to statements from German Chancellor Frederich Merz on Jan. 28. The remarks from Merz were in response to a Zelenskyy speech a day earlier, in which he stated that Ukraine would aim to achieve EU membership by 2027.

incidents.title: Trump weighs strike options on Iran
incidents.description: Trump is said to be weighing strike options against senior Iranian leadership, security forces, and nuclear infrastructure with a goal of sparking new protests and achieving regime change, according to unnamed U.S. officials cited by CNN and Reuters. Trump has issued a series of public threats against Iran, as he ordered the deployment of an “armada” including the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group and other military assets across the region.

incidents.title: EU Commission recgonizes Iran guard core as a terrorist organization
incidents.description: Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas announced the EU will recognize Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist group in response to the IRGC’s role in the violent suppression of Iran’s mass protest movement.

incidents.title: Turkiye offers to mediate between US and Iran
incidents.description: Türkiye has offered to play a leading role in mediating between the U.S. and Iran in an attempt to de-escalate regional tensions, while Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs Badr Abdelatty spoke separately with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Minister of Foreign Affairs Abbas Araghchi.

incidents.title: Russian Forces Expand their Offensive in Pokrovsk, Ukraine
incidents.description: Russian forces expanded their offensive around the Ukrainian city of Pokrovsk, while Russia continued its intensified campaign of bombardment against Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure.

incidents.title: Putin is Willing to Meet with Zelenskyy Directly
incidents.description: Senior Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russian President Vladimir Putin is willing to meet directly with Zelenskyy, on the condition that the meeting take place in Moscow. Such a meeting may involve participation from U.S. President Donald Trump, according to an unnamed U.S. official cited by the Kyiv Independent.

incidents.title: Syrian President meets with Putin
incidents.description: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa met with Putin in Moscow on Jan. 28, amid reports that Russian forces were beginning a withdrawal from Syrian territory. Moscow is seeking a negotiation to maintain a troop presence in Syria

incidents.title: Australian PM demands to have control of port of Darwin from Chinese company
incidents.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated he was committed to regaining control of the Darwin Port, which had been leased to Chinese company Landbridge in 2015 for 99 years. The statement has drawn words of warning from Beijing.

incidents.title: China provides permission for companies to use Nvidia chips
incidents.description: China has given its approval for ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent to purchase more than 400,000 H200 chips from Nvidia. Beijing had previously warned domestic manufacturers against purchasing these chips, and according to sources. Other companies have started requesting subsequent approvals

incidents.title: US and Taiwan agree to new trade conditions
incidents.description: The U.S. and Taiwan held talks under the Economic Prosperity Partnership Dialogue, agreeing to coordinate further on supply chain resiliency related to AI, digital infrastructure, and uncrewed aircraft systems. Taiwan endorsed the principles of the U.S.-led “Pax Silica” initiative, though the U.S. delegation did not acknowledge a timeframe for Taiwan’s entry to the initiative

incidents.title: US Trump Administration Faces Backlash for the Killing of Alex Pretti
incidents.description: The Trump administration faced widespread backlash for its response to the killing of 37-year-old Alex Pretti by a group of federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers. Following large-scale protests, the agents involved were placed on leave, while immigration enforcement chief Greg Bovino was also moved back to his previous post in California. The Trump administration has stated it would push for de-escalation, while the director of the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, Todd Lyons, was summoned by a Minnesota judge. The backlash to Pretti’s death led to the Democratic Party largely opposing a new spending bill that would see increased funding for ICE among other government services. However, Schumer is reported to have reached a deal with the government that would increase restrictions on federal immigration agents.

incidents.title: Marco Rubio Testifies Before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee
incidents.description: Rubio appeared before a Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing, where he was questioned by both Democrats and Republicans. Rubio testified that the U.S. would retain interim control of Venezuela’s sanctioned oil, which the U.S. would sell with the profits used to benefit Venezuela. The U.S. also returned a seized sanctioned oil tanker to a Venezuelan port this week. This comes as U.S. intelligence officials have raised doubts about whether current Venezuelan leader Delcy Rodriguez would continue to cooperate with the United States

incidents.title: Demark is Negotiating the Status of Greenland with the US
incidents.description: The Danish Foreign Ministry confirmed that Denmark is negotiating the status of Greenland with the United States. The ministry stated the objective was to address the U.S.’s security concerns in the Arctic while respecting Denmark’s red lines. Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said he would not yield to any foreign pressure, while Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated that the world order of the past 80 years is over

incidents.title: Saudi Arabia and UAE inform US it can't use their airspaces in case of war
incidents.description: At least two key U.S. regional partners, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, have informed U.S. and Iranian officials that they will not allow their airspace to be used by the U.S. military in the event of an attack against Iran.

incidents.title: US and Philippines conduct joint military patrol
incidents.description: The U.S. and the Philippines conducted a joint patrol near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, with China responding by accusing the Philippines of “co-opting” the U.S. in disturbing the peace

incidents.title: Trump threatens higher tariffs if South Korea doe not invest more
incidents.description: Trump threatened to raise tariffs on South Korean automobiles, lumber, and pharmaceuticals to 25%, citing a lack of commitment by Seoul to deliver on its pledge to invest $350 billion in U.S. South Korean Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol said he would ask lawmakers to accelerate the investment bill as a result.

incidents.title: EU and India sign trade deal
incidents.description: The European Union and India concluded negotiations for an expanded trade deal that would see the EU’s exports to India double by 2032, with India reducing tariffs by 96.6% in value on EU imports

incidents.title: Japan PM advocates for more positive relations with US
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reaffirmed the need for Japan’s strategic alliance with the U.S. while distancing herself from previous comments made about the risks of a Chinese attack on Taiwan

incidents.title: Finnish PM meets with Xi to discuss mutual cooperation
incidents.description: Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo met with Xi, who expressed a readiness to work with Finland to uphold a U.N.-centered system as China continues its diplomatic outreach to the EU

incidents.title: EU approves ban on Russian gas exports
incidents.description: On Jan. 26, EU member states approved a ban on the purchase of Russian gas exports by Nov. 1, 2027. The measure was passed with the support of 24 out of 27 member states.

incidents.title: Israel receives remains of final hostage
incidents.description: Israeli Defense Forces confirmed on Jan. 26 that Israel has received the remains of the final hostage who had been held by Hamas in Gaza. The transfer of remains marks a significant step in the implementation of the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas toward the start of Phase II of the plan

incidents.title: Xi Jinping removes top military officals
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping has removed the vice chairman of the Central Military Commission, Zhang Youxia and chief of staff Liu Zhenli From their positions. Both are under investigation amid accusations that they leaked secrets on China’s nuclear arsenal to the U.S. and took bribes. Taiwan has said it is closely monitoring the situation.

incidents.title: USA Rare Earth Reports SIgning of Letter of Intent for US Government Funding
incidents.description: USA Rare Earth reported it had signed a letter of intent with the U.S. government to secure $277 million in federal funding and a $1.3 billion loan under the CHIPS Act to aid development of a mine in Sierra Blanca, Texas, as well as a magnet manufacturing plant in Stillwater, Oklahoma, with expected openings in 2028 and 2027, respectively. The U.S. Department of Commerce will take a 10% stake in the company as part of the deal.

incidents.title: Security Gurantee Document Ready to Sign by the US
incidents.description: A security guarantees document is “100% ready” for signing by the U.S., according to a statement from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy following the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. Zelenskyy also acknowledged that issues over the territorial control of Donbas and the operational control of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant remain unresolved. According to sources cited by the Financial Times, U.S. officials are pushing Ukraine to cede the roughly 20% of Donbas territory that remains unoccupied by Russia before committing to security guarantees.

incidents.title: Israeli forces kill two civilians
incidents.description: On Jan. 25, Israeli forces killed at least two Palestinians in Gaza and carried out numerous airstrikes against Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon.

incidents.title: US plans to draw back forces from South Korea
incidents.description: The U.S. Department of Defense unveiled its 2026 National Defense Strategy, which calls for a “more limited” role in deterring North Korea, placing a greater onus on South Korea to do so. The document also called for the U.S. to ensure China does not “dominate” in the region, though without calling for confrontation and without mentioning Taiwan.

incidents.title: UAE Global South Utilities Company has Fully Withdrawn from Yemen
incidents.description: UAE Global South Utilities Company (GSU) has fully withdrawn from Yemen and handed all its operational solar assets to the public electricity corporation of Yemen. The handover included major solar power plants at Aden and Shabwa with a generation capacity of 53 megawatts (MW) and 120 MW, respectively. This . This came after the Yemeni government formally requested that all Emirati companies leave the country due to political tensions. A pullout of the GSU technical team was required to ensure personnel safety.

incidents.title: Ukraine Largest Power Company Warns of Russian Energy Strikes Impact
incidents.description: At the World Economic Forum in Davos, Maxim Timchenko, the chief executive officer of Ukraine’s largest power company, DTEK, warned that Russian strikes targeting the country’s energy infrastructure had created conditions for a humanitarian catastrophe and asked that such attacks stop. Russian strikes knocked out 60% to 70% of DTEK's power producing capacity. Millions of Ukrainians have endured temperatures as low as -20 degrees Celsius (-4 Fahrenheit) with availability of only 3 to 4 hours of electricity per day. Russian forces have since been ordered to halt their attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure for one week, until Feb 3. The EU is supplying hospitals and shelters with emergency generators after these warnings.

incidents.title: French Navy Seizes Russian Oil Tanker in Mediterranean With Allied Support
incidents.description: The French navy seized a Russian oil vessel in the Mediterranean on Jan. 22 that had been traveling between Spain and Morocco. French President Emmanuel Macron said the operation was carried out with the support of “several of our allies.”

incidents.title: Putin Accepts Board of Peace Invitation, Backs Use of Frozen Assets for Gaza and Ukraine
incidents.description: Putin accepted his invitation to join the Board of Peace and said Russia supports the use of $1 billion of frozen assets held by the United States to pay for Russia’s entry to the body and to provide for the “restoration” of Gaza and Ukraine.

incidents.title: Trump’s Board of Peace Charter Signed in Davos as Netanyahu Joins Amid Gaza Disputes
incidents.description: The founding charter of Trump’s Board of Peace, which does not mention Gaza, was signed in Davos on Jan. 22. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accepted Trump’s invitation to join the Board of Peace, despite significant disputes with the United States over key details of ceasefire Phase II implementation, including the governance of Gaza, the disarmament of Hamas and the composition of the proposed International Security Force. While the Board of Peace was proposed to oversee the implementation of the Israel/Hamas ceasefire and the eventual post-Hamas governance of Gaza, it is being repurposed by Trump to address numerous international conflicts.

incidents.title: Japanese Prime Minister Announces the Dissolvement of Parliament
incidents.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced she would be dissolving Parliament this week in anticipation of a snap election scheduled for Feb. 8. She further announced plans to scrap the current 8% sales tax on food, briefly lowering the value of the Yen.

incidents.title: Trump Meets Zelenskyy at Davos as U.S. Envoys Hold Talks With Putin in Moscow
incidents.description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met on the sidelines of the Davos summit in Switzerland on Jan. 22, while U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law and adviser Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. While speaking at Davos prior to meeting with Putin, Witkoff said that “a lot of progress” has been made and that “one last issue” remained to be resolved.

incidents.title: Blast Kills 11 Syrian Soldiers, Threatening Ceasefire Between Damascus and SDF
incidents.description: At least 11 Syrian soldiers were killed by an explosion at a military facility in northeast Syria on Jan 21., threatening to derail a fragile four-day ceasefire between the Syrian government and the SDF. Syrian officials said the explosion was the result of an SDF drone strike, while the SDF denies responsibility and attributes the attack to Syrian soldiers mishandling explosives located at the facility.

incidents.title: US House of Representatives Release its Reading of the Consolidated Appropriations Act
incidents.description: The U.S. House of Representatives released its reading of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, earmarking $1.15 billion for defense cooperation and support for Taiwan.

incidents.title: U.S., Ukraine, and Russia to Hold Trilateral Talks in Abu Dhabi Jan. 23–24
incidents.description: The U.S., Ukraine and Russia are scheduled to participate in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi from Jan. 23-24.

incidents.title: Trump Inaugurated his "Board of Peace" During the World Economic Forum in Davos
incidents.description: Trump inaugurated his “Board of Peace” during the World Economic Forum in Davos, with a signing ceremony marking the official founding of the body. Putin, Netanyahu, and Belarussian President Aleksandr Lukashenko are among the signatories. European leaders have held off on joining the board, citing concerns with the aforementioned leaders and constitutional incompatibility. Following French President Emmanuel Macron’s refusal to join, Trump announced he would impose 200% tariffs on French alcohol imports.

incidents.title: The European Commission Issues a Draft Proposal to Phase Out Components and Equipment from High-Risk Suppliers
incidents.description: The European Commission issued a draft proposal that requires the bloc to phase out components and equipment from high-risk suppliers in critical sectors, in accordance with the EU Cybersecurity Act. The move was criticized by China’s Huawei.

incidents.title: IDF Kills at Least 11 in Gaza, Strikes Hezbollah Targets in Lebanon and Along Syria Border
incidents.description: The Israel Defense Forces killed at least 11 Palestinians in Gaza and conducted multiple airstrikes against Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and along the Lebanese/Syrian border over the week.

incidents.title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Oil Infrastructure, Wounding at Least 13 in North Caucasus Attack
incidents.description: Ukraine conducted numerous attacks against Russian oil infrastructure, including an attack in the North Caucasus region on Jan. 21 that wounded at least 13 people.

incidents.title: U.S. Transfers 150 ISIS Detainees From Syria to Iraq, More Moves Expected
incidents.description: U.S. forces on Jan. 21 conducted the transfer of 150 ISIS members previously detained by Kurdish forces in northeast Syria to Iraq, where they were placed under the formal custody of the Iraqi government. Up to 7,000 additional ISIS detainees are likely to be transferred to Iraq, according to unnamed U.S. officials cited by the Wall Street Journal.

incidents.title: Ukraine’s New Defense Minister Pledges Data-Driven War Overhaul, Sets 2026 Casualty Target
incidents.description: Newly appointed Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov vowed a “data-driven overhaul” of Ukraine’s war effort. In a separate statement, Fedorov said that Ukraine will aim to kill 50,000 Russians per month during 2026.

incidents.title: British Prime Minister Will Visit Beijing Next Week
incidents.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer will visit Beijing next week, with both sides aiming to rekindle stronger economic relations, including through a new “U.K.-China CEO Council.”

incidents.title: US Approves the Sale of P-8A Maritime Patrol Aircraft and Torpedoes to Singapore
incidents.description: The United States approved the sale of P-8A maritime patrol aircraft and torpedoes to Singapore, worth approximately $2.3 billion.

incidents.title: US President Gives Speech at World Economic Forum in Davos
incidents.description: Following a week of doubling down on his ambitions to “acquire” Greenland, Trump gave a speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos where he stated he would not be using force to acquire the island. Following the meeting, he announced in a Truth Social post that he would not be imposing tariffs on European countries supportive of Greenland and that he had reached a “framework of a future deal” with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. European leaders nevertheless still expressed skepticism over Trump’s goals and methods, calling for increased European autonomy in the defense and industrial sectors.

incidents.title: US Court of Appeals Repeals Ruling Banning the Use of Pepper Spracy Against Nonviolent Protestors by Federal Officers
incidents.description: The U.S. 8th Circuit Court of Appeals repealed an earlier ruling by a lower court that placed a ban on the use of pepper spray against non-violent protestors by federal officers, as anti-ICE protests continue across Minnesota. The Army’s 11th Airborne Division based in Alaska has been placed on standby for possible deployment to the state, should Trump invoke the Insurrection Act. The Justice Department has further subpoenaed several Minnesota officials, including Governor Tim Walz and Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey, both of whom the department has accused of obstructing the work of law enforcement officials.

incidents.title: China Warns the Phillipines to Cease Provocations in the Scarborough Shoal
incidents.description: China claims to have driven a Philippine government aircraft away from the disputed Scarborough Shoal, urging the Philippines to “cease provocations.”

incidents.title: China Confirms It Recieves an Invitation from Trump to Join His "Board of Peace"
incidents.description: China confirmed it had received an invitation from Trump to join his “Board of Peace” but has not revealed whether it accepted the invitation.

incidents.title: Chinese Exports of Rare Earth Magnets to Japan Fell 8% in December
incidents.description: Chinese exports of rare earth magnets to Japan fell 8% in December to 280 metric tons, compared to November’s 305 tons, as tensions over Japan’s comments over Taiwan continued.

incidents.title: Seven Chadian Soldiers Killed in Clash with RSF on the Border with Sudan
incidents.description: Seven soldiers from Chad were killed during a clash with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on the border with Sudan. The RSF described the incident as “unintentional” and expressed willingness to cooperate with Chad on ongoing investigations to hold the people responsible to account.

incidents.title: About 200 ISIS Detainees Escape Kurdish Custody Amid Clashes in Northeast Syria
incidents.description: Around 200 ISIS members are estimated to have escaped Kurdish detention in northeast Syria’s Shadaddi on Jan. 20 after Kurdish forces left the detention facility in response to clashes with the Syrian army.

incidents.title: Russia Intensifies Winter Strikes on Ukraine’s Energy Grid as Mass Evacuations Continue
incidents.description: Russia continued its intensified winter campaign against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure as Kyiv deals with its most significant energy crisis of the war, including an attack of more than 300 drones and missiles launched against energy infrastructure during the overnight period of Jan. 19-20. According to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, 600,000 people have evacuated Kyiv so far in January.

incidents.title: The United Kingdom Has Given its Approval for the Construction of a New Chinese Embassy in London
incidents.description: The United Kingdom has given its approval for the construction of a new Chinese embassy in London. The embassy would be China’s largest in Europe, and the move follows a drawn-out debate on whether the location of the embassy was a risk to the national security of the United Kingdom.

incidents.title: Trump Pushes Pentagon to Draw Up “Decisive” Military Strike Options Against Iran
incidents.description: Trump ordered the U.S. Department of Defense to draw up "decisive options” for strikes against Iran, according to unnamed U.S. officials cited by the Wall Street Journal.

incidents.title: Wildfires Kill at Least 20 in Chile as Heatwave Fuels State of Crisis
incidents.description: Chile is battling wildfires that have killed at least 20 people and forced thousands to evacuate, burned thousands of acres, and destroyed hundreds of buildings. A state of crisis has been declared by President Gabriel Boric in the affected districts, allowing the military to help thousands of firefighters combat over 30 fires. A heatwave with temperatures above 100°F and strong, changing winds have worsened the fires.

incidents.title: Syria and SDF Agree to Ceasefire as Damascus Warns of Attacks if Integration Deadline Missed
incidents.description: The Syrian government and the Kurdish-led SDF agreed to a ceasefire on Jan. 20, following a rapid ground campaign from the Syrian army against SDF forces. Damascus has issued a warning that the Syrian army will attack the Kurdish-held cities of Hasakah and Qamishli if the SDF does not agree to integrate into the central Syrian government by Jan. 23.

incidents.title: Chinese Military Flies a Reconnaissance Drone over Taiwanese-Controlled Pratas Islands in South China Sea
incidents.description: The Chinese military flew a reconnaissance drone over the Taiwanese-controlled Pratas Islands in the South China Sea, a move Taiwan called “provocative and irresponsible.”

incidents.title: Ukraine Faces Largest Wartime Energy Crisis as Russia Destroys Grid and EU Imports Surge
incidents.description: Ukraine is experiencing its largest-ever wartime energy crisis due to Russia's intensified strikes and is significantly expanding its energy import capacity with European partners. Russian strikes destroyed Ukraine's electricity grid, leaving it fulfilling 60% of national demand in January 2026. Electricity imports from the EU increased by 14% compared to the end of last year, and total gas imports from western neighbors are rising. In addition, Ukraine is implementing more resilient decentralization energy projects, such as renewable expansion and large-scale energy storage.

incidents.title: Canadian Prime Minister Met with Chinese President
incidents.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Chinese President Xi Jinping with both sides hailing a rekindling of cooperative relations in agriculture and energy sectors while reducing tariffs on electric vehicles and canola oil

incidents.title: Ugandan Authorities Impose a Nationwide Internet Blackout
incidents.description: Authorities imposed a nationwide internet blackout in the days leading to the country’s general election on Jan. 15, following months of police crackdowns on opposition leaders and supporters. President Yoweri Museveni seeks a seventh term.

incidents.title: US and Taiwan Sign a New Trade Deal
incidents.description: The U.S. and Taiwan signed a new trade deal that will see tariffs on Taiwanese imports reduced from 20% to 15%, while Taiwan pledges a combined $500 billion in investment in the U.S.’s semiconductor industry. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company pledged to open five more facilities in the U.S. as part of the deal.

incidents.title: President Trump Threatens Military Action in Response to Iranian Crackdowns
incidents.description: Trump threatened military action in response to the Iranian government’s crackdown against a nationwide protest movement. The U.S. ordered the evacuation of nonessential personnel from U.S. military bases in the Middle East, as Iran threatened retaliation before Trump backtracked on his threats.

incidents.title: Japan and the Phillipines Agree to Deepen Defense Cooperation
incidents.description: Japan and the Philippines agreed to deepen defense cooperation by allowing mutual use of each other’s logistics and supplies whil increasing joint exercises.

incidents.title: Turkish Fighter Jets Will Deploy to Estonia
incidents.description: The Turkish Ministry of Defense announced that Turkish fighter jets will deploy to Estonia in August 2026 for four months, before rotating to Romania as part of an effort to bolster NATO airspace security.

incidents.title: President Trump Tells Reporters "Killing in Iran is Stopping"
incidents.description: On Jan. 14, Trump told reporters that the “killing in Iran is stopping,” and that “executions, or an execution” have also been halted. According to reporting from the Financial Times, a joint diplomatic effort among Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Qatar, Oman, and Egypt convinced Trump that a U.S. strike on Iran would have a destabilizing effect on regional security and global energy prices.

incidents.title: President Trump Threatens to Invoke the Insurrection Act and Deploy Troops to Minnesota
incidents.description: Trump threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act and deploy troops to Minnesota, as local protests against immigration authorities have grown following multiple deaths during Immigration and Customs Enforcement actions. Around 3,000 federal officers have already been deployed in the state, Minnesota Gov. Mike Waltz has appealed to the president to tone down his rhetoric,

incidents.title: Armenia Stated Plans to Extend Access to the Trump Corridor
incidents.description: Armenia stated it plans to extend access for the development of the “Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity” corridor for the next 49 years. This comes as Azerbaijan released four Armenian prisoners from Nagorno-Karabakh.

incidents.title: China Warns Domestic Firms Not to Purchase Cybersecurity Software from the US
incidents.description: China has warned domestic firms not to purchase and use cybersecurity software produced by the U.S. or Israel in the latest push for increased technological self-reliance.

incidents.title: The Foreign Ministers of Denmark and Greenland Visit Washington
incidents.description: The foreign ministers of Denmark and Greenland, Lars Lokke Rasmussen and Vivian Motzfeldt, traveled to Washington this week following repeated assertions by the Trump administration of the U.S.’s ambitions to own Greenland. Following the meeting, both sides agreed to establish a working group to continue the discussion, despite “fundamental disagreements” remaining. Following the meeting, Germany, Sweden, Norway, and the UK have sent troops to Greenland to assess how best to contribute to the island’s security.

incidents.title: EU Details 90 Billion Euro Loan for Ukraine
incidents.description: On Jan. 14, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen detailed a 90 billion euro loan for Ukraine, 60 billion of which is earmarked for military aid.

incidents.title: At Least 2,571 Deaths Reported Related to Iranian Protests
incidents.description: The U.S.-based Human Rights Activists News Agency reported at least 2,571 deaths related to Iranian protests as of Jan. 14. Unnamed sources inside Iran have reported a significantly higher casualty count, although the total could not be independently verified.

incidents.title: Hezbollah Officials Claim Efforts by Lebanese Government Are Risking Civil War
incidents.description: Senior Hezbollah official Mahmoud Qmati said that ongoing efforts by the Lebanese government to force the disarmament of the group risk plunging the nation into “civil war.”

incidents.title: Russia Accuses Ukraine of Drone Strikes on Greek Oil Vessel in Greek Waters
incidents.description: Russian defense officials accused Ukraine of being behind drone strikes that struck a Greek-owned, Maltese-flagged oil vessel in Greek waters on Jan. 13. Ukrainian officials have not commented on the attack, which was condemned by the Greek government.

incidents.title: Syrian Military Establishes a Civilian Evacuation Corridor
incidents.description: The Syrian military established a civilian evacuation corridor near Aleppo, possibly in preparation for an offensive against Kurdish forces.

incidents.title: Turkish Intelligence Informs the IRGC of Kurdish Military Crossings Into Iran
incidents.description: According to an unnamed senior Iranian official cited by Reuters, Turkey’s MIT intelligence service has informed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that Kurdish militants in Iraq are attempting to cross into Iran and “take advantage” of ongoing instability.

incidents.title: The Trump Administration Gave Formal Approval for Nvidia to Sell its H200 Chips to China
incidents.description: The Trump administration gave formal approval for Nvidia to sell its H200 chips to China, subject to certain restrictions. The company has already received orders for 2 million chips, exceeding its current inventory of 700,000. Chinese customs agents have been warned that the chips were not allowed to enter China.

incidents.title: President Trump Meets with Venezuelan Opposition Leader
incidents.description: Trump met with Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado in Washington, D.C., for the first time since President Nicolás Maduro’s capture by U.S. forces. At the same time, Trump met with a representative of the current Venezuelan government, while the U.S. State Department warned U.S. citizens to leave the country following reports that armed groups have set up roadblocks in order to find and capture Americans.

incidents.title: Nigeria Launches $2 Billion National Climate Change Fund
incidents.description: Nigeria officially launched a $2 billion national climate change fund to support the country's energy transition plan. This fund will provide financial assistance to projects that aim to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases and improve climate resilience throughout Nigeria. Separately, the United Arab Emirates and Nigeria signed a comprehensive partnership agreement with the intention of enhancing trade and investment in several areas, including climate-smart infrastructure, digital trade, and renewable energy.

incidents.title: Russia Intensifies Campaign Targeting Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure
incidents.description: Russia has intensified its winter campaign targeting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, leading to sustained power outages across Ukrainian cities, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced a state of emergency in Ukraine’s energy sector.

incidents.title: South Korean President Met with Japanese Prime Minister
incidents.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung met with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Nara, Japan where they pledged to increase economic and strategic cooperation.

incidents.title: Taiwan Confirms it Will Produce Artillary Shells with the US
incidents.description: Taiwan’s Armaments Bureau confirmed that the island would jointly produce 155 mm artillery shells, while the country’s vice minister of National Defense confirmed that talks with U.S. suppliers over more weapons sales were underway.

incidents.title: US Seizures of Santioned Shadow Fleet Oil Tankers Have Exacerbated International Tensions
incidents.description: U.S. seizures of sanctioned shadow fleet oil tankers with ties to Venezuela in international waters has halted Venezuela’s oil exports and exacerbated international tensions. The loss of export revenue could deepen the recession gripping Venezuela's oil-dependent economy and worsen humanitarian conditions in the country. China and Russia claim that the seizures constitute a violation of international laws. Russia asserted that it will continue to control oil assets it has developed in the country and will continue to honor its international partners.

incidents.title: EU Publishes its Proposal for a Minimum Price Offer for Chinese Electic Vehicle Imports
incidents.description: The EU published its proposal for a minimum price offer for Chinese electric vehicle imports, potentially replacing the tariffs of up to 35% currently in place and potentially allowing European automakers access to China as an EV export hub.

incidents.title: Ukraine Trying to Finalize Security Guarantees Document and Meet with US
incidents.description: Zelenskyy said on Jan. 12 that he directed senior Ukrainian negotiators to finalize a “historic” security guarantees document and to arrange a meeting with U.S. representatives for signing. Despite recent optimism from senior U.S. negotiators Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Jan. 14 that he believes Russian President Vladimir Putin is ready to make a deal, while Zelenskyy is “holding up the effort.”

incidents.title: US Investment Consortium Awarded Lithium Mining Rights
incidents.description: Ukraine awarded lithium mining rights to the U.S. investment consortium Dobra Lithium Holdings, as part of an ongoing effort to court U.S. diplomatic favor and infrastructural investment.

incidents.title: US Accuses Russia of Dangerous Escalation in Ukraine War
incidents.description: U.S. officials accused Russia of a “dangerous and inexplicable escalation” of the war in Ukraine, following the launch of a nuclear-capable Oreshnik missile that struck Ukrainian territory near its border with Poland.

incidents.title: President Trump Announces a 25% Tariff on Any Country Doing Business with Iran
incidents.description: On Jan. 13, Trump announced a 25% tariff on “any country doing business” with Iran.

incidents.title: Hamas Announces That it Will Dissolve its Governing Body Inside Gaza Relying on Stipulations
incidents.description: Hamas announced it would dissolve its governing body inside Gaza once a Palestinian technocratic committee is in place, in alignment with the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal. Witkoff said the U.S. is moving into Phase II of the deal, aimed at achieving the disarmament of Hamas and establishing a post-Hamas governing body. Security conditions on the ground, the pending transfer of the remains of a final deceased Israeli hostage in Gaza, and diplomatic disputes between key actors are likely to impede the progress of the ceasefire deal.

incidents.title: US Justice Department Served Grand Jury Subpoenas to the Federal Reserve
incidents.description: The Justice Department served grand jury subpoenas to the Federal Reserve, threatening a criminal indictment of Chairman Jerome Powell regarding his testimony before the Senate Banking Committee in June 2025, about renovations to the Fed’s headquarters. The move received backlash domestically and internationally, and Powell stated these threats were made within the context of a pressure campaign by the administration for the Fed to lower interest rates.

incidents.title: IDF Kills at Least 18 Palestinians Across Gaza
incidents.description: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) killed at least 18 Palestinians in a series of shootings and bombings in across Gaza.

incidents.title: North Korea Accuses South Korea Military of Flying Drones Across Their Shared Border
incidents.description: North Korea accused the South Korean military of flying drones across their shared border, warning of strong consequences despite Seoul’s denials.

incidents.title: 21 Syrians Killed After Skirmishes Between the Syrian Army and Kurdish Forces in Aleppo
incidents.description: In Syria, at least 21 people were killed and thousands displaced as fighting broke out between the Syrian army and Kurdish forces in Aleppo. The most recent skirmishes broke out after the ongoing talks over the integration of the SDF into the Syrian army stalled.

incidents.title: STC Announces its Dissolution in Yemen
incidents.description: Following a Saudi-led campaign and the ending of the UAE’s military mission in Yemen, the STC announced its dissolution on Jan 9.

incidents.title: China's Ministry of Commerce Bans Export of Dual-Use Goods to Japan
incidents.description: China’s Ministry of Commerce has banned the export of “dual-use” goods to Japan, specifically to any Japanese entities that could contribute to an enhancement of its military capabilities.

incidents.title: Chinese Companies Are Expected to Place Orders for Nvidia's H200 Chips
incidents.description: Chinese companies are expected to place orders for Nvidia’s H200 chips in the first quarter of 2026, though Beijing has increased efforts to push companies to use domestically fabricated chips instead and possibly halt orders from Nvidia.

incidents.title: India is Scrapping Some Restrictions on Chinese Companies' Abilities to Bid for Government Contracts
incidents.description: India is scrapping some restrictions on Chinese companies’ abilities to bid for government contracts, as the country pushes for strengthened economic relations with China.

incidents.title: 42 People Killed and 2,200 Detained by Iranian Government During Protests
incidents.description: At least 42 people have been killed and 2,200 detained by the Iranian government during ongoing protest activity as of Jan. 8. On Jan. 9, the Iranian government triggered an internet blackout across the country. The nationwide protest movement was sparked primarily by faltering economic conditions

incidents.title: Lebanese Government Declares State Monopoly Over Arms in Southern Lebanon
incidents.description: The Lebanese government declared it had established a state monopoly over arms in southern Lebanon. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netenyahu disputed the claims, describing the status of disarmament efforts as “encouraging” but “insufficient.”

incidents.title: US Seizes Russian-Flagged Oil Vessel Protected by Russian Naval Assets in North Atlantic
incidents.description: The U.S. seized a Russian-flagged oil vessel protected by Russian naval assets in the North Atlantic after the vessel attempted to bypass a U.S. blockade enforcing sanctions on Venezuela. The vessel’s crew did not offer resistance, and Russian naval assets did not intervene.

incidents.title: US President has "Greenlit" Proposed Bipartisan Sanctions Package on Russia's Energy Sector
incidents.description: U.S. Sen. Lindsay Graham said U.S. President Donald Trump has “greenlit” a proposed bipartisan sanctions package targeting Russia’s energy sector. The legislation would enact secondary sanctions against major buyers of Russian energy exports, including India, Brazil and China.

incidents.title: Domestic Backlash Soars Over ICE Killing of a Woman in Minneapolis
incidents.description: An Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot dead a 37-year-old woman in Minneapolis following the agency’s deployment to Minnesota as part of the administration’s crackdown on migration.
